Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

Khuddakanikāye

Khuddaka Nikāya: The Minor Collection

Nettivibhāvinī

Nettivibhāvinī: Elucidating the Pathfinder

Ganthārambhakathā

Introduction to the Text

Yajitabbaṃ [V 0.0145][M 0.0001] yajitvāna, namitabbaṃ namāmahaṃ;

Yajanādyānubhāvena, antarāye jahaṃ sadā.

Having worshipped what ought to be worshipped, I bow to what ought to be bowed to; by the power of worship and so forth, may I always abandon obstacles.

Yena yā racitā netti, yena sā anumoditā;

Yehi saṃvaṇṇanā katā, tesānubhāvanissito.

By whom the Netti was composed, by whom it was approved, by whom its explanations were made—I rely on their power.

Kiñci kiñci saritvāna, līnālīnānusandhyādiṃ;

Karissaṃ jinasuttānaṃ, hitaṃ nettivibhāvanaṃ.

Recalling whatever I can, and the connections both subtle and manifest, I will compose a beneficial explanation of the Guide for the welfare of the Victor’s teachings.

Appameyyaguṇo [V 0.0146] mahādhammarājavhayo bhave;

Acchariyo abbhuto yo, bodhisambhārapūraṇo.

The one of immeasurable qualities, called the great king of Dhamma; the marvelous, the astonishing, who fulfills the accumulations for enlightenment.

Nānāraṭṭhissarissaro, seṭṭho sāsanapaggaho;

Pāsaṃsarājapāsaṃso, narācinteyyacintako.

The overlord of many realms, foremost, a support for the Teaching; praised by praiseworthy kings, a thinker of thoughts unthinkable by men.

Cintitakārako rājā, siraṭṭhimālapālako;

Ajeyyajeyyako mahācetyādikārako sadā.

A king who fulfills thoughts, the guardian of the crown and garland; always the conqueror of the unconquered, the maker of great shrines and the like.

Assāmaccena byattena, jinacakkahitatthinā;

Anantasutināmena, sakkaccaṃ abhiyācito.

Earnestly requested by his minister, named Anantasuti, who was intelligent and desired the welfare of the Conqueror's domain.

Kāmaṃ saṃvaṇṇanā katā, therāsabhehi gambhīrā;

Gambhīrattā tu jānituṃ, jinaputtehi dukkarā.

Indeed, a profound exposition was made by the chief elders; but due to its profundity, it is difficult for the sons of the Victor to understand.

Tasmā [M 0.0002] yācitānurūpena, karissaṃ sādaraṃ suṇa;

Sissasikkhanayānugaṃ, yottaṃ nettivibhāvananti.

Therefore, in accordance with the request, I shall compose this elucidation of the Netti, a guide that follows the method for training disciples. Listen with respect.

1. Saṅgahavāraatthavibhāvanā

1. The Elucidation of the Meaning of the Section on Inclusion

Tattha yassa sikkhattayasaṅgahassa navaṅgassa satthusāsanavarassa atthasaṃvaṇṇanaṃ yaṃ nettippakaraṇaṃ kātukāmo, tassa nettippakaraṇassa nissayaṃ visayabhūtaṃ saṃvaṇṇetabbasahitaṃ, saṃvaṇṇetabbaṃ eva vā salokapālena tilokena sadā pūjetabbassa ceva namassitabbassa ca naruttamassa satthuno sāsanavaraṃ vidūheva ñātabbaṃ. Etaṃ sāsanavaraṃ tāva dassento taṃjanakena, taṃvijānakavidūhi ca niyametuṃ, ratanattayaguṇaparidīpanañca kātuṃ –

Here, for one who wishes to compose the Nettippakaraṇa—which is an exposition of the meaning of the excellent Dispensation of the Teacher, a Dispensation comprising nine divisions and embracing the threefold training—it is to be known by the wise that this excellent Dispensation of the supreme Teacher, who is always worthy of homage and veneration by the three worlds together with their guardians, is the basis and scope of that Nettippakaraṇa, along with what is to be explained, or simply what is to be explained. In order to show this excellent Dispensation, to establish it by its originator and by the wise who understand it, and to illuminate the qualities of the Triple Gem, he states:

“Yaṃ loko pūjayate, salokapālo sadā namassati ca;

Tasseta sāsanavaraṃ, vidūhi ñeyyaṃ naravarassā”ti. – paṭhamagāthamāha;

“That excellent Dispensation of the best of men, which the world with its guardians always honors and venerates, should be known by the wise.” – Thus he spoke the first verse.

Imāya [V 0.0147] hi paṭhamagāthāya “etaṃ sāsanavaraṃ ñeyya”nti ettakameva ekantato karaṇavisesabhāvena adhippetaṃ. Eteneva visesakaraṇena ekantādhippetanettivisayasāsanavarassa dassitattā. Ekantādhippetasāsanavarameva nettisaṃvaṇṇanāya saṃvaṇṇetabbattā visayaṃ teneva vakkhati aṭṭhakathācariyo –

For by this first verse, only this much is intended as a uniquely significant action: 'this excellent Dispensation should be known.' Because this very significant action reveals the excellent Dispensation which is the exclusively intended scope of the Netti, and because only this exclusively intended excellent Dispensation is to be expounded in the exposition of the Netti, the commentator will therefore state its scope:

“Etaṃ idāni amhehi vibhajitabbahāranayapaṭṭhānavicāraṇavisayabhūtaṃ sāsanaṃ ādikalyāṇatādiguṇasampattiyā varaṃ aggaṃ uttamaṃ nipuṇañāṇagocaratāya paṇḍitavedanīyamevā”ti (netti. aṭṭha. saṅgahavāravaṇṇanā) ca,

“This Dispensation, which is now the subject of our investigation into the Paṭṭhāna, the guidelines (naya), and the modes of conveying (hāra) that are to be analyzed, is excellent, supreme, and foremost due to its possession of qualities such as being good in the beginning; and because it is the domain of subtle knowledge, it is knowable only by the wise.” (Netti Commentary, Section on Inclusion) and,

“Etaṃ tividhampi ‘sāsanavara’nti padena saṅgaṇhitvā tattha yaṃ paṭhamaṃ, taṃ itaresaṃ adhigamūpāyoti sabbasāsanamūlabhūtaṃ, attano pakaraṇassa ca visayabhūtaṃ pariyattisāsanamevā”ti (netti. aṭṭha. saṅgahavāravaṇṇanā) ca,

“Having summarized these three kinds with the term ‘excellent Dispensation,’ among them, that which is first is the means for the attainment of the others, is the root of the entire Dispensation, and is the scope of our own treatise; it is solely the scriptural Dispensation.” (Netti Commentary, Section on Inclusion) and,

“Idāni [M 0.0003] yaṃ vuttaṃ ‘sāsanavaraṃ vidūhi ñeyya’nti, tattha nettisaṃvaṇṇanāya visayabhūtaṃ pariyattidhammameva pakārantarena niyametvā dassetu”nti (netti. aṭṭha. saṅgahavāravaṇṇanā) ca.

“Now, regarding what was said, ‘The excellent Dispensation should be known by the wise,’ the intention there is to show the scriptural teaching—which is the subject matter of the Netti exposition—by defining it through another method.” (Netti Commentary, Section on Inclusion)

Tattha pariyattisāsanassāpi mūlaṃ hotīti vuttaṃ “sabbasāsanamūlabhūta”nti. Etena kammasādhanenapi adhippetatthe siddhe nānāvidhasādhakavacanaṃ nānāvādānaṃ anokāsakaraṇatthāya kataṃ. Svākkhātatādidhammaguṇā pana sāsanassa visesadesakanaravarasaddena vā paridīpakatthabhāvena vā dīpitā avinābhāvato. Sāsanavarassa pana janakasambandhipekkhattā “naravarassā”ti vuttaṃ. Tena ca aggapuggalo sāsanavarajanako vācakatthasambandhibhāvena vutto. Anaññasādhāraṇamahākaruṇāsabbaññutaññāṇādiguṇavisesā pana janakasambandhibhūtassa narassa visesakenavarasaddena vā paridīpakatthabhāvena vā dīpito.

Therein, it is stated by the phrase ‘being the root of the entire Dispensation’ that it is also the root of the scriptural Dispensation. By this instrumental expression, once the intended meaning is established, various statements of proof are made in order to leave no room for diverse doctrines. The qualities of the Dhamma, such as being well-proclaimed, are illuminated either by the word ‘naravara’ (best of men), which indicates the distinction of the Dispensation, or by their nature as illuminators of the meaning, due to their inseparability. Moreover, because the excellence of the Dispensation is considered in relation to its originator, it is said, ‘of the best of men.’ By this, the foremost person, the originator of the excellent Dispensation, is spoken of through the connection between the word and its meaning. And the specific, unparalleled qualities, such as great compassion and omniscient knowledge, are illuminated either by the word ‘vara’ (excellent) which qualifies the man who is their originator, or by their nature as illuminators of the meaning.

Kiṃ nu so sāsanavarajanako naravaro paramatthova, udāhu pūjanīyo ceva namassanīyo cāti vuttaṃ “yaṃ loko…pe… namassati cā”ti, tena sāsanavarajanako naravaro paramatthova na hoti, atha kho salokapālena lokena sadā sabbakālesu pūjanīyo ceva namassanīyo cāti visesito thomitoti.

Is that originator of the excellent Dispensation, the best of men, the ultimate reality itself, or is he one to be honored and venerated? It is said: “Whom the world… venerates.” Therefore, that originator of the excellent Dispensation, the best of men, is not the ultimate reality itself, but rather he is specifically praised as one to be honored and venerated by the world with its guardians at all times.

Ettha [V 0.0148] ca pūjananamassanacetanāvācakena vā pūjananamassanasaddena phalūpacārattho puññamahattasaṅkhāto pūjanīyabhāvo ceva āsavakkhayañāṇapadaṭṭhānasabbaññutaññāṇādiguṇasaṅkhāto namassanīyabhāvo ca dīpakatthabhāvena pariggahetvā dīpito. Tenāha aṭṭhakathācariyo “bhagavato sadevakassa lokassa pūjanīyavandanīyabhāvo, aggapuggalabhāvo ca vuccamāno guṇavisiṭṭhataṃ dīpetī”tiādi (netti. aṭṭha. saṅgahavāravaṇṇanā).

Here, by the word indicating the intention to honor and venerate, or by the term for honor and veneration itself, there is illuminated—by way of figurative extension to the result—the state of being worthy of honor, known as greatness of merit, and the state of being worthy of veneration, known by qualities such as the knowledge of the destruction of the taints, the basis for omniscient knowledge. These are shown by being understood as illuminators of the meaning. Therefore, the commentator said: “The Blessed One's state of being worthy of honor and veneration by the world with its devas, and his state as the foremost individual, being spoken of, illuminates his distinction in virtue,” and so on (Netti Commentary, Section on Inclusion).

Tādisassa naravarassa tādisaṃ sāsanavaraṃ kiṃ yena kenaci viññeyyanti vuttaṃ “vidūhī”ti. Tena tipiṭakadharā ariyabhūtā paṇḍitā vācakatthabhāvena gahitā, suppaṭipannatādisaṅghaguṇā pana vandadhātuvacanena vā dīpakatthabhāvena vā dīpitāti. Evaṃ pariggahetvā dīpite ratanattayaguṇe sandhāya “evaṃ paṭhamagāthāya sātisayaṃ ratanattayaguṇaparidīpanaṃ katvā”ti (netti. aṭṭha. saṅgahavāravaṇṇanā) vakkhati, na gāthāya niravasesatthe. Tattha [M 0.0004] evanti evaṃ sāsanavaradassanabhūtāya paṭhamagāthāyāti atthova daṭṭhabbo. Apare panācariyā “imāya paṭhamagāthāya ekantato adhippetānādhippetavacanāni ceva vācakatthadīpakatthavisesāni ca suṭṭhu avicāretvā ‘evaṃ paṭhamagāthāya sātisayaṃ ratanattayaguṇaparidīpanaṃ katvā’ti vacanacchāyaṃ nissāya sātisayaṃ ratanattayaguṇaparidīpanaṃ kātuṃ ‘yaṃ lokotyādimāhā’ti ca sātisayaratanattayaguṇe dassento ‘yaṃ lokotyādimāhā’ti” ca vadanti. Tesaṃ vādo amhākaṃ nakkhamati. Kāraṇaṃ pana mayā heṭṭhā vuttānusārena ñātabbanti ayaṃ padānukkamānurūpānusandhyattho.

Of such a best of men, such an excellent Dispensation—is it to be known by just anyone? Thus it is said, “by the wise.” By this, the wise, the noble ones who are bearers of the Tipiṭaka, are taken in the sense of the speaker, while the qualities of the Saṅgha, such as being of good practice, are illuminated either by the word for paying homage or in the sense of an illuminator. With reference to the qualities of the Triple Gem thus understood and illuminated, it will be said, “In this way, having abundantly illuminated the qualities of the Triple Gem with the first verse…” (Netti Commentary, Section on Inclusion), which refers not to the exhaustive meaning of the verse. Therein, ‘thus’ should be understood to mean ‘by this first verse, which is a means of seeing the excellent Dispensation.’ Other teachers, however, without properly investigating the intended and unintended statements of this first verse, nor the distinctions between the literal and the illustrative sense, and relying merely on the shadow of the words, “In this way, having abundantly illuminated the qualities of the Triple Gem with the first verse…,” say that he spoke “Whom the world…” in order to abundantly illuminate the qualities of the Triple Gem, and showing those abundant qualities, he spoke “Whom the world…”. Their doctrine is not acceptable to us. The reason for this should be understood according to what has been stated by me above. This is the meaning of the connection that accords with the sequence of the words.

Atha vā ekaṃ samayaṃ jambuvanasaṇḍe nisīditvā sissānaṃ hitaṃ cintento, attano abhinīhārasampattiṃ passanto, sammāsambuddhena pasaṃsito, mahākaccāyano satthārā anumoditaṃ sāsanāyattaṃ navaṅgassatthavaṇṇanaṃ soḷasahārādianekatthavidhaṃ nettippakaraṇaṃ ārabhanto, “yaṃ loko”tyādimāha. Yadi evaṃ yathāvuttappakāraṃ nettippakaraṇabhūtaṃ soḷasahārātyādikaṃ ārabhitabbaṃ, taṃ anārabhitvā kasmā nettippakaraṇato bahibhūtaṃ “yaṃ loko”tyādikaṃ ārabhitabbaṃ, seyyathāpi ambaṃ puṭṭho labujaṃ byākareyya, labujaṃ puṭṭho ambaṃ byākareyya, evameva nettippakaraṇamārabhanto aññaṃ ārabhatīti? Tathāpi yassa yathāvuttassa sāsanavarassa atthasaṃvaṇṇanaṃ yaṃ nettippakaraṇaṃ kātukāmo yassa nettippakaraṇassa visayabhūtaṃ saṃvaṇṇetabbasahitaṃ, saṃvaṇṇetabbaṃ eva vā taṃ sāsanavaraṃ tāva dassento taṃjanakena, taṃvijānakavidūhi ca niyametuṃ, ratanattayaguṇaparidīpanañca kātuṃ “yaṃ loko”tyādimāha. Ayaṃ līnantaracodanāsahito anusandhyattho.

Or at one time, sitting in the Jambu Grove, considering the welfare of his disciples, seeing the fulfillment of his own aspiration, praised by the Fully Enlightened One, Mahākaccāyana, approved by the Teacher, intending to begin the Nettippakaraṇa—an explanation of the meaning of the ninefold teaching through various methods beginning with the sixteen modes, a work belonging to the dispensation—said, “What the world…” If it is so, why should one begin with “What the world…,” which is outside of the Nettippakaraṇa, instead of beginning with the sixteen modes and other aspects as described, which constitute the Nettippakaraṇa? It would be like someone asked about a mango answering about a breadfruit, or asked about a breadfruit answering about a mango. Similarly, when beginning the Nettippakaraṇa, he begins with something else. Nevertheless, wishing to compose the Nettippakaraṇa, which is an exposition of the meaning of the excellent teaching as described, he first presents that excellent teaching itself—the subject of the Nettippakaraṇa, along with what is to be expounded, or simply what is to be expounded—in order to establish it for those who gave rise to it and for the learned who understand it, and to illuminate the qualities of the Triple Gem; thus he begins with “What the world…” This is the connected meaning, along with the implicit objection.

“Yaṃ [V 0.0149] loko pūjayate, salokapālo sadā namassati ca;

Tasseta sāsanavaraṃ, vidūhi ñeyyaṃ naravarassā”ti. –

“Whom the world with its protectors reveres, and always pays homage to; this is the excellent teaching of that Best of Men, to be known by the wise.”

Niggahitalopaṃ katvā racitā gāthā ariyāsāmaññalakkhaṇena sampannā. Kathaṃ? Pubbaḍḍhe tiṃsa mattā, aparaḍḍhe sattavīsa mattā. Sampiṇḍitā sattapaññāsa mattāva bhavanti. Akkharānaṃ pana imissaṃ gāthāyaṃ sattatiṃsa. Tesu garukkharā vīsati, lahukkharā sattarasa bhavanti. “Tassetaṃ sāsanavara”nti pana sānunāsikaṃ virujjhati.

The verse, composed with elision of the niggahita, possesses the general characteristics of the Āriyā meter. How so? In the first half, there are thirty morae; in the latter half, twenty-seven morae. Combined, they total fifty-seven morae. As for the syllables in this verse, there are thirty-seven. Among them, twenty are heavy syllables, and seventeen are light. The reading “Tassetaṃ sāsanavara,” however, with the nasal, is problematic.

Tattha [M 0.0005] niddesattho aṭṭhakathānusārena vijānitabbo. Salokapālo sabbo sattaloko sakkaccaṃ sabbaññutaññāṇādianekaguṇānussaraṇena vā pūjetabbapūjanena vā paṭipattipūjanena vā sadā sabbakālesu sakkaccaṃ yaṃ naravaraṃ pūjayate ceva namassati ca, tassa pūjetabbassa ceva namassitabbassa ca satthuno naravarassa tilokaggassa mayā saṃvaṇṇetabbasahitaṃ, saṃvaṇṇetabbaṃ eva vā vidūheva ñeyyaṃ ñātabbaṃ. Nipuṇañāṇagocaraṃ etaṃ mayā buddhiyaṃ ṭhapitaṃ sāsanavaraṃ mayā ārabhitabbassa nettippakaraṇassa visayanti paṭhamaṃ jānitabbaṃ dassetvā tassa atthasaṃvaṇṇanābhūtaṃ nettippakaraṇaṃ ahaṃ ārabhissāmi, taṃ tumhe sādhavo suṇātha manasi karothāti samudāyayojanā, avayavayojanāpi kātabbā.

Here, the meaning of the exposition should be understood in accordance with the commentary. The entire world of beings, together with its protectors, always, at all times, carefully reveres and pays homage to that Best of Men, the foremost in the three worlds, through remembrance of his many qualities such as omniscience, or through the worship of what is worthy of worship, or through the worship of practice. That excellent teaching of the Teacher, the Best of Men, the foremost in the three worlds, who is worthy of reverence and homage, should be known by the wise, either together with my exposition or simply as it is to be expounded. Having first shown that this excellent teaching—which is the domain of subtle knowledge and which I have established in my mind as the subject matter of the Nettippakaraṇa that I am about to undertake—I shall then commence the Nettippakaraṇa, which is an exposition of its meaning. ‘Good people, listen to it and pay attention!’—this is the overall construction; a part-by-part construction should also be made.

Kathaṃ? “Salokapālo loko”ti visesanavisesitabbabhāvena yojanā. Lokapālo vajjetvā avaseso loko ca na hoti, atha kho lokapālasahito lokoti viseseti. “Loko pūjayate ceva namassati cā”ti kattukārakaākhyātakiriyābhāvena yojanā “yo karoti, sa kattā”ti vuttattā. Yo loko kārako, so kattā hotu. Yo loko pūjayate ceva namassati ca, kathaṃ so kattāti? “Yo karoti, sa kattā”ti suttassa “yo karoti kiriyaṃ nipphādeti, so kiriyānipphādako kattā”ti atthasambhavato sayanabhuñjanādisabbakiriyānipphādako kattāyeva hoti. Ayañca loko pūjananamassanakiriyānipphādakoyevāti. Kathaṃ ayaṃ loko kiriyānipphādakoti? “Loko”ti sattapaññattiyā paramatthato avijjamānāyapi paññāpetabbo santāne pavattamāno hadayavatthunissito cittuppādo gahetabbo, so yathārahaṃ hetādhipatisahajātādipaccayena paccayo nipphādako bhave. Evaṃ lokassa kattukārakabhāvo vijānitabboti paccayapaccayuppannabhāvena yojanā. Esa nayo tīsu piṭakesupi evarūpesu ṭhānesu.

How? ‘The world with its protectors’ is to be construed by way of the relation between qualifier and qualified. It is not that the world is what remains apart from the world-protectors; rather, it specifies that the world is together with the world-protectors. ‘The world both reveres and pays homage’ is to be construed by way of the agent-action relation of the finite verb, because it is said, ‘Whoever acts, that is the agent.’ Let the world that is the doer be the agent. How is the world that both reveres and pays homage an agent? Because from the rule, ‘Whoever acts, that is the agent,’ the meaning arises, ‘Whoever performs an action, that is the performer of the action,’ the performer of all actions such as lying down and eating is indeed the agent. And this world is indeed the performer of the actions of revering and paying homage. How is this world the performer of actions? By ‘world,’ although as a designation for a being it is ultimately non-existent, should be understood the arising of consciousness that occurs in the continuum, is based on the heart-base, and is to be designated. That, as appropriate, becomes a producing condition through conditions such as root-cause, dominance, and co-nascence. In this way, the world’s nature as an agent-doer should be understood by way of the relation between condition and conditioned. This is the method in the three Piṭakas in such instances.

“Yaṃ [V 0.0150] naravaraṃ pūjayate ceva namassati cā”ti kammakārakaākhyātakiriyābhāvena yojanā “yaṃ karoti, taṃ kamma”nti vuttattā. Yaṃ kātabbaṃ, taṃ kammaṃ hotu. Yaṃ pūjayati ceva namassati ca, kathaṃ taṃ kammanti? “Yaṃ [M 0.0006] karoti, taṃ kamma”nti suttassa “yaṃ karoti kiriyāya sambajjhati, kiriyāya sambajjhitabbaṃ kamma”nti atthasambhavato karaṇavācakavacanīyādisabbakiriyāya sambajjhitabbaṃ kammaṃ hotveva. Ayañca naravaro pūjananamassanakiriyāya vācakavacanīyabhāvena sambajjhitabboyevāti. Kathaṃ ayaṃ naravaro vacanīyoti? Pūjananamassanacetanāya ārammaṇakaraṇavasena naravaro vacanīyo, cetanā vācakā, evaṃ vācakavacitabbabhāvo hotveva. “Yaṃ naravara”nti paññattiyā paramatthato avijjamānāyapi paññāpetabbo santānavasena pavattamāno lokiyalokuttaraguṇasahito khandhapañcako vutto, so ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo, cetanā paccayuppannāti paccayapaccayuppannabhāvena yojanā. Esa nayo tīsu piṭakesu evarūpesu ṭhānesu.

‘The Best of Men whom [the world] both reveres and pays homage to’ is to be construed by way of the object-action relation of the finite verb, because it is said, ‘Whatever one acts upon, that is the object.’ Let what is to be acted upon be the object. How is he whom one both reveres and pays homage to an object? According to the meaning that arises from the rule ‘Whatever one acts upon, that is the object’—namely, ‘Whatever is connected with the action, that which is to be connected with the action is the object’—all that is to be connected with any action, such as the instrumental, the verbal, the spoken, etc., is indeed the object. And this Best of Men is indeed to be connected with the action of revering and paying homage by way of being the one spoken of. How is this Best of Men the one spoken of? The Best of Men is the one spoken of by being the object and instrument of the intention to revere and pay homage; the intention is the speaker. Thus, the relation of speaker and spoken-of is indeed established. By ‘the Best of Men,’ although as a designation it is ultimately non-existent, is meant the five aggregates occurring in a continuum, endowed with worldly and supramundane qualities, which is to be designated. That is the condition through the object-condition; the intention is the conditioned. Thus, the relation between condition and conditioned is to be construed. This is the method in the three Piṭakas in such instances.

“Tassa naravarassā”ti visesanavisesitabbabhāvena yojanā. Naravaro nāma nimantitabbādiko na hoti, atha kho pūjetabbo namassitabbo evāti viseseti. Tassa pūjetabbassa ceva namassitabbassa ca naravarassa sāsanavaranti jaññajanakabhāvena yojanā. Sāsanavaraṃ nāma paccekabuddhasāvakabuddharājarājādīnaṃ sāsanavaraṃ na hoti, pūjetabbassa ceva namassitabbassa ca naravarassa tilokasseva sāsanavaranti niyameti.

‘Of that Best of Men’ is to be construed by way of the relation between qualifier and qualified. The Best of Men is not merely one to be invited and so on; rather, it specifies that he is indeed one to be revered and paid homage to. ‘The excellent teaching of that Best of Men, who is worthy of reverence and homage’ is to be construed by way of the relation between what is to be known and what generates it. The excellent teaching is not the excellent teaching of Paccekabuddhas, disciple-buddhas, kings, great kings, and so on; rather, it is determined that it is the excellent teaching of that Best of Men, who is worthy of reverence and homage, for the three worlds.

“Vidūhi ñeyya”nti kattukārakakitakiriyābhāvena yojanā. Kattubhāvo heṭṭhā vuttova. “Vidūhī”ti sattapaññattiyā paramatthato avijjamānāyapi paññāpetabbo santāne pavattamāno sāsanavare sammohadhaṃsakañāṇasahito hadayavatthunissito cittuppādo vutto, so yathārahaṃ hetādhipatisahajātādipaccayena paccayo nipphādako bhave. Ñā-itidhātuyā atthabhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ paccayuppannaṃ nipphādeyyaṃ bhave, evaṃ paccayapaccayuppannabhāvena yojanā.

‘To be known by the wise’ is to be construed by way of the agent-doer relation of the participial verb. The nature of the agent has already been stated above. By ‘the wise,’ although as a designation for a being it is ultimately non-existent, is meant the arising of consciousness that occurs in the continuum, is based on the heart-base, is endowed with knowledge that dispels delusion concerning the excellent teaching, and is to be designated. That, as appropriate, becomes a producing condition through conditions such as root-cause, dominance, and co-nascence. Knowledge, which is the meaning of the root ‘ñā,’ would be the conditioned that is to be produced. Thus, it is to be construed by way of the relation between condition and conditioned.

“Ñeyyaṃ sāsanavara”nti visesanavisesyabhāvena yojanā. Sāsanavaraṃ nāma na yena kenaci ñeyyaṃ, atha kho vidūheva saṇhasukhumañāṇena ñeyyaṃ sāsanavaranti viseseti.

‘The excellent teaching to be known’ is to be construed by way of the relation between qualifier and qualified. The excellent teaching is not to be known by just anyone; rather, it specifies that the excellent teaching is to be known only by the wise with their subtle and refined knowledge.

“Etaṃ sāsanavara”nti visesanavisesyabhāvena yojanā. Sāsanavaraṃ nāma mayā buddhiyaṃ aṭṭhapitaṃ appavattetabbaṃ hoti, mayā idāni nettippakaraṇassa visayabhāvena buddhiyaṃ viparivattamānaṃ ṭhapetabbaṃ pavattetabbaṃ sāsanavaranti [M 0.0007] viseseti. Etaṃ sāsanavaraṃ nettippakaraṇassa [V 0.0151] visayanti yojanā kātabbā. Tenāha “etaṃ idāni amhehi vibhajitabbahāranayapaṭṭhānavicāraṇavisayabhūtaṃ sāsana”nti (netti. aṭṭha. saṅgahavāravaṇṇanā). Iccevaṃ nettiyā paṭhamagāthāya saṅkhepena yojanattho samatto.

‘This excellent teaching’ is to be construed by way of qualifier and qualified. The excellent teaching is not something that, having been established in my mind, is to be left unexpressed; rather, it specifies that the excellent teaching is now to be established and expressed by me, revolving in my mind as the subject matter of the Nettippakaraṇa. The construction ‘This excellent teaching is the subject matter of the Nettippakaraṇa’ should be made. Therefore, it is said: ‘This teaching is now the subject matter of investigation into the methods of distribution and principles to be analyzed by us’ (Netti. Aṭṭha. Saṅgahavāravaṇṇanā). Thus, the meaning of the construction of the first verse of the Netti is concisely concluded.

Tattha yanti aniyamanaravarassa satthuno vācakaṃ payogavantasabbanāmaṃ. Aniyamo ca pūjananamassanakiriyāya aniyamitattā vutto, na naravarato aññasattassa sambhavatoti. Esa nayo sesāniyatesupi tīsu piṭakesu. Lokiyanti ettha puññāpuññāni, tabbipāko cāti loko.Ettha sattanikāye puññāpuññāni lokiyanti pavattanti, tabbipāko ca lokiyati pavattati, iti sattanikāyassa puññāpuññānaṃ, tabbipākassa ca pavattanassa ādhārabhāvato “etthā”tipadena niddiṭṭho sattanikāyo lokonāma. Pūjayateti viggahavirahitaṃ ākhyātapadaṃ, sakkaccaṃ pūjanaṃ karoti.

Herein, ‘yaṃ’ is a meaningful pronoun referring to the Teacher, the noble one, who is unspecified. And ‘unspecified’ is stated because of being unspecified with regard to the action of honoring and paying homage, meaning it does not occur to any other being apart from the noble one. This is the method also in the remaining unspecified instances in the three Piṭakas. Herein, ‘world’ (loka) means wholesome and unwholesome actions and their results. In this context, wholesome and unwholesome actions occur mundanely in the realm of beings, and their results also occur mundanely. Thus, because the realm of beings is the basis for the occurrence of wholesome and unwholesome actions and their results, the realm of beings indicated by the word ‘herein’ is called ‘world’. ‘Pūjayati’ is a finite verb without analysis, meaning ‘he performs honoring carefully.’

Lokaṃ pālentīti lokapālā, puññāpuññānañceva tabbipākassa ca pavattanādhārattā lokā ca. Ke te? Cattāro mahārājāno, indayamavaruṇakuverā vā, khattiyacatumahārājasakkasuyāmasantusitasunimmitaparanimmitavasavattimahābrahmādayo vā. Pālanañcettha issariyādhipaccena taṃtaṃsattalokassa aññamaññavihesananivāraṇādiāṇāpavattāpanayasaparivāraṭṭhānantarādiniyyādanā, saha lokapālehi yo vattatīti salokapālo. Atha vā ye hirottappā lokaṃ pālenti, iti pālanato te hirottappā lokapālā. Tenāha bhagavā “dveme, bhikkhave, sukkā dhammā lokaṃ pālentī”ti (a. ni. 2.9; itivu. 42). Lokapālehi hirottappehi samannāgato loko salokapālo nāma. Hirottappasampanno hi sappuriso loko sakkaccaṃ sadā sabbakālesu pūjayati ceva namassati ca pāpahirijigucchanato, dhammacchandavantatāya ca.

They protect the world, thus they are world-protectors (lokapālā); and because they are the basis for the occurrence of wholesome and unwholesome actions and their results, they are also ‘worlds’ (lokā). Who are they? The Four Great Kings, or Indra, Yama, Varuṇa, and Kuvera; or the khattiyas, the Four Great Kings, Sakka, Suyāma, Santusita, Sunimmita, Paranimmita, Vasavatti, Mahābrahmā, and so forth. And herein, protection refers to the exercise of sovereignty and dominion, the issuing of commands to prevent mutual harm among beings in their respective realms, the maintenance of order, the assignment of places, the settling of disputes, and so forth. That which exists together with the world-protectors is called ‘salokapālo’. Alternatively, those moral shame (hiri) and moral dread (ottappa) that protect the world—because of this protection, moral shame and moral dread are world-protectors. Therefore, the Blessed One said: ‘Monks, these two bright qualities protect the world’ (AN 2.9; Itiv. 42). The world endowed with moral shame and moral dread, which are world-protectors, is called ‘salokapālo’. For the world, in the sense of a virtuous person endowed with moral shame and moral dread, always respectfully honors and pays homage to the noble one at all times, out of disgust for evil and because of their inclination toward the Dhamma.

Aññe pana pūjentā namassantāpi kadāciyeva pūjenti namassanti, na sabbadāti. Sadāti pūjananamassanakālavācakaviggahavirahitaṃ vikappanāmaṃ, sabbanāmaṃ vā. Namassatīti viggahavirahitaṃ ākhyātapadaṃ, sakkaccaṃ namassanaṃ karoti. Tassetāti [M 0.0008] ettha tassāti niyamavācakaṃ payogavantasabbanāmaṃ viggahavirahitameva. Niyamo ca pūjananamassanakiriyāya visesito. Tasmā tassa pūjananamassanakiriyāya niyamitabbassa pūjetabbassa namassitabbassa naravarassāti attho yuttova. Sesaniyamesu aññesupi eseva nayo. Etanti ācariyena vibhajitabbahāranayapaṭṭhānavicāraṇavisayabhūtassa [V 0.0152] sāsanavaraparāmasanaṃ payogavantasabbanāmaṃ viggahavirahitaṃ.

Others, however, even when honoring and paying homage, sometimes honor and pay homage, but not always. ‘Sadā’ is a derivative noun or a pronoun, indicating the time of honoring and paying homage, without grammatical analysis. ‘Namassati’ is a finite verb without grammatical analysis, meaning ‘he performs paying homage carefully.’ In ‘tass’etaṃ’, ‘tassa’ is a meaningful pronoun indicating determination, without grammatical analysis. And the determination is specified by the action of honoring and paying homage. Therefore, the meaning ‘of that noble one, who is worthy of honor and homage, who is to be determined by the action of honoring and paying homage’ is indeed appropriate. The same method applies to other determinations as well. ‘Etaṃ’ is a meaningful pronoun without grammatical analysis, referring to the excellent teaching, which is the subject matter of the teacher’s investigation into the methods of distribution and principles to be analyzed.

Sāsati etenāti sāsanaṃ, etena navavidhasuttantena, navavidhasuttantasahitena vā varena sabbena samatthe veneyye diṭṭhadhammikasamparāyikaparamatthehi tividhayānamukhena yathārahaṃ satte sāsati anusāsati vineti. Iti sāsanānusāsanakiriyānusārena veneyyasattānaṃ jānanapaṭipajjanādhigamassa kāraṇakaraṇattā “etenā”ti padena niddiṭṭhaṃ navavidhasuttantaṃ, navavidhasuttantasahitaṃ vā varaṃ sabbaṃ sāsanaṃ nāma. Navavidhasuttantadesanāya hi veneyyānaṃ jānanaṃ purimajānanena pacchimajānanaṃ, jānanena paṭipajjanena pacchimapaṭipajjanena adhigamo, purimādhigamena pacchimādhigamo hoti. Tena vuttaṃ “saddhā sīlaṃ sutaṃ cāgo paññā saddhāya sīlassa sutassa cāgassa paññāyā”ti (paṭṭhā. 1.1.423) ca “paṭhamassa jhānassa parikammaṃ paṭhamassa jhānassa”tyādi (paṭṭhā. 1.1.423) ca. Sāsadhātuyā desanāsaddo ca taṃjanako desanāñāṇasampayuttacittuppādo ca mukhyattho, taṃupanissayapaccayā veneyyānaṃ atthajānanapaṭipajjanaadhigamanādi kāraṇūpacārattho, “etenā”ti padena vuttāya sāsanabhūtāya nāmapaññattiyā karaṇasattisaṅkhātā upanissayapaccayasatti phalūpacārattho. Iti-saddopi tameva nāmapaññattiyā upanissayapaccayasattiṃ hetubhāvena parāmasati, tassā sattiyā ādhārabhūtā nāmapaññatti yu-paccayattho. Eseva nayo tīsu piṭakesu evarūpesu ṭhānesu.

It is called 'sāsana' because it instructs (sāsati) by means of this. Through this ninefold division of the Suttas, or through the noble, all-encompassing teaching (vara) combined with the ninefold division of the Suttas, it rightly instructs, guides, and trains beings capable of being taught (veneyya) in three ways according to their suitability: for their welfare in this life, in the next life, and for the ultimate goal. Thus, in accordance with the act of instructing and guiding, because it is the cause and instrument of knowledge, practice, and attainment for beings to be taught, the ninefold division of the Suttas—or the noble, all-encompassing teaching combined with the ninefold division of the Suttas—is designated by the word 'etena' as the entire 'sāsana.' For through the teaching of the ninefold division of the Suttas, for the trainees, subsequent knowledge arises from prior knowledge; attainment arises from knowledge, practice, and subsequent practice; and subsequent attainment arises from prior attainment. Therefore, it is said: 'Faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom—for faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom' (Paṭṭhā. 1.1.423), and 'The preliminary work for the first Jhāna, for the first Jhāna itself,' and so on (Paṭṭhā. 1.1.423). The primary meaning of the root 'sās' is the word 'desanā' (teaching) and the mind-moment conjoined with knowledge of the teaching that generates it. Figuratively, due to it being a supporting condition, it indicates enabling beings to understand the meaning, to practice, to attain, and so on. The instrumental force, which is a decisive support condition, of the nominal designation of instruction, stated by the word 'etena,' figuratively represents the result. The word 'iti' also refers to that same decisive support condition of the nominal designation as a cause. The nominal designation, which is the basis for that force, is the meaning of the yu-suffix. This same principle applies to similar instances throughout the three Piṭakas.

Ekantaniyyānaṭṭhena, anaññasādhāraṇaguṇatāya ca uttamaṭṭhena varaṃ uttamaṃ, pariyattisāsanamhi phalaniyyādanato, magganiyyānahetubhāvato ca niyyānaṭṭhena, sāvakādīhi ajaniyattā asādhāraṇaṭṭhena ca uttamaṭṭhena varaṃ, varitabbanti vā varaṃ. Yathāvuttassa sāsanassa paṇḍitehi abhipatthitasamiddhihetutāya varitabbattā patthetabbattā sāsanavaraṃ nāma, yathāvuttaṭṭhena vā sāsanañca taṃ varañcāti sāsanavaraṃ. Ca-saddena sattibhedaṃ, taṃ-saddena atthābhedaṃ desseti.

By way of being the definitive vehicle, by way of having qualities not common to others, and by way of being supreme, it is excellent and supreme. Because it yields fruit within the Dispensation of learning, and because it is the causal condition for the path as a vehicle, it is a vehicle. By way of not being generated by disciples and others, and by way of being unshared, it is supreme, excellent, or select, or it is 'vara' because it should be chosen. Because it should be chosen and desired by the wise as the cause of the accomplishment wished for, regarding the Dispensation as described, it is called the excellent Dispensation. Or, by way of what has been described, it is both the Dispensation and the excellent, thus 'sāsanavara.' The word 'ca' indicates a distinction in essence; the word 'taṃ' signifies identity in meaning.

Vidantīti [M 0.0009] vidū. Ye paṇḍitā yathāsabhāvato kammakammaphalāni, kusalādibhede ca dhamme vidanti, iti vidanato te paṇḍitā vidū nāma, tehi. Ñātabbanti ñeyyaṃ. Ñā-dhātuyā nippariyāyato ārammaṇikaṃ ñāṇaṃ vuttaṃ, ṭhānūpacārato sāsanavarassa ārammaṇapaccayabhāvo dassito, iti-saddena ārammaṇapaccayabhāvo parāmasito. Tassa iti-saddena parāmasitabbassa ārammaṇapaccayabhāvassa ādhāraṃ sāsanavaraṃ ṇya-paccayatthoti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ñāṇaṃ arahatīti vā ñeyyaṃ, vidūnaṃ ñāṇaṃ jānanaṃ ārammaṇabhāvena arahatīti attho. Imasmiṃ naye taddhitapadaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ.

They know, thus they are 'vidū' (knowers). Those wise ones who know actions and their results according to their true nature, and also the states (dhamma) in their wholesome and unwholesome divisions—thus, because they know, those wise ones are called 'vidū.' By them. 'Ñātabba' means 'to be known,' thus 'ñeyya.' From the root 'ñā,' direct object-oriented knowledge is stated. Through the figurative application of 'basis,' the excellent teaching's nature as an object-condition is shown. The word 'iti' refers to this object-condition. It should be seen that the excellent teaching is the basis for that object-condition which is referred to by the word 'iti,' and this is the meaning of the 'ṇya' suffix. Alternatively, 'ñeyya' means 'worthy of knowledge'—that is, the knowledge, the knowing of the wise, is worthy of being an object. In this interpretation, the derived word should be understood.

Narati [V 0.0153] netīti naro. Yo puriso attānaṃ itthīnaṃ uccaṭṭhānaṃ narati neti, iti naranato nayanato so puriso naro nāma. So hi puttabhūtopi mātuyā pituṭṭhāne tiṭṭhati, kaniṭṭhabhātubhūtopi jeṭṭhabhaginīnaṃ pituṭṭhāne tiṭṭhati. Atha vā naritabbo netabboti naro. So hi jātakālato paṭṭhāya yāva attano sabhāvena attānaṃ dhāretuṃ samattho na hoti, tāva parehi netabbo, na tathā añño tiracchānādikoti. Ettha pana satthuvisayatāya narati veneyyasatteti naroti attho adhippeto. Satthā hi satte apāyādito sugatiṃ vā maggaphalanibbānaṃ vā netīti. Sabbaññutaññāṇādianekaguṇasamannāgatattā varo uttamo, varitabbo patthetabboti vā varo, tilokaggo. Pakatiyā uccaṭṭhānaṭṭho naro guṇuttamena samannāgato varo, naro ca so varo cāti naravaro. Ca-ta-saddānaṃ atthabhedo vuttova, visesanaparapadasamāsoyaṃ. Yena vuttaṃ “aggapuggalassāti attho”ti (netti. aṭṭha. saṅgahavāravaṇṇanā). Aññe pana “narānaṃ, naresu vā varoti naravaro”ti vadanti, taṃ vacanaṃ “aggapuggalassāti attho”ti (netti. aṭṭha. saṅgahavāravaṇṇanā) aṭṭhakathāvacanena virujjhati maññe. Tassa naravarassāti. Iccevaṃ nettippakaraṇassa ādigāthāya samāsena ca vacanattho samatto.

He leads, thus he is a 'nara' (man). That man who leads himself to a high position among women—thus, from leading, that man is called a 'nara.' For even as a son, he stands in the father’s place for his mother; as a younger brother, he stands in the father’s place for his elder sisters. Alternatively, he is a 'nara' because he is to be led. For from the time of birth until he is not capable of sustaining himself by his own nature, he must be led by others—not so with other animals and such. Here, however, in the context of the Teacher, the intended meaning is that he leads beings fit to be taught, thus he is a 'nara.' For the Teacher leads beings from states of woe to a good destination, or to the path, fruition, and Nibbāna. Endowed with many qualities such as omniscience, he is the best, the supreme—or he is 'vara' because he is to be chosen and aspired to, the foremost in the three worlds. By nature, a man is of high standing; endowed with supreme qualities, he is the best. He is both a 'nara' and the best, thus 'naravara.' The distinction in meaning of the particles 'ca' and 'ta' has already been stated—this is a descriptive compound. As it is said: 'The meaning is “the foremost individual”' (Netti-aṭṭha, Saṅgahavāravaṇṇanā). Others, however, say: '“The best among men, or of men, is naravara,”' but that statement, I think, is contradicted by the commentary's words: 'The meaning is “the foremost individual”' (Netti-aṭṭha, Saṅgahavāravaṇṇanā). 'Of that Best of Men'—thus, with this, the meaning of the words of the opening verse of the Nettippakaraṇa, in brief and in detail, is complete.

Sarūpattho yojanatthavacanatthānusārena vijānitabbo. Tathāpi visuṃ suṭṭhu jānanatthāya puna vattabbo. “Ya”nti padassa anaññasādhāraṇasabbaññutaññāṇādianekaguṇasampanno salokapālena lokena pūjetabbo ceva namassitabbo ca sāsanavaradesako tilokaggo sarūpattho. “Loko”ti padassa yathāvuttalokapālasahito saddhācāgādisampanno [M 0.0010] sabbasattaloko sarūpattho. Lokasaddo ekavacanayuttopi jātisaddattā niravasesato satte saṅgaṇhāti yathā “mahājano”ti. Kāmañcettha lokasaddo “lokavidū”tyādīsu saṅkhārabhājanesupi pavatto, pūjananamassanakiriyāsādhanattā pana sattalokeva vācakabhāvena pavattoti. Tenāha “pūjanakiriyāyogyabhūtatāvasenā”ti (netti. aṭṭha. saṅgahavāravaṇṇanā).

The essential meaning should be understood in accordance with the meaning of connection and the meaning of expression. Nevertheless, in order to understand each aspect clearly, it should be stated again. The essential meaning of the word 'yaṃ' is the one who is incomparable, endowed with many qualities such as omniscience, to be honored and revered by the world together with its guardians, the teacher of the excellent Dispensation, the foremost in the three worlds. The essential meaning of the word 'loko' is the entire world of beings, endowed with faith, generosity, and other virtues, together with its guardians as previously described. The term 'loka,' though singular in form, encompasses all beings without exception due to its generic nature, just as the term 'mahājana' (the great multitude) does. Moreover, although the term 'loka' can apply to the world of formations and the container world in expressions like 'lokavidū' (knower of the world), here it primarily denotes the world of beings in its expressive function because it facilitates acts of honor and veneration. Therefore, it is said: 'By way of its state of being suitable for the act of honoring' (Netti-aṭṭha, Saṅgahavāravaṇṇanā).

Pūjayateti ettha pūjanakiriyāya mukhyato pūjanasaṅkhāto pūjentānaṃ cittuppādo sarūpattho, phalūpacārena taṃcittuppādassa ārammaṇapakatūpanissayabhūtā vuttappakārā sabbe buddhaguṇā sarūpatthā. Te-vibhattipaccayassa pūjanakiriyāsādhako vuttappakāro loko ca sarūpattho, evaṃ sati atthabhedābhāvato dvīsu vācakesu ekova vācako vattabbo, kasmā ekasmiṃ atthe dve vācakā vuttāti? Nāyaṃ doso dvinnaṃ vācakānaṃ sāmaññavisesavācakattā. Lokasaddo hi pūjanakiriyāsādhako, aññakiriyāsādhako ca vadatīti sāmaññavācako ca hoti. Pūjayate-saddo lokapūjanaitthipūjanapurisapūjanatiracchānapūjanādikiriyāsādhakañca vadatīti sāmaññavācako[V 0.0154]. Tasmā pūjayate-saddo lokasaddassa sarūpattho, pūjanakiriyāsādhako ca na aññakiriyāsādhakoti niyameti. Lokasaddo ca pūjayatesaddassa sarūpattho pūjanakiriyāsādhako. Loko pana pūjanakiriyāsādhako itthipurisatiracchānādikoti niyameti. Tīsu piṭakesu aññesupi evarūpesu ṭhānesu eseva nayo.

Here, in 'pūjayate,' the essential meaning is primarily the mental state of those who honor, designated as honoring. Figuratively, by extension to the result, all the Buddha's qualities of the type mentioned, which are the object and natural decisive support for that mental state, are also the essential meaning. The world of the type mentioned, which accomplishes the act of honoring and is indicated by the 'te' suffix, is also the essential meaning. If this is so, since there is no difference in meaning, only one expression should be stated for the two terms. Why then are two expressions used for a single meaning? This is not a flaw, for the two terms express generality and specificity. Indeed, the term 'loka' refers to what accomplishes the act of honoring, and also to what accomplishes other actions—thus, it is a general expression. The term 'pūjayate' refers to what accomplishes the honoring of the world, the honoring of women, the honoring of men, the honoring of animals, and other such actions—thus, it is also a general expression. Therefore, the term 'pūjayate' has the essential meaning of the term 'loka,' and it specifies that it accomplishes the act of honoring and not other actions. And the term 'loka' has the essential meaning of the term 'pūjayate,' and it specifies that the world, which accomplishes the act of honoring, includes women, men, animals, and the like. This same principle applies to other similar instances found in the three Piṭakas.

“Salokapālo”ti padassa yathāvuttaseṭṭhalokapālasahagato, pūjananamassanakiriyāsādhako ca sattanikāyo sarūpattho. “Sadā”ti padassa rattidivasakālo atītabhagavato dharamānakālo tato parakālo abhinīhārato yāva sāsanantaradhānā kālo tato parakālo sarūpattho. So pana anāgatabuddhuppajjanakālo atītasammāsambuddhe idāni pūjayanti namassanti viya pūjayissati ceva namassissati ca. Namassatīti ettha namassanakiriyāya mukhyato namassanasaṅkhāto cittuppādo sarūpattho, phalūpacārena taṃcittuppādassa ārammaṇapakatūpanissayabhūtā vuttappakārā sabbe buddhaguṇā sarūpattho. Ti-vibhattipaccayassa [M 0.0011] namassanakiriyāsādhako yathāvuttasattanikāyo loko ca sarūpattho, atthabhedābhāvepi dvinnaṃ vācakānaṃ pavattabhāvo heṭṭhā vuttova. “Cā”ti padassa idhekacco pūjentopi na namassati, namassantopi na pūjeti ca, ayaṃ pana sattanikāyo loko pūjayati ceva namassati cāti samuccayattho sarūpattho.

The essential meaning of the term 'salokapālo' is the assembly of beings that accomplishes the acts of worship and veneration, together with the excellent guardian deities of the world as previously mentioned. The essential meaning of the word 'sadā' encompasses the time of day and night, the lifetime of the past Blessed One, the time thereafter, the period from the aspiration until the disappearance of the Dispensation, and the time thereafter. And in that future time of a Buddha's arising, they will worship and venerate, just as they now worship and venerate the perfectly self-enlightened Buddhas of the past. Here, in 'namassati,' the essential meaning is primarily the mental state designated as veneration. Figuratively, by extension to the result, all the Buddha's qualities of the type mentioned, which serve as the object and natural decisive support for that mental state, are also the essential meaning. The world, which is the assembly of beings as previously described and accomplishes the act of veneration, indicated by the 'ti' inflection, is also the essential meaning. Even when there is no difference in meaning, the reason for the occurrence of two terms is as explained previously. The essential meaning of the word 'ca' is that while some may worship without venerating, or venerate without worshipping, this assembly of beings, this world, both worships and venerates, conveying a meaning of combination.

Tassāti ettha taṃ-saddassa sabbaññutaññāṇādianekaguṇasamannāgato pūjetabbo namassitabbo tilokaggo satthā sarūpattho, chaṭṭhīvibhattiyā janakassa naravarassa jaññena sāsanavarena sambandho padhānasarūpattho, jaññasāsanavarassa janakena naravarena sambandho apadhānasarūpattho. Tīsu piṭakesu evarūpesu aññesupi eseva nayo.

Here, in 'tassa,' the essential meaning of the word 'taṃ' is the Teacher, the foremost in the three worlds, endowed with qualities such as omniscience, worthy of worship and veneration. The connection, expressed by the sixth case ending, of the originator, the Best of Men, with the originated, the excellent teaching, is the primary essential meaning. The connection of the originated, the excellent teaching, with the originator, the Best of Men, is the secondary essential meaning. This is the method in other similar instances throughout the three Piṭakas.

“Eta”nti padassa ācariyena vibhajitabbahāranayapaṭṭhānavicāraṇavisayabhūtaṃ sāsanaṃ sarūpattho. “Sāsanavara”nti padassāpi tameva sarūpattho, etaṃ sāsanavaraṃ pariyattipaṭipattipaṭivedhabhedena tividhampi pariyattisāsanameva sabbasāsanamūlabhūtattā, nettippakaraṇassa visayabhūtattā ca visesato adhippetaṃ tassa mūlabhūtabhāvato vinayasaṃvaṇṇanādīsu bahūpakārena dassitoti amhehi na vattabbo. Vadantopi aññaṃ racitabbaṃ racituṃ asamatthova hutvā vadatīti gahitabbo vadeyya.

The essential meaning of the word 'etaṃ' (this) is the teaching that is the domain of the teacher's analysis, method of application, and investigation of principles. The essential meaning of the word 'sāsanavara' (excellent teaching) is also the same. This excellent teaching, though threefold by way of learning, practice, and realization, is specifically intended here as the teaching of learning (pariyatti) because it is the root of all teachings and particularly because it is the subject matter of the Nettippakaraṇa. Due to its foundational nature, its usefulness is extensively demonstrated in works like the Vinaya commentaries; therefore, it is not for us to say otherwise. Even if someone were to speak against this, they should be understood as speaking because they are actually incapable of composing anything better.

Taṃ pana pariyattisāsanaṃ vimuttirasavasena ekavidhaṃ, dhammavinayavasena duvidhaṃ, vinayapiṭakasuttantapiṭakaabhidhammapiṭakavasena tividhaṃ[V 0.0155], āṇādesanāvohāradesanāparamatthadesanāvasena tividhaṃ, yathāparādhasāsanāyathānulomasāsanāyathādhammasāsanābhedenapi tividhaṃ, saṃvarāsaṃvarakathādiṭṭhiviniveṭhanakathānāmarūpaparicchedakathābhedenapi tividhaṃ. Ettha ca desanā desakādhīnā, sāsanaṃ sāsitabbāyattaṃ, kathā kathetabbatthāpekkhāti viseso. Dīghanikāyo, majjhimanikāyo, saṃyuttanikāyo, aṅguttaranikāyo, khuddakanikāyoti nikāyabhedena pana pañcavidhaṃ; suttageyyaveyyākaraṇagāthāudānaitivuttakajātakaabbhutadhammavedallabhedena pana navavidhaṃ; dhammakkhandhabhedena pana caturāsītidhammakkhandhasahassavidhaṃ; “saṃkilesabhāgiyavāsanābhāgiyanibbedhabhāgiyaasekkhabhāgiyāti amissāni cattāri; saṃkilesabhāgiyavāsanābhāgiyasaṃkilesabhāgiyanibbedha bhāgiyasaṃkilesabhāgiyaasekkhabhāgiyavāsanābhāgiyanibbedhabhāgiyāti missakadukāni cattāri; saṃkilesabhāgiyavāsanābhāgiyaasekkhabhāgiyasaṃkilesabhāgiyavāsanā bhāgiyanibbedhabhāgiyāti [M 0.0012] missakatikāni dve; taṇhāsaṃkilesadiṭṭhisaṃkilesaduccaritasaṃkilesataṇhāvodānabhāgiyadiṭṭhiva- udānabhāgiyaduccaritavodānabhāgiyātichā”ti (netti. 89) soḷasannaṃ suttānaṃ bhedena soḷasavidhaṃ; “lokiyalokuttaralokiyalokuttarasattādhiṭṭhānadhammādhiṭṭhānasattadhammādhiṭṭhānañāṇañeyya- ñāṇañeyyadassanabhāvanādassanabhāvanāsakavacanaparavacanasakavacanaparavacana vissajjanīyaavissajjanīyavissajjanīyaavissajjanīyakammavipākakammavipākakusala akusalakusalākusalaanuññātapaṭikkhittaanuññātapaṭikkhittathavassa bhedena aṭṭhavīsatividha”nti (netti. 112) evamādibahuvidhaṃ pariyattisāsanaṃ nettippakaraṇassa visesato visayaṃ. Tassa visayabhāve sati paṭipattipaṭivedhasaṅkhātaṃ sāsanadvayampi tammūlakattā visayaṃ hoti pariyāyatoti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

That scriptural teaching is of one kind in terms of the essence of liberation; of two kinds in terms of Dhamma and Vinaya; of three kinds in terms of the Vinaya Piṭaka, Sutta Piṭaka, and Abhidhamma Piṭaka; of three kinds in terms of instruction by command, instruction by exposition, and instruction by ultimate meaning; and also of three kinds in terms of disciplinary instruction according to the offense, instruction in accordance with suitability, and instruction in accordance with the Dhamma. It is also of three kinds in terms of discourses on restraint and non-restraint, discourses on disentangling wrong views, and discourses on distinguishing name and form. Here, exposition depends on the expounder, the teaching depends on those to be taught, and discourse depends on the subject matter to be discussed—this is the distinction. By division into Nikāyas, it is fivefold: the Dīgha Nikāya, Majjhima Nikāya, Saṃyutta Nikāya, Aṅguttara Nikāya, and Khuddaka Nikāya. By division into the nine parts, it is: Sutta, Geyya, Veyyākaraṇa, Gāthā, Udāna, Itivuttaka, Jātaka, Abbhutadhamma, and Vedalla. By division into Dhamma-sections, it is eighty-four thousand Dhamma-sections. 'Four unmixed categories: pertaining to defilement, pertaining to latent tendencies, pertaining to penetration, and pertaining to the adept. Four mixed pairs: pertaining to defilement and latent tendencies, pertaining to defilement and penetration, pertaining to defilement and the adept, and pertaining to latent tendencies and penetration. Two mixed triplets: pertaining to defilement, latent tendencies, and the adept, and pertaining to defilement, latent tendencies, and penetration. Sixteen kinds by division into suttas: defilement of craving, defilement of views, defilement of misconduct, pertaining to the purification from craving, pertaining to the purification from views, pertaining to the purification from misconduct, and so forth' (Netti. 89). 'Twenty-eight kinds by division into: worldly and supramundane; beings as the basis and Dhamma as the basis; knowledge and the knowable; vision and development; one's own speech and another's speech; answerable and unanswerable; action and result; skillful and unskillful; permitted and prohibited, and so forth' (Netti. 112). Thus, the scriptural teaching is of many kinds, and the Nettippakaraṇa particularly takes this as its domain. Since it has this domain, the two teachings, namely, practice and realization, are also to be regarded as its domain by implication because they are rooted in it.

“Vidūhī”ti padassa yathāvuttasāsanavarassa saparasantānapavattanapavattāpanādivasena vijānanasamattho saṇhasukhumañāṇādiguṇasampanno kalyāṇaputhujjanasotāpannādiko puggalo sarūpattho. “Ñeyya”nti padassa tādisehi vidūhi saṇhasukhumañāṇādinā vijānitabbaṃ sāsanavaraṃ sarūpattho. “Naravarassā”ti padassa ekavidhādibhedassa sāsanavarassa janako anekaguṇasampanno tilokaggo sarūpattho. Iccevaṃ nettiyā ādigāthāya sarūpattho saṅkhepena vijānitabbo.

The essential meaning of the word 'vidūhi' (by the wise) is a person capable of understanding the excellent teaching as described—by means of the continuation and establishment of one's own and others' mental continua, and so forth—endowed with qualities such as subtle and refined knowledge, including virtuous ordinary people, stream-enterers, and so on. The essential meaning of the word 'ñeyya' (knowable) is the excellent teaching that is to be understood by such wise ones through subtle and refined knowledge, and so on. The essential meaning of the word 'naravarassa' (of the best of men) is the originator of the excellent teaching, which is of one kind and so forth, endowed with many qualities, the foremost in the three worlds. Thus, in brief, the essential meaning of the introductory verse of the Netti should be understood in this way.

Evaṃ tassā anusandhyādīnaṃ jānitabbabhāve satipi ajānanto viya pucchitvā dosaṃ āropetvā parihāravasenāpi gambhīrādhippāyassa anākulassa visesajānanaṃ bhavissati. Tasmā pucchitvā dosaṃ ropetvā parihāravasena gambhīrādhippāyaṃ sampiṇḍetvā kathayissaṃ. Amhākācariya kimatthaṃ “yaṃ loko”tyādimāha? Nettippakaraṇaṃ kātuṃ. Evaṃ sati nettippakaraṇabhūtaṃ “soḷasahārā netti”tyādikaṃ eva vattabbaṃ, kasmā taṃ avatvā tato nettippakaraṇato aññaṃ “yaṃ loko pūjayate”tyādimāha. Seyyathāpi samuddaṃ gacchanto himavantaṃ gacchati, himavantaṃ gacchanto [V 0.0156] samuddaṃ gacchati, evameva nettippakaraṇaṃ karonto [M 0.0013] sāsanavaradassanaṃ karotīti? Saccaṃ, tathāpi yassa saṃvaṇṇanaṃ nettippakaraṇaṃ kātukāmo taṃ sāsanavaraṃ paṭhamaṃ dassetuṃ “yaṃ loko”tyādimāha. Evaṃ sati “etaṃ sāsanavara”nti ettakameva vattabbaṃ, kasmā “yaṃ loko”tyādi vuttanti? Taṃ sāsanavaraṃ janakena naravarena niyametvā thometuṃ vuttaṃ. Tathāpi “tassa naravarassā”ti ettakameva vattabbaṃ, kasmā “yaṃ loko”tyādi vuttanti? Taṃ janakaṃ naravaraṃ lokapālena lokaseṭṭhena saddhiṃ sabbena lokena pūjanīyanamassanīyabhāvena thometuṃ “yaṃ loko”tyādi vuttaṃ. Pūjentāpi vanditvā pūjenti, tasmā “pūjayate”ti ettakameva vattabbanti? Tathāpi keci kesañci pūjāsakkārādīni karontāpi tesaṃ apākaṭaguṇatāya namakkāraṃ na karonti. Evaṃ bhagavato yathābhūtaabbhuggatasaddatāya pana bhagavantaṃ pūjetvāpi vandatiyevāti dassetuṃ “namassati cā”ti vuttaṃ. Pūjento, namassanto ca na kadāciyeva, atha kho sabbakālanti dassetuṃ “sadā”ti vuttaṃ. Tādisassa naravarassa tādisaṃ sāsanavaraṃ saṇhasukhumañāṇasampannehi vidūheva sukhumañāṇeneva ñeyyanti sāsanavaraṃ thometuṃ “vidūhi ñeyya”nti vuttaṃ.

Thus, even though its contextual connection and so forth should be known, yet if one asks as if not knowing and imputes a fault, by way of refutation a non-confused, special understanding of the profound intention will arise. Therefore, having asked and imputed a fault, by way of refutation I will condense the profound intention and speak. 'Our teacher, for what purpose did he say, “That which the world…” and so forth?' 'To compose the Nettippakaraṇa.' 'If so, that which constitutes the Nettippakaraṇa, “The sixteen hārā of the Netti…” and so forth, should alone be said. Why, without saying that, did he instead say something other than the Nettippakaraṇa, such as “That which the world reveres…?”' 'Is it that just as one going to the ocean goes to the Himālaya, and one going to the Himālaya goes to the ocean, in the same way, one who composes the Nettippakaraṇa also reveals the excellent teaching?' 'That is true. Nevertheless, he who wishes to compose the Nettippakaraṇa, which is a commentary on it, first presents that excellent teaching by saying “That which the world…” and so forth.' 'If so, only “This is the excellent teaching” should be said. Why was “That which the world…” and so forth stated?' 'It was said to praise that excellent teaching, having been established by the noble originator.' 'Even so, only “Of that noble originator” should be said. Why was “That which the world…” and so forth stated?' 'It was said to praise that originator, the best of men, as worthy of veneration and homage by the entire world, together with the world-protectors and the foremost of the world.' 'Even those who revere also pay homage while revering, so should only “reveres” be said?' 'Yet, some, while performing acts of reverence and honor toward certain others, do not pay homage to them due to the obscurity of their virtues. But in the case of the Blessed One, to show that due to his truly arisen and exalted renown, even after revering him, one indeed pays homage, it was said, “and pays homage.” To show that one reveres and pays homage not just at some time, but at all times, it was said, “always.” To praise the excellent teaching, it was said, “to be known by the wise,” meaning that such an excellent teaching of such a noble man is to be known only by the subtle knowledge of the wise endowed with subtle and refined knowledge.'

Ettha ca “pūjayate, namassatī”ti etehi pūjananamassanakiriyāya hetubhūtā sabbaññutaññāṇādayo aneke lokiyalokuttaraguṇā pakāsitā honti te guṇe āgamma sabbalokassa pūjananamassanacetanāya pavattanato. Tesu hi kiñci sarūpato, kiñci anumānato sāriputtattherādayo anussaranti, pūjenti, namassanti. Tena vuttaṃ “anussaretha sambuddha”nti (saṃ. ni. 1.249). Ekadesaguṇāpi pūjārahā namassanārahā, kasmā sabbepi guṇā pakāsitāti? Sabbaguṇadassanena bodhisambhārasambharaṇamahākaruṇāyogasaṅkhātahetuñāṇapahāna- ānubhāvarūpakāyasampattisaṅkhātaphalahitajjhāsayindriya- pākakālāgamanadesanāñāṇasaṅkhātasattu- pakārasampadāvasena thomanā dassitā. Tena attahitapaṭipatti, parahitapaṭipatti ca nirupakkilesūpagamanāpagamanañca lokasamaññānupapavatti, tadanatidhāvanañca caraṇasampatti, vijjāsampatti ca attādhipatitā, dhammādhipatitā ca lokanāthaattanāthatā ca pubbakārikataññutā ca aparantapatā, anattantapatā ca buddhakaraṇadhammabuddhabhāvasiddhi ca paratāraṇaattatāraṇañca [M 0.0014] sattānuggahacittatā, dhammavirattacittatā ca pakāsitā bhavanti. Tena sabbappakārena anuttaradakkhiṇeyyatāuttamapūjanīyanamassanīyabhāvapūjananamassanakiriyāya ca khettaṅgatabhāvaṃ pakāseti. Tena pūjanakanamassanakānaṃ yathicchitabbapayojanasampatti pakāsitāti sabbaguṇā pakāsitāti.

Here, by the phrases 'is honored, is revered,' the omniscient knowledge and other numerous worldly and supramundane qualities—which are the cause for acts of veneration and homage—are revealed, because the intention of veneration and homage of the entire world proceeds based on those qualities. Indeed, the Venerable Sāriputta and others recollect, honor, and revere some of these qualities directly and some by inference. Thus, it is said: 'Recollect the Fully Enlightened One' (Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.249). If even a portion of the qualities are worthy of honor and reverence, why are all qualities revealed? Through the vision of all qualities, praise is demonstrated by way of the accumulation of the requisites for enlightenment, the great compassion, the knowledge of causes, the abandonment of defilements, the perfection of the physical body endowed with power, the intention for the welfare of the fruit of practice, the ripening of faculties, the knowledge of the opportune time for teaching, and the accomplishment of helping beings. Thereby, the practice for one's own benefit and the practice for others' benefit, undefiled approach and withdrawal, acting in accordance with worldly conventions and not transgressing them, perfection of conduct and perfection of knowledge, self-mastery and Dhamma-mastery, the state of being a refuge for the world and a refuge for oneself, gratitude for past deeds, not tormenting others and not tormenting oneself, the accomplishment of the state of Buddhahood by means of the qualities that make one a Buddha, the deliverance of others and oneself, a mind that helps beings and a mind dispassionate towards phenomena are revealed. Thus, in every way, the unsurpassed worthiness of offerings, the highest state of being worthy of veneration and homage, and the quality of being a fertile field for acts of veneration and homage are demonstrated. Thereby, the fulfillment of the desired purpose for those who honor and revere is revealed. Hence, all qualities are revealed.

Ādikalyāṇatādiguṇasampattiyā [V 0.0157] varaṃ aggaṃ uttamaṃ, nipuṇañāṇagocaratāya paṇḍitavedanīyañca, tasmā “varaṃ ñeyya”nti vacanehi svākkhātatādayo sabbe dhammaguṇā pakāsitā. Ariyasaccapaṭivedhena samugghātakilesasammohāyeva paramatthato paṇḍitā bālyādisamatikkamanato, tasmā bhāvitalokuttaramaggā, sacchikatasāmaññaphalā ca puggalā visesato “vidū”ti vuccanti. Te hi yathāvuttasāsanavaraṃ aviparītato ñātuṃ, netuñca saparasantāne sakkuṇanti. Tasmā ye suppaṭipannatādayo anekehi suttapadehi saṃvaṇṇitā, te ariyasaṅghaguṇāpi niravasesato “vidūhī”ti padena pakāsitāti. Evaṃ nettiyā paṭhamagāthāya “etaṃ sāsanavara”nti padena sāsanattayaṃ saṅgaṇhitvā tattha itaresaṃ dvinnaṃ adhigamūpāyabhāvato sabbasāsanamūlabhūtassa, attano nettippakaraṇassa ca visayabhūtassa pariyattisāsanavarassa dassanamukhena sabbe ratanattayaguṇāpi thomanāvasena nayatova pakāsitā honti. Nayato hi dassitā sabbe guṇā niravasesā gahitā bhavanti, na sarūpato. Tenāha bhagavantaṃ ṭhapetvā paññavantānaṃ aggabhūto dhammasenāpatisāriputtattheropi buddhaguṇaparicchedanamanuyutto “apica me dhammanvayo vidito”ti (dī. ni. 2.146) bhagavatāpi –

Because of the perfection of qualities such as being good in the beginning, it is excellent, supreme, and highest; and because it is to be understood by the wise, being within the range of subtle knowledge, therefore, by the words 'excellent to be known,' all the qualities of the Dhamma, such as being well-proclaimed, are revealed. Those who have uprooted defilements and delusion by penetrating the Noble Truths are, in the ultimate sense, the wise, because they have transcended foolishness and the like. Therefore, persons who have developed the supramundane path and have realized the fruits of recluseship are especially called 'the wise' (vidū). For they are able to understand the aforementioned excellent Teaching without distortion and to guide others in their own and others' mental continuums. Therefore, those qualities of the noble Sangha, such as being of good practice, which are praised in many sutta passages, are also revealed without remainder by the word 'by the wise' (vidūhī). Thus, in the first verse of the Netti, the phrase 'this excellent Teaching' encompasses the three kinds of Teaching. Among these, because the other two are the means for attainment, by way of showing the excellent scriptural Teaching—which is the root of the entire Teaching and the subject of this Nettippakaraṇa itself—all the qualities of the Triple Gem are also praised and revealed by way of method. For when shown by way of method, all qualities are grasped without remainder, not in their intrinsic nature. Therefore, even the venerable Sāriputta, the General of the Dhamma, the foremost among the wise apart from the Blessed One, when engaged in determining the Buddha's qualities, said, 'Moreover, the sequence of the Dhamma is known to me' (Dīgha Nikāya 2.146); and by the Blessed One also it was said:

“Evaṃ acintiyā buddhā, buddhadhammā acintiyā;

Acintiye pasannānaṃ, vipāko hoti acintiyo”ti. (apa. thera 1.1.82; netti. 95) –

Thus, Buddhas are inconceivable, the qualities of a Buddha are inconceivable; for those with faith in the inconceivable, the result is inconceivable.

Gāthā vuttā. Tattha buddhadhammāti buddhaguṇā. Amhākaṃ pana yāvajīvaṃ ratanattayaguṇaparidīpane atiussāhantānampi sarūpato nīharitvā dassetuṃ asamatthabhāvo pageva paṇḍitehi veditabboti.

This verse was spoken. Here, 'qualities of a Buddha' means the qualities of the Buddha. But as for us, even striving with the utmost zeal throughout our lives to elucidate the qualities of the Triple Gem, our inability to extract and show them in their intrinsic nature should be understood by the wise beforehand.

Iccevaṃ [M 0.0015] –

Thus:

“Yaṃ loko pūjayate, salokapālo sadā namassati ca;

Tasseta sāsanavaraṃ, vidūhi ñeyyaṃ naravarassā”ti. –

Whom the world with its protector honors, and always reveres; His, the best of men, is this excellent teaching, to be understood by the wise.

Niggahitalopavasena vuttāya gāthāya saṅkhepena kathito anusandhyādiko samattoti.

By the verse spoken with the elision of the nasal, the connection and so forth, briefly stated, is concluded.

“Yaṃ loko pūjayate, sa lokapālo sadā namassati ca;

Taṃ tassa sāsanavaraṃ, vidūhi ñeyyaṃ naravarassā”ti. –

Whom the world honors, and that world-protector always reveres; that excellent teaching of his, of the best of men, is to be known by the wise.

Gāthaṃ [V 0.0158] apare paṭhanti. Tassāpi anusandhyattho vuttanayova. Yojanattho pana viseso. Tattha hi salokapālo loko yassa satthuno naravarassa yaṃ sāsanavaraṃ saṃvaṇṇetabbasahitaṃ, saṃvaṇṇetabbaṃ eva vā pūjayate ceva namassati ca, tassa lokapālassa satthuno taṃ pūjetabbaṃ, namassitabbañca vidūheva viññātabbaṃ, etaṃ sāsanavaraṃ nettippakaraṇassa visayanti gahetabbanti yojanā. Yojanākāropi heṭṭhā vuttanayova.

Others recite this verse. Its connected meaning is in the same way as stated. The meaning of its construction, however, is different. The interpretation is as follows: The world with its protector honors and reveres that excellent teaching of that teacher, the best of men, together with what is to be praised, or simply what is to be praised. That which is to be honored and revered of that teacher, the world-protector, is to be understood only by the wise; and this excellent teaching is to be taken as the subject of the Nettippakaraṇa. The mode of construction is also as stated before.

Viggahatthopi viseso. Imasmiñhi naye lokaṃ pālentīti lokapālā, yathāvuttacatumahārājādayo. Tehi lokapālehi sahitaṃ sabbalokaṃ pāleti lokagganāyakattāti lokapāloti bhagavāpi lokapālasaddena vutto. So hi “tassā”ti ettha taṃ-saddena parāmasīyati, tasmā tassa lokapālassa satthuno naravarassāti attho gahito. Yadi evaṃ lokapālo guṇībhūto apadhāno padhānabhūtaṃ lokaṃ visesetvā vinivatto, kathaṃ taṃ-saddena parāmasīyatīti? Lokavisesako samānopi sāsanavarāpekkhatāya janakasāmibhāvena sambandhivisesabhūtattā padhānabhūto viya parāmasīyatīti. Bhagavā sāsanavarassa sāmibhāvena gahito. Kathaṃ sāsanavarassa sāmī bhagavā sāsanavaraṃ pūjayatīti? Na cāyaṃ virodho. Buddhā hi bhagavanto dhammagaruno, te sabbakālaṃ dhammamapacayamānāva viharantīti. Buddhānañhi dhammagarudhammāpacayamānabhāvo “yaṃnūnāhaṃ…pe… tameva dhammaṃ sakkatvā garuṃ katvā mānetvā pūjetvā upanissāya vihareyya”nti (a. ni. 4.21) vutto, tasmā lokapālo bhagavā sāsanavaraṃ [M 0.0016] pūjayatīti daṭṭhabbo. Evaṃ sati lokapālo bhagavā sāsanavaraṃ pūjayatīti attho yutto hotu, kathaṃ lokapālo bhagavā sāsanavaraṃ namassatīti yuttoti? Yuttova “namassatī”ti padassa garukaraṇena tanninnapoṇapabbhāroti atthassāpi labbhanato. Bhagavā hi dhammagarutāya sabbakālaṃ dhammaninnapoṇapabbhārabhāvena viharatīti. Vuttañhetaṃ “yena sudaṃ niccakappaṃ viharāmī”tiādi. Sesamettha heṭṭhā vuttanayena vā saṃvaṇṇanāsu vuttanayena vā ñātabbanti amhehi na vitthārīyati.

The meaning of the analysis is also different. In this method, 'they protect the world' (lokaṃ pālenti), thus they are 'world-protectors' (lokapālā), such as the aforementioned Four Great Kings and others. The Blessed One is also called a 'world-protector' by the word 'lokapāla' because, being the supreme leader of the world, he protects the entire world together with these world-protectors. He is referred to by the pronoun 'ta' here in the word 'tassa'; therefore, the meaning 'of that teacher, the best of men, who is the world-protector' is taken. If so, if the world-protector, being secondary and subordinate, is set aside after qualifying the world, which is primary, how is he referred to by the pronoun 'ta'? Even though he is a qualifier of the world, because of his connection with the excellent teaching and his being a special relation as its originator and master, he is referred to as if he were primary. The Blessed One is taken as the master of the excellent teaching. How can the Blessed One, being the master of the excellent teaching, honor the excellent teaching? This is not a contradiction. For the Blessed Buddhas have the Dhamma as their guide, and they always live honoring the Dhamma. Indeed, the fact that the Buddhas have the Dhamma as their guide and honor the Dhamma is stated: 'What if I were to live honoring, respecting, esteeming, worshiping, and relying on that very Dhamma?' (Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.21). Therefore, it should be understood that the Blessed One, the world-protector, honors the excellent teaching. This being so, let the meaning 'the Blessed One, the world-protector, honors the excellent teaching' be fitting; but how is it fitting that the Blessed One, the world-protector, reveres the excellent teaching? It is indeed fitting, because the word 'namassati' also yields the meaning of 'to hold in high esteem, to be inclined, sloped, and disposed towards it.' For the Blessed One, out of reverence for the Dhamma, always lives in a state of being inclined, sloped, and disposed towards the Dhamma. And this was said: 'That by which I live for all time...' and so on. The rest here should be understood either by the method stated previously or by the method stated in the commentaries, so it is not elaborated upon by us.

Evaṃ paṭhamagāthāya “sāsanavara”nti padena tividhampi sāsanaṃ saṅgaṇhitvā tattha pariyattisāsanameva attano nettippakaraṇassa visayaṃ niyametvā dassento “dvādasa padāni”tyādimāha. Atha vā paṭhamagāthāya ratanattayathomanena saha nettippakaraṇatāvisayaṃ sāsanavaraṃ ācariyena dassitaṃ, “tassa sāsanavaraṃ kiṃ sabbaṃyeva nettippakaraṇassa visayaṃ, udāhu pariyattisāsanamevā”ti pucchitabbattā pariyattisāsanabhūtaṃ suttamevāti dassento “dvādasa padāni sutta”ntiādimāha. Tattha “sāsanavara”nti sāmaññena vuttampi pariyattisuttameva sāsanavaranti [V 0.0159] gahetabbanti attho. “Taṃ pana katividha”nti vattabbattā “dvādasa padānī”ti vuttaṃ, saṅkhepato pabhedena dvādasavidhanti attho. Pabhedato dvādasavidhampi byañjanapadaatthapadato pana duvidhamevāti dassetuṃ “taṃ sabbaṃ byañjanañca attho cā”ti vuttaṃ. “Tasmiṃ dvaye ekameva sarūpato nettippakaraṇassa visayanti viññeyyaṃ, udāhu ubhaya”nti pucchitabbattā ubhayanti dassetuṃ “taṃ viññeyyaṃ ubhaya”nti vuttaṃ. Vacanavacanīyabhāvena sambandhe yasmiṃ byañjane, atthe ca “sutta”nti vohāro pavatto, taṃ ubhayaṃ sarūpato nettippakaraṇassa visayanti viññeyyanti attho. “Kinti viññeyya”nti vattabbattā “ko attho, byañjanaṃ katama”nti vuttaṃ. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – chabyañjanapadachaatthapadabhedena dvādasavidhaṃ byañjanapadaatthapadavasena duvidhaṃ sabbapariyattisaṅkhātaṃ suttaṃ mama nettippakaraṇassa visayaṃ sāsanavaranti ñātabbaṃ. Sarūpato pucchitvā atthapadaṃ, byañjanapadañca sarūpato ñātabbanti.

Thus, in the first verse, having encompassed the three kinds of Teaching by the word 'sāsanavara', and therein, having determined that only the scriptural teaching is the subject of his own Nettippakaraṇa, he states, beginning with 'twelve terms'. Alternatively, in the first verse, the excellent teaching, which is the subject of the Nettippakaraṇa, was shown by the teacher along with homage to the Triple Gem. Then, since it is to be asked, 'Is that entire excellent teaching the subject of the Nettippakaraṇa, or is it only the scriptural teaching?', to indicate that it is solely the sutta, which is the scriptural teaching, he states, beginning with 'twelve terms, the sutta'. Here, the word 'sāsanavara', though spoken generally, should be understood as referring specifically to the scriptural sutta as the excellent teaching. Since it is to be asked, 'Of how many kinds is it?', it is said, 'twelve terms', meaning that it is twelvefold in classification, in brief. Though it is twelvefold in classification, from the perspective of wording-terms and meaning-terms, it is only twofold. To show this, it is stated, 'all that is wording and meaning'. Then, since it is to be asked, 'In those two, should one understand that only one is the subject of the Nettippakaraṇa in its intrinsic nature, or both?', to indicate that it is both, it is said, 'that should be understood as both'. The meaning is this: in the relationship between the expression and what is to be expressed, wherever the designation 'sutta' applies to both wording and meaning, both should be understood as the subject of the Nettippakaraṇa in their intrinsic nature. Since it is to be asked, 'How should it be understood?', it is said, 'what is the meaning, and what is the wording?'. This is what is said: The sutta, comprising all scriptural teachings, is twelvefold by way of six wording-terms and six meaning-terms, and twofold by way of wording-terms and meaning-terms. It should be known as the excellent teaching that is the subject of my Nettippakaraṇa. Having inquired about their intrinsic nature, the meaning-term and the wording-term should be understood in their intrinsic nature.

Evaṃ paṭhamagāthāya “sāsanavara”nti vuttassa suttassa pariyattibhāvañceva atthapadabyañjanapadabhāvena veditabbattañca dassetvā idāni tassa suttassa pavicayūpāyaṃ [M 0.0017] nettippakaraṇaṃ padatthavibhāgena dassetuṃ “soḷasahārā”tyādimāha. Atha vā dutiyagāthāya nettippakaraṇassa visayaṃ sāsanavaraṃ niyametvā dassitaṃ, “netti nāma katamā, katividhā”ti pucchitabbattā nettināma ettikāti saṅkhepato dassetuṃ “soḷasahārā”tyādimāha. Tattha tassa sāsanassa suttassa atthapariyeṭṭhi nettisaṃvaṇṇanā mayā mahākaccāyanena niddiṭṭhā netti nāma soḷasahārasamudāyā pañcanayasamudāyā aṭṭhārasamūlapadasamudāyāti vijānitabbāti.

Thus, having shown in the first verse the sutta's nature as scriptural teaching and its knowability by way of meaning-terms and wording-terms, he now states, beginning with 'sixteen modes', to show the Nettippakaraṇa, which is the method of analysis for that sutta, by way of the division of terms and meanings. Alternatively, in the second verse, the excellent teaching, which is the subject of the Nettippakaraṇa, was shown by way of definition. Then, since it is to be asked, 'What is the Netti called? How many kinds is it?', to briefly indicate the extent of the Netti, he states, beginning with 'sixteen modes'. Herein, it should be known that the investigation of the meaning of that teaching, the sutta—the exposition of the Netti pointed out by me, Mahākaccāyana—is the Netti, a collection of sixteen modes, a collection of five ways, and a collection of eighteen root terms.

Te hārādayo kenaṭṭhena netti nāma? Veneyyasatte ariyadhammaṃ netīti nettīti evamādi attho saṃvaṇṇanāsu (netti. aṭṭha. ganthārambhakathā) vuttova. Imāya tatiyagāthāyapi “mahākaccānena niddiṭṭhā”ti pāṭho sundaro. “Mahākaccāyanena niddiṭṭhā”ti vā pāṭho, na sundaro. Lakkhaṇañhi mayā heṭṭhā vuttanti. “Soḷasahārādisamudāyā nettī”ti vuttā, te hārā suttassa byañjanavicayo vā honti, atthavicayo vā, nayā ca byañjanavicayo vā honti, atthavicayo vāti vicāraṇāyaṃ sati “ime imassa vicayo”ti niyametvā dassetuṃ “hārā byañjanavicayo”tiādimāha. Tattha hārā suttassa byañjanavicayo honti, na atthavicayo soḷasahārānaṃ mūlapadaniddhāraṇaṃ vajjetvā byañjanamukheneva saṃvaṇṇanābhāvato. Tayo pana nayā suttassa atthavicayo honti, tiṇṇaṃ nayānaṃ mūlapadasaṅkhātaavijjādisabhāvadhammaniddhāraṇamukheneva suttassa atthasaṃvaṇṇanābhāvatoti.

By what meaning are those modes and so forth called 'Netti'? It is called 'Netti' because it leads trainable beings to the noble Dhamma—this and similar meanings are already stated in the commentaries (Netti. Aṭṭha. Ganthārambhakathā). Even in this third verse, the reading 'expounded by Mahākaccāna' is good. The reading 'expounded by Mahākaccāyana', however, is not good, for the characteristic has been stated by me below. It is said, 'The Netti is the collection of the sixteen modes, etc.' When there is an investigation as to whether these modes are an analysis of the wording of the sutta or an analysis of its meaning, and whether the ways are an analysis of the wording or an analysis of the meaning, to show definitively that 'this is the analysis of that,' it is said, 'the modes are an analysis of the wording,' and so on. Here, the modes are an analysis of the wording of the sutta, not of its meaning, because apart from the determination of the root terms of the sixteen modes, the exposition is solely by way of the wording. But the three ways are an analysis of the meaning of the sutta, because the exposition of the meaning of the sutta is solely by way of determining the nature of things such as ignorance, designated as root terms of the three ways.

“Taṃ [V 0.0160] ubhayaṃ sutte saṃvaṇṇanābhāvena kenaci katthaciyeva yojetabbaṃ, udāhu sabbathā sabbattha yojita”nti pucchitabbabhāvato taṃ ubhayaṃ sabbattha suttesu sabbathā yojitanti dassetuṃ “ubhayaṃ pariggahīta”nti vuttaṃ. Hārā ceva nayā ca ubhayaṃ suttassa atthaniddhāraṇavasena parito samantato gahitaṃ sabbathā suttesu yojitanti.

Since it is to be asked, 'Should both be applied in the sutta in the manner of an exposition by someone only in certain places, or are they applied everywhere in all ways?', to show that both are applied everywhere in the suttas in all ways, it is stated, 'both are comprehended'. Both the modes and the ways are fully comprehended from all sides for determining the meaning of the sutta, and thus are applied in all ways throughout the suttas.

“Hārādisamudāyabhūtaṃ nettisaṅkhātaṃ suttaṃ kathaṃ saṃvaṇṇetabbaṃ suttaṃ saṃvaṇṇetī”ti vattabbabhāvato vuttaṃ “vuccati suttaṃ yathāsutta”nti. Nettisaṅkhātaṃ saṃvaṇṇanāsuttaṃ saṃvaṇṇetabbasuttānurūpaṃ yathā yena yena desanāhārena vā aññena vā saṃvaṇṇetabbaṃ, tena tena vuccati saṃvaṇṇetīti [M 0.0018] attho. Atha vā “nettisaṅkhātaṃ suttaṃ kittakaṃ saṃvaṇṇetabbaṃ suttaṃ saṃvaṇṇetī”ti vattabbabhāvato vuttaṃ “vuccati suttaṃ yathāsutta”nti. Tattha yathāsuttaṃ yaṃ yaṃ suttaṃ bhagavatā vuttaṃ, taṃ taṃ sabbaṃ suttaṃ nettisaṅkhātaṃ suttaṃ vuccati vadati assādādīnavadassanavasena saṃvaṇṇetīti. Tena vuttaṃ “nettinayena hi saṃvaṇṇetuṃ asakkuṇeyyaṃ nāma suttaṃ natthī”ti (netti. aṭṭha. saṅgahavāravaṇṇanā).

Since it is to be asked, 'How does the sutta known as the Netti, which is a collection of modes and so forth, expound the sutta to be expounded?', it is said, 'The sutta is expounded according to the sutta.' The meaning is that the exposition-sutta known as the Netti expounds the sutta to be expounded in accordance with it, by whatever teaching-mode or other means it should be expounded; by that means it is said to expound.
