As by night, so by day: Just as during the nighttime, even when darkness accompanied by the four factors is present, the sphere of forms is clearly penetrated—without difficulty—by means of the aforementioned concentration, when accompanied by the divine eye-knowledge; so too, during the daytime, whether the sphere of forms is subtle, or obscured by some wall or other barrier, or located at an extreme distance, it is clearly penetrated—without difficulty—by means of the aforementioned concentration, when accompanied by the divine eye-knowledge. This meaning should be understood.

Yathā [V 0.0241] yathāvuttasamādhissa divasabhāge dibbasotañāṇānuparivattibhāvena sukhumassa saddāyatanassa vā kenaci pākārādinā tirohitassa saddāyatanassa [M 0.0105] vā atidūraṭṭhāne pavattassa saddāyatanassa vā suṭṭhu paṭivijjhanameva, na duppaṭivijjhanaṃ, tathā rattibhāgepi yathāvuttasamādhissa dibbasotañāṇānuparivattibhāvena sukhumassa saddāyatanassa vā kenaci pākārādinā tirohitassa saddāyatanassa vā atidūraṭṭhāne pavattassa saddāyatanassa vā suṭṭhu paṭivijjhanameva, na duppaṭivijjhananti ayaṃ nayopi netabbo. Tena vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ –

Just as during the daytime, by means of the aforementioned concentration, when accompanied by the divine-ear knowledge, subtle sound-objects—whether obscured by some wall or other barrier, or occurring in extremely distant places—are clearly penetrated—without difficulty; so too during the nighttime, by means of the aforementioned concentration, when accompanied by the divine-ear knowledge, subtle sound-objects—whether obscured by some wall or other barrier, or occurring in extremely distant places—are clearly penetrated—without difficulty. This principle should also be extended. Therefore, it is said in the commentary:

“Yathā pureti yathā samādhissa pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇānuparivattibhāvenā”tiādiṃ vatvā “yathā ca rūpāyatane vuttaṃ, tathā samādhissa dibbasotañāṇānuparivattitāya saddāyatane ca netabba”nti (netti. aṭṭha. 14).

Having said, 'As in the past,' meaning 'as by means of concentration, when accompanied by the knowledge of the recollection of past lives,' and so forth, it is also said: 'And as was stated regarding the form sphere, so too should it be applied to the sound sphere by means of concentration, when accompanied by the divine-ear knowledge.'

“Ñāṇamūlakādisamādhinā pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇānuparivattibhāvādisahitena kiṃ bhāvetī”ti pucchitabbattā “iti vivaṭenā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha itīti evaṃ vuttappakārena. Apariyonaddhenāti nīvaraṇādivigamanena. Sappabhāsaṃ cittanti iddhipādasampayuttaṃ maggacittaṃ bhāveti. Iddhipādasampayutte maggacitte uppajjamāne hi maggacittasahabhūni kusalāni saddhindriyavīriyindriyasatindriyasamādhindriyapaññindriyabhūtāni pañcindriyāni uppajjanti. Maggacitte nirujjhamāne anuppajjanabhāvena nirujjhanti ekacittakkhaṇikattā. Evaṃ maggaviññāṇassa nirodhā paññā ca sati ca nirujjhatīti yojanā.

Since it is to be asked, 'What does one develop by means of concentration rooted in knowledge, etc., accompanied by the state of following upon the knowledge of the recollection of past lives, etc.?' it is said, 'Thus, openly,' and so forth. Herein, 'thus' means in the manner described. 'Unconfined' means by the removal of the hindrances, etc. 'A luminous mind' refers to developing path-consciousness associated with the bases of psychic power. For when path-consciousness associated with the bases of psychic power arises, the five faculties—the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom—which are wholesome and arise simultaneously with path-consciousness, also arise. When path-consciousness ceases, they cease without arising again, due to their existence for a single moment of consciousness. Thus, with the cessation of path-consciousness, wisdom and mindfulness also cease—this is the connection.

“Kassa viññāṇassa nirodhā nāmarūpaṃ nirujjhatī”ti vattabbattā “nāmarūpañcā”tiādi vuttaṃ, paṭisandhiviññāṇassa nirodhā nāmarūpañca nirujjhatīti vuttaṃ hoti. Atha vā “viññāṇassa nirodhā paññā ca sati cāti vuttāni pañcindriyāni evaṃ nirujjhantī”ti vattabbattā nāmarūpañca nirujjhati, nirujjhamānaṃ pana nāmarūpaṃ paṭisandhiviññāṇassa nirodhā nirujjhatīti dassetuṃ “nāmarūpañcā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha nāmarūpañcāti maggena taṇhāavijjādike anupacchinne uppajjanārahaṃ vedanādikkhandhattayaṃ, bhūtupādārūpañca. Viññāṇahetukanti uppajjanārahaṃ paṭisandhiviññāṇaṃ hetu assa nāmarūpassāti viññāṇahetukaṃ. Viññāṇapaccayā nibbattanti viññāṇena paccayena nibbattaṃ. Tassāti uppajjanārahassa paṭisandhiviññāṇassa. Hetūti taṇhāavijjādiko kileso. Viññāṇanti uppajjanārahaṃ paṭisandhiviññāṇaṃ. Anāhāranti appaccayaṃ. Anabhinanditanti kāmataṇhādīhi [M 0.0106] anabhinanditabbaṃ. Appaṭisandhikanti punabbhavābhisandahanarahitaṃ. Nti tādisaṃ viññāṇaṃ. Ahetūti [V 0.0242] natthi hetusaṅkhātaṃ paṭisandhiviññāṇaṃ imassa nāmarūpassāti ahetu. Appaccayanti sahāyavirahena natthi paccayā saṅkhārā imassāti appaccayaṃ. Evaṃ paṭisandhiviññāṇassa nirodhā nāmarūpañca nirujjhatīti.

Since it is to be stated, 'With the cessation of which consciousness does name-and-form cease?' it is said, 'and name-and-form,' and so forth, meaning that with the cessation of rebirth-linking consciousness, name-and-form also ceases. Alternatively, since it is to be stated, 'With the cessation of consciousness, wisdom and mindfulness, that is, the five faculties mentioned, cease in this way,' it is said, 'and name-and-form also ceases.' But to show that the name-and-form that is ceasing ceases with the cessation of rebirth-linking consciousness, it is said, 'and name-and-form,' and so on. Herein, 'and name-and-form' refers to the three aggregates beginning with feeling, capable of arising when craving, ignorance, and so forth are not yet cut off by the path, as well as materiality derived from the primary elements. 'Caused by consciousness' means that the rebirth-linking consciousness capable of arising is the cause of that name-and-form. 'Arisen from consciousness as condition' means arisen with consciousness as a condition. 'Of that' refers to the rebirth-linking consciousness capable of arising. 'Cause' means the defilements such as craving and ignorance. 'Consciousness' means the rebirth-linking consciousness capable of arising. 'Without nutriment' means without a condition. 'Not delighted in' means not to be delighted in by sensual craving, etc. 'Without rebirth-linking' means devoid of connection to renewed existence. Thus it refers to such a consciousness. 'Without cause' means there is no rebirth-linking consciousness reckoned as the cause of this name-and-form. 'Without condition' means there are no formations as conditions due to the absence of a support. Thus, with the cessation of rebirth-linking consciousness, name-and-form also ceases.

“Paññāsatīnañceva nāmarūpassa ca vuttappakārena nirujjhanabhāvo kathaṃ amhehi saddahitabbo”ti vattabbattā “tenāha bhagavā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Vattabbākārena paññāsatīnañceva nāmarūpassa ca nirujjhanabhāvajānanako bhagavā yathānirujjhanabhāvadīpakaṃ “yametaṃ…pe… etthetaṃ uparujjhatī”ti gāthāvacanaṃ āha. Tena gāthāvacanena tumhehi mayā vutto nirujjhanabhāvo saddahitabboyevāti. Etthāpi paññāsatināmarūpānaṃ nirujjhanaṃ ajānantena tattha vā saṃsayantena ajitena pucchitabbattā “adiṭṭhajotanā pucchāti vā diṭṭhasaṃsandanā pucchāti vā paññādīnaṃ anekatthattā dhammato vā anekādhiṭṭhānā pucchāti vā dhammādhiṭṭhānā pucchā”ti vā iccevamādipucchāvicayo niddhāretabbo. “Sarūpadassanavissajjananti vā anekādhiṭṭhānavissajjananti vā dhammādhiṭṭhānavissajjana”nti vā iccevamādivissajjanavicayo niddhāretabbo.

"How are we to have faith in the fact that wisdom, mindfulness, and name-and-form cease in the manner stated?" Because this was to be said, it is stated, "Therefore, the Blessed One said," and so on. The Blessed One, knowing the fact of the cessation of wisdom, mindfulness, and name-and-form in the manner to be described, spoke the verse elucidating the nature of their cessation: "Whatever this is... here it ceases." By this verse, the nature of cessation I have described should indeed be believed by you. Here too, because it must be asked by Ajita, who does not know the cessation of wisdom, mindfulness, and name-and-form, or who doubts it, the analysis of the question should be determined thus: "Is it a question to illuminate the unseen? Or a question to confirm the seen? Or, because wisdom and so forth have multiple meanings, is it a question from multiple standpoints based on the Dhamma? Or is it a question based on the Dhamma?" And the analysis of the reply should be determined thus: "Is it a reply that reveals the intrinsic nature? Or a reply from multiple standpoints? Or a reply based on the Dhamma?"

Evaṃ sattādhiṭṭhānādipucchāvissajjanāni ceva dhammādhiṭṭhānādipucchāvissajjanāni ca visuṃ visuṃ dassetvā pucchāvicayo ceva vissajjanavicayo ca ācariyena vibhatto, amhehi ca ñāto, “sattādhiṭṭhānadhammādhiṭṭhānesu ekato dassitesu pucchāvissajjanesu kathaṃ pucchāvicayo ceva vissajjanavicayo ca amhehi viññātabbo”ti pucchitabbattā sattādhiṭṭhānadhammādhiṭṭhānaṃ pucchaṃ nīharitvā tattha vicayaṃ vibhajanto “ye ca saṅkhatadhammāse”tiādimāha. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana –

Thus, having separately shown the questions and answers based on beings and those based on the Dhamma, the analysis of questions and the analysis of answers have been distinguished by the teacher and are known by us. Because it would be asked, "How should the analysis of questions and the analysis of answers be understood by us when the questions and answers based on beings and on the Dhamma are shown together?", he extracts the question concerning the bases of beings and the Dhamma and, dividing the analysis thereof, speaks beginning with, "Those which are conditioned phenomena..." In the commentary, however—

“Evaṃ anusandhipucchampi dassetvā heṭṭhā sattādhiṭṭhānā, dhammādhiṭṭhānā ca pucchā visuṃ visuṃ dassitāti idāni tā saha dassetuṃ “ye ca saṅkhatadhammāse’tiādi āraddha”nti (netti. aṭṭha. 14) –

"Thus, having also shown the connecting question, and since the questions based on beings and on the Dhamma were shown separately below, now to present them together, 'And those conditioned phenomena...' and so forth is begun" (Netti. Aṭṭha. 14).

Vuttaṃ. Tassāyaṃ attho – idha sāsane ye arahanto saṅkhatadhammā honti, puthū bahūyeva satta janā sekkhā sīlādisikkhamānā honti, tesaṃ [M 0.0107] arahantāvañceva sekkhānañca iriyaṃ paṭipattiṃ meṃ mahā puṭṭho nipako tvaṃ bhagavā pabrūhi mārisa iti āyasmā ajito pucchanto āhāti.

It is said. This is its meaning: here in this Dispensation, those who are Arahants are conditioned phenomena, and there are many beings, numerous people, who are trainees, training in virtue and so forth. Of them—both the Arahants and the trainees—their conduct and practice, you, O Blessed One, discerning one, having been asked by me, declare it, O venerable sir. Thus Venerable Ajita asked.

15. Tassaṃ gāthāyaṃ “kittakāni pucchitānī”ti vattabbattā “imānī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Padatthānurūpaṃ pucchitabbattā “imāni tīṇi padāni pucchitānī”ti vuttaṃ. “Ye ca [V 0.0243] …pe… mārisā”ti gāthāyaṃ ye pañhā pucchitā, te pañhā tayo honti, “kissa kena kāraṇena tayo hontī”ti pucchitabbattā “kissa…pe… yogenā”ti vuttaṃ. Sekkhā ariyā ca asekkhā ariyā ca vipassanāpubbaṅgamaṃ pahānañcāti sekhāsekhavipassanāpubbaṅgamappahānāni, tesaṃ yogoti sekhā…pe… yogo, tena sekhā…pe… yogena. Evaṃ pucchāvidhinā hi yasmā “ye ca saṅkhatadhammāse…pe… mārisā”ti gāthamāha, tasmā tayo pañhā hontīti daṭṭhabbā.

15. Regarding that verse, because it should be stated, "How many things were asked?", it is said, "these," and so on. Because it should be asked in accordance with the meaning of the terms, it is stated, "these three points were asked." In the verse, "And those... O venerable sir," the questions that were asked are three. Because it should be asked, "By what, for what reason, are they three?", it is stated, "by what... by the connection." Noble trainees, noble non-trainees, and abandonment preceded by insight—these are the abandonments preceded by insight concerning trainees and non-trainees; their connection is the connection of trainees, non-trainees, and abandonment preceded by insight; by that connection. Because he spoke the verse, "And those conditioned phenomena... O venerable sir," with this method of questioning, it should therefore be seen that there are three questions.

“Ye ca saṅkhatadhammāse”ti iminā asekkhānaṃ arahattaṃ pucchati, “ye ca sekkhā puthū idhā”ti iminā sekkhāsekkhānaṃ sekkhasikkhanaṃ pucchati, “tesaṃ me nipako iriyaṃ, puṭṭho pabrūhi mārisā”ti iminā sekkhāsekkhānaṃ vipassanā pubbabhāge tadaṅgappahānaṃ pucchati. “Adiṭṭhajotanā pucchāti vā diṭṭhasaṃsandanā pucchāti vā sattādhiṭṭhānā pucchāti vā anekādhiṭṭhānā pucchā”ti vā iccevamādipucchāvicayo niddhāretabbo.

"And those who are conditioned phenomena"—with this, he asks about the Arahantship of the non-trainees. "And those who are trainees, many here"—with this, he asks about the training of a trainee, in relation to both trainees and non-trainees. "Of them, O discerning one, their conduct... being asked by me, declare it, O venerable sir"—with this, he asks about the abandonment-in-part in the preliminary stage of insight of the trainees and non-trainees. The analysis of the question should be determined thus: "Is it a question to illuminate the unseen, or a question to confirm the seen, or a question based on beings, or a question from multiple standpoints?"

Sattadhammādhiṭṭhānaṃ pucchaṃ nīharitvā pucchāvicayo ācariyena vibhatto, amhehi ca ñāto, “tassaṃ pucchāyaṃ katamā vissajjanāgāthā”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha vissajjanā”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Tatthāti tassaṃ gāthāyaṃ. “Kāmesu…pe… paribbaje”ti vissajjanāgāthā bhagavatā vuttā. Kāmesūti kāmīyantīti kāmā, tesu kāmesu. Vatthukāmesu kilesakāmena paṇḍitehi nābhigijjheyya. Manasā nāvilosiyāti āvilabhāvakare byāpādavitakkādayo ceva kāyaduccaritādayo ca dhamme pajahanto paṇḍito manasā anāvilo suppasanno bhaveyya. Kusalo sabbadhammānanti sabbadhammānaṃ aniccatādinā paritulitattā aniccatādīsu pañcasu khandhesu kusalo cheko. Satoti kesādīsu saratīti sato. Bhikkhūti saṅkhatadhamme bhayādito ikkhatīti bhikkhu. Paribbajeti [M 0.0108] tadaṅgavikkhambhanasamucchedappahānabhāvena kilesakāmavatthukāme pari samantato vajjeyya.

Having extracted the question concerning the Dhamma with seven bases, the analysis of the question was explained by the teacher, and it is known by us. Because it is to be asked, 'In that question, what is the reply verse?', the passage beginning 'therein, the reply' was started. 'Therein' means in that verse. 'In sensual pleasures... let him wander forth'—this is the reply verse spoken by the Blessed One. 'In sensual pleasures' means those things that are desired are sensual pleasures; in those sensual pleasures. Regarding sensual objects, a wise person should not be greedy through the defilement of desire. 'With mind unclouded'—by abandoning states which cause agitation, such as thoughts of ill-will and bodily misconduct, the wise one should be unclouded in mind, very serene. 'Skilled in all phenomena'—because all phenomena are weighed by way of impermanence and so on, one is skilled in the five aggregates with regard to impermanence and so on. 'Mindful'—one is mindful because one is mindful of the parts of the body, beginning with the hair of the head. 'A bhikkhu'—one is a bhikkhu because one sees conditioned phenomena as fearful and so on. 'Let him wander forth'—one should completely avoid the defilements of sensual pleasure and the objects of sensual pleasure by way of abandonment by substitution of opposites, abandonment by suppression, and abandonment by cutting off.

Pucchāgāthāyaṃ “nipako”ti padena pasaṃsitena bhagavatā vissajjanāgāthā vuttā, tassa bhagavato yena anāvaraṇañāṇena ukkaṃsagatena pakkabhāvo dassito, taṃ anāvaraṇañāṇaṃ tāva kāyakammādibhedehi vibhajitvā dassento “bhagavato sabbaṃ kāyakamma”ntiādimāha. Tattha anāvaraṇañāṇena jānitvā kataṃ sabbaṃ kāyakammaṃ ñāṇapubbaṅgamaṃ ñāṇānuparivatti. Esa nayo sesesupi. Atīte aṃseti atītabhave saparakkhandhādike koṭṭhāse aññāṇena appaṭihataṃ bhagavato [V 0.0244] ñāṇadassanaṃ. Anāgate aṃseti anāgatabhave saparakkhandhādike koṭṭhāse. Paccuppanne aṃseti paccuppanne bhave saparakkhandhādike koṭṭhāse.

The reply verse was spoken by the Blessed One, who was praised with the word 'discerning' in the question verse, thereby showing the perfect nature of that Blessed One's supreme, unobstructed knowledge. To explain that unobstructed knowledge by dividing it into types such as bodily action, he said, 'All the bodily actions of the Blessed One...' and so on. Herein, all bodily action, done having known by unobstructed knowledge, is preceded by knowledge and followed by knowledge. This same method applies to the rest. 'In the past part' means the Blessed One’s knowledge and vision is unobstructed by ignorance regarding past existences, in the sections concerning one's own and others' aggregates. 'In the future part' means in future existences, in the sections concerning one's own and others' aggregates. 'In the present part' means in the present existence, in the sections concerning one's own and others' aggregates.

“Ñāṇadassanassa katarasmiṃ paṭighāto”ti pucchitabbattā pucchaṃ ṭhapetvā paṭighātavisayaṃ dassetuṃ “ko cā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Atha vā “paccuppannabhave saparakkhandhādike koṭṭhāse aññesampi ñāṇadassanaṃ bhaveyya, tadanusārena atītānāgatakoṭṭhāsesupi katarasmiṃ aññesaṃ ñāṇadassanassa paṭighāto bhaveyyā”ti pucchitabbattā pucchaṃ ṭhapetvā paṭighātavisayaṃ niyametvā dassetuṃ “ko cā”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha ko cāti kva katarasmiṃ samaye aññesaṃ ñāṇadassanassa paṭighāto bhaveyyāti pucchi.

Because it was to be asked, 'Where is there an obstruction to knowledge and vision?', having formulated the question, the passage beginning 'and where?' was stated to show the sphere of obstruction. Or alternatively, because it was to be asked, 'In the present existence, in sections such as those concerning one's own and others' aggregates, others too might have knowledge and vision. In accordance with that, in the past and future sections as well, where would there be an obstruction to the knowledge and vision of others?', having formulated the question, 'and where?' was stated to define and show the sphere of obstruction. Therein, 'and where?' means it was asked, 'Where, at what time, would there be an obstruction to the knowledge and vision of others?'

Anicce, dukkhe, anattaniye ca aññesaṃ aññāṇaṃ yaṃ adassanaṃ atthi, aññāṇādassanasaṅkhāto sabhāvo ñāṇadassanassa paṭighāto bhavati, na saparakkhandhādidassanamattapaṭighāto. Etena aniccato lakkhaṇattaye pavattassa ñāṇadassanassa aññesaṃ durabhisambhavaṃ, bhagavato ca ñāṇadassanassa aññehi asādhāraṇataṃ dasseti. Bhagavato hi lakkhaṇattayavibhāvanena veneyyā catusaccappaṭivedhaṃ labhanti. “Bhagavato ñāṇadassanapaṭighātābhāvena aññesañca ñāṇadassanassa paṭighātabhāvo katamāya upamāya amhākaṃ pākaṭo”ti vattabbabhāvato upamāya pākaṭaṃ kātuṃ “yathā idhā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha idha sattaloke cakkhumā puriso ākāse tārakāni passeyya, gaṇanasaṅketena [M 0.0109] “ettakānī”ti no ca jāneyya yathā, evaṃ aññesaṃ ñāṇadassanassa paṭighāto ayaṃ aññāṇadassanasabhāvo bhavati.

Regarding the impermanent, suffering, and what is not-self, whatever ignorance and lack of vision others have, that state, designated as ignorance and lack of vision, is an obstruction to knowledge and vision, not merely an obstruction to seeing one's own and others' aggregates and so forth. By this, it shows that the knowledge and vision which proceeds with regard to the three characteristics, beginning with impermanence, is difficult for others to attain, and it demonstrates that the Blessed One’s knowledge and vision is unshared by others. For through the Blessed One’s explanation of the three characteristics, those capable of being guided attain realization of the four noble truths. Because it should be said, 'Since the Blessed One’s knowledge and vision is without obstruction, while that of others is obstructed, by what simile can this be made clear to us?', to make it clear by a simile, the passage beginning 'Just as here…' is stated. Here, in this world of beings, a man with sight might see the stars in the sky, but he would not know by counting and convention that 'there are this many'. In the same way, this state of ignorance and lack of vision is the obstruction to the knowledge and vision of others.

Bhagavato pana tathā abhāvato kenaci aññāṇena adassanena appaṭihataṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ bhavatīti attho daṭṭhabbo. “Bhagavato ñāṇadassanassa appaṭihatabhāvo kasmā amhehi saddahitabbo”ti pucchitabbattā “anāvaraṇañāṇadassanā hi buddhā bhagavanto”ti vuttaṃ. “Nipakassa…pe… bhagavato anāvaraṇañāṇaṃ kāyakammādibhedehi ācariyena vibhajitvā dassitaṃ, amhehi ca ñātaṃ, pacchā gāthāya ‘iriya’nti padena pucchitā sekkhāsekkhapaṭipadā kathaṃ vijānitabbā”ti vattabbattā sekkhāsekkhapaṭipadaṃ dassetuṃ “tattha sekhenā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha tatthāti tasmiṃ vissajjane. Sekhenāti sikkhanasīlena puggalena rajanīyesu rūpārammaṇādīsu dhammesu gedhā cittaṃ rakkhitabbaṃ, pariyuṭṭhānīyesu āghātavatthūsu dosā cittaṃ rakkhitabbaṃ.

However, since that is not the case for the Blessed One, the meaning should be understood that his knowledge and vision is unobstructed by any ignorance or lack of seeing. Because it is to be asked, 'Why should we have faith that the Blessed One's knowledge and vision is unobstructed?', it is said, 'For the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, possess unobstructed knowledge and vision.' Because it should be said: 'Regarding the discerning one... the Blessed One's unobstructed knowledge, in its distinctions of bodily action and so on, has been explained by the teacher, and it is known by us. Afterwards, how is the practice of the trainee and the adept, which was asked about with the word 'conduct' in the verse, to be understood?', to show the practice of the trainee and the adept, the passage beginning 'Therein, by the trainee...' was stated. Therein, 'therein' means in that reply. By 'the trainee' is meant that a person whose nature is to train should guard the mind from greed towards desirable things, such as visible forms and so on, and guard the mind from aversion towards obsessive grounds for hatred.

“Tesu [V 0.0245] gedhadosesu katamaṃ nivārento bhagavā vissajjanagāthāyaṃ katamaṃ padamāhā”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha yā icchā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha tatthāti gedhadosesu. Icchāti rāgicchā. Mucchāti lobhamohasahagatamohamucchā. Patthanāti rāgapatthanā. Piyāyanāti taṇhāpiyāyanāva, na mettāpiyāyanā. Kīḷanāti gedhakīḷanā. Etāni hi gedhapariyāyavacanāni. Taṃ gedhasaṅkhātaṃ icchādikaṃ nivārento bhagavā “kāmesu nābhigijjheyyā”ti evaṃ visuṃ visuṃ pakārena āha.

Since it should be asked, 'Among those instances of greed and aversion, which one was the Blessed One preventing when he spoke which word in the reply verse?', the passage beginning 'therein, that desire' was stated. Therein, 'therein' refers to greed and aversion. 'Desire' means desire rooted in lust. 'Infatuation' means the infatuation of delusion accompanied by greed and delusion. 'Longing' means longing rooted in lust. 'Cherishing' refers to the cherishing of craving, not the cherishing of loving-kindness. 'Play' means the play of greed. These are indeed synonyms for greed. The Blessed One, preventing that which is designated as greed—that is, desire and so on—said, 'One should not be greedy in sensual pleasures,' thus speaking in various distinct ways.

Pariyuṭṭhānavighātaṃ dosaṃ nivārento bhagavā “manasānāvilo siyā”ti evaṃ visuṃ visuṃ pakārena āhāti yojanā. Gedhadosānaṃ visuṃ visuṃ nivārento bhagavā dve padāni āhāti vuttaṃ, “taṃ kena atthena saddahitabba”nti vattabbattā “tathā hi sekho”tiādi vuttaṃ. Rajanīyesu abhigijjhanto sekho anuppannaṃ lobhapadhānaṃ kilesañca uppādeti, uppannaṃ kilesañca phātiṃ abhivaḍḍhanaṃ karoti, pariyuṭṭhānīyesu āvilo sekho anuppannaṃ dosapadhānaṃ kilesañca uppādeti, uppannaṃ kilesañca phātiṃ vaḍḍhanaṃ karoti, iti iminā paṭikkhepaatthena taṃ mama vacanaṃ saddahitabbanti adhippāyo.

Preventing aversion, which is an obsessive disturbance, the Blessed One says, 'May the mind be undisturbed,' thus explaining in various ways—this is the connection. It is said that the Blessed One speaks two phrases, separately restraining greed and aversion. Since it should be asked, 'With what meaning should this be accepted?', therefore 'For thus a learner...' is stated. A learner, clinging to alluring things, generates unarisen defilements based on greed and causes arisen defilements to grow and increase. A disturbed learner, regarding things that cause obsession, generates unarisen defilements based on aversion and causes arisen defilements to grow and increase. Thus, by way of this rejection, the intention is that my words should be accepted.

“Kiṃ [M 0.0110] pana anabhigijjhanto, anāvilo ca sekkho agedhadosanivāraṇameva karoti, udāhu uttaripi paṭipadaṃ pūretī”ti pucchitabbattā uttaripi paṭipadaṃ pūretiyevāti dassento “yo pana anāvilasaṅkappo”tiādimāha. Tattha anāvilasaṅkappoti natthi āvilakarā saṅkappā byāpādasaṅkappavihiṃsāsaṅkappā etassāti anāvilasaṅkappo, icchādigedhassa abhāvena anabhigijjhanto vāyamati kusalavāyāmaṃ pavatteti. “Kathaṃ vāyamatī”ti pucchitabbattā “so anuppannāna”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha soti uparibhāvanāmaggabhāvatthāya paṭipajjamāno sekkho. Anuppannānantiādīnaṃ attho sakkā aṭṭhakathāvacaneneva (netti. aṭṭha. 15-16) jānitunti na vibhatto.

Since it should be asked, 'Does a trainee who is free from covetousness and untainted merely prevent greed and aversion, or does one also fulfill the higher practice?', to show that one also fulfills the higher practice, it is said: 'Moreover, one whose intentions are untainted.' Here, 'one whose intentions are untainted' means one who does not have intentions that cause taint, namely, intentions of ill will and intentions of harmfulness—thus, one whose intentions are untainted. Being free from covetousness due to the absence of desire and greed, one strives and exerts skillful effort. Since it should be asked, 'How does one strive?', 'He, for unarisen...' etc. is said. Here, 'he' refers to the trainee who is practicing for the purpose of attaining the state of the path of higher development. The meaning of 'unarisen...' etc., can be understood through the commentary itself (Netti. Aṭṭha. 15-16), and thus is not elaborated.

16. Yenāti asubhādīnaṃ anussaraṇalakkhaṇena indriyena taṇhāmayitavatthūsu kāmataṇhāya sahajātaṃ vitakkaṃ vāreti, idaṃ asubhādianussaraṇalakkhaṇaṃ indriyaṃ satindriyaṃ. Yena mahaggatabhāvappattena avikkhepena byāpādavitakkaṃ vāreti, idaṃ avikkhepasaṅkhātaṃ indriyaṃ samādhindriyaṃ. Yena sammappadhānena vihiṃsāvitakkaṃ vāreti, idaṃ sammappadhānasaṅkhātaṃ indriyaṃ vīriyindriyaṃ. Yena sammādiṭṭhisaṅkhātena indriyena uppannuppanne…pe… nādhivāseti, idaṃ sammādiṭṭhisaṅkhātaṃ indriyaṃ paññindriyaṃ. Imesu catūsu indriyesu saha uppajjamānā yā saddahanā okappanā [V 0.0246] uppajjati, anāvilabhāvato idaṃ saddahanasaṅkhātaṃ indriyaṃ saddhindriyaṃ. Imāni sekkhassa pañcindriyāni.

16. That faculty which, by its characteristic of recollecting the unattractive and so forth, restrains the thought co-arisen with sensual craving regarding objects of craving—this faculty, with its characteristic of recollecting the unattractive and so forth, is the faculty of mindfulness. That faculty which, by the non-distraction that has attained a sublime state, restrains the thought of ill will—this faculty, designated as non-distraction, is the faculty of concentration. That faculty which, by right effort, restrains the thought of harmfulness—this faculty, designated as right effort, is the faculty of energy. That faculty which, by the faculty designated as right view, does not tolerate arisen... this faculty, designated as right view, is the faculty of wisdom. Among these four faculties, the conviction and trust that arise simultaneously—due to its unclouded nature—this faculty, designated as conviction, is the faculty of faith. These are the five faculties of a trainee.

Ekasmiṃyeva visaye jeṭṭhakabhāvaṃ na pāpuṇeyyuṃ, attano visaye jeṭṭhakabhāvaṃ pāpuṇituṃ arahanti, “katamaṃ indriyaṃ kattha visaye jeṭṭhakabhāvaṃ pavatta”nti pucchitabbabhāvato idaṃ indriyaṃ imasmiṃ visaye pavattanti dassento “tattha saddhindriyaṃ kattha daṭṭhabba”ntiādimāha. Tattha tatthāti tesu indriyesu catūsu sotāpattiyaṅgesu saddhindriyaṃ jeṭṭhakabhāvaṃ pavattanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evaṃ sesesupi yojetabbaṃ. Kiṃ nu sekkho paññindriyeva appamatto’ti bhagavatā vutto thomito, udāhu sabbehi kusalehi dhammehīti pucchitabbattā sabbehi kusalehi dhammehi pañcindriyapamukhehi vutto thomito hotīti dassetuṃ “evaṃ sekho”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha evaṃ pañcindriyānaṃ nibbattidassanena sekho puggalo [M 0.0111] sabbehi kusalehi dhammehi appamattoti bhagavatā vutto thomito anāvilatāya manasāti yojanā. “Sekkhassa anāvilatā kena saddahitabbā”ti vattabbattā “tenāha bhagavā manasānāvilo siyā”ti vuttaṃ. Bhagavatā “manasānāvilo siyā”ti vuttattā sekkhassa anāvilatā tumhehi saddahitabbāti.

In a single sphere, they would not attain preeminence; they are worthy to attain preeminence in their own sphere. Since it should be asked, 'Which faculty operates with preeminence in which sphere?', to show that this faculty operates in this sphere, it is said, 'Where should the faculty of faith be seen?' and so on. Therein, among the four factors of stream-entry, the faculty of faith should be seen as operating with preeminence. The same should be applied to the rest. Since it should be asked whether the Blessed One said and praised a trainee as being heedful only through the faculty of wisdom, or through all wholesome qualities, to show that he was said and praised as being so through all wholesome qualities headed by the five faculties, it is said, 'Thus, a trainee...' and so on. Herein, the construction is as follows: by showing the arising of the five faculties, the trainee is said and praised by the Blessed One as being heedful through all wholesome qualities, with a mind free from affliction. Since it should be asked, 'By what should the trainee's freedom from affliction be believed?', it is said, 'Therefore, the Blessed One said, "May his mind be free from affliction."' Since the Blessed One said, 'May his mind be free from affliction,' the trainee's freedom from affliction should be believed by you.

17. Sekkhassa matthakappattā paṭipadā ācariyena vibhattā, amhehi ca ñātā, “kathaṃ asekkhassa matthakappattā paṭipadā ñātabbā”ti vattabbattā asekkhassa matthakappattaṃ paṭipadaṃ vibhajitvā dassetuṃ “kusalo sabbadhammāna”ntiādimāha. Tattha sabbadhammānanti sabbesu dhammesu matthakappattāya paṭipadāya asekkho kusalo chekataroti bhagavatā vutto thomito anāvilatāya manasāti. Asekkhassa sabbadhammesu yaṃ kosallaṃ dassetukāmo, tassa kosallassa visayabhūte sabbadhamme tāva puggalādhiṭṭhānena vibhajitvā dassetuṃ “loko nāmā”tiādimāha. Tattha “sabbadhammāna”nti iminā vuttadhammasaṅkhāto loko nāma kilesaloko, bhavaloko, indriyalokoti tividho hotīti yojanā. Tattha parittadhammaṭṭho kilesajananaṭṭhena kileso, kusalādipavattanaṭṭhena loko cāti kilesaloko. Mahaggatadhammaṭṭho bhavanaṭṭhena bhavo, vuttanayena loko cāti bhavaloko. Saddhindriyādidhammaṭṭho ādhipaccaṭṭhayogavasena indriyabhūto hutvā saddhindriyādipattanaṭṭhena loko cāti indriyaloko.

17. The path that has reached the summit for a trainee has been analyzed by the teacher and is known by us. Since it should be asked, 'How is the path that has reached the summit for a non-trainee to be known?', to analyze and show the path that has reached the summit for a non-trainee, he said, 'Skilled in all phenomena,' and so on. Herein, 'in all phenomena' means that the non-trainee is said and praised by the Blessed One as skilled and very adept in all phenomena by means of the path that has reached the summit, with a mind free of turbidity. Wishing to show the non-trainee's skill in all phenomena, to first analyze and show all phenomena which are the domain of that skill with the individual as the basis, he said, 'The world is called...' and so on. Herein, the construction is: the world, designated as the phenomena referred to by 'all phenomena,' is threefold: the world of defilements, the world of existence, and the world of faculties. Among these, that which consists of limited phenomena is 'defilement' in the sense of generating defilements, and it is 'world' in the sense of being the sphere of wholesome states and so forth; thus it is the world of defilements. That which consists of sublime phenomena is 'existence' in the sense of becoming, and it is 'world' in the manner described; thus it is the world of existence. That which consists of phenomena such as the faculty of faith is a 'faculty' by virtue of its connection to the meaning of sovereignty, and it is 'world' in the sense of being the sphere of the faculty of faith and so forth; thus it is the world of faculties.

“Tīsu lokesu katamena katamo samudāgacchatī”ti pucchitabbattā “tatthā”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Saddhādiindriyāni ko nibbattetī”ti pucchitabbattā “so indriyāni nibbattetī”ti vuttaṃ[V 0.0247]. Tattha soti yo puggalo kilesalokasaṅkhāte parittadhamme, bhavalokasaṅkhāte mahaggatadhamme ca taṃtaṃsampādanavasena ṭhito, so puggalo saddhindriyādīni indriyāni attasantāne nibbatteti.

Since it is to be asked, 'Among the three worlds, from which does which one arise?', 'therein' and so forth is stated. Since it is to be asked, 'Who produces the faculties beginning with faith?', 'he produces the faculties' is stated. Herein, 'he' is the individual who is established in the limited phenomena designated as the world of defilements and in the sublime phenomena designated as the world of existence by means of accomplishing this and that; that individual produces the faculties beginning with faith in his own mental continuum.

“Indriyesu attasantānesu punappunaṃ nibbattāpanavasena vuḍḍhāpiyamānesu kā paññā bhavatī”ti pucchitabbattā “indriyesū”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha neyyassāti abhiññeyyassa. Pariññāti rūpārūpadhamme salakkhaṇato, paccayato [M 0.0112] ca pariggahādivasena pavattapaññā. “Sā pariññā katividhena upaparikkhitabbā”ti pucchitabbattā “sā duvidhenā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha sā pariññā dassanapariññāya ca bhāvanāpariññāya ca duvidhena viññūhi upaparikkhitvā gahetabbāti. Dassanapariññāyāti ca dassanamaggapaññājanikāya ñātapariññāyāti attho gahetabbo. Tena aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ “dassanapariññāti ñātapariññā”ti (netti. aṭṭha. 17). Bhāvanāpariññāyāti bhāvanāmaggapaññājanikāya tīraṇapariññāya saddhiṃ pahānapariññāyāti attho.

Since it should be asked, 'When the faculties in one’s own continuum are being developed by being repeatedly produced, what wisdom arises?', 'regarding the faculties' and so forth is stated. Herein, 'of what is to be known' means 'of what is to be directly known.' 'Full understanding' is the wisdom that proceeds by way of grasping, etc., material and immaterial phenomena according to their specific characteristics and their conditions. Since it should be asked, 'In how many ways should this full understanding be examined?', 'it is twofold' and so forth is stated. Herein, that full understanding should be grasped by the wise after examining it in two ways: as the full understanding of vision and the full understanding of development. By 'full understanding of vision,' the meaning to be taken is the full understanding by knowing, which generates the wisdom of the path of vision. Therefore it is said in the commentary: 'Full understanding of vision is full understanding by knowing' (Netti. Aṭṭha. 17). By 'full understanding of development,' the meaning is the full understanding by investigating together with the full understanding by abandoning, which generates the wisdom of the path of development.

“Sā duvidhenā’tiādinā vutto attho atisaṅkhepo na sakkā viññātuṃ, vitthāretvā kathehī”ti vattabbattā “yadā hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha yadāti balavavipassanuppajjanakāle. Sekhoti sikkhanasīlatāya kalyāṇaputhujjano ceva sotāpannādiko ca. Ñeyyanti ñātabbaṃ rūpādikaṃ saṅkhāraṃ. Parijānātīti pariggahādiñāṇena pariggahetvā jānāti nibbidāñāṇasahagatena. Tassāti kalyāṇaputhujjanassa ceva sotāpannādikassa ca. Dve dhammāti kalyāṇaputhujjanassa balavavipassanādhammo ceva sotāpannādikassa ca balavavipassanādhammo ca. Yathākkamaṃ dassanakosallaṃ sotāpattimaggañāṇañceva bhāvanākosallaṃ sakadāgāmimaggādikañca santāne pavattāpanavasena gacchanti.

Since it should be said, 'The meaning stated as "it is twofold" and so forth is too concise and cannot be understood; explain it in detail,' 'when indeed' and so forth is stated. Herein, 'when' refers to the time when strong insight arises. 'A trainee' refers to both a virtuous ordinary person and a stream-enterer and so forth, by virtue of their nature of training. 'What is to be known' refers to the formations, such as form and so forth, that are to be known. 'He fully understands' means he knows by having comprehended with the knowledge of grasping and so forth, accompanied by the knowledge of disenchantment. 'His' refers to both the virtuous ordinary person and the stream-enterer and so forth. 'Two things' refers to the state of strong insight in a virtuous ordinary person and the state of strong insight in a stream-enterer and so forth. Respectively, they lead to skill in vision—that is, the knowledge of the path of stream-entry—and skill in development—that is, the path of a once-returner and so forth—by causing these to arise in the mental continuum.

“Pubbe yaṃ ñāṇaṃ ‘neyyassa pariññā’ti vuttaṃ, taṃ ñāṇaṃ katividhena veditabba”nti pucchitabbattā “taṃ ñāṇaṃ pañcavidhena veditabbaṃ…pe... sacchikiriyā”ti vuttaṃ. “Tāsu vipassanābhedena bhinnāsu pañcasu abhiññādīsu katamā abhiññā, katamā pariññā, katamaṃ pahānaṃ, katamā bhāvanā, katamā sacchikiriyā”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha katamā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha tatthāti abhiññādīsu. Yaṃ dhammānaṃ salakkhaṇe ñāṇanti rūpadhammānaṃ kakkhaḷādisalakkhaṇe, arūpadhammānaṃ phusanādisalakkhaṇe ārammaṇakaraṇavasena pavattaṃ yaṃ ñāṇaṃ hetuphalajānanahetujānanasaṅkhātā dhammapaṭisambhidā ceva hetuphalajānanasaṅkhātā atthapaṭisambhidā ca bhavati. Ayaṃ salakkhaṇena saddhiṃ hetuphalajānanā paññā abhiññā nāma.

Since it should be asked, 'The knowledge previously called "the full understanding of what is to be known"—in how many ways is that knowledge to be understood?', it is said: 'That knowledge is to be understood in five ways… up to… realization.' Since it should be asked, 'Among those five—higher knowledge and so forth—which are distinguished by the classification of insight, which is higher knowledge, which is full understanding, which is abandoning, which is development, and which is realization?', 'Herein, which...' and so on is stated. Herein, that is, among higher knowledge and so forth: The knowledge of the specific characteristics of phenomena—that is, the knowledge which proceeds by taking as its object the specific characteristics of material phenomena, such as hardness, and of immaterial phenomena, such as contact—becomes both the discrimination of phenomena, which is designated as the knowing of cause-and-effect and the knowing of cause, and the discrimination of meaning, which is designated as the knowing of cause-and-effect. This wisdom, which is the knowing of cause-and-effect together with specific characteristics, is called higher knowledge.

Evanti [V 0.0248][M 0.0113] vuttappakārena. Abhiññāñāṇena abhijānitvā. Yā parijānanātiādīsu “idaṃ anavajjaṃ kusalaṃ, idaṃ sāvajjaṃ akusalaṃ, idaṃ akusalavipākajanakaṃ sāvajjaṃ, idaṃ kusalavipākajanakaṃ anavajjaṃ, idaṃ saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ kaṇhaṃ, idaṃ asaṃkiliṭṭhaṃ sukkaṃ, idaṃ kusalaṃ anavajjādikaṃ sevitabbaṃ, idaṃ akusalaṃ sāvajjādikaṃ na sevitabba”nti evaṃ aniccādito kalāpasammasanādivasena gahitā sammasitā ime vipassanāya ārammaṇabhūtā saṅkhatadhammā idaṃ udayabbayañāṇādiphalaṃ ānisaṃsaṃ anukkamena nibbattāpenti. Tannibbattavipassanāya uppajjanato upacāraṃ uppādenti, evaṃ anukkamena gahitānaṃ pavattitānaṃ tesaṃ udayabbayañāṇādīnaṃ ayaṃ saccānubodhapaṭivedho atthoti paricchinditvā yā parijānanā pavattā, sā ayaṃ parijānanā pariññā nāmāti yojetvā, evaṃ vuttappakārāya pariññāpaññāya parijānitvā pahātabbā, bhāvetabbā, sacchikātabbā ca tayo dhammā avasiṭṭhā bhavanti. “Ye akusalā, te pahātabbā”ti yā parijānanā paññā pavattā, idaṃ pahānaṃ pahānañāṇaṃ. “Ye kusalā, te bhāvetabbā”ti yā parijānanā paññā pavattā, sā bhāvanāpaññā. “Yaṃ asaṅkhataṃ, idaṃ sacchikiriya”nti yā parijānanā paññā pavattā, sā sacchikiriyāpaññāti yojetvā aṭṭhakathādhippāyena aviruddho attho gahetabbo.

Thus, in the manner explained. Having directly known with the knowledge of direct knowledge. Regarding the full understanding that occurs in instances such as discerning—'This is blameless and wholesome, this is blameworthy and unwholesome, this is blameworthy and produces unwholesome results, this is blameless and produces wholesome results, this is defiled and dark, this is undefiled and bright, this wholesome and blameless should be cultivated, this unwholesome and blameworthy should not be cultivated'—these conditioned phenomena, being the object for insight, are grasped and contemplated through the analysis of aggregates and so on in terms of impermanence, etc., and sequentially produce the benefit, the fruit such as the knowledge of arising and passing away. From the arising of insight thus produced, they bring about access. In this way, having determined that the penetration of the comprehension of the truths is the meaning of these knowledges, such as the knowledge of arising and passing away, which are sequentially grasped and occur, the full understanding that occurs is called full understanding (pariññā). Thus, having fully understood through the wisdom of full understanding of the kind described, three things remain: to be abandoned, developed, and realized. The wisdom that arises in fully understanding, 'Whatever is unwholesome should be abandoned,' is the knowledge of abandoning. The wisdom that arises in fully understanding, 'Whatever is wholesome should be developed,' is the wisdom of development. The wisdom that arises in fully understanding, 'Whatever is unconditioned should be realized,' is the wisdom of realization. Having construed it thus, the meaning should be understood in accordance with the commentary’s intention, without contradiction.

Abhiññādayo pañcavidhā paññā ācariyena vibhattā, amhehi ca ñātā, “tāhi pariññāhi jānanto puggalo ‘ki’nti vuccati thomīyatī”ti vattabbattā “yo eva”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha yo puggalo evaṃ vuttappakārena jānāti, ayaṃ jānanto puggalo paccayuppannesu dhammesu kusalattā chekattā “atthakusalo”ti vuccati thomīyati, paccayadhammesu kusalattā “dhammakusalo”ti ca catunnaṃ ekattādīnaṃ nayānaṃ yuttatāya kovidattā “kalyāṇatākusalo”ti ca phalasamāpattīsu kovidattā “phalatākusalo”ti ca vaḍḍhīsu kovidattā “āyakusalo”ti ca avaḍḍhīsu kovidattā “apāyakusalo”ti ca accāyike kicce vā bhaye vā uppanne sati tassa kiccassa, bhayassa vā tikicchanasamatthe ṭhānuppattiyakāraṇe kovidattā “upāyakusalo”ti ca mahantesu abhikkamādīsu satisampajaññāya sampannattā “mahatā kosallena samannāgato”ti ca vuccati thomīyati. “Tassa [M 0.0114] asekkhassa atthādīsu kusalabhāvo kathaṃ saddahitabbo”ti vattabbattā “tenāhā”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Kusalo sabbadhammāna”nti vuttattā saddahitabboti adhippāyo.

The five kinds of wisdom, beginning with direct knowledge, have been analyzed by the teacher and are known to us. Therefore, since it should be said, “A person who knows through these full understandings—how is that person praised?”, it is stated, “Indeed, that one…” Here, the person who knows in the manner described is called “skilled in meaning” and is praised because of his skill and proficiency in phenomena that have arisen from conditions. He is called “skilled in the Dhamma” due to his proficiency in causal phenomena, “skilled in what is auspicious” because of his competence in the suitability of the four unities and other methods, “skilled in fruition” due to his mastery in attainments of fruition, “skilled in growth” because of his expertise in increases, and “skilled in decline” due to his understanding of losses. He is called “skilled in means” because of his ability to handle urgent tasks or dangers when they arise, due to his competence in the cause for the arising of a state capable of remedying that task or danger. He is also called “endowed with great skill” because he is accomplished in mindfulness and clear comprehension in major undertakings such as going forward or backward. Since it should be asked, “How should the skilled nature of that non-trainee in meaning and other matters be believed?” it is said, “Therefore…” Because it is stated, “Skilled in all phenomena,” the intention is that it should be believed.

“Kusalo [V 0.0249] sabbadhammāna”nti padassa attho ācariyena vibhatto, amhehi ca ñāto, “sato bhikkhu paribbaje”ti padassa attho kathaṃ amhehi vitthārato viññāto”ti vattabbattā “sato bhikkhu paribbaje”tiādi vuttaṃ. Atha vā “sato bhikkhu paribbaje”ti bhagavatā vuttaṃ, “kattha pavattena satisahitena ñāṇena sampanno sato kimatthaṃ paribbaje”ti pucchitabbattā “imesu pavattena satisahitañāṇena sampanno sato imamatthaṃ paribbaje”ti niyametvā dassento “sato bhikkhu paribbaje”tiādimāha. Tattha tenāti yo abhikkamādīsu pavattena satisahitañāṇena samannāgato sato asekkhabhikkhu, tena asekkhabhikkhunā pariniṭṭhitasikkhattā aññapayojanābhāvato diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāratthaṃ abhikkante…pe… tuṇhībhāvena satena satisahitena sampajānena ñāṇena vihātabbaṃ catuiriyāpathaparivattanasaṅkhātaṃ viharaṇaṃ pavattetabbaṃ.

“The meaning of the phrase ‘skilled in all phenomena’ has been explained by the teacher and is known to us. But how is the meaning of the phrase ‘a mindful monk wanders’ to be understood by us in detail?” Since this should be said, “a mindful monk wanders” and so on is stated. Alternatively, “a mindful monk wanders” was spoken by the Blessed One. Because the question should be asked: “Endowed with knowledge accompanied by mindfulness that has arisen in what sphere, being mindful, for what purpose does he wander?”, thus, determining and showing that “Endowed with knowledge accompanied by mindfulness that has arisen in these matters, being mindful, he wanders for this purpose,” the phrase “a mindful monk wanders” and so on was spoken. Here, ‘by him’ refers to that non-trainee monk who is mindful, endowed with knowledge accompanied by mindfulness that has arisen in going forward and so forth. By that non-trainee monk, because his training is complete and there is no further purpose, for the sake of dwelling happily in this very life, while going forward… and so on… in silence, he should dwell mindfully, with knowledge accompanied by mindfulness and clear comprehension. The dwelling, designated as the changing of the four postures, should be carried on.

“Yā sekkhāsekkhapaṭipadā niddiṭṭhā, imā sekkhāsekkhapaṭipadā saṅkhepato katividhā”ti pucchitabbattā imā paṭipadāsaṅkhātā cariyā saṅkhepato puggalavasena dveti dassetuṃ “imā dve cariyā”tiādimāha. Tattha yā cariyā bhāvetabbakusalādibhedena vā atthakosallādibhedena vā abhikkamādīsu satisampajaññabhedena vā niddiṭṭhā, imā cariyā dveti bhagavatā anuññātā anujānanavasena desitā, visuddhānaṃ arahantānaṃ ekā cariyā, visujjhantānaṃ sekkhānaṃ ekā cariyāti puggalavasena dveti daṭṭhabbā.

Since it should be asked, “The paths of the trainees and the non-trainees have been described. How many kinds of these paths of the trainees and non-trainees are there in brief?”, to show that these practices, designated as paths, are in brief twofold according to the individual, he said, “These are the two practices.” Herein, the practices that have been described with distinctions such as wholesome to be developed, etc., or skill in meaning, etc., or mindfulness and clear comprehension in advancing, etc., are taught by the Blessed One as twofold, permitted by way of approval. For the purified arahants, there is one practice; for the purifying trainees, there is one practice. Thus, they should be seen as twofold according to the individual.

“Asekkhoyeva kasmā ‘sato abhikkamatī’tiādinā vuccati thomīyati, kalyāṇaputhujjanopi ‘sato abhikkamatī’tiādinā vuccati thomīyatī”ti vattabbattā “katakiccāni hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Arahato indriyāni katakiccāni, indriyānaṃ katakiccattā yaṃ pucchaṃ pucchitabbaṃ, taṃ sabbaṃ catubbidhaṃ dukkhassa pariññābhisamayena bojjhitabbaṃ…pe… nirodhassa sacchikiriyābhisamayena bojjhitabbaṃ bhave. Catubbidhaṃ idaṃ bojjhaṃ bojjhitabbaṃ yo asekkho sativepullappattattā evaṃ pariññābhisamayādinā jānāti, ayaṃ [M 0.0115] asekkho nippariyāyena “rāgassa khayāya, dosassa khayāya, mohassa khayāya sato abhikkamati, sato paṭikkamatī”ti vuccati thomīyati. Sekkhopi yathāvuttaṃ bojjhaṃ bojjhitabbaṃ attano pariññābhisamayādinā jānāti, tasmā “sato…pe… mohassā”ti vuccati thomīyatīti veditabbo. Tena vuttaṃ “ke visujjhantā? Sekkhā”ti.

Since it should be said, “Why is only the non-trainee praised with the words ‘mindfully advances,’ etc., when even a virtuous ordinary person is praised with the words ‘mindfully advances,’ etc.?”, it is said: “Because their duties are done.” The faculties of the arahant have fulfilled their duties. Since the faculties have fulfilled their duties, whatever question is to be asked, all of it should be understood through the fourfold comprehension of the full understanding of suffering… up to… the comprehension of the realization of cessation. The non-trainee who, having attained the fullness of mindfulness, knows this fourfold object of understanding that is to be understood through the comprehension of full understanding and so on, is praised without qualification: “For the destruction of lust, for the destruction of hatred, for the destruction of delusion, one advances mindfully, retreats mindfully.” The trainee, too, knows the aforesaid object of understanding that is to be understood through their own comprehension of full understanding and so on; therefore, it should be understood that they too are praised: “mindfully… up to… for the destruction of delusion.” Hence, it is said: “Who are the purifying? The trainees.”

“Kasmā sekkhāsekkhānaṃ satisampajaññena abhikkamanādibhāvo, rāgādīnañca khayabhāvo [V 0.0250] saddahitabbo”ti vattabbattā vuttaṃ “tenāha bhagavā sato bhikkhu paribbaje”ti. “Bhagavato sabbaṃ kāyakammaṃ ñāṇapubbaṅgama’ntiādinā (netti. 15) manāpikesu kāmesu nābhigijjhanabhāvo, amanāpikesu kāmesu manasā anāvilabhāvo, sabbadhammesu kusalabhāvo, satisampajaññena samannāgatassa paribbajanabhāvo ācariyena niddiṭṭho, so nābhigijjhanabhāvādiko kasmā amhehi saddahitabbo”ti pucchitabbattā vuttaṃ “tenāha kāmesu…pe… paribbaje”ti. Imissā gāthāyapi pucchāvissajjanavicayo pubbe ekādhiṭṭhānādidhammādhiṭṭhānādivasena vuttanayānusārena veditabbo.

Since it should be said, "Why should the advancing, etc., of trainees and non-trainees with mindfulness and clear comprehension, and the destruction of lust, etc., be believed?", it is said: "Therefore, the Blessed One said: 'Mindful, a bhikkhu should wander.'" By the words, "All bodily actions of the Blessed One are preceded by knowledge," etc. (Netti. 15), the state of not being greedy for agreeable sensual pleasures, the state of mind not being disturbed by disagreeable sensual pleasures, the state of being skilled in all phenomena, and the state of wandering endowed with mindfulness and clear comprehension, have been indicated by the teacher. Since it should be asked, "Why should this state of non-greed, etc., be believed by us?", it is said: "Therefore, he said: 'In sensual pleasures... up to... should wander.'" In this verse too, the investigation of question and answer should be understood according to the method previously stated by way of the establishment of the teaching on one basis, etc.

Vicayahāravibhaṅge ajitasuttaṃ nīharitvā pucchāvissajjanavicayo ācariyena vibhatto, amhehi ca ñāto, “katamo suttantaresu pucchāvissajjanavicayo”ti pucchitabbattā ajitasutte pucchāvissajjanavicayanayānusārena suttantaresupi pucchāvissajjanāni nīharitvā pucchāvicayavissajjanavicayā yojetabbāti dassetuṃ “evaṃ pucchitabbaṃ, evaṃ vissajjitabba”nti vuttaṃ. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana –

In the Analysis of the Mode of Investigation, the teacher has analyzed the investigation of questions and answers by extracting the Ajita Sutta, and this is known by us. Because it should be asked, 'What is the investigation of questions and answers in other suttas?', to show that, following the method of the investigation of questions and answers in the Ajita Sutta, the questions and answers in other suttas should also be extracted and the investigation of questions and the investigation of answers applied, it is said, 'Thus it should be asked, thus it should be answered.' In the commentary, however—

Ettāvatā ca mahāthero vicayahāraṃ vibhajanto ajitasuttavasena pucchāvicayaṃ, vissajjanavicayañca dassetvā idāni suttantaresupi pucchāvissajjanavicayānaṃ nayaṃ dassento evaṃ pucchitabbaṃ, evaṃ vissajjitabba’nti āhā”ti (netti. aṭṭha. 17) –

"Thus, the great elder, when analyzing the mode of investigation, demonstrated the investigation of questions and the investigation of answers by way of the Ajita Sutta. Now, to show the method of investigating questions and answers in other suttas as well, he said, 'Thus should it be asked, and thus should it be answered.'" (Netti. Aṭṭha. 17)

Vuttaṃ. Tattha evanti ajitasutte (su. ni. 1038 ādayo; cūḷani. vatthugāthā 57, ajitamāṇavapucchāniddesa 1 ādayo) vuttapucchāvicayānusārena pucchāvasena pavattasuttaṃ nīharitvā pucchāvicayo vibhajetabbo, evaṃ ajitasutte (su. ni. 1038 ādayo; cūḷani. vatthugāthā 57 ādayo, ajitamāṇavapucchāniddesa 1 ādayo) vuttavissajjanavicayānusārena suttantaresupi vissajjanavasena pavattasuttaṃ nīharitvā vissajjanavicayo vibhajetabbo.

It is said. Herein, 'thus' means: according to the investigation of questions stated in the Ajita Sutta (Sn. 1038 ff.; Cūḷaniddesa, Vatthugāthā 57; Ajitamāṇavapucchāniddesa 1 ff.), the investigation of questions should be analyzed by extracting a sutta that proceeds by way of questions. Similarly, according to the investigation of answers stated in the Ajita Sutta (Sn. 1038 ff.; Cūḷaniddesa, Vatthugāthā 57 ff.; Ajitamāṇavapucchāniddesa 1 ff.), the investigation of answers should be analyzed by extracting a sutta that proceeds by way of answers, even in other suttas.

Pucchāvissajjanavicayā [M 0.0116] ācariyena vibhattā, amhehi ca ñātā, “katamo suttaanugītivicayo”ti pucchitabbattā “suttassa ca anugītī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha suttassāti nīharitasuttassa. Anugītīti suttantaradesanāsaṅkhātā anugīti. Atthato ca byañjanato ca samānetabbāti tassā anugītiyā atthato, byañjanato ca saṃvaṇṇetabbasuttena samānā sadisī kātabbā, tasmiṃ vā saṃvaṇṇiyamānasutte anugīti suttatthato, byañjanato ca samānetabbā[V 0.0251]. “Atthato asamāne ko nāma doso āpajjeyyā”ti pucchitabbattā atthāpagataṃ hi byañjanaṃ samphappalāpaṃ bhavatī”ti vuttaṃ. “Atthato asamāne doso vutto, amhehi ca ñāto, byañjanato asamāne pana ko nāma doso āpajjatī”ti pucchitabbattā “dunnikkhittassa padabyañjanassa atthopi dunnayo bhavatī”ti vuttaṃ. Tasmā sadosattā anugītiyā vā suttena atthabyañjanūpetaṃ saṅgāyitabbaṃ.

The investigations of questions and answers have been analyzed by the teacher and are known by us. Because it should be asked, 'What is the investigation of the subsequent recitation?', it was said, 'And the subsequent recitation of the sutta,' etc. Herein, 'of the sutta' means of the extracted sutta. 'Subsequent recitation' means the subsequent recitation reckoned as another sutta-teaching. It should be made equal in meaning and phrasing—that is, the subsequent recitation should be made similar to the sutta being commented upon in meaning and phrasing, or, in that sutta being commented upon, the subsequent recitation should be made equal to the sutta in meaning and phrasing. Because it should be asked, 'If it is unequal in meaning, what fault would arise?', it was said, 'For phrasing devoid of meaning becomes frivolous talk.' Because it should be asked, 'The fault when it is unequal in meaning has been stated and is known by us, but what fault arises when it is unequal in phrasing?', it was said, 'Of a poorly placed word and phrase, the meaning is also hard to grasp.' Therefore, because of this faultiness, either the subsequent recitation or the sutta should be recited, endowed with meaning and phrasing.

Anugītivicayo ācariyena vibhatto, amhehi ca ñāto, “katamo suttassa vicayo”ti pucchitabbattā suttañcā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha suttañcāti niddhāritasuttañca. “Idaṃ niddhāritasuttaṃ nāma bhagavatā vuttaṃ āhaccavacanaṃ kiṃ, udāhu saṅgāyantehi vuttaṃ anusandhivacanaṃ ki”nti pavicinitabbaṃ, “idaṃ niddhāritasuttaṃ nītatthaṃ kiṃ, udāhu neyyatthaṃ ki”nti pavicinitabbaṃ, “idaṃ niddhāritasuttaṃ saṃkilesabhāgiyaṃ kiṃ, udāhu vāsanābhāgiyaṃ ki”nti pavicinitabbaṃ, “idaṃ niddhāritasuttaṃ nibbedhabhāgiyaṃ kiṃ, udāhu asekkhabhāgiyaṃ ki”nti pavicinitabbaṃ. Evaṃ pavicinitvā yadi āhaccavacanaṃ bhave, evaṃ sati “āhaccavacana”nti niddhāretvā gahetabbaṃ. Yadi asekkhasuttaṃ bhave, evaṃ sati “asekkhasutta”nti niddhāretvā gahetabbaṃ, ñātanti attho.

The investigation of the subsequent recitation has been analyzed by the teacher and is known by us. Because it should be asked, 'What is the investigation of the sutta?', 'and the sutta' etc., was stated. Herein, 'and the sutta' refers to the determined sutta. One should investigate: 'Is this determined sutta spoken by the Blessed One as a direct statement, or is it spoken by those who recite it as a connecting statement?' One should investigate: 'Is this determined sutta of definitive meaning, or is it of interpretable meaning?' One should investigate: 'Is this determined sutta pertaining to defilement, or is it pertaining to habit-energy?' One should investigate: 'Is this determined sutta pertaining to penetration, or is it pertaining to the state of no further training?' Having investigated thus, if it is a direct statement, then, having determined it as such, it should be taken as a 'direct statement.' If it is a sutta pertaining to the state of no further training, then, having determined it as such, it should be taken as a 'sutta pertaining to the state of no further training.' This is the meaning of 'known.'

“Suttaṃ pavicinitvā suttassa atthabhūtāni sabbāni saccāni niddhāretvā kattha padese passitabbānī”ti pucchitabbattā pucchaṃ ṭhapetvā imasmiṃ padese passitabbānīti dassetuṃ “kuhiṃ imassa suttassa sabbāni…pe… pariyosāne”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha imassa suttassāti yaṃ suttaṃ vicinituṃ niddhāritaṃ, imassa suttassa catusaccavinimuttassa suttatthassa abhāvato sabbāni saccāni tasseva suttassa ādimajjhapariyosāne passitabbānīti attho.

Because it should be asked: 'Having investigated the sutta and determined all the truths that constitute the meaning of the sutta, in what section should they be seen?', to show in what section they should be seen, it is said: 'Where in this sutta are all... at the conclusion?' Herein, 'of this sutta' refers to the sutta that has been determined for investigation. Because there is no meaning of this sutta that is separate from the four truths, all the truths should be seen in the beginning, middle, and end of that very sutta—this is the meaning.

Yathāvuttaṃ [M 0.0117] suttavicayaṃ nigamento “evaṃ suttaṃ pavicetabba”nti āha. “Na yathāvuttapucchādīnaṃ pavicetabbabhāvo amhehi jānitabbo saddahitabbo”ti vattabbabhāvato “tenāha…pe… anugītī”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha tena yathāvuttapucchādīnaṃ vicetabbabhāvena āyasmā mahākaccāno “yaṃ pucchitañca…pe… anugītī”tiādikaṃ yaṃ vacanaṃ āha, tena vacanena vicetabbabhāvo tumhehi jānitabbo saddahitabbovāti vuttaṃ hoti.

Concluding the investigation of the sutta as described, he said, 'Thus the sutta should be investigated.' Because it could be said, 'The fact that the questions and so on as described are to be investigated is not to be known or believed by us,' it is said, 'Therefore he said... subsequent recitation.' Herein, this means: by the statement which the venerable Mahākaccāna spoke, beginning 'What was asked... subsequent recitation,' on account of the fact that the questions and so on as described are to be investigated, by that statement you should know and believe that they are to be investigated.

“Yathāvuttappakāro ca vicayo hāro paripuṇṇo kiṃ, udāhu aññopi niddhāretvā yojetabbo atthi ki”nti pucchitabbattā “niyutto vicayo hāro”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha pucchāvicayavissajjanavicayapubbāparavicayaanugītivicayasuttavicayā [V 0.0252] sarūpato vibhattā, tehi avaseso assādādivicayopi yathārahaṃ niddhāretvā yutto yuñjitabboti adhippāyo.

Because it should be asked, 'Is the mode of investigation of the kind described complete, or is there also another to be determined and applied?', it is said, 'The mode of investigation is established.' Herein, the investigations—of questions, of answers, of prior and subsequent, of subsequent recitation, and of the sutta—are analyzed according to their own nature; the intention is that by these, the remaining investigations, such as that of gratification and so on, should also be determined as appropriate and applied.

Iti vicayahāravibhaṅge sattibalānurūpā racitā

Thus, in the Analysis of the Mode of Investigation, this was composed in accordance with my strength and ability.

Vibhāvanā niṭṭhitā.

The Elucidation is concluded.

Paṇḍitehi pana aṭṭhakathāṭīkānusārena gambhīrattho vitthārato vibhajitvā gahetabboti.

However, the profound meaning should be thoroughly analyzed and grasped by the learned according to the commentaries and sub-commentaries.

3. Yuttihāravibhaṅgavibhāvanā

3. The Elucidation of the Analysis of the Mode of Reasoning.

18. Yena yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūtena vicayahāravibhaṅgena padapañhādayo vicitā, so saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūto vicayahāravibhaṅgo paripuṇṇo, “katamo yuttihāravibhaṅgo”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha katamo yuttihāro”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha tatthāti tesu niddiṭṭhesu soḷasasu hāresu katamo saṃvaṇṇanāviseso yuttihāro yuttihāravibhaṅgoti pucchi. “Sabbesaṃ hārāna”ntiādiniddesassa idāni vuccamāno “ayaṃ yuttihāro”tiādiko vitthārasaṃvaṇṇanāviseso yuttihāravibhaṅgo nāmāti viññeyyo. Tena vuttaṃ “tattha katamo yuttihārotiādi yuttihāravibhaṅgo”ti (netti. aṭṭha. 18). Ayaṃ yuttihāro kiṃ nāma suttatthaṃ yuttāyuttivasena yojayatīti yuñjitabbaṃ suttatthaṃ [M 0.0118] pucchati. Suttattho pana duvidho atathākārena gayhamāno, tathākārena gayhamāno atthoti. Tattha atathākārena gayhamānova attho yāthāvato yuttiniddhāraṇena yojetabbo, itaro pana bhūtakathanamattena yojetabbo. Yasmā panāyaṃ yuttigavesanā nāma saṃvaṇṇanā mahāpadesehi vinā na sambhavati, tasmā yuttihāraṃ vibhajanto tassa yuttihārassa lakkhaṇaṃ paṭhamaṃ upadisituṃ “cattāro mahāpadesā”tiādimāha. Tattha mahāpadesāti mahante buddhādayo apadisitvā vuttāni kāraṇāni, mahantāni vā dhammassa apadesāni patiṭṭhānāni. Apadisīyateti apadeso, buddho apadeso etassa kāraṇassāti buddhāpadeso. Sesesupi eseva nayo netabbo. “Buddhassa sammukhā etaṃ suttaṃ mayā suta”nti vatvā ābhatassa ganthassa suttavinayehi saṃsandanaṃ dhammo, asaṃsandanaṃ adhammoti vinicchayakāraṇaṃ [V 0.0253] mahāpadesoti adhippāyo. “Buddhassa sammukhā mayā ābhataṃ, saṅghassa sammukhā mayā ābhataṃ, sambahulattherānaṃ sammukhā mayā ābhataṃ, ekattherassa sammukhā mayā ābhata”nti vatvā ābhatassa ganthassa yāni byañjanapadaatthapadāni santi, tāni padabyañjanāni bhagavatā desite sutte otarayitabbāni anuppavesitāni, vinaye rāgādivinaye sandassayitabbāni saṃsandetabbāni. Dhammatāyaṃ upanikkhipitabbāni pakkhipitabbāni. Yadi suttatthena, vinayatthena, dhammatāya ca aviruddhāni honti, evaṃ sati tava ābhatapadabyañjanāni yuttānīti vinicchayantehi vatvā gahetabbānīti adhippāyo.

18. By whatever special exposition of the mode of investigation the words, questions, etc., are distinguished, that special exposition of the mode of investigation is complete. Since it is to be asked, “What is the exposition of the mode of reasoning?” it is said, “Herein, what is the mode of reasoning?” and so on. Here, among those sixteen modes mentioned, it is asked, “What is the special exposition of the mode of reasoning? What is the exposition of the mode of reasoning?” Now, in the explanation beginning with “For all modes,” the detailed special exposition called “This is the mode of reasoning” and so on is to be understood as the exposition of the mode of reasoning. Therefore, it is said, “Herein, what is the mode of reasoning?” and so on, the exposition of the mode of reasoning (Netti. Aṭṭha. 18). This mode of reasoning questions the meaning of the Sutta to be connected, in terms of whether it connects the meaning of the Sutta appropriately or inappropriately. The meaning of the Sutta is twofold: meaning taken incorrectly, and meaning taken correctly. Here, the meaning taken incorrectly should be connected by determining the proper reasoning, while the other should be connected merely by stating the facts. Since this search for reasoning, which is an exposition, does not occur without the Great References, therefore, when analyzing the mode of reasoning, he first states “The four Great References” and so on, in order to point out the characteristic of that mode of reasoning. Here, “Great References” means the great reasons stated by referring to the great ones such as the Buddha, or the great foundations of the Dhamma. “A reference” (apadeso) means that which is referred to; the Buddha is a reference for this cause—thus, the Buddha-reference. The same method should be applied to the rest. The intention is that after saying, “This Sutta was heard by me in the presence of the Buddha,” the text brought forth should be compared with the Suttas and the Vinaya: what accords is Dhamma, what does not accord is not Dhamma—this is the Great Reference for decision. After saying, “This was brought by me in the presence of the Buddha, in the presence of the Sangha, in the presence of many elders, in the presence of one elder,” the words and phrases of the text brought forth should be inserted into the Sutta taught by the Blessed One, introduced into it, and compared with the Vinaya in terms of the subduing of lust and so on. They should be placed within the Dhamma-nature. If they are not in conflict with the meaning of the Sutta, the meaning of the Vinaya, and the Dhamma-nature, then those who decide should say and accept that the words and expressions you have brought are appropriate—this is the intention.

Suttavinayadhammatāsu otarayitabbāni sandassayitabbāni upanikkhipitabbānīti ācariyena vuttāni, “kattha sutte, kattha vinaye, kattha dhammatāya”nti vattabbattā “katamasmiṃ sutte”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha catūsu ariyasaccesūti catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ dassanakesu suttesu. Rāgo vinassati vūpasamati etena asubhādināti rāgavinayaṃ, kiṃ taṃ? Asubhādinimittaṃ, taṃ assa atthīti rāgavinayo, ko so? Asubhādinimittadassanako suttantaviseso. Esa nayo dosavinayotiādīsupi. Paṭiccasamuppādo nāma sassatadiṭṭhiucchedadiṭṭhiṃ vivajjetvā ekattanayādīnaṃ dīpanena avijjādisaṅkhārādisabhāvadhammānaṃ paccayapaccayuppannabhāvadīpakoti vuttaṃ “katamissaṃ dhammatāyaṃ upanikkhipitabbāni? Paṭiccasamuppāde”ti.

“They should be inserted, compared, and placed within the Sutta, Vinaya, and Dhamma-nature,” as stated by the teacher. Since it is to be asked, “In which Sutta? In which Vinaya? In which Dhamma-nature?” therefore, “In which Sutta?” and so on is stated. Here, “in the four Noble Truths” means in the Suttas that are expositions of the four Noble Truths. “Lust is destroyed and calmed by this,” namely, by the foul and so on—thus, “subduing of lust” (rāgavinaya). What is that? The sign of the foul and so on. That exists for him—thus, “subduing of lust.” What is that? A particular Suttanta that is an exposition of the sign of the foul and so on. The same method should be applied to “subduing of hatred” and so on. Dependent Origination, by avoiding the eternalist view and the annihilationist view, and by illuminating the aspects of oneness and so on, is said to be the illuminator of the nature of phenomena such as ignorance and formations, in terms of their being causes and effects. Thus it is said: “Under which Dhamma-nature should they be placed? Under Dependent Origination.”

“Suttādīsu [M 0.0119] avatarante sandissante avilomente kiṃ na janetī”ti vattabbato “catūsū”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha “buddhādīnaṃ sammukhā mayā ābhata”nti vatvā ābhatagantho catūsu ariyasaccesu yadi avatarati, evaṃ sati ābhatagantho āsave na janeti. Rāgādikilesavinaye yadi sandissati, evaṃ sati ābhatagantho āsave na janeti. Dhammatañca yadi na vilometi, evaṃ sati ābhatagantho āsave na janetīti attho daṭṭhabbo.

Since it is to be said, “When inserted into the Suttas and so on, when compared, when not contradicting, what does it not generate?” therefore, “In the four” and so on is stated. Herein, if the text brought forth, after saying, “I have brought this in the presence of the Buddha and others,” is inserted into the four Noble Truths, then the text brought forth does not generate taints. If it is compared with the subduing of defilements such as lust, then the text brought forth does not generate taints. And if it does not contradict the Dhamma-nature, then the text brought forth does not generate taints—this meaning should be understood.

“Kimatthaṃ yuttihāravibhaṅge cattāro mahāpadesā ābhatā”ti vattabbattā “catūhi mahāpadesehī”tiādimāha. Tattha ābhataganthe yaṃ yaṃ atthajātaṃ, yaṃ yaṃ dhammajātaṃ vā catūhi mahāpadesehi yujjati, taṃ taṃ atthajātaṃ vā taṃ taṃ dhammajātaṃ vā saṃvaṇṇetabbasutte gahetabbaṃ. Yena yena kāraṇena ca catūhi mahāpadesehi yujjati, taṃ taṃ kāraṇaṃ saṃvaṇṇanāvasena saṃvaṇṇetabbasutte gahetabbaṃ. Yathā yathā pakārena catūhi mahāpadesehi yujjati, so so pakāro saṃvaṇṇanāvasena saṃvaṇṇetabbasutte gahetabbo. Evaṃ gāhaṇatthaṃ cattāro mahāpadesā ābhatāti attho.

Since it is to be asked, “For what purpose are the four Great References introduced in the exposition of the mode of reasoning?” therefore, “By the four Great References” and so on is stated. Herein, in the text brought forth, whatever content of meaning or whatever content of teaching accords with the four Great References, that content of meaning or that content of teaching should be taken into the Sutta to be explained. And by whatever reason it accords with the four Great References, that reason should be taken into the Sutta to be explained in the manner of an exposition. In whatever way it accords with the four Great References, that way should be taken into the Sutta to be explained in the manner of an exposition. Thus, the four Great References are introduced for the purpose of taking in this way—this is the intention.

19. Catūhi [V 0.0254] mahāpadesehi yuttaṃ aviruddhaṃ taṃ taṃ atthajātaṃ gahetabbanti ācariyena vuttaṃ, “kattha kena yuttiniddhāraṇaṃ kātabba”nti vattabbattā “pañhaṃ pucchitenā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Pañhe pañhaṃ pucchitena puggalena yuttiniddhāraṇaṃ kātabbanti. Tattha pañhanti pañhitabbaṃ sabhāvadhammaṃ. Pucchitenāti vissajjetuṃ samatthena paṇḍitapuggalena. Pañheti pucchāvasena pavattapāṭhe. Padāni kati kittakāni hontīti padaso paṭhamaṃ pariyogāhitabbaṃ yuttihārena vicetabbaṃ vīmaṃsitabbaṃ. “Kathaṃ vicetabba”nti pucchitabbattā “yadi sabbānī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha sabbāni padānīti pucchitapāṭhe niravasesāni padāni ekaṃ samānaṃ atthaṃ yadi abhivadanti, evaṃ sati atthavasena eko pañho. Esa nayo sesesupi. Tena vuttaṃ “tadatthassekassa ñātuṃ icchitattā”ti (netti. aṭṭha. 19).

19. The teacher has stated that whatever content of meaning is consistent and not contradictory with the four Great References should be taken. Since it is to be asked, “Where and by whom should the determination of reasoning be made?” therefore, 'by the one who has been asked' and so on is stated. In the question, the determination of reasoning should be made by the person who has been asked the question. Here, 'question' (pañhaṃ) means the nature of the phenomenon to be inquired into. By 'one who has been asked' (pucchitena) is meant a wise person capable of answering. By 'question' (pañhe) is meant the passage that proceeds by way of questioning. First, the words should be thoroughly examined, how many words there are and of what kind; then analyzed and investigated through the mode of reasoning. Since it is to be asked, “How should it be investigated?” therefore, “If all…” and so on is stated. Here, “all the words” means all the words without remainder in the questioned passage. If they all convey one and the same meaning, then the question is one in terms of meaning. The same principle applies to the rest. Therefore, it is said, “Because there is a wish to know that one meaning” (Netti. Aṭṭha. 19).

Ekanti atthavasena ekavidhaṃ pañhaṃ. Upaparikkhamānena puggalena aññātabbaṃ daḷhaṃ jānitabbaṃ. “Ko ājānanākāro”ti pucchitabbattā ājānanākāraṃ dassento “kiṃ ime dhammā”tiādimāha. Tattha “ye hi pariyattidhammā [M 0.0120] saṃvaṇṇetabbā, ime pariyattidhammā nānatthā honti kiṃ, nānābyañjanā honti kiṃ, udāhu imesaṃ pariyattidhammānaṃ eko attho hoti, byañjanameva nānaṃ hoti ki”nti yuttito vicetvā aññātabbanti yojanā. “Yathāvutto pañho kiṃ bhave”ti pucchitabbattā yathāvuttaṃ pañhaṃ ekadesaṃ dassetuṃ “yathā kiṃ bhave”ti pucchitvā “yathā sā”tiādimāha.

By “one” (ekaṃ) is meant a question that is of one kind in terms of meaning. It should be firmly known by the person investigating. Since it is to be asked, “What is the way of knowing?” to show the way of knowing, he said, “Are these phenomena…?” and so on. Here, the explanation is that one should investigate reasonably and understand whether these textual teachings that are to be expounded have different meanings, or different expressions, or whether these textual teachings have one meaning and only the expressions are different. Since it is to be asked, “What would the aforementioned question be?” in order to show a part of the aforementioned question, having asked, “What is it like?” he said, “Just as that…” and so on.

Tassaṃ pucchāgāthāyaṃ – coraghātakena manussena coro abbhāhato viya kena dhammena sattaloko sadā abbhāhato, māluvalatāya attano nissitarukkho parivārito ajjhotthaṭo viya kena dhammena sattaloko sadā parivārito ajjhotthaṭo, visappītakhurappena sallena otiṇṇo anupaviṭṭho viya kena sallena sattaloko sadā otiṇṇo anupaviṭṭho, kissa kena kāraṇena sattaloko sadā dhūpāyito santāpitoti yojanā.

In that questioning verse—just as a thief is struck down by an executioner, by what phenomenon is the world of beings always struck down? Just as a māluvā creeper surrounds and overwhelms the tree on which it depends, by what phenomenon is the world of beings always surrounded and overwhelmed? Just as one is entered and penetrated by an arrow with a poisoned tip, by what arrow is the world of beings always entered and penetrated? By what, for what cause, is the world of beings always smoked and tormented?—this is the explanation.

“Imāya pucchāgāthāya kittakāni padānī”ti pucchitabbattā “imānī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha pucchitānīti pucchitatthāni padāni cattāri honti. “Kittakā pañhā”ti pucchitabbattā “te tayo pañhā”ti vuttaṃ.

Since it should be asked, “How many words are in this verse of questioning?” “These…” and so on is stated. Here, the words that are questioned, that is, the words whose meaning is questioned, are four. Since it should be asked, “How many questions are there?” “Those are three questions” is stated.

Bhagavā devatāya hi yasmā vissajjeti, iti tasmā vissajjanato “tayopañhā”ti viññāyati. “Katamā vissajjanagāthā”ti pucchitabbattā –

Since the Blessed One indeed responds to the deity, therefore, from the response, it is understood as “three questions.” Since it should be asked, “Which is the response verse?”—

“Maccunābbhāhato [V 0.0255] loko, jarāya parivārito;

Taṇhāsallena otiṇṇo, icchādhūpāyito sadā”ti. –

“The world is struck by death, surrounded by old age, pierced by the dart of craving, always smoked by desire.”

Vuttaṃ. Tassaṃ vissajjanagāthāyaṃ – coraghātakena manussena coro abbhāhato viya maccunā sattaloko sadā abbhāhato, māluvalatāya attano nissitarukkho parivārito ajjhotthaṭo viya jarāya sattaloko sadā parivārito ajjhotthaṭo, visappītakhurappena sallena otiṇṇo anupaviṭṭho viya taṇhāsallena sattaloko sadā otiṇṇo anupaviṭṭho, icchāya sattaloko sadā dhūpāyito santāpitoti yojanā.

It is said. In that response verse—just as a thief is struck down by an executioner, so too is the world of beings always struck down by death; just as the tree on which it depends is surrounded and overwhelmed by a māluvā creeper, so too is the world of beings always surrounded and overwhelmed by old age; just as one is pierced and penetrated by an arrow with a poisoned barb, so too is the world of beings always pierced and penetrated by the arrow of craving; the world of beings is always smoked and tormented by desire—this is the explanation.

20. “Katamaṃ maccu, katamā jarā”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha jarā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha tatthāti tissaṃ vissajjanagāthāyaṃ. Dutiyapade vuttā jarā ca paṭhamapade [M 0.0121] vuttaṃ maraṇañca imāni dve saṅkhatassa khandhapañcakassa saṅkhatalakkhaṇāni honti, saṅkhataṃ khandhapañcakaṃ muñcitvā visuṃ na upalabbhatīti attho. “Saṅkhatalakkhaṇānaṃ jarāmaraṇānaṃ kathaṃ bhedo jānitabbo”ti vattabbattā “jarāyaṃ ṭhitassā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha jarāyaṃ ṭhitassa aññathattanti ṭhitassa khandhappabandhassa yaṃ aññathattaṃ, ayaṃ pākaṭajarā nāma, na khaṇaṭṭhitijarā. Maraṇaṃ vayoti sammutimaraṇaṃ cutiyeva hoti, na khaṇikamaraṇaṃ, na samucchedamaraṇaṃ. Tena vuttaṃ “uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyatī”ti (saṃ. ni. 3.38; a. ni. 3.47; kathā. 214).

20. Since it should be asked, “What is death, what is aging?” “therein aging” and so on was said. Therein, `tattha` refers to that response verse. Aging, mentioned in the second line, and death, mentioned in the first line—these two are conditioned characteristics of the conditioned five aggregates, meaning that they are not found separately from the conditioned five aggregates. Since it should be said, “How is the distinction between the conditioned characteristics of aging and death to be understood?” “for one established in aging” and so on was said. Therein, “alteration for one established in aging” means the alteration of the established continuum of aggregates—this is called manifest aging, not the momentary aging of persistence. “Death is dissolution” means conventional death, which is simply decease, not momentary death, nor the death of annihilation. Therefore, it is said: “Arising is evident, dissolution is evident, alteration of what is established is evident.”

Yadi ṭhitasseva maraṇaṃ siyā, evaṃ sati jarāmaraṇānaṃ nānattaṃ yuttaṃ na siyā, ayutte sati “te tayo pañhā”ti vacanampi ayuttamevāti vattabbato “tattha jarāya cā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha tatthāti tissaṃ vissajjanagāthāyaṃ vuttāya jarāya ca vuttassa maraṇassa ca atthato nānattaṃ yuttaṃ.

If death were to occur only for one who is established in aging, then the distinction between aging and death would not be fitting. If that were unfitting, it would have to be said that the statement “those are three questions” would also be unfitting. Therefore, “therein, of aging…” and so forth is stated. Therein, the distinction in meaning between the aging and death spoken of in that response verse is fitting.

“Kena kāraṇena yuttaṃ, kathaṃ kāraṇena nānattaṃ sampaṭicchitabba”nti vattabbattā “gabbhagatāpi hi mīyantī”ti vuttaṃ. Jaraṃ appattā gabbhagatāpi sattā hi yasmā mīyanti, tasmā nānattaṃ sampaṭicchitabbaṃ. “Gabbhagatāpi jarappattā bhaveyyu”nti vattabbattā “na ca te jiṇṇā bhavantī”ti vuttaṃ. Jarappattāpi ajiṇṇattā jiṇṇajaraṃ appattāva mīyanti, evaṃ idhādhippetassa jiṇṇajarāvirahitassa maraṇassa sambhavato aññā jarā, aññaṃ maraṇanti ñātabbanti vuttaṃ hoti. “Na gabbhagatānaṃyeva jiṇṇajaraṃ appattaṃ maraṇaṃ atthi, aññesampi atthī”ti vattabbabhāvato [V 0.0256] “atthi ca devānaṃ maraṇa”nti vuttaṃ. “Devāpi cirakālasambhavato jaraṃ pattā bhaveyyu”nti vattabbattā “na ca tesaṃ sarīrāni jīrantī”ti vuttaṃ. “Jarāmaraṇānaṃ nānatte kāraṇaṃ ettakamevā”ti vattabbattā aññampi atthīti dassetuṃ “sakkate vā”tiādi vuttaṃ.
