There, among those sixteen designated modes of teaching, etc., which special mode of exposition is called the method of designations, the analysis of the method of designations? This is what is asked. Now, the detailed special mode of exposition beginning with 'the teaching by way of conventional language,' which I am about to state regarding the exposition 'The Blessed One teaches one Dhamma with various designations,' etc., should be understood as the method of designations, what is called the analysis of the method of designations.

“Yāhi [M 0.0188] vividhāhi paññattīhi ekaṃ dhammaṃ bhagavā deseti, katamā tā vividhā paññattiyo”ti pucchitabbattā “yā pakatikathāyā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha pakatikathāyāti assādādipadatthavisesaṃ aniddhāretvā atthasabhāvena pavattāya kathāya sādhukaṃ manasikāradhammakathāya yā desanā yathādhippetamatthaṃ veneyyasantāne nikkhipati patiṭṭhapeti pakārena ñāpeti, tasmā nikkhepapaññatti, tāya paññattiyā dhammaṃ desetīti attho. “Yā paññatti ‘pakatikathāya [V 0.0315] desanā’ti vuttā, katamā sā”ti pucchitabbattā tathā pucchitvā vitthārato dassetuṃ “kā ca pakatikathāya desanā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana –“iti ‘pakatikathāya desanā’ti saṅkhepena vuttamatthaṃ vitthārena vibhajituṃ ‘kā ca pakatikathāya desanā’ti pucchitvā ‘cattāri saccānī’tiādimāhā”ti (netti. aṭṭha. 39) vuttaṃ. Tattha desanādesetabbassa bhedabhāvepi abhedopacārena “desanā cattāri saccānī”ti vuttaṃ, catunnaṃ saccānaṃ paññatti desanā nāmāti attho.

Since it should be asked, 'By which various designations does the Blessed One teach the one Dhamma, and what are those various designations?', it is therefore said, 'by way of conventional discourse,' and so on. Herein, 'by way of conventional discourse' means the teaching that, without determining the specific meanings of terms such as 'gratification,' places, establishes, and makes known in a special way the intended meaning in the mental continuum of those to be trained, through a well-considered discourse on the Dhamma that proceeds by way of its essential nature. Hence, it is called the designation of placement. By that designation, he teaches the Dhamma—this is the meaning. Since it should be asked, 'What is the designation called “teaching by way of conventional discourse”?', having asked thus, to explain in detail, it is said, 'And what is the teaching by way of conventional discourse?' and so on. In the commentary, however, it is said: 'Thus, to analyze in detail the meaning stated concisely as “teaching by way of conventional discourse,” the question “And what is the teaching by way of conventional discourse?” is asked, and then “The Four Truths,” etc., is stated' (Netti. Aṭṭha. 39). Herein, though there is a distinction between the teaching and what is to be taught, they are spoken of as the same by way of a figurative identification: 'The teaching is the Four Truths'—this is said. The meaning is that the designation of the four truths is called the teaching.

“Kathaṃ taṃ saccapaññattiṃ bhagavā āhā”ti pucchitabbattā “yathā bhagavā āhā”ti vuttaṃ. Yathā yena pakārena bhagavā yaṃ yaṃ paññattiṃ āha, tathā tena pakārena sā paññatti jānitabbā. “Idaṃ dukkha”nti yaṃ paññattiṃ bhagavā āha, ayaṃ “idaṃ dukkha”nti paññatti pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ nikkhepapaññatti, channaṃ dhātūnaṃ nikkhepapaññatti, aṭṭhārasannaṃ dhātūnaṃ nikkhepapaññatti, dvādasannaṃ āyatanānaṃ nikkhepapaññatti, dasannaṃ indriyānaṃ nikkhepapaññattīti yojanā kātabbā. Khandhadhātuāyatanindriyāni ca lokiyāneva. Pīḷanasaṅkhatasantāpavipariṇāmatthatāsāmaññena ekattaṃ upanetvā “idaṃ dukkha”nti vuttā. Dasannaṃ indriyānanti cakkhusotaghānajivhākāyaitthipurisajīvitamanavedanindriyānaṃ dasannaṃ. Anubhavanalakkhaṇena ekalakkhaṇattā vedanindriyaṃ ekanti gahitaṃ, saddhindriyādīni pana maggapariyāpannattā na gahitāni.

Since it should be asked, 'How did the Blessed One state that designation of truth?', it is said, 'As the Blessed One stated.' In whatever way the Blessed One stated any designation, in that very way that designation should be understood. The designation 'This is suffering' that the Blessed One stated—this designation 'This is suffering' is a designation of the exposition of the five aggregates, a designation of the exposition of the six elements, a designation of the exposition of the eighteen elements, a designation of the exposition of the twelve sense bases, and a designation of the exposition of the ten faculties. This is how the connection should be made. And the aggregates, elements, sense bases, and faculties are only worldly. Having brought them together into a unity due to their common characteristic of being oppressive, conditioned, tormenting, and subject to change, it is said, 'This is suffering.' As for the ten faculties, they are the faculties of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, femininity, masculinity, life, mind, and feeling. Because of having the single characteristic of experiencing, the feeling faculty is taken as one; however, the faculties of faith and so forth, being included in the path, are not taken.

Kabaḷīkāreti ṭhānūpacārena voharite ojāsaṅkhāte āhāre, rāgo ariyamaggena appahātabbattā anusayavasena, āsāvasena vā patthanāvasena vā atthi nandī. Atthi taṇhāti etthāpi eseva nayo. Patiṭṭhitaṃ viruḷhanti paṭisandhiākaḍḍhanasamatthatāpattiyā patiṭṭhitattā patiṭṭhitañceva viruḷhañcāti gahetabbaṃ. Saṅkhārānanti punabbhavanibbattakassa bhavassa abhinibbattihetukānaṃ [M 0.0189] saṅkhārānaṃ. Jātijarāmaraṇanti abhinibbattanalakkhaṇā jāti, na uppādova, paripākalakkhaṇā jarā, na ṭhitiyeva, bhedanalakkhaṇaṃ maraṇaṃ, na bhaṅgameva. Tena vuttaṃ “sasokaṃ sadaraṃ saupāyāsa”nti.

Regarding morsel food: in the nutriment called 'nutritive essence,' which is spoken of by way of a figurative use of its basis, there is delight, which is lust. Because it has not been abandoned by the noble path, it exists by way of latent tendency, or by way of influx, or by way of aspiration. 'There is craving'—here too, the same method applies. 'Established, they grow'—this should be understood as 'both established and grown' because, being established, it has attained the capacity to attract rebirth-linking. 'Regarding formations': of the formations that are the causes for the production of becoming, which generates renewed existence. 'Birth, aging, and death': birth has the characteristic of origination, not merely arising; aging has the characteristic of maturation, not merely persisting; death has the characteristic of disintegration, not merely dissolution. Therefore, it is said: 'with sorrow, with distress, with despair.'

“Phasse ce, bhikkhave, āhāre…pe… manosañcetanāya ce, bhikkhave, āhāre…pe… viññāṇe ce, bhikkhave, āhāre atthi rāgo…pe… vadāmī”ti ayaṃ paññatti dukkhassa ca samudayassa ca pabhavassa paññāpanato pabhavapaññatti nāma.

'Monks, if there is lust for the nutriment of contact... if, monks, for the nutriment of mental volition... if, monks, for the nutriment of consciousness there is lust... I say...'—this designation is called the designation of origin, because it makes known the source of suffering and of its origin.

Vaṭṭavasena paññattibhedo ācariyena vibhatto, amhehi ca ñāto, “kathaṃ vivaṭṭavasena paññattibhedo [V 0.0316] vibhatto”ti vattabbattā “kabaḷīkāre ce, bhikkhave, āhāre natthi rāgo”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Kabaḷīkāre…pe… anupāyāsanti vadāmī”ti ayaṃ paññatti dukkhassa pariññāya ca paññāpanato pariññāpaññatti nāma, samudayassa pahānassa ca paññāpanato pahānapaññatti nāma, maggassa bhāvanāya ca paññāpanato bhāvanāpaññatti nāma, nirodhassa sacchikiriyāya ca paññāpanato sacchikiriyāpaññatti nāma.

The classification of designations by way of the round of existence has been analyzed by the teacher and is known to us. Since it should be stated, 'How is the classification of designations by way of the cessation of the round analyzed?', it is said, 'Monks, if there is no lust for nutriment in the form of a morsel of food...' and so on. 'Nutriment in the form of a morsel of food... I say, without despair'—this designation is called the designation of full understanding because it makes known the full understanding of suffering; it is called the designation of abandonment because it makes known the abandonment of the origin; it is called the designation of development because it makes known the development of the path; and it is called the designation of realization because it makes known the realization of cessation.

40. Vivaṭṭavasena paññattibhedo ācariyena vibhatto, amhehi ca ñāto, “kathaṃ sammasanavasena paññattibhedo vibhatto”ti vattabbattā “samādhiṃ, bhikkhave, bhāvethā”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Samādhiṃ, bhikkhave, bhāvetha…pe… yathābhūtaṃ pajānātī”ti ayaṃ paññatti maggassa bhāvanāya ca paññāpanato bhāvanāpaññatti nāma, dukkhassa pariññāya ca paññāpanato pariññāpaññatti nāma, samudayassa pahānassa ca paññāpanato pahānapaññatti nāma, nirodhassa sacchikiriyāya ca paññāpanato sacchikiriyāpaññatti nāma.

40. The classification of designations by way of the cessation of the round of existence has been analyzed by the teacher and is known to us. Since it should be stated, 'How is the classification of designations by way of thorough investigation analyzed?', it is said, 'Develop concentration, monks...' and so on. 'Develop concentration, monks... one understands as it really is'—this designation is called the designation of development because it makes known the development of the path; it is called the designation of full understanding because it makes known the full understanding of suffering; it is called the designation of abandonment because it makes known the abandonment of the origin; and it is called the designation of realization because it makes known the realization of cessation.

Sammasanavasena paññattibhedo ācariyena vibhatto, amhehi ca ñāto, “kathaṃ upādānakkhandhavasena paññattibhedo vibhatto”ti vattabbattā “rūpaṃ, rādha, vikirathā”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Rūpaṃ, rādha, vikiratha…pe… nibbāna”nti ayaṃ paññatti taṇhāsaṅkhātassa rodhassa nirodhassa ca paññāpanato nirodhapaññatti nāma, assādassa nibbidāya ca paññāpanato nibbidāpaññatti nāma, dukkhassa pariññāya ca paññāpanato pariññāpaññatti nāma, samudayassa pahānassa ca paññāpanato pahānapaññatti nāma, maggassa bhāvanāya ca paññāpanato bhāvanāpaññatti nāma, nirodhassa sacchikiriyāya ca paññāpanato sacchikiriyāpaññatti nāma.

The classification of designations by way of thorough investigation has been analyzed by the teacher and is known to us. Since it should be stated, 'How is the classification of designations by way of the aggregates of clinging analyzed?', it is said, 'Rādha, scatter form...' and so on. 'Rādha, scatter form... Nibbāna'—this designation is called the designation of cessation because it makes known the cessation of the obstruction called craving; it is called the designation of disenchantment because it makes known disenchantment with gratification; it is called the designation of full understanding because it makes known the full understanding of suffering; it is called the designation of abandonment because it makes known the abandonment of the origin; it is called the designation of development because it makes known the development of the path; and it is called the designation of realization because it makes known the realization of cessation.

“Rūpavedanāsaññāsaṅkhāraviññāṇāni [M 0.0190] vikiranto viddhaṃsento vikīḷaniyaṃ karonto paññāya taṇhākkhayāya paṭipajjanto kiṃ pajānātī”ti pucchitabbattā “so ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānātī”tiādi vuttaṃ. “So ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānātīti…pe… nirodhagāminipaṭipadāti yathābhūtaṃ pajānātī”ti ayaṃ paññatti saccānaṃ paṭivedhassa paññāpanato paṭivedhapaññatti nāma, dassanabhūmiyā nikkhepassa ca paññāpanato nikkhepapaññatti nāma, maggassa bhāvanāya ca paññāpanato bhāvanāpaññatti nāma, sotāpattiphalassa sacchikiriyāya ca paññāpanato sacchikiriyāpaññatti nāma. “So ‘ime āsavā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti…pe… ‘āsavā asesaṃ nirujjhantī’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānātī”ti ayaṃ paññatti khayeñāṇassa uppādassa ca paññāpanato uppādapaññatti nāma, anuppādeñāṇassa okāsassa ca [V 0.0317] paññāpanato okāsapaññatti nāma, maggassa bhāvanāya ca paññāpanato bhāvanāpaññatti nāma, dukkhassa pariññāya ca paññāpanato pariññāpaññatti nāma, samudayassa pahānassa ca paññāpanato pahānapaññatti nāma, vīriyindriyassa ārambhassa ca paññāpanato ārambhapaññatti nāma, āsāṭikānaṃ āhaṭanāya ca paññāpanato āhaṭanāpaññatti nāma, bhāvanābhūmiyā nikkhepassa ca paññāpanato nikkhepapaññatti nāma, pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ abhinighātassa ca paññāpanato abhinighātapaññatti nāma.

Because it should be asked, 'One who scatters, demolishes, and treats as a plaything form, feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness, and who practices for the destruction of craving through wisdom—what does he understand?', it is said: 'He understands “this is suffering” as it actually is,' and so on. 'He understands “this is suffering” as it actually is... he understands “this is the path leading to the cessation of suffering” as it actually is.' This designation is called the designation of penetration because it makes known the penetration of the truths; it is called the designation of exposition because it makes known the exposition in the stage of vision; it is called the designation of development because it makes known the development of the path; and it is called the designation of realization because it makes known the realization of the fruit of stream-entry. 'He understands “these are the taints” as it actually is... he understands “the taints cease without remainder” as it actually is.' This designation is called the designation of arising because it makes known the arising of the knowledge of destruction; it is called the designation of opportunity because it makes known the opportunity for the knowledge of non-arising; it is called the designation of development because it makes known the development of the path; it is called the designation of full understanding because it makes known the full understanding of suffering; it is called the designation of abandonment because it makes known the abandonment of the origin; it is called the designation of exertion because it makes known the exertion of the faculty of energy; it is called the designation of striking because it makes known the striking of the unassailable; it is called the designation of exposition because it makes known the exposition in the stage of development; and it is called the designation of suppression because it makes known the suppression of evil, unwholesome states.

41. Vaṭṭavasena vā vivaṭṭavasena vā dhammasammasanavasena vā upādānakkhandhavasena vā pajānanavasena vā saccesu nānāvidho paññattibhedo ācariyena vibhatto, amhehi ca ñāto, “kathaṃ teparivaṭṭavasena saccesu paññattibhedo vibhatto”ti vattabbattā teparivaṭṭavasena saccesu paññattibhedaṃ dassetuṃ “idaṃ dukkhanti me, bhikkhave”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana – “evaṃ vaṭṭavivaṭṭamukhena sammasanaupādānakkhandhamukheneva saccesu paññattivibhāgaṃ dassetvā idāni teparivaṭṭavasena dassetuṃ ‘idaṃ dukkhanti me bhikkhave’tiādi āraddha”nti (netti. aṭṭha. 41) vuttaṃ. Tattha pubbe parijānanato paṭṭhāya. Ananussutesūti parijānanavasena ananussutesu catūsu saccadhammesu. Cakkhunti paṭhamaṃ nibbānadassanaṭṭhena cakkhu nāma. Yathāsabhāvato kiccaparijānanaṭṭhena sacchikiriyaparijānanaṭṭhena ñāṇaṃ nāma. Yathāsabhāvato [M 0.0191] kiccaparijānanādīnaṃ paṭivijjhitvā pajānanaṭṭhena paññā nāma. Tathā viditakaraṇaṭṭhena vijjā nāma. Ālokobhāsakaraṇaṭṭhena āloko nāma. Idaṃ cakkhādikaṃ sabbaṃ paññāvevacanameva. “Idaṃ dukkhanti me bhikkhave…pe… udapādī”ti ayaṃ paññatti saccānaṃ desanāya paññāpanato desanāpaññatti nāma, sutamayiyā paññāya nikkhepassa ca paññāpanato nikkhepapaññatti nāma, anaññātaññassāmītindriyassa sacchikiriyāya ca paññāpanato sacchikiriyāpaññatti nāma, dhammacakkassa pavattanāya ca paññāpanato pavattanāpaññatti nāma.

41. Whether by way of the round of rebirth, or by way of the cessation of the round, or by way of comprehension of the Dhamma, or by way of the clinging-aggregates, or by way of full understanding—the various classifications of designations regarding the truths have been expounded by the Teacher and are known to us. Therefore, because it is to be stated, 'How are the classifications of designations regarding the truths expounded by way of the threefold round?', the passage beginning with 'This is suffering, monks' has been commenced to show the classifications of designations regarding the truths by way of the threefold round. In the commentary, it is stated: 'Having thus shown the divisions of designations regarding the truths through the approach of the round and its cessation, as well as through the approach of comprehension and the clinging-aggregates, now, to show them by way of the threefold round, the passage beginning with “This is suffering, monks” has been commenced' (Netti. Aṭṭha. 41). Here, this begins from prior full understanding. 'Unheard before' refers to the four truths unheard before by way of full understanding. 'Eye' is so called in the sense of first seeing Nibbāna. 'Knowledge' is so called in the sense of fully understanding its function according to its own nature and in the sense of fully understanding its realization. 'Wisdom' is so called in the sense of understanding by having penetrated their nature, function, and so on. 'True knowledge' is so called in the sense of making things known. 'Light' is so called in the sense of illuminating. All these—eye, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light—are synonyms for wisdom. The designation beginning with 'This is suffering, monks... arose' is called the designation of teaching because it makes known the teaching of the truths; it is called the designation of exposition because it makes known the exposition of wisdom born of learning; it is called the designation of realization because it makes known the realization of the faculty of 'I shall know what has not been known'; and it is called the designation of turning because it makes known the turning of the Wheel of Dhamma.

“Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhaṃ pariññeyyaṃ…pe… udapādī”ti ayaṃ paññatti maggassa bhāvanāya paññāpanato bhāvanāpaññatti nāma, cintāmayiyā paññāya nikkhepassa ca paññāpanato nikkhepapaññatti nāma, aññindriyassa sacchikiriyāya ca paññāpanato sacchikiriyāpaññatti nāma.

"This suffering, however, should be fully understood… it arose." This designation is called the designation of development because it makes known the development of the path; it is called the designation of exposition because it makes known the exposition of wisdom born of thought; and it is called the designation of realization because it makes known the realization of the faculty of final knowledge.

“Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhaṃ pariññātaṃ…pe… udapādī”ti ayaṃ paññatti maggassa bhāvanāya paññāpanato bhāvanāpaññatti nāma, bhāvanāmayiyā paññāya nikkhepassa ca paññāpanato [V 0.0318] nikkhepapaññatti nāma, aññātāvino indriyassa sacchikiriyāya ca paññāpanato sacchikiriyāpaññatti nāma, dhammacakkassa pavattanāya ca paññāpanato pavattanāpaññatti nāma.

"This suffering has been fully understood… it arose." This designation is called the designation of development because it makes known the development of the path; it is called the designation of exposition because it makes known the exposition of wisdom born of development; it is called the designation of realization because it makes known the realization of the faculty of one who has known; and it is called the designation of turning because it makes known the turning of the Wheel of Dhamma.

Teparivaṭṭavasena saccesu nānāvidho paññattibhedo ācariyena vibhatto, amhehi ca ñāto, “kathaṃ kusalākusalādivasena desitadhammassa paññattibhedo vibhatto”ti vattabbattā “tulamatulañca sambhava”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Atha vā dhammacakkasutte paññattibhedo ācariyena vibhatto, amhehi ca ñāto, “tulamatulañcātiādigāthāya kathaṃ paññattibhedo vibhatto”ti vattabbattā “tulamatulañcā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tulīyati paricchijjīyatīti tulaṃ, kāmāvacarakammaṃ, natthi tulaṃ sadisaṃ aññaṃ lokiyakammaṃ assa mahaggatakammassāti atulaṃ, rūpārūpāvacarakammaṃ. Punabbhavaṃ sambhavati etena saṅkhārenāti sambhavo, taṃ sambhavaṃ. Punabbhavaṃ saṅkharotīti bhavasaṅkhāro. Ajjhatte vipassanāvasena ramatīti ajjhattarato. Samathavasena samādhiyatīti samāhito. Attani sambhavatīti attasambhavo, taṃ attasambhavaṃ. Muni sambuddho sambhavaṃ bhavasaṅkhāraṃ tulañca atulañca avassaji, ajjhattarato samāhito kavacaṃ abhindi iva, evaṃ attasambhavaṃ abhindi padālayīti yojanā kātabbā. Atha vā muni sambuddho “pañcakkhandhā aniccā [M 0.0192] dukkhā anattā vipariṇāmadhammā, nibbānaṃ pana niccaṃ sukhaṃ asaṅkhataṃ avipariṇāmadhamma”nti tulaṃ tulayanto atulaṃ nibbānaṃ disvā sambhavaṃ bhavasaṅkhāraṃ ariyamaggena avassaji. Kathaṃ avassaji? So hi muni vipassanāvasena ajjhattarato ca hutvā, samathavasena upacārappanāsu samāhito ca hutvā kavacaṃ abhindi iva, evaṃ attasambhavaṃ attani sañjātaṃ kilesaṃ abhindi padālayi, kilesābhāvena kammañca jahīti gāthāttho gahetabbo.

The various classifications of designations regarding the truths by way of the threefold round have been expounded by the Teacher and are known to us. Because it should be stated, 'How is the classification of designations of the taught Dhamma expounded by way of the wholesome, unwholesome, and so on?', it is said: 'the measured, the immeasurable, and the arising,' and so on. Alternatively, the classification of designations has been expounded by the Teacher in the Dhammacakkasutta and is known to us. Because it should be stated, 'How is the classification of designations expounded in the verse beginning with “the measured and the immeasurable”?', it is said: 'the measured and the immeasurable,' and so on. That which is weighed or demarcated is 'the measured'; this is sense-sphere kamma. 'There is no other worldly kamma equal or similar to this sublime kamma'; this is 'the immeasurable', which is form-sphere and formless-sphere kamma. 'Rebirth arises by means of this formation'; this is 'arising' (sambhava). 'It constructs rebirth'; this is the formation of existence (bhavasaṅkhāro). 'One delights internally by way of insight'; this is 'one who delights inwardly' (ajjhattarato). 'One is composed by way of serenity'; this is 'composed' (samāhito). 'It arises in oneself'; this is 'self-arising' (attasambhavo), that self-arising. The sage, the Fully Awakened One, abandoned the arising, the formation of existence, both the measured and the immeasurable. Delighting inwardly and composed, he shattered self-arising just as one might shatter armor—this is how the connection should be made. Alternatively, the sage, the Fully Awakened One, while weighing 'the measured'—that is, 'the five aggregates are impermanent, suffering, non-self, and subject to change, whereas Nibbāna is permanent, blissful, unconditioned, and not subject to change'—and seeing the immeasurable Nibbāna, abandoned the arising, the formation of existence, by means of the noble path. How did he abandon it? That sage, being one who delights inwardly by way of insight and composed by way of serenity in access and absorption, shattered self-arising—the defilement arisen in himself—just as one might shatter armor. Through the absence of defilements, he also abandoned kamma—this is how the meaning of the verse should be understood.

“Tulamatulañca sambhava”nti paññatti sabbadhammānaṃ abhiññāya paññāpanato abhiññāpaññatti nāma, dhammapaṭisambhidāya nikkhepassa ca paññāpanato nikkhepapaññatti nāma, “bhavasaṅkhāramavassaji munī”ti paññatti samudayassa pariccāgassa ca paññāpanato pariccāgapaññatti nāma, dukkhassa pariññāya ca paññāpanato pariññāpaññatti nāma, “ajjhattarato samāhito”ti paññatti kāyagatāya satiyā bhāvanāya ca paññāpanato bhāvanāpaññatti nāma, cittekaggatāya ṭhitiyā ca paññāpanato ṭhitipaññatti nāma, “abhindi kavacamivattasambhava”nti paññatti cittassa abhinibbidāya ca paññāpanato abhinibbidāpaññatti nāma, sabbaññutāya upādānassa ca paññāpanato upādānapaññatti nāma, avijjāṇḍakosānaṃ padālanāya ca paññāpanato padālapaññatti nāma, “yathāvutto paññattippabhedo kena saddahitabbo”ti vattabbattā “tenāhā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tathāvuttassa paññattippabhedassa [V 0.0319] sambhavato bhagavā yaṃ “tulamatula”ntiādigāthamāha, tathāsambhavato yathāvuttāya gāthāya yathāvutto paññattippabhedo saddahitabboti.

"The measured, the immeasurable, and the arising" is a designation for the direct knowledge of all phenomena, hence called the designation of direct knowledge; and for the exposition of the analytical knowledge of the Dhamma, hence called the designation of exposition. "The sage abandoned the formation of existence" is a designation for the abandonment of the origin, hence called the designation of abandonment; and for the full understanding of suffering, hence called the designation of full understanding. "Delighting inwardly, composed" is a designation for the development of mindfulness of the body, hence called the designation of development; and for the stability of one-pointedness of mind, hence called the designation of stability. "He shattered the armor, as it were, of self-arising" is a designation for disenchantment with the mind, hence called the designation of disenchantment; for omniscience and for clinging, hence called the designation of clinging; and for the breaking open of the egg-shell of ignorance, hence called the designation of breaking open. Because it should be asked, "By what means should the classification of designations as stated be believed?", the words "Therefore he said..." and so on were spoken. Since the Blessed One spoke the verse beginning with "the measured and the immeasurable," from which the aforesaid classification of designations arises, therefore, because it arises thus from the aforesaid verse, the aforesaid classification of designations should be believed.

“Tulamatulañcā”tiādigāthāyaṃ paññattippabhedo ācariyena vibhatto, amhehi ca ñāto.

The classification of designations in the verse beginning with "The measured and the immeasurable" has been analyzed by the Teacher, and is known to us.

‘Yo dukkhamaddakkhi yatonidānaṃ, kāmesu so jantu kathaṃ nameyya;

Kāmā hi loke saṅgoti ñatvā, tesaṃ satīmā vinayāya sikkhe’ti. –

'He who has seen suffering and its origin, how could that being incline towards sensual pleasures? Having known that sensual pleasures are an attachment in the world, the mindful one should train for their removal.'

Gāthāyaṃ pana kathaṃ paññattibhedo vibhatto”ti vattabbattā “yo dukkhamaddakkhī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yo āraddhavipassako jantu yatonidānaṃ sabbaṃ tebhūmakaṃ [M 0.0193] hetuphalaṃ dukkhaṃ addakkhi, so āraddhavipassako jantu kāmesu kathaṃ nameyya nametuṃ nārahati. Kāmā loke “saṅgo”ti hi yasmā passitabbā, tasmā nametuṃ nārahati, iti etaṃ dukkhabhāvaṃ dukkhahetubhāvaṃ ñatvā tesaṃ kāmānaṃ vinayāya vūpasamāya satimā kāyagatāsatisampanno tīṇi sikkhāni sikkhe sikkheyyāti gāthāttho saṅkhepena viññātabbo. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (netti. aṭṭha. 41) pana vitthārena saṃvaṇṇito.

Because it should be asked, 'But how is the classification of designations analyzed in this verse?', the words 'One who saw suffering...' and so on were spoken. The being who has commenced insight, who has seen all suffering—which is the cause and effect in the three realms—and its origin, how could that being who has commenced insight incline towards sensual pleasures? He is not fit to incline towards them. For sensual pleasures in the world should be seen as an 'attachment'; therefore, he is not fit to incline towards them. Knowing this state of suffering and its cause, for the sake of the removal and pacification of those sensual pleasures, the mindful one, endowed with mindfulness directed to the body, should train in the three trainings—this is the meaning of the verse to be understood briefly. In the commentary (Netti. Aṭṭha. 41), however, it is explained in detail.

“Yo dukkha”nti paññatti dukkhassa vevacanassa ca pariññāya ca paññāpanato vevacanapaññatti, pariññāpaññatti ca hoti. “Yatonidāna”nti paññatti samudayassa pabhavassa ca pahānassa ca paññāpanato pabhavapaññatti ceva pahānapaññatti ca hoti. “Addakkhī”ti paññatti ñāṇacakkhussa vevacanassa ca paṭivedhassa ca paññāpanato vevacanapaññatti ceva paṭivedhapaññatti ca hoti. “Kāmesu so jantu kathaṃ nameyyā”ti paññatti kāmataṇhāya vevacanassa ca anabhinivisassa ca paññāpanato vevacanapaññatti ceva anabhinivesapaññatti ca hoti. “Kāmā hi loke saṅgoti ñatvā”ti paññatti kāmānaṃ paccatthikato dassanassa ca paññāpanato dassanapaññatti nāma. Kāmā hi anatthajānanato paccatthikasadisā.

The designation 'One who... suffering' is a designation for a synonym of suffering and for its full understanding; hence it is a synonym-designation and a full understanding-designation. The designation 'from what source' is a designation for the origin and its source, and for abandonment; hence it is an origin-designation and an abandoning-designation. The designation 'saw' is a designation for a synonym of the eye of wisdom and for its penetration; hence it is a synonym-designation and a penetration-designation. The designation 'how should that being incline towards sensual pleasures?' is a designation for a synonym of craving for sensual pleasures and for non-adherence; hence it is a synonym-designation and a non-adherence-designation. The designation 'having known that sensual pleasures are an attachment in the world' is a designation for seeing sensual pleasures as adversaries; hence it is a seeing-designation. For sensual pleasures, by producing harm, are like adversaries.

“Kīdisā hutvā anatthajanakā”ti pucchitabbattā “kāmā hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Kāmā rāgaggiādīhi antodayhanato aṅgārakāsūpamā ca, pūtibhāvāpajjanato maṃsapesūpamā ca, bahi aññena dayhanato pāvakakappā jalitaggikkhandhūpamā ca, patiṭṭhānābhāvato papātūpamā ca, visasadisehi dosādīhi parahiṃsanato uragopamā ca. “Tesaṃ satīmā”ti paññatti pahānāya apacayassa ca paññāpanato apacayapaññatti nāma, kāyagatāya satiyā nikkhepassa ca paññāpanato [V 0.0320] nikkhepapaññatti nāma, maggassa bhāvanāya ca paññāpanato bhāvanāpaññatti nāma. “Vinayāya sikkhe”ti paññattirāgavinayassa dosavinayassa mohavinayassa paṭivedhassa ca paññāpanato paṭivedhapaññatti nāma. “Jantū”ti paññatti yogissa vevacanassa ca paññāpanato vevacanapaññatti nāma.

Since it should be asked, 'In what way are they producers of harm?', it is said, 'For sensual pleasures...' and so on. Sensual pleasures are like a pit of embers because they burn inwardly with the fire of lust and so on; like a piece of meat because they lead to putridity; like a blazing mass of fire because they are burnt from without by another; like a precipice because they lack a foundation; and like a snake because they harm others with venomous states such as hatred. The designation 'the mindful one, for them' is a designation for abandonment and for decline, hence called the designation of decline; for the establishment of mindfulness directed to the body, hence called the designation of establishment; and for the development of the path, hence called the designation of development. The designation 'should train for removal' is a designation for the penetration of the removal of lust, the removal of hatred, and the removal of delusion; hence it is called the designation of penetration. The designation 'a being' is a designation for a synonym of a yogi; hence it is called the designation of synonyms.

“Jantūti sāmaññasattavācako saddo kasmā yogivācakoti viññātabbo”ti vattabbattā “yadā hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yogī yadā yasmiṃ kāle [M 0.0194] kāmā saṅgoti pajānāti, tadā tasmiṃ kāle so yogī kāmānaṃ anuppādāya kusale dhamme kāyagatāsatiādīhi uppādayati, so kusale dhamme uppādento yogī anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya vāyamati kusalavīriyaṃ karoti, tasmā yogīvācako jantusaddoti viññātabbo. “Jantū”ti ayaṃ paññatti appattassa kusalassa jhānadhammādikassa pattiyā vāyāmassa ca paññāpanato vāyāmapaññatti nāma, oramattikāya asantuṭṭhiyā nikkhepassa ca paññāpanato nikkhepapaññatti nāma. “So anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya vāyamatī”ti ayaṃ paññatti vāyāmapaññatti, “hetuso uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā vāyamatīti paññatti katamā paññattī”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha so uppannāna”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha tasmiṃ “anuppannāna”ntiādimhi. “So uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā vāyamatī”ti ayaṃ paññatti bhāvanāya appamādassa ca paññāpanato appamādapaññatti nāma, vīriyindriyassa nikkhepassa ca paññāpanato nikkhepapaññatti nāma, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ārakkhassa ca paññāpanato ārakkhapaññatti nāma, adhicittasikkhāya ṭhitiyā ca paññāpanato ṭhitipaññatti nāma. “Kena yathāvuttappakāro paññattippabhedo saddahitabbo”ti vattabbattā “tenāhā”tiādi vuttaṃ.

Since it should be asked, 'The word 'jantu' is a common term for a being, so why should it be understood as a term for a yogi?', it was stated, 'When indeed...' and so on. When a yogi understands at a certain time that sensual pleasures are an attachment, at that time that yogi, for the non-arising of sensual pleasures, develops wholesome states with mindfulness of the body and so on. A yogi, developing these wholesome states, strives for the arising of unarisen wholesome states and exerts wholesome effort. Therefore, the word 'jantu' should be understood as a term for a yogi. This designation 'a being' is called the designation of striving because it signifies the striving for the attainment of wholesome qualities, such as jhāna, that have not been attained; it is also called the designation of relinquishment because it signifies the laying aside of dissatisfaction with what is inferior. 'He strives for the arising of unarisen wholesome states'—this is a designation of striving. Since it must be asked, 'What designation is meant by “he strives for the stability of arisen wholesome states”?', it was stated, 'There, regarding those arisen...' and so on. There, in the context of 'unarisen,' etc. 'He strives for the stability of arisen wholesome states'—this is a designation of heedfulness because it signifies heedfulness in development; it is also a designation of establishment because it signifies the establishing of the faculty of energy; it is a designation of guarding because it signifies the protection of wholesome states; and it is a designation of stability because it signifies stability in the training in the higher mind. Since it must be said, 'By what means should the aforementioned classification of designations be believed?', it was stated, 'Therefore he said...' and so on.

“Yo dukkhamaddakkhi yatonidāna”ntiādigāthāya paññattippabhedo ācariyena vibhatto, amhehi ca ñāto.

By the verse beginning, 'He who saw suffering and its origin,' the classification of designations has been analyzed by the Teacher and is understood by us.

“Mohasambandhano loko, bhabbarūpova dissati;

Upadhibandhano bālo, tamasā parivārito;

Assirī viya khāyati, passato natthi kiñcananti. –

The world is bound by delusion, appearing as if it were substantial; the fool is bound by attachments, enveloped in darkness. He appears as if without splendor; for one who sees, there is nothing there.

Gāthāyaṃ pana kathaṃ paññattippabhedo vibhatto”ti vattabbattā “mohasambandhano”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha mohasambandhanoti mohahetukehi saṃyojanehi sambandho. Lokoti appahīnasaṃyojano sattaloko. Bhabbarūpova [V 0.0321] dissatīti abhabbopi attā bhabbarūpova bhabbajātiko viya bālānaṃ avipassakānaṃ dissati. Upadhibandhanoti kilesūpadhīhi bandhitabbo. Yu-paccayo hi kammatthe vihito. Upadhīsu vā kilesānaṃ bandhanaṃ yassa bālassāti upadhibandhano. Dve avaḍḍhiyo lāti gaṇhātīti bālo. Tamasā sammohena parivārito paṭicchādito paṇḍitānaṃ vipassakānaṃ assirī viya sirīvirahito viya khāyati [M 0.0195] upaṭṭhāti. Passato paññācakkhunā passantassa paṇḍitassa kiñcanaṃ natthīti saṅkhepattho daṭṭhabbo.

In this verse, since it must be stated how the classification of designations is distinguished, it is said, 'bound by delusion,' and so on. Here, 'bound by delusion' means being bound by the fetters caused by delusion. 'The world' refers to the world of beings who have not abandoned the fetters. 'Appearing as if it were capable' means that even though incapable, a person appears to the foolish and those who lack insight as if he were of a capable nature. 'Bound by attachments' means to be bound by the attachments that are the defilements. The suffix '-ana' is indeed used here in the sense of the object. Or, he is 'bound by attachments' because for that fool the binding of the defilements is in the attachments. A 'fool' (bālo) is one who grasps the two kinds of decline. 'Enveloped in darkness' means shrouded by the darkness of delusion; he appears or presents himself to the wise and those with insight as if without splendor, devoid of glory. 'For one who sees... there is nothing'—for the wise person who sees with the eye of wisdom, there is no impediment—this is the brief meaning that should be understood.

“Mohasambandhano loko”ti paññatti mohasīsena gahitānaṃ vipallāsānaṃ desanāya paññāpanato desanāpaññatti nāma. “Bhabbarūpova dissatī”ti paññatti lokassa viparītassa viparītākārena upaṭṭhahantassa paññāpanato viparītapaññatti nāma. “Upadhibandhano bālo”ti paññatti pāpakānaṃ icchāvacarānaṃ pabhavassa paññāpanato pabhavapaññatti nāma. “Upadhibandhano bālo”ti paññatti pariyuṭṭhānānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ bandhanakiccassa paññāpanato kiccapaññatti nāma. “Upadhibandhano bālo”ti paññatti kilesānaṃ bandhanabalamūhanabalānaṃ paññāpanato balapaññatti nāma. “Upadhibandhano bālo”ti paññatti saṅkhārānaṃ viruhanāya paññāpanato viruhanāpaññatti nāma. “Tamasā parivārito”ti paññatti avijjandhakārassa desanāya paññāpanato desanāpaññatti nāma, avijjandhakārassa vevacanassa ca paññāpanato vevacanapaññatti nāma. “Assirī viya khāyatī”ti paññatti dibbacakkhussa dassanakiriyāya paññāpanato dassanapaññatti nāma. “Assirī viya khāyatī”ti paññatti paññācakkhussa nikkhepassa paññāpanato nikkhepapaññatti nāma. “Passato natthi kiñcana”nti paññatti sattānaṃ ariyānaṃ paṭivedhassa paññāpanato paṭivedhapaññatti nāma.

'The world is bound by delusion'—this is a designation of teaching because it designates the teaching about the distortions grasped with delusion at their head. 'Appearing as if it were capable'—this is a designation of inversion because it designates the inverted way the inverted world appears. 'The fool is bound by attachments'—this is a designation of origin because it designates the origin of evil things that arise from desire. 'The fool is bound by attachments'—this is a designation of function because it designates the binding function of obsessive unwholesome states. 'The fool is bound by attachments'—this is a designation of power because it designates the binding power and deluding power of the defilements. 'The fool is bound by attachments'—this is a designation of growth because it designates the growth of formations. 'Enveloped in darkness'—this is a designation of teaching because it designates the teaching about the darkness of ignorance; it is also a designation of synonyms because it designates a synonym for the darkness of ignorance. 'Appears as if without splendor'—this is a designation of vision because it designates the act of seeing with the divine eye. 'Appears as if without splendor'—this is a designation of establishment because it designates the establishment of the eye of wisdom. 'For one who sees, there is no impediment'—this is a designation of penetration because it designates the penetration attained by noble beings.

“Katamaṃ kiñcana”nti pucchitabbattā “rāgo kiñcana”ntiādi vuttaṃ. “Yathāvutto paññattippabhedo kathaṃ amhehi saddahitabbo”ti vattabbattā “tenāhā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yathāvuttassa paññattippabhedassa sambhavato bhagavā yaṃ “mohasambandhano”tiādimāha, tathāsambhavato tāya gāthāya yathāvutto paññattippabhedo gāthānusārena saddahitabbo.

Since it should be asked, 'What is an impediment?' it was said, 'Lust is an impediment,' and so on. Since it should be said, 'How are we to accept the aforementioned classification of designations?' it was said, 'Therefore he said...' and so on. Because the Blessed One spoke the verse beginning 'bound by delusion,' and because the aforementioned classification of designations is consistent with it, this classification should be accepted in accordance with the verse.

“Mohasambandhano loko”tiādigāthāya paññattippabhedo ācariyena vibhatto, amhehi ca ñāto, “atthi, bhikkhave, ajāta’ntiādipāṭhassa paññattippabhedo kathaṃ vibhatto”ti pucchitabbattā “atthi bhikkhave”tiādipāḷimāha. “Sā pana pāḷi kimatthaṃ bhagavatā vuttā”ti ce puccheyya? Paramatthato avijjamānattā nibbānaṃ natthi, tasmā “atthi nibbāna”nti [V 0.0322] vacanaṃ sasavisāṇavacanaṃ viya anatthaṃ, vohāramattametanti vadantānaṃ micchāvādaṃ bhañjituṃ bhagavatā vuttāti daṭṭhabbā.

The classification of designations in the verse beginning, 'The world is bound by delusion,' has been analyzed by the Teacher and is understood by us. But since it should be asked, 'How is the classification of designations analyzed for the passage beginning, “There is, O bhikkhus, an unborn”?' the text beginning 'There is, O bhikkhus' is cited. If one should ask, 'For what purpose was this text spoken by the Blessed One?' it should be understood that the Blessed One spoke it to refute the wrong view of those who say: 'Because in the ultimate sense it is non-existent, Nibbāna does not exist; therefore the statement “There is Nibbāna” is meaningless, like the statement “There is a hare’s horn”; it is merely a conventional expression.'

Kutocipi [M 0.0196] ajātattā abhūtattā ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ. Paccayehi akatattā akataṃ. Saṅkhatābhāvato asaṅkhataṃ nibbānaṃ atthi. Etaṃ ajātādikaṃ nibbānaṃ no ce abhavissa, evaṃ sati nissaraṇaṃ na paññāyetha, nibbānassa ca ariyamaggaphalānaṃ ārammaṇattā, maggaphalānañca kilesānaṃ samucchindanato paṭippassambhanato, samucchindanena ca tividhassa vaṭṭassa apavaṭṭanato ajātādikaṃ nibbānaṃ atthiyevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Because it is not born from anything and has not come to be, it is unborn and unbecome. Because it is not made by conditions, it is unmade. Because it is devoid of the conditioned, the unconditioned Nibbāna exists. If this Nibbāna—the unborn, etc.—did not exist, then an escape would not be discerned. And since Nibbāna is the object for the noble path and its fruition, and since the path and fruition uproot and pacify the defilements, and since through this uprooting they bring about the rolling back of the threefold round, it should be understood that Nibbāna—the unborn, etc.—truly exists.

“Atthi, bhikkhave, ajātaṃ…pe… asaṅkhata”nti ayaṃ paññatti nibbānassa desanāpaññatti ca nibbānassa vevacanapaññatti ca hoti. “Nayidha jātassa…pe… paññāyethā”ti ayaṃ paññatti saṅkhatassa vevacanapaññatti ca saṅkhatassa upanayanapaññatti ca hoti. “Yasmā ca…pe… asaṅkhata”nti ayaṃ paññatti nibbānassa vevacanapaññatti ca nibbānassa jotanāpaññatti ca hoti. “Yasmā jātassa…pe… paññāyatī”ti ayaṃ paññatti nibbānassa vevacanapaññatti ca maggassa saṃsārato niyyānikapaññatti ca nissaraṇapaññatti ca hotīti paññattiviseso paṇḍitehi niddhāretvā gahetabbo.

'There is, O bhikkhus, the unborn… the unconditioned.' This is a teaching designation of Nibbāna and a synonym designation of Nibbāna. 'Here for what is born... an escape would not be discerned.' This is a synonym designation of the conditioned and also an implicative designation of the conditioned. 'And since there is… the unconditioned.' This is a synonym designation of Nibbāna and also an illuminating designation of Nibbāna. 'Therefore for what is born… an escape is discerned.' This is a synonym designation of Nibbāna, a designation of the path as the way of release from saṃsāra, and a designation of escape. These distinctions in designation should be determined and understood by the wise.

“Yathāvutto nibbānassa paññattippabhedo kena saddahitabbo”ti vattabbattā “tenāha bhagavā”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Tenāha āyasmā”tiādyānusandhyādiattho ceva “niyutto paññattihāro”ti anusandhyādiattho ca vuttanayānusārena veditabbo.

Since it should be asked, 'By whom should the classification of designations for Nibbāna as described be accepted?' it is said, 'Therefore, the Blessed One said,' etc. And the meaning of the connection with 'Therefore, the Venerable said,' etc., and the meaning connected with 'The Method of Designations is concluded,' should be understood in accordance with the method stated above.

Iti paññattihāravibhaṅge sattibalānurūpā racitā

Thus, the Analysis of the Conveyance of Designations was composed in accordance with my ability and strength.

Vibhāvanā niṭṭhitā.

The Elucidation is concluded.

Paṇḍitehi pana aṭṭhakathāṭīkānusārena gambhīrattho vitthārato vibhajitvā gahetabboti.

However, the profound meaning should be analyzed in detail and grasped by the wise in accordance with the commentaries and subcommentaries.

12. Otaraṇahāravibhaṅgavibhāvanā

12. The Elucidation of the Analysis of the Conveyance of Descent

42. Yena [V 0.0323] yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūtena paññattihāravibhaṅgena paññattiyo vibhattā, so saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūto vibhaṅgo paripuṇṇo, “katamo otaraṇo hāravibhaṅgo”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha katamo otaraṇo hāro”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha tatthāti tesu niddiṭṭhesu soḷasasu desanāhārādīsu [M 0.0197] katamo saṃvaṇṇanāviseso otaraṇo hāro otaraṇahāravibhaṅgo nāmāti pucchati. “Yo ca paṭiccuppādo”tiādiniddesassa idāni mayā vuccamāno “uddhaṃ adho sabbadhi vippamutto”tiādiko vitthārasaṃvaṇṇanāviseso otaraṇo hāro otaraṇahāravibhaṅgo nāmāti gahetabbo.

42. The particular analysis by which designations were analyzed in the Analysis of the Conveyance of Designations, that particular analysis is now complete. Since the question, 'What is the Analysis of the Conveyance of Descent?' is to be asked, the passage beginning, 'Therein, what is the conveyance of descent?' was stated. Herein, 'therein' refers to those sixteen indicated conveyances of exposition, etc., and he asks: 'What particular exposition is the conveyance of descent, called the Analysis of the Conveyance of Descent?' The detailed particular exposition beginning 'upward, downward, everywhere released,' which is now being stated by me in reference to the indication beginning 'And what is dependent origination,' should be understood as the conveyance of descent, the Analysis of the Conveyance of Descent.

Tattha pāṭhe “katame paṭiccasamuppādādayo niddhāretvā katamehi niddhāritehi dhammehi otaratī”ti pucchitabbattā imasmiṃ pāṭhe ime paṭiccasamuppādādayo niddhāretvā imehi niddhāritehi dhammehi otaratīti dassetuṃ “uddhaṃ adho sabbadhi vippamutto”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha uddhanti kāmadhātuto uddhaṃ uparibhāge pavattāya rūpadhātuarūpadhātuyā. Adhoti rūpadhātuto heṭṭhābhāge pavattāya kāmadhātuyā. Sabbadhīti sabbasmiṃ kāmarūpaarūpadhātumhi. Vippamuttoti paṭisandhivasena appavattanato vippamutto asekkho. Ayaṃ sekkho dassanamaggena sakkāyadiṭṭhiyā samugghātattā “ahaṃ asmī”ti anānupassī viharati. Evaṃ sekkhāya vimuttiyā ceva asekkhāya vimuttiyā ca sekkho ceva asekkho ca atiṇṇapubbaṃ oghaṃ apunabbhavāya vimutto udatārīti gāthāttho gahetabbo.

Here, in the text, since the question should be asked, 'Having specified which things beginning with dependent origination, by which specified phenomena does one descend?', the passage beginning 'upward, downward, everywhere released' was stated in order to show that in this text, having specified these things beginning with dependent origination, one descends by these specified phenomena. Therein, 'upward' refers to the form realm and the formless realm, which occur in the upper region above the sensual realm. 'Downward' refers to the sensual realm, which occurs in the lower region below the form realm. 'Everywhere' means in the entire sensual, form, and formless realms. 'Released' means the non-learner, who is released from occurring again by way of rebirth-linking. This learner dwells not contemplating 'I am' because identity view has been eradicated by the path of vision. Thus, the meaning of the verse should be understood as: by means of the learner's liberation and the non-learner's liberation, both the learner and the non-learner, being liberated unto non-renewal of being, have crossed over the flood not crossed before.

Tasmiṃ gāthāpāṭhe “katame niddhāretvā katamehi otaratī”ti pucchitabbattā “uddhanti rūpadhātū”tiādi vuttaṃ. Uddhanti manussalokato uddhaṃ cātumahārājikādayopi gahitāti atthasambhavato taṃ nivattetuṃ “rūpadhātu arūpadhātū”ti vuttaṃ. Adhoti manussabhavato adho cattāro apāyabhūmiyo ca gahitāti atthasambhavato taṃ nivattetuṃ “kāmadhātū”ti vuttaṃ. Sabbadhīti catubhūmiketi atthasambhavato “tedhātuke”ti vuttaṃ. Ayaṃ asekkhā vimuttīti vimuttassa asekkhassa yā virāgatā atthi, ayampi virāgatā asekkhaphalavimutti. “Uddhaṃ adho sabbadhi vippamutto”ti pāṭhe vuttappakārā ayaṃ asekkhā vimutti niddhāritāti attho. Niddhāritāya asekkhāya vimuttiyā yāni saddhādipañcindriyāni niddhāritāni, tāniyeva asekkhāni [V 0.0324] pañcindriyāni bhavanti. Ayaṃ vuttappakārā otaraṇā indriyehi vimuttiyā otaraṇā nāma pavesanā nāma.

In that verse text, since the question, 'Having specified which, by which does one descend?' is to be asked, the passage beginning, 'Upward means the form realm' was stated. As for 'upward,' since the meaning could possibly be taken as above the human world including the realm of the Four Great Kings and so on, to prevent this, 'the form realm and the formless realm' was stated. As for 'downward,' since the meaning could possibly be taken as the four planes of deprivation below human existence, to prevent this, 'the sensual realm' was stated. As for 'everywhere,' since the meaning could possibly be taken as the four planes, 'in the triple realm' was stated. This is the non-learner's liberation: the dispassion that exists for the liberated non-learner, this dispassion is the liberation that is the non-learner's fruit. The meaning is that in the text, 'Upward, downward, everywhere released,' this non-learner's liberation of the kind stated is specified. With the specification of the non-learner's liberation, the five faculties beginning with faith that are specified become the very five faculties of the non-learner. This kind of descent as stated is called the descent by the faculties, that is, the entrance into liberation.

Tāniyeva asekkhāni pañcindriyāni vijjāya upakārakattā, paññāpadaṭṭhānattā vā vijjā bhavanti. Vijjuppādā tādisāya vijjāya uppādā uppādahetuto [M 0.0198] avijjānirodho avijjāya nirodho hoti…pe… dukkhakkhandhassa nirodho hoti, ayaṃ vuttappakārā otaraṇā paṭiccasamuppādehi otaraṇā nāma.

Those very same five faculties of the non-learner, because they are helpful to true knowledge or are the basis for wisdom, become true knowledge. From the arising of true knowledge, that is, from the arising of such knowledge as a cause, there is the cessation of ignorance... there is the cessation of the mass of suffering. This kind of descent as stated is called the descent by means of dependent origination.

Tāniyeva asekkhāni pañcindriyāni tīhi khandhehi saṅgahitāni saddhāvīriyehi sīlasambhavato, satiyā ca paññānuvattakattā. Sesā vuttanayānusārena veditabbā.

Those very same five faculties of the non-learner are included in the three aggregates; faith and energy are included due to their arising from virtue, and mindfulness because it attends on wisdom. The rest should be understood in accordance with the method already stated.

“Uddhaṃ adho sabbadhi vippamutto”ti pāṭhe niddhāretvā otaraṇā ācariyena vibhattā, amhehi ca ñātā, “ayaṃ ahasmīti anānupassī”ti pāṭhe “katame niddhāretvā katamehi otaraṇehi otaratī”ti vattabbattā “ayaṃ ahasmīti anānupassīti ayaṃ sakkāyadiṭṭhiyā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yo ayaṃ sekkho “ahamasmī”ti nānupassī, tassa sekkhassa sakkāyadiṭṭhiyā yo samugghāto atthi, yā samugghātasaṅkhātā samugghātavimutti sekkhā vimutti hoti, tassā sekkhāya vimuttiyā yāni saddhādipañcindriyāni niddhāritāni, tāniyeva sekkhāni pañcindriyāni bhavanti. Ayaṃ vuttappakārā otaraṇā indriyehi otaraṇā nāma. Sesā vuttanayānusārena veditabbā.

The descent in the text 'Upward, downward, everywhere released' has been analyzed by the teacher and understood by us. In the text 'not contemplating "this I am,"' since it should be asked, 'Having specified what, by which descents does one descend?', the passage beginning 'This "not contemplating \'this I am\'" refers to the eradication of identity view' was stated. For that learner who does not contemplate 'I am,' there is the eradication of identity view. That eradication, known as liberation through eradication, is the learner's liberation. For that learner's liberation, the five faculties beginning with faith that are specified become the very five faculties of the learner. This kind of descent as stated is called the descent by the faculties. The rest should be understood in accordance with the method already stated.

43. “Uddhaṃ adho”tiādigāthāyaṃ otaraṇā ācariyena vibhattā, amhehi ca ñātā, “nissitassa calita”ntiādipāṭhe “katame niddhāretvā katamehi otaratī”ti pucchitabbattā “nissitassa calitaṃ, anissitassa calitaṃ natthī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Nissitassa puggalassa calitaṃ calanaṃ atthi, anissitassa puggalassa calitaṃ calanaṃ natthi. Calite calane asati passaddhi bhavati, passaddhiyā sati vijjamānāya nati na hoti, natiyā asati avijjamānāya āgatigati na hoti, āgatigatiyā asati avijjamānāya cutūpapāto na hoti, cutūpapāte asati avijjamāne idha chasu ajjhattikāyatanesu attānaṃ neva passati, huraṃ vā chasu bāhirāyatanesu attānaṃ na passati, ubhayaṃ antarena vajjetvā phassādisamudāyesu dhammesu attānaṃ na passati, esova paṭiccasamuppādo “avijjānirodhā”tiādiko dukkhassa anto avasānaṃ karotīti attho.

43. In the verse beginning 'Upward, downward,' the descent has been analyzed by the teacher and is known to us. In the text beginning 'For the dependent there is agitation,' since the question, 'Having specified which, by which does one descend?' is to be asked, the passage beginning 'For one who is dependent, there is agitation; for one who is not dependent, there is no agitation' was stated. For a dependent person there is agitation; for a non-dependent person there is no agitation. When there is no agitation, there is tranquility. When tranquility is present, there is no bending. When there is no bending, there is no coming and going. When there is no coming and going, there is no passing away and reappearing. When there is no passing away and reappearing, one sees no self here in the six internal sense bases, nor a self yonder in the six external sense bases, nor, avoiding both, does one see a self in the phenomena in the collections beginning with contact. This is the meaning: this very dependent origination, beginning 'with the cessation of ignorance,' brings about the end, the conclusion, of suffering.

Nissitassa [V 0.0325] calitanti ettha “nissayo katividho”ti pucchitabbattā “nissitassa calitanti nissayo nāmā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tatthāti tesu duvidhesu taṇhānissayadiṭṭhinissayesu [M 0.0199] yā cetanā rattassa puggalassa niddhāritā, ayaṃ cetanādhammo taṇhānissayo nāma. Yā cetanā mūḷhassa puggalassa niddhāritā. Ayaṃ cetanādhammo diṭṭhinissayo nāma. Sā duvidhā cetanā pana saṅkhārā nāma. Saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ…pe… sabbo paṭiccasamuppādo niddhārito. Ayaṃ vuttappakārā otaraṇā paṭiccasamuppādehi otaraṇā nāma.

Here, regarding 'For the dependent there is agitation,' since the question, 'How many kinds of dependence are there?' is to be asked, the passage beginning, 'For the dependent there is agitation means dependence...' was stated. Herein, among those two kinds—dependence on craving and dependence on views—the volition specified for a lustful person is called the phenomenon of volition as dependence on craving. The volition specified for a deluded person is called the phenomenon of volition as dependence on views. But these two kinds of volition are called formations. 'With formations as condition, consciousness arises...'—thus the entire dependent origination is specified. This kind of descent as stated is called the descent by means of dependent origination.

Tatthāti tasmiṃ taṇhānissayadiṭṭhinissaye yā vedanā rattassa puggalassa niddhāritā, ayaṃ sukhā vedanā. Yā cetanā sammūḷhassa puggalassa niddhāritā, ayaṃ adukkhamasukhā vedanā. Yebhuyyena sesā vuttanayānusārena veditabbā.

Herein, in that dependence on craving and dependence on views, the feeling specified for a lustful person is pleasant feeling. The feeling specified for a thoroughly deluded person is neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The rest should be understood for the most part in accordance with the method already stated.

44. “Nissitassa calita”ntiādipāṭhe otaraṇā ācariyena vibhattā, amhehi ca ñātā.

44. In the text beginning 'For the dependent there is agitation,' the descent has been analyzed by the teacher and is known to us.

“Ye keci sokā paridevitā vā…pe…

Piyaṃ na kayirātha kuhiñci loke”ti. –

Whatever sorrows or lamentations... One should not make anything dear anywhere in the world.

Gāthāpāṭhe “katame niddhāretvā katamehi otaratī”ti pucchitabbattā “ye keci sokā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Ye keci sokā vā yā kāci paridevitā vā anekarūpā yā kāci dukkhā vā lokasmiṃ sambhavanti. Ete sokādayo piyaṃ paṭicca pabhavanti, piye asante ete sokādayo na bhavanti. Tasmā piye asante sokādīnaṃ abhāvato yesaṃ vītasokānaṃ kuhiñci lokepi natthi, te vītasokā sukhino bhavanti. Tasmā vītasokānaṃ sukhasampannattā asokaṃ virajaṃ patthayāno sappuriso kuhiñci loke piyaṃ na kayirāthāti gāthāttho.

In the verse text, since the question, 'Having specified which, by which does one descend?' is to be asked, the passage beginning 'Whatever sorrows' was stated. Whatever sorrows, or whatever lamentations, or whatever various kinds of suffering arise in the world, these sorrows and so on arise in dependence on what is dear. When there is nothing dear, these sorrows and so on do not exist. Therefore, since sorrows and so on are absent when there is nothing dear, those who are free from sorrow, for whom there is nothing dear anywhere in the world, are happy. Thus, because those free from sorrow are endowed with happiness, a good person aspiring for the sorrowless, dustless state should not make anything dear anywhere in the world. This is the meaning of the verse.

“Ye keci sokā paridevitā vā, dukkhā ca lokasmimanekarūpā piyaṃ paṭicca pabhavanti ete”ti ettha pāṭhe yā vedanā niddhāritā, ayaṃ dukkhā vedanā. Sesā vuttanayānusārena veditabbā.

In the text, 'Whatever sorrows or lamentations, and various kinds of suffering in the world, these arise in dependence on what is dear,' the feeling that is specified here is painful feeling. The rest should be understood in accordance with the method already stated.

“Ye keci sokā”tiādigāthāpāṭhe otaraṇā ācariyena vibhattā, amhehi ca ñātā[V 0.0326], “kāmaṃ kāmayamānassā”tiādigāthāpāṭhe “katame [M 0.0200] niddhāretvā katamehi otaratī”ti vattabbattā “kāmaṃ kāmayamānassā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tassaṃ gāthāyaṃ attho heṭṭhā vuttova.

In the verse text beginning 'Whatever sorrows,' the descent has been analyzed by the teacher and is known to us. In the verse text beginning 'For one desiring a sensual pleasure,' since it should be said, 'Having specified which, by which does one descend?', the passage beginning 'For one desiring a sensual pleasure' was stated. The meaning of that verse has already been stated previously.

Tatthāti tasmiṃ “pītimano hotī”ti pāṭhe yā pītimanatā vuttā niddhāritā, ayaṃ pītimanatā anunayo hoti. “Sallaviddhova ruppatī”ti pāṭhe yaṃ ruppanaṃ āha, idaṃ ruppanaṃ paṭighaṃ hoti, anunayo ca paṭighañca niddhāritāti attho.

Herein, in the passage 'he becomes joyful,' the joyfulness that is mentioned and determined—this joyfulness is inclination. In the passage 'he suffers like one struck by a dart,' the suffering that is mentioned—this suffering is aversion. Thus, inclination and aversion are determined—this is the meaning.

“Anunaye ca paṭighe ca niddhārite katamo dhammo niddhārito”ti vattabbattā “anunayo paṭighañca pana taṇhāpakkho”ti vuttaṃ. Taṇhāpakkhoti taṇhāpakkhattā taṇhā niddhāritā. “Anunayo taṇhāpakkho hotu, paṭighaṃ pana taṇhāpakkhaṃ na siyā”ti ce vadeyya? Paṭighassa attasinehavasena pavattanato paṭighampi taṇhāpakkhaṃ hoti. “Taṇhāya niddhāritāya katamo niddhārito”ti vattabbattā “taṇhāya ca panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Dasannaṃ rūpāyatanānaṃ taṇhāya padaṭṭhānattā dasa rūpāni āyatanāni niddhāritāni. Ayaṃ vuttappakārā otaraṇā āyatanehi otaraṇā nāma. Sutte āgatā paṭiccasamuppādādayo tena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesena nayena niddhāritā, suttatthamukhena vā niddhāritā, tena…pe… nayena niddhāritesu paṭiccasamuppādādīsu yo saṃvaṇṇanānayaviseso tadatthavācakavasena vā tadatthañāpakavasena vā otarati pavisati samosarati, so saṃvaṇṇanānayaviseso otaraṇo hāro nāmāti adhippāyo daṭṭhabbo. Sesesupi vuttanayānusārena otaraṇā gahetabbā. “Tenāha āyasmā”tiādyānusandhyādiattho ceva “niyutto otaraṇo hāro”ti anusandhyādiattho ca vuttanayānusārena veditabbo.

Since it should be asked, 'When attraction and repulsion are determined, which dhamma is determined?', it was stated, 'Attraction and repulsion are on the side of craving.' As they are on the side of craving, craving is determined. If one were to say, 'Let attraction be on the side of craving, but repulsion should not be,' then because repulsion arises through self-love, repulsion too is on the side of craving. Since it should be asked, 'When craving is determined, what is determined?', it was stated, 'By craving,' etc. Because the ten form sense-bases serve as the foundation for craving, the ten forms as sense-bases are determined. This kind of descent, as stated, is called descent through the sense-bases. The dependent origination and other teachings that appear in the suttas are determined by that special method of analysis, or determined by the meaning of the suttas. Thus... among the dependent origination and other teachings determined by those methods, whatever special method of analysis descends, penetrates, or converges—whether by way of expressing the meaning or by way of making the meaning known—that special method of analysis is to be understood as the 'descent mode.' The remaining descents should also be understood in accordance with the explained manner. Both the meaning of the connection, etc., beginning 'Therefore, the Venerable said...' and the meaning of the connection, etc., 'the established descent mode' should be understood in accordance with the explained manner.

Iti otaraṇahāravibhaṅge sattibalānurūpā racitā

Thus, in the exposition of the descent mode, this has been composed in accordance with my ability and strength.

Vibhāvanā niṭṭhitā.

The elucidation is concluded.

Paṇḍitehi pana aṭṭhakathāṭīkānusārena gambhīrattho vitthārato vibhajitvā gahetabboti.

However, the profound meaning should be analyzed in detail and grasped by the learned, in accordance with the commentaries and sub-commentaries.

13. Sodhanahāravibhaṅgavibhāvanā

13. Elucidation of the Exposition of the Purification Mode

45. Yena [V 0.0327][M 0.0201] yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūtena otaraṇahāravibhaṅgena otaretabbā suttatthā vibhattā, so saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūto vibhaṅgo paripuṇṇo, “katamo sodhanahāravibhaṅgo”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha katamo sodhano hāro”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha tatthāti tesu niddiṭṭhesu soḷasasu desanāhārādīsu katamo saṃvaṇṇanāviseso sodhano hāro sodhanahāravibhaṅgo nāmāti pucchati. “Vissajjitamhi pañhe”tiādiniddesassa idāni mayā vuccamāno “yathā āyasmā ajito”tiādiko vitthārasaṃvaṇṇanāviseso sodhanahāravibhaṅgo nāmāti gahetabbo. “Kathaṃ tattha pañhe sodhano hāro viññātabbo”ti vattabbattā “yathā āyasmā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yathā yena pakārena āyasmā ajito pārāyane bhagavantaṃ pañhaṃ pucchati, tathā tena pakārena vissajjitamhi pañhe ayaṃ sodhano hāro viññātabboti. “Niyametvā vibhajehī”ti vattabbattā niyametvā vibhajituṃ “kenassū”tiādi vuttaṃ. Gāthāttho vuttova.

45. That special method of explanation, the exposition of the descent mode, by which the sutta meanings to be descended into were analyzed, is now complete. Since it should be asked, 'What is the exposition of the purification mode?', it is said, 'Herein, what is the purification mode?' and so on. The word `tattha` means: among those sixteen designated modes of teaching, etc., it asks which special method of explanation is the purification mode, called the exposition of the purification mode. The instruction beginning 'When the question has been answered,' etc., means that the extensive special method of explanation that I am now explaining, beginning 'as the Venerable Ajita,' etc., is to be understood as what is called the exposition of the purification mode. Because it should be said, 'How is the purification mode to be understood in that question?', it is said, 'as the Venerable,' etc. Just as, in whatever manner, the Venerable Ajita asks the Blessed One a question in the Pārāyana, so in that manner, in the answered question, this purification mode is to be understood. Because it should be said, 'Having determined, analyze,' in order to analyze after determining, 'by what,' etc., is stated. The meaning of the verse has already been stated.

“Kenassu nivuto loko, kenassu nappakāsati;

Kissābhilepanaṃ brūsi, kiṃsu tassa mahabbhaya”nti. –

“By what, indeed, is the world enveloped? By what does it not shine forth? What do you call its defilement? What is its great fear?”

Pucchāvasena pavattagāthāyañca –

And in the verse that proceeds by way of questioning:

“Avijjāya nivuto loko, (ajitāti bhagavā,)

Vivicchā pamādā nappakāsati;

Jappābhilepanaṃ brūmi, dukkhamassa mahabbhaya”nti. –

“The world is shrouded by ignorance, (Ajita,” said the Blessed One,) “it does not shine forth because of perplexity and heedlessness; I declare craving to be its defilement, suffering its great fear.”

Vissajjanavasena pavattagāthāyañcāti imāsu dvīsu gāthāsu “kenassu nivuto loko”ti iminā padena pañhe pucchite “avijjāya nivuto loko”ti iminā padena bhagavā “kenassu nivuto loko”ti padaṃ tadatthe aññāṇasaṃsayādimalānaṃ apanayanena sodheti. Tadatthe hi vissajjite aññāṇasaṃsayādīnaṃ abhāvato attho sodhito nāma, atthe ca sodhite padampi sodhitaṃyeva. Tenāha aṭṭhakathāyaṃ – “tadatthassa vissajjanato”ti (netti. aṭṭha. 45), ṭīkāyañca “tabbisayaaññāṇasaṃsayādimalāpanayanena sodhetī”ti vuttaṃ. No ca ārambhanti pucchituṃ ārabhitabbaṃ [M 0.0202] sabbagāthāpadaṃ, gāthātthaṃ vā, ñātuṃ icchitassa sabbassa atthassa vissajjanavasena apariyositattā [V 0.0328] bhagavā “avijjāya nivuto loko”ti ettakeneva padena sodheti. Sesesupi esa nayo.

And in the verse that proceeds by way of answering: In these two verses, when the question is asked with the phrase 'By what, indeed, is the world enveloped?', the Blessed One purifies the phrase 'By what, indeed, is the world enveloped?' with the phrase 'The world is enveloped by ignorance,' by removing the stains of ignorance, doubt, and so on, concerning its meaning. For when its meaning is answered, the meaning is said to be purified because of the absence of ignorance, doubt, and so on. And when the meaning is purified, the phrase itself is purified. Therefore, the commentary says: 'Because of the answering of that meaning,' and the sub-commentary states: 'He purifies it by removing the stains of ignorance, doubt, and so on concerning that subject.' However, the Blessed One does not purify the entire initial question—every phrase of the verse or the meaning of the verse. Because the entire meaning wished to be known is not concluded by way of an answer, he purifies with just this phrase: 'The world is enveloped by ignorance.' The same method applies to the rest.

“Kiṃsu tassa mahabbhaya”nti iminā padena pañhe pucchite “dukkhamassa mahabbhaya”nti padena bhagavatā ārambho ñātuṃ icchito attho suddho sodhito hoti. Sesagāthāsupi eseva nayo.

When the question is asked with the phrase 'What is its great fear?', with the phrase 'Suffering is its great fear,' the meaning intended to be known from the beginning is pure and purified by the Blessed One. The same method applies to the remaining verses.

Yattha pañhe evaṃ niravasesavissajjanavasena ārambho suddho sodhito bhavati, so pañho vissajjito sodhito bhavati. Yattha pañhe evaṃ niravasesavissajjanavasena ārambho yāva asuddho asodhito bhavati, tāva so pañho vissajjito sodhito na bhavatīti yojanā. “Tenāhā”tiādyānusandhyādyattho ceva “niyutto sodhano hāro”ti anusandhyādyattho ca vuttanayānusārena veditabbo.

Where, in a question, the beginning becomes pure and purified by way of a complete answering, that question is answered and purified. And so long as the beginning of a question remains impure and unpurified, to that extent that question is not answered and purified by way of a complete answering—this is the connection. Both the meaning of the connection, etc., beginning 'Therefore, he said,' and the meaning of the connection, etc., 'the established purification mode,' should be understood in accordance with the explained manner.

Iti sodhanahāravibhaṅge sattibalānurūpā racitā

Thus, in the exposition of the purification mode, this has been composed in accordance with my ability and strength.

Vibhāvanā niṭṭhitā.

The elucidation is concluded.

Paṇḍitehi pana aṭṭhakathāṭīkānusārena gambhīrattho vitthārato vibhajitvā gahetabboti.

However, the profound meaning should be analyzed in detail and grasped by the learned, in accordance with the commentaries and sub-commentaries.

14. Adhiṭṭhānahāravibhaṅgavibhāvanā

14. Elucidation of the Exposition of the Determination Mode

46. Yena yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūtena vibhaṅgena pañhādayo sodhitā, so saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūto paripuṇṇo, “katamo adhiṭṭhānahāravibhaṅgo”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha katamo adhiṭṭhāno hāro”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha tatthāti tesu niddiṭṭhesu soḷasasu desanāhārādīsu katamo saṃvaṇṇanāviseso paṭiniddesato adhiṭṭhāno hāro adhiṭṭhānahāravibhaṅgo nāmāti pucchati. “Ekattatāya dhammā, yepi ca vemattatāya niddiṭṭhā”tiādiniddesassa idāni mayā vuccamāno “ye tattha niddiṭṭhā, tathā te dhārayitabbā”tiādiko vitthārasaṃvaṇṇanāviseso adhiṭṭhānahāravibhaṅgo nāmāti gahetabbo.

46. That special method of explanation, the exposition by which the questions and so forth were purified, is now complete. Since it is to be asked, 'What is the analysis of the determination mode?', it is said, 'Therein, what is the determination mode?' and so on. The word `tattha` means: among those sixteen modes of exposition, etc., that are enumerated, it asks which special method of explanation, by way of counter-definition, is called the determination mode, the analysis of the determination mode. The detailed analytical exposition now being stated by me, which is the instruction beginning 'Those phenomena declared in unity, and also those enumerated in diversity,' and continuing with 'Those enumerated there should be understood accordingly,' should be taken as the analysis of the determination mode.

“Ye [M 0.0203] dhammā suttesu ekattatāya ca vemattatāya ca niddiṭṭhā, te dhammā kiṃ pana tatheva dhārayitabbā[V 0.0329], udāhu aññathāpi vikappayitabbā”ti pucchitabbattā “ye tatthā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha tesu suttantesu ye dukkhasaccādayo dhammā ekattatāya ca vemattatāya ca niddiṭṭhā, te dukkhasaccādayo dhammā tathā ekattatāya ca vemattatāya ca dhārayitabbā upalakkhitabbā, na aññathā vikappayitabbā.

Because it is to be asked, “Are those phenomena declared in the suttas in unity and in diversity to be maintained exactly as declared, or should they be interpreted differently?”, it is said, “Those there,” and so on. There, in those suttas, those phenomena such as the truths of suffering and so forth that are declared in unity and in diversity, those phenomena such as the truths of suffering and so forth should be maintained and understood in unity and in diversity, not interpreted differently.

“Sāmaññakappanāya vohārabhāvena anavaṭṭhānato katamā ekattatā, katamā vemattatā”ti pucchitabbattā “dukkhanti ekattatā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Dukkhanti jātiādivisesamanapekkhitvā yā dukkhasāmaññatā vuttā, sā ayaṃ dukkhasāmaññatā dukkhassa ekattatā nāma. “Tattha katamaṃ dukkha”nti pucchitā “jāti dukkhā, jarā dukkhā…pe... viññāṇaṃ dukkha”nti jātiādivisesamapekkhitvā yā dukkhavisesatā vuttā, sā ayaṃ dukkhavisesatā dukkhassa vemattatā nāma. Tatthāti ye dukkhādayo dhammā sutte vuttā, tattha tesu dukkhādīsu atthesu.

Because it is to be asked, “Due to the instability of general designation and conventional expression, what is unity, what is diversity?”, it is said, “Suffering is unity,” and so on. “Suffering”—the generality of suffering that is stated without regard to the specifics of birth and so forth, that generality of suffering is called the unity of suffering. When asked, “Therein, what is suffering?” and answered, “Birth is suffering, aging is suffering… consciousness is suffering”—the specificity of suffering that is stated with regard to the specifics of birth and so forth, that specificity of suffering is called the diversity of suffering. “Therein” refers to those phenomena such as suffering and so forth that are stated in the discourse, therein, in those meanings of suffering and so forth.

Dukkhasamudayoti “taṇhā ponobhavikā”ti visesamanapekkhitvā yā samudayasāmaññatā vuttā, sā ayaṃ samudayasāmaññatā samudayassa ekattatā nāma. “Tattha katamo samudayo”ti pucchitvā “yāyaṃ taṇhā…pe… vibhavataṇhā”ti visesaṃ apekkhitvā yā samudayavisesatā vuttā, sā ayaṃ samudayavisesatā samudayassa vemattatā nāma.

The origin of suffering: The generality of the origin that is stated without regard to the specifics of “craving that leads to renewed existence,” that generality of the origin is called the unity of the origin. When asked, “Therein, what is the origin?” and answered, “This craving… craving for non-existence”—the specificity of the origin that is stated with regard to the specifics, that specificity of the origin is called the diversity of the origin.

Dukkhanirodhoti “tassāyeva taṇhāya asesavirāganirodho”ti visesamanapekkhitvā yā nirodhasāmaññatā vuttā, sā ayaṃ nirodhasāmaññatā nirodhassa ekattatā nāma. “Tattha katamo dukkhanirodho”ti pucchitvā “yo tassāyeva taṇhāya asesavirāganirodho cāgo paṭinissaggo mutti anālayo”ti visesamapekkhitvā yā nirodhavisesatā vuttā, sā ayaṃ nirodhavisesatā nirodhassa vemattatā nāma.

The cessation of suffering: The generality of cessation that is stated without regard to the specifics of “the remainderless fading away and cessation of that very craving,” that generality of cessation is called the unity of cessation. When asked, “Therein, what is the cessation of suffering?” and answered, “The remainderless fading away and cessation of that very craving, the giving up, the relinquishment, the release, the non-attachment”—the specificity of cessation that is stated with regard to the specifics, that specificity of cessation is called the diversity of cessation.

Dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadāti? Paṭipadāti sammādiṭṭhiādivisesamanapekkhitvā yā nirodhagāminipaṭipadāsāmaññatā vuttā, sā ayaṃ nirodhagāminipaṭipadāsāmaññatā maggassa ekattatā nāma. “Tattha katamā dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā”ti [M 0.0204] pucchitvā “ayameva ariyo…pe… sammāsamādhī”ti sammādiṭṭhiādivisesamapekkhitvā yā visesadukkhanirodhagāminipaṭipadatā vuttā, sā ayaṃ visesadukkhanirodhagāminipaṭipadatā maggassa vemattatā nāma.

The path leading to the cessation of suffering: The generality of the path leading to cessation that is stated without regard to the specifics of right view and so forth, that generality of the path leading to cessation is called the unity of the path. When asked, “Therein, what is the path leading to the cessation of suffering?” and answered, “This Noble… right concentration”—the specificity of the path leading to the cessation of suffering that is stated with regard to the specifics of right view and so forth, that specificity of the path leading to the cessation of suffering is called the diversity of the path.

Maggoti nirayagāmimaggādivisesamanapekkhitvā yā sāmaññamaggatā vuttā, sā ayaṃ sāmaññamaggatā [V 0.0330] maggassa ekattatā nāma. “Tattha katamo maggo”ti pucchitvā “nirayagāmī maggo…pe… nibbānagāmī maggo”ti nirayagāmimaggādivisesaṃ apekkhitvā yā visesamaggatā vuttā, sā ayaṃ visesamaggatā maggassa vemattatā nāma.

The path: The generality of the nature of a path that is stated without regard to the specifics of the path leading to hell and so forth, that generality of the nature of a path is called the unity of the path. When asked, “Therein, what is the path?” and answered, “The path leading to hell… the path leading to Nibbāna”—the specificity of the nature of a path that is stated with regard to the specifics of the path leading to hell and so forth, that specificity of the nature of a path is called the diversity of the path.

Nirodhoti paṭisaṅkhānirodhādivisesaṃ anapekkhitvā yā sāmaññanirodhatā vuttā, sā ayaṃ sāmaññanirodhatā nirodhassa ekattatā nāma. “Tattha katamo nirodho”ti pucchitvā “paṭisaṅkhānirodho…pe… sabbakilesanirodho”ti paṭisaṅkhānirodhādivisesaṃ apekkhitvā yā visesanirodhatā vuttā, sā ayaṃ visesanirodhatā nirodhassa vemattatā nāma.

Cessation: The generality of cessation that is stated without regard to the specifics of cessation through discernment and so forth, that generality of cessation is called the unity of cessation. When asked, “Therein, what is cessation?” and answered, “Cessation through discernment… up to… cessation of all defilements”—the specificity of cessation that is stated with regard to the specifics of cessation through discernment and so forth, that specificity of cessation is called the diversity of cessation.

Rūpanti cātumahābhūtikādivisesamanapekkhitvā yā sāmaññarūpatā vuttā, sā ayaṃ sāmaññarūpatā rūpassa ekattatā nāma. “Tattha katamaṃ rūpa”nti pucchitvā “cātumahābhūtikaṃ…pe… vāyodhātuyā cittaṃ virājetī”ti cātumahābhūtikādivisesamapekkhitvā yā visesarūpatā vuttā, sā ayaṃ visesarūpatā rūpassa vemattatā nāma.

Form: The generality of form that is stated without regard to the specifics of the four great elements and so forth, that generality of form is called the unity of form. When asked, “Therein, what is form?” and answered, “Consisting of the four great elements… up to… one becomes dispassionate towards the air element”—the specificity of form that is stated with regard to the specifics of the four great elements and so forth, that specificity of form is called the diversity of form.

48. Avijjāti dukkheaññāṇādivisesamanapekkhitvā yā avijjāsāmaññatā vuttā, sā ayaṃ avijjāsāmaññatā avijjāya ekattatā nāma. “Tattha katamā avijjā”ti pucchitvā “dukkhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye aññāṇaṃ…pe… avijjālaṅghī moho akusalamūla”nti dukkheaññāṇādivisesamapekkhitvā yā avijjāvisesatā vuttā, sā ayaṃ avijjāvisesatā avijjāya vemattatā nāma.

48. Ignorance: The generality of ignorance that is stated without regard to the specifics of ignorance of suffering and so forth, that generality of ignorance is called the unity of ignorance. When asked, “Therein, what is ignorance?” and answered, “Ignorance of suffering, ignorance of the origin of suffering… up to… the bar of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root”—the specificity of ignorance that is stated with regard to the specifics of ignorance of suffering and so forth, that specificity of ignorance is called the diversity of ignorance.

Vijjāti dukkheñāṇādivisesamanapekkhitvā yā vijjāsāmaññatā vuttā, sā ayaṃ vijjāsāmaññatā vijjāya ekattatā nāma. “Tattha katamā vijjā”ti pucchitvā “dukkhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye ñāṇaṃ…pe… dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpanna”nti dukkheñāṇādivisesamapekkhitvā yā [M 0.0205] vijjāvisesatā vuttā, sā ayaṃ vijjāvisesatā vijjāya vemattatā nāma.

Knowledge: The generality of knowledge that is stated without regard to the specifics of knowledge of suffering and so forth, that generality of knowledge is called the unity of knowledge. When asked, “Therein, what is knowledge?” and answered, “Knowledge of suffering, knowledge of the origin of suffering… up to… the enlightenment factor of investigation of states, a path factor included in the path”—the specificity of knowledge that is stated with regard to the specifics of knowledge of suffering and so forth, that specificity of knowledge is called the diversity of knowledge.
