When the mind is purified of craving and ignorance, it is purified of all defilements. Therefore, because they are specifically the corruptions of the mind, these two phenomena are mentioned. For when craving and ignorance are abandoned by the path of arahantship, no defilement whatsoever remains unabandoned.

“Vuttappakārā taṇhāavijjā vuttappakārānaṃ vipallāsānaṃyeva mūlakāraṇaṃ honti kiṃ, udāhu sakalassa vaṭṭassāpi mūlakāraṇaṃ honti ki”nti vattabbattā vuttappakārā taṇhāavijjā vuttappakārānaṃ mūlakāraṇaṃ honti yathā, evaṃ sakalassa vaṭṭassāpi mūlakāraṇaṃ hontīti dassetuṃ “tesa”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha yesaṃ puggalānaṃ cittaṃ arakkhitaṃ, micchādiṭṭhihatañca hoti, tesaṃ puggalānaṃ. Yesaṃ avijjānīvaraṇānaṃ taṇhāsaṃyojanānaṃ pubbakoṭi na paññāyati, tehi avijjānīvaraṇehi taṇhāsaṃyojanehi saṃsāre sandhāvantānaṃ saṃsarantānaṃ puggalānaṃ sakiṃ nirayaṃ māravasagamanena sandhāvanaṃ saṃsaraṇaṃ hoti, sakiṃ tiracchānayoniṃ sandhāvanaṃ saṃsaraṇaṃ hoti, sakiṃ pettivisayaṃ sandhāvanaṃ saṃsaraṇaṃ hoti, sakiṃ asurakāyaṃ sandhāvanaṃ saṃsaraṇaṃ hoti, sakiṃ deve sandhāvanaṃ saṃsaraṇaṃ hoti, sakiṃ manusse sandhāvanaṃ saṃsaraṇaṃ hotīti attho.

Because it must be stated 'Are craving and ignorance, as described, only the root causes of the described perversions, or are they also the root cause of the entire cycle of existence?', to show that just as craving and ignorance, as described, are the root causes of the described perversions, so too are they the root cause of the entire cycle of existence, the phrase 'for those' etc. is stated. Here, 'for those individuals' means for those individuals whose minds are unguarded and struck down by wrong view. For those for whom the prior end of the hindrances of ignorance and the fetters of craving is not discerned, the meaning is that for individuals wandering and transmigrating in saṃsāra due to these hindrances of ignorance and fetters of craving, that wandering and transmigrating is sometimes to hell, a wandering and transmigrating due to coming under the power of Māra; sometimes the wandering and transmigrating is to the animal realm; sometimes the wandering and transmigrating is to the realm of ghosts; sometimes the wandering and transmigrating is to the body of asuras; sometimes the wandering and transmigrating is to the gods; and sometimes the wandering and transmigrating is to humans.

“Micchādiṭṭhihatena cā”ti suttappadesena desito attho ācariyena vibhatto, amhehi ca ñāto, “thinamiddhābhibhūtenāti suttappadesena desito attho kathaṃ vibhatto”ti vattabbattā “thinamiddhābhibhūtenā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Cittassa viññāṇakkhandhassa yā akallatā akammaniyatā atthi, idaṃ akallattaṃ akammaniyattaṃ thinaṃ nāma. Yaṃ kāyassa līnattaṃ vedanādikkhandhattayalīnattaṃ atthi, idaṃ kāyassa līnattaṃ middhaṃ nāmāti thinamiddhasarūpameva vuttaṃ. Tehi thinamiddhehi cittassa abhibhūtabhāvādiko pana suviññeyyattā na vutto, avuttepi yesaṃ puggalānaṃ cittaṃ [M 0.0224] thinamiddhehi abhibhūtaṃ, tesaṃ puggalānaṃ tena cittena cittasīsena saṃyojanena saṃsāre māravasagamanena sandhāvanaṃ saṃsaraṇaṃ pariyosānasabhāvo vitthāretvā gahetabbo.

The meaning taught by the sutta passage, ‘and by one struck down by wrong view,’ has been analyzed by the teacher and is known to us. Because it must be stated, ‘How is the meaning taught by the sutta passage, “by one overcome by sloth and torpor,” analyzed?’, the passage beginning ‘by one overcome by sloth and torpor’ is stated. The unsuitability, the unworkability, of the mind, of the consciousness aggregate, that exists—this unsuitability, this unworkability, is called sloth. The languor of the body, the languor of the three aggregates beginning with feeling, that exists—this languor of the body is called torpor. Thus, only the nature of sloth and torpor is stated. However, the state of the mind being overcome by this sloth and torpor, etc., is not stated because it is easily understood. Even when not stated, for those individuals whose minds are overcome by sloth and torpor, their wandering and transmigrating in saṃsāra, their going under Māra's power with that mind, with the mind as chief, by the fetter, should be understood in detail as having the nature of a conclusion.

“Vasaṃ mārassa gacchatīti suttappadesena desito attho kathaṃ vibhatto”ti vattabbattā “vasaṃ mārassa gacchatī”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha kilesamārassāti kileso dānādipuññe māreti nivāretīti atthena māroti kilesamāro. Iminā kilesamāraṃ nissāya pavattattā abhisaṅkhāramārakhandhamāramaccumārā [V 0.0348] ca gahitā, ca-saddena vā gahitāti veditabbā. Sattamārassāti devaputtamārassa. Atha vā “devaputtamārassā”ti avatvā “sattamārassā”ti vuttattā yo yo rājacorādiko dānādīni vā issariyabhogādīni vā māreti, so so rājacorādikopi gahito, tasmā yassa kassaci sattamārassāti attho. Vasanti icchaṃ lobhaṃ adhippāyaṃ ruciṃ ākaṅkhaṃ āṇaṃ āṇattiṃ. Gacchatīti upagacchati upeti anuvattati anugacchati nātikkamatīti attho. “Kasmā vasaṃ gacchatī”ti vattabbattā “so hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yo satto arakkhitacittena ca micchādiṭṭhihatacittena ca thinamiddhābhibhūtacittena ca samannāgato hoti, so satto avijjānīvaraṇādīhi nivuto hutvā saṃsārābhimukho hi yasmā hoti, na visaṅkhārābhimukho, tasmā mārassa vasaṃ gacchatīti attho.

Since it should be stated, 'How is the meaning taught by the sutta passage, “He goes under the sway of Māra,” analyzed?' it is said, 'he goes under the sway of Māra.' Herein, 'of the Māra of defilements': a defilement is called a māra in the sense that it kills or obstructs meritorious deeds such as giving; this is the Māra of defilements. By this, since they proceed in dependence on the Māra of defilements, the Māra of formations, the Māra of aggregates, and the Māra of death are also included; or they should be understood as included by the particle 'ca.' 'Of the Māra of a being': this refers to the Māra who is a deva's son. Alternatively, since it is said 'of the Māra of a being' without saying 'of the Māra who is a deva's son,' any king, thief, or other being who destroys generosity and so on, or sovereignty and enjoyments, is also included. Thus, the meaning is 'of any being whatsoever who is a māra.' 'Sway' means wish, greed, intention, preference, longing, command, order. 'Goes' means he approaches, comes to, complies with, follows, does not transgress. Since it should be stated, 'Why does he go under the sway?' the passage beginning 'for he' is stated. Because any being who is endowed with an unguarded mind, a mind destroyed by wrong view, and a mind overcome by sloth and torpor is shrouded by the hindrances of ignorance and so on and is thus facing saṃsāra, not the unconditioned, therefore he goes under the sway of Māra. This is the meaning.

“Arakkhitenātiādikassa yassa suttassa attho vibhatto, tena ‘arakkhitenā’tiādikena suttena kittakāni saccāni desitānī”tivattabbattā “imāni bhagavatā”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Arakkhitenā”tiādisuttena bhagavatā imāni dve saccāni desitāni dukkhaṃ, samudayo cāti. Kathaṃ desitāni? Abhidhammanissitāya kathāya ceva suttantanissitāya kathāya ca desitāni. Tāsu kathāsu abhidhammanissitāya kathāya desite sati “arakkhitena cittenā”ti iminā padena arakkhitaṃ rattampi cittaṃ, arakkhitaṃ duṭṭhampi cittaṃ, arakkhitaṃ mūḷhampi cittaṃ bhagavatā desitaṃ ñāpitaṃ. Tattha rattacittaṃ lobhasahagatacittuppādavasena aṭṭhavidhaṃ, duṭṭhacittaṃ paṭighasampayuttacittuppādavasena dubbidhaṃ, mūḷhacittaṃ momūhacittuppādavasena dubbidhanti veditabbaṃ. Imesañhi cittuppādānaṃ vasena yā cakkhundriyādīnaṃ agutti anārakkhā uppannā, tāya aguttiyā anārakkhāya cittaṃ arakkhitaṃ hoti phalūpacārenāti.

Since it should be stated, 'By the sutta beginning with “By an unguarded,” the meaning of which has been analyzed, how many truths were taught?' the passage beginning 'These by the Blessed One' was stated. By the sutta beginning with 'By an unguarded,' the Blessed One taught these two truths: suffering and its origin. How were they taught? They were taught by way of an exposition dependent on the Abhidhamma and by way of an exposition dependent on the Suttanta. Among these, when taught by way of the exposition dependent on the Abhidhamma, through the phrase 'by an unguarded mind,' the Blessed One taught and made known that an unguarded mind is a mind affected by lust, a mind affected by hate, and a mind affected by delusion. Herein, the mind affected by lust should be understood as eightfold, by way of the eight types of consciousness accompanied by greed; the mind affected by hate as twofold, by way of the two types of consciousness connected with aversion; and the mind affected by delusion as twofold, by way of the two types of consciousness accompanied by deep delusion. For, on account of these arisings of consciousness, a lack of guarding and protection of the faculties, such as the eye faculty, arises. Because of that lack of guarding and protection, the mind is 'unguarded' by a figurative extension to the result.

“Micchādiṭṭhihatenā”ti [M 0.0225] iminā padena micchādiṭṭhisaṃsaṭṭhaṃ cittaṃ desitaṃ, taṃ diṭṭhisampayuttacittuppādavasena catubbidhanti veditabbaṃ. Tañhi micchādiṭṭhiyā saṃsaṭṭhabhāvena micchādiṭṭhivasānugatattā micchādiṭṭhihataṃ nāmāti. “Thinamiddhābhibhūtenā”ti iminā padena thinamiddhena saṃsaṭṭhaṃ cittaṃ desitaṃ, taṃ sasaṅkhārikacittuppādavasena pañcavidhanti veditabbaṃ. Tañhi thinamiddhena saṃsaṭṭhabhāvena thinamiddhavasānugatattā thinamiddhābhibhūtaṃ nāmāti evaṃ ye dvādasākusalā cittuppādakaṇḍe “katame dhammā akusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye akusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hotī”tiādinā (dha. sa. 365) vitthārato vattabbā, te dvādasākusalacittuppādā tīhi padehi bhagavatā desitāti veditabbā. “Mārassā”ti padena pañca mārā gahitā. Tesu kilesamāro [V 0.0349] “cattāro āsavā, cattāro oghā, cattāro yogā, cattāro ganthā, cattāri upādānāni, aṭṭha nīvaraṇā, dasa kilesā”ti (dha. sa. 1102 ādayo) desito. Abhisaṅkhāramāro pana “kusalā cetanā (vibha. 226) akusalā cetanā (vibha. 226) kusalaṃ kammaṃ akusalaṃ kamma”ntiādinā desito. Khandhamāro pana “attabhāvo pañcakkhandhā”tiādinā desito. Maccumāro pana “cuti cavanatā”tiādinā (vibha. 193) desito. Evaṃ tāvettha abhidhammanissitāya kathāya desito attho daṭṭhabbo.

By the phrase 'by one destroyed by wrong view,' a mind associated with wrong view is taught. This should be understood as fourfold, by way of the four types of consciousness connected with wrong view. For it is called 'destroyed by wrong view' because it is associated with wrong view and follows its influence. By the phrase 'by one overcome by sloth and torpor,' a mind associated with sloth and torpor is taught. This should be understood as fivefold, by way of the five types of prompted consciousness. For it is called 'overcome by sloth and torpor' because it is associated with sloth and torpor and follows their influence. Thus it should be understood that the twelve unwholesome arisings of consciousness—which are to be explained in detail in the section on arisings of consciousness with the words, 'What things are unwholesome? At a time when an unwholesome consciousness has arisen...' (Dhs §365)—are taught by the Blessed One with these three phrases. By the word 'of Māra,' the five māras are included. Among them, the Māra of defilements is taught as: 'the four taints, the four floods, the four yokes, the four bodily ties, the four kinds of clinging, the eight hindrances, the ten defilements' (cf. Dhs §1102ff). The Māra of formations, in turn, is taught as: 'wholesome volition, unwholesome volition, wholesome kamma, unwholesome kamma,' and so on. The Māra of aggregates, in turn, is taught as: 'personal existence, the five aggregates,' and so on. The Māra of death, in turn, is taught as: 'passing away, decease,' and so on (Vibh §193). Thus, the meaning taught here by way of the exposition dependent on the Abhidhamma should be understood.

Suttantanissitāya pana kathāya desite sati “cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā nimittaggāhī hoti anubyañjanaggāhī, yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ cakkhundriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ, tassa saṃvarāya na paṭipajjati, na rakkhati cakkhundriyaṃ, cakkhundriye na saṃvaraṃ āpajjati…pe… sotindriye na saṃvaraṃ āpajjati… ghānindriye na saṃvaraṃ āpajjati… jivhindriye na saṃvaraṃ āpajjati… kāyindriye na saṃvaraṃ āpajjati… manindriye na saṃvaraṃ āpajjatī”ti (ma. ni. 1.347) evaṃ puggalādhiṭṭhānena yaṃ chadvārikacittaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ chadvārikacittaṃ “arakkhitena cittenā”ti iminā padena desitaṃ. Yā micchādiṭṭhiyo pubbantakappanavasena vā aparantakappanavasena vā pubbantāparantakappanavasena vā micchā abhinivisantassa ayoniso ummujjantassa “sassato loko”ti vā “asassato loko”ti vā “na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti vā uppannā, tāhi [M 0.0226] diṭṭhīhi vā, yā ca diṭṭhiyo “imā cattāro sassatavādā…pe… paramadiṭṭhadhammanibbānavādā”ti brahmajālasuttādīsu (dī. ni. 1.30 ādayo) vuttā, tāhi diṭṭhīhi vā sampayuttaṃ yaṃ cittaṃ “micchādiṭṭhihatena cā”ti iminā padena desitaṃ.

Now, when taught by way of the exposition dependent on the Suttanta: the six-door consciousness that is spoken of with a person as its basis—as in the passage: 'Having seen a form with the eye, he grasps its signs and features. Since, if he were to dwell with the eye faculty unrestrained, evil unwholesome states of covetousness and displeasure might flood him, he practises its restraint; he guards the eye faculty, he undertakes the restraint of the eye faculty… he undertakes the restraint of the ear faculty… of the nose faculty… of the tongue faculty… of the body faculty… of the mind faculty' (MN I 347)—that six-door consciousness is taught by the phrase 'by an unguarded mind.' The consciousness connected with wrong views—either with those wrong views that arise for one who wrongly adheres and improperly emerges with theories about the past, the future, or both the past and the future, such as 'the world is eternal' or 'the world is not eternal' or 'the Tathāgata does not exist after death'; or with those wrong views spoken of in the Brahmajāla Sutta and other suttas, such as 'these four kinds of eternalism… the doctrines of Nibbāna in this very life' (DN I 30ff)—that consciousness is taught by the phrase 'and by one destroyed by wrong view.'

“Thinaṃ nāma cittassa akammaññatā, middhaṃ nāma vedanādikkhandhattayassa akammaññatā”ti vā “thinaṃ anussāhasaṃsīdanaṃ, middhaṃ ussāhasattivighāto”ti vā yāni thinamiddhāni vuttāni, tehi thinamiddhehi yaṃ cittaṃ abhibhūtaṃ ajjhotthaṭaṃ, taṃ cittaṃ “thinamiddhābhibhūtenā”ti iminā padena desitaṃ.

The mind that is overcome and overwhelmed by that sloth and torpor which are spoken of either as: 'Sloth is the unwieldiness of the mind; torpor is the unwieldiness of the three aggregates beginning with feeling,' or as: 'Sloth is the sinking of energy; torpor is the impairment of the power of energy'—that mind is taught by the phrase 'by one overcome by sloth and torpor.'

“Vaso nāma icchā lobho adhippāyo ruci ākaṅkhā āṇā āṇattī”ti yo vaso vutto, so vaso “vasa”nti iminā padena desito. “Pañca mārā – khandhamāro abhisaṅkhāramāro maccumāro devaputtamāro kilesamāro”ti yo māro vutto, so māro “mārassā”ti iminā desito. “Gacchati, upagacchati, upeti, anuvattati, anugacchati, nātikkamatī”ti [V 0.0350] yo puggalo vutto, so puggalo “gacchatī”ti iminā desitoti. Evaṃ desitesu dhammesu akusalā samudayasaccaṃ, “vasaṃ mārassa gacchatī”ti iminā padena ye pañcupādānakkhandhe upādāya paññatto puggalo vutto, te pañcupādānakkhandhā dukkhasaccanti dve saccāni desitāni. “Kimatthāya dve saccāni desitānī”ti pucchitabbattā “tesaṃ bhagavā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tesaṃ dvinnaṃ saccānaṃ pariññāya ca pahānāya ca “arakkhitenā”tiādi dhammaṃ bhagavā deseti, tāni dve saccāni “arakkhitenā”tiādikena ñāpetīti attho.

The sway that is spoken of as 'wish, greed, intention, preference, longing, command, order' is taught by the word 'sway.' The Māra that is spoken of as 'the five māras—the Māra of aggregates, the Māra of formations, the Māra of death, the Māra of the deva's son, and the Māra of defilements'—is taught by the word 'of Māra.' The person who is spoken of as one who 'goes, approaches, comes to, complies with, follows, does not transgress' is taught by the word 'goes.' Among the things thus taught, the unwholesome is the truth of the origin. By the phrase 'he goes under the sway of Māra,' the person who is designated in dependence on the five aggregates subject to clinging is spoken of; those five aggregates subject to clinging are the truth of suffering. Thus two truths are taught. Since it should be asked, 'For what purpose are the two truths taught?' the passage beginning 'The Blessed One for them' is stated. The Blessed One teaches the Dhamma beginning with 'By an unguarded' for the full understanding and for the abandonment of these two truths. The meaning is that he makes known those two truths by the passage beginning with 'By an unguarded.'

“Tesu dvīsu saccesu kassa saccassa pariññāya, kassa saccassa pahānāya desetī”ti pucchitabbattā “dukkhassa pariññāya, samudayassa pahānāyā”ti vuttaṃ. “Pariññāpahānehi katamāni saccāni desitānī”ti vattabbattā “yena cā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yena arahattamaggena parijānāti, yena arahattamaggena pajahati ca, ayaṃ arahattamaggo maggasaccaṃ nāma. Yaṃ nibbānadhammaṃ ārabbha taṇhāya, avijjāya ca pahānaṃ jātaṃ, ayaṃ nibbānadhammo nirodho nirodhasaccaṃ nāmāti. Evaṃ cattāri saccāni bhagavatā desitāni.

Since it should be asked, 'Among those two truths, for the full understanding of which truth and for the abandonment of which truth does he teach?' it is said: 'For the full understanding of suffering, for the abandonment of the origin.' Since it should be stated, 'Which truths are taught by means of full understanding and abandonment?' the passage beginning 'And by which' is stated. That path of arahantship by which one fully understands and by which one abandons is called the truth of the path. That state of Nibbāna, taking which as object the abandonment of craving and ignorance occurs, that state of Nibbāna is cessation, the truth of cessation. Thus the four truths have been taught by the Blessed One.

“Catunnaṃ [M 0.0227] saccānaṃ desitabhāvo kena viññātabbo”ti vattabbattā “tenāhā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tesu catūsu saccesu samudayasaccena assādo gahito, dukkhasaccena ādīnavo gahito, maggasaccanirodhasaccehi nissaraṇaṃ gahitaṃ, samudayappahānavasena sabbagatipajahanaṃ jātaṃ, sabbagatipajahanaṃ phalanti gahitaṃ. Yena rakkhitacittatādikena sabbagatipajahanaṃ jātaṃ, so rakkhitacittatādiko upāyoti gahito, arakkhitacittatādikassa paṭisedhanamukhena rakkhitacittatādikassa niyojanaṃ bhagavato āṇattīti gahitanti desanāhārena nānāsuttesu dassitā assādādayo “arakkhitenā”tiādike ekasmiṃyeva sutte nīharitvā dassitā.

Because it should be stated, 'By what should the teaching of the four truths be understood?' it is therefore stated, 'Thus he said,' and so on. Among these four truths, gratification is taken as the truth of the origin; danger is taken as the truth of suffering; escape is taken as the truths of the path and cessation. Through the abandonment of the origin, the abandonment of all destinations is accomplished; the abandonment of all destinations is taken as the fruit. That guarding of the mind, etc., by which the abandonment of all destinations is accomplished, that guarding of the mind, etc., is taken as the means. The application of guarding the mind, etc., by way of negating the unguarded state of mind, etc., is taken as the Blessed One’s command. Thus, the gratification, etc., shown in various suttas by way of the guideline of teaching, are extracted and shown in a single sutta, in the passage beginning, 'by the unguarded…'.

“Assādādīnaṃ nīharitvā dassitabhāvo kena viññātabbo saddahitabbo”ti vattabbattā “tenāhā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Ettha ca yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesena nānāsuttesu assādādayo nīharitvā dassitā, so saṃvaṇṇanāviseso desanāhāravibhaṅgo nāma. Yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesena ekasmiṃyeva sutte assādādayo nīharitvā dassitā, so saṃvaṇṇanāviseso desanāhārasampāto nāmāti viseso daṭṭhabbo.

Because it should be stated, 'By what is the extraction and demonstration of gratification, etc., to be understood and believed?' it is therefore stated, 'Thus he said,' and so on. Here, that particular mode of exposition by which gratification, etc., are extracted and shown in various suttas is called the Analysis of the Guideline of Teaching. That particular mode of exposition by which gratification, etc., are extracted and shown in a single sutta is called the Convergence of the Guideline of Teaching. This distinction should be understood.

“Ettakova desanāhārasampāto paripuṇṇo”ti vattabbattā “niyutto desanāhārasampāto”ti vuttaṃ. Ekekasmiṃyeva sutte assādādayo yena yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūtena desanāhārasampātena nīharitvā [V 0.0351] yathārahaṃ dassitā, so so saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūto desanāhārasampāto niyutto yathārahaṃ niddhāretvā yujjitabboti attho gahito.

Because it should be said, 'The Convergence of the Guideline of Teaching is now complete,' it is said, 'The Convergence of the Guideline of Teaching is applied.' The meaning is understood as follows: in each single sutta, gratification and so on are extracted and shown as appropriate by whichever particular exposition constitutes the Convergence of the Guideline of Teaching. That very particular exposition, the Convergence of the Guideline of Teaching, is applied and should be connected as appropriate after having been determined.

Iti desanāhārasampāte sattibalānurūpā racitā

Thus is composed this explanation on the Convergence of the Guideline of Teaching, in accordance with my ability and power.

Vibhāvanā niṭṭhitā.

The Elucidation is finished.

Paṇḍitehi pana…pe… gahetabboti.

But by the wise ...pe... it should be understood.

2. Vicayahārasampātavibhāvanā

2. The Elucidation of the Convergence of the Guideline of Investigation

53. Yena [M 0.0228] desanāhārasampātena assādādayo ācariyena vibhattā, amhehi ca ñātā, so desanāhārasampāto paripuṇṇo, “katamo vicayahārasampāto”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha katamo vicayo hārasampāto”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tatthāti tesu desanāhārasampātādīsu soḷasasu hārasampātesu katamo saṃvaṇṇanāviseso vicayahārasampāto nāmāti pucchati. Imesu dhammesu ayaṃ dhammo yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesena vicayitabbo, so saṃvaṇṇanāviseso vicayahārasampāto nāmāti niyametvā vibhajituṃ “tattha taṇhā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana –

53. That Convergence of the Guideline of Teaching by which gratification and so on have been analyzed by the teacher and understood by us is now complete. Because it should be asked, 'What is the Convergence of the Guideline of Investigation?' it is said, 'Therein, what is the Convergence of the Guideline of Investigation?' and so on. 'Therein' means: among those sixteen convergences of the guidelines, beginning with the Convergence of the Guideline of Teaching, which particular exposition is called the Convergence of the Guideline of Investigation?—so he asks. In order to define and analyze that 'the particular exposition by which a phenomenon among these phenomena is to be investigated is called the Convergence of the Guideline of Investigation,' it is said, 'Therein, craving…' and so on. But in the commentary—

“Evaṃ desanāhārasampātaṃ dassetvā idāni vicayahārasampātaṃ dassento yasmā desanāhārapadatthavicayo vicayahāro, tasmā desanāhāre vipallāsahetubhāvena niddhāritāya taṇhāya kusalādivibhāgapavicayamukhena vicayahārasampātaṃ dassetuṃ ‘tattha taṇhā duvidhā’tiādi āraddha”nti (netti. aṭṭha. 53) –

“Having thus shown the Convergence of the Guideline of Teaching, now, in showing the Convergence of the Guideline of Investigation, since the investigation of the meaning of the terms of the Guideline of Teaching is the Guideline of Investigation, therefore, in order to show the Convergence of the Guideline of Investigation by way of investigating the division into wholesome states and so on with regard to the craving that has been determined to be the cause of distortion in the Guideline of Teaching, the passage beginning 'Therein, craving is twofold…' was started.” (Netti. Aṭṭha. 53)

Vuttaṃ. Tattha tatthāti tasmiṃ “arakkhitena cittenā”tiādisuttatthe desanāhārasampātena saṃvaṇṇite akusaladhamme “taṇhā”ti niddhāritā sabbataṇhā. Kusalāpīti catubhūmake kusale uddissa pavattā taṇhāpi. Akusalāpīti akusaladhamme uddissa pavattā taṇhāpīti duvidhā hotīti vicayitabbā. Tena vuttaṃ ṭīkāyaṃ – “kusaladhammārammaṇāti kusaladhamme uddissa pavattamattaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, na tesaṃ ārammaṇapaccayataṃ, idha ‘kusalā dhammā’ti lokuttaradhammānampi adhippetattā”ti.

It is said. Therein. 'Therein' means: in the meaning of the sutta beginning 'With an unguarded mind…,' which was expounded by the Convergence of the Guideline of Teaching, all craving is determined as 'craving' among the unwholesome states. 'Wholesome' means also the craving that arises in relation to wholesome states in the four planes. 'Unwholesome' means also the craving that arises in relation to unwholesome states. Thus it should be investigated as being twofold. Therefore it is said in the subcommentary: 'With a wholesome state as object: this is said referring merely to that which arises in relation to wholesome states, not to their being an object-condition, since here 'wholesome states' is also intended to include supramundane states.'

“Kusalā [V 0.0352] taṇhā kiṃgāminī, akusalā taṇhā kiṃ gāminī”ti pucchitabbattā “akusalā saṃsāragāminī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Atha vā “katamo kusalākusalataṇhānaṃ viseso”ti pucchitabbattā “akusalā saṃsāragāminī”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Taṇhā nāma saṃsāragāminī hotu, kathaṃ apacayagāminī”ti vattabbattā “pahānataṇhā”ti vuttaṃ, pahānassa hetubhūtā taṇhā pahānataṇhāti attho, pahātabbataṇhaṃ āgamma yaṃ pahānaṃ pavattetabbaṃ, tena pavattetabbena pahānena apacayaṃ gacchatīti vuttaṃ hoti.

Because it should be asked, 'Wholesome craving leads to what, and unwholesome craving leads to what?' it is stated, 'Unwholesome craving leads to saṃsāra,' and so on. Or, because it should be asked, 'What is the distinction between wholesome and unwholesome craving?' it is stated, 'Unwholesome craving leads to saṃsāra,' and so on. Because it should be said, 'Granted that craving leads to saṃsāra, but how does it lead to decline?' it is stated, 'Craving for abandoning.' The meaning is: craving that serves as a cause for abandoning is called 'craving for abandoning.' It is said that one goes to decline by means of that abandoning that should be undertaken, which itself depends on the craving that is to be abandoned.

“Kiṃ [M 0.0229] pana taṇhāyeva kusalākusalāti dubbidhā, udāhu aññopi kusalākusalāti dubbidho”ti vattabbattā “mānopī”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Katamo māno kusalo, katamo māno akusalo”ti pucchitabbattā “yaṃ mānaṃ nissāya mānaṃ pajahati, ayaṃ māno kusalo. Yo pana māno dukkhaṃ nibbattayati, ayaṃ māno akusalo”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha yaṃ mānaṃ…pe… kusaloti yaṃ mānaṃ nissāya upanissāya pahānaṃ pavattitaṃ, tena pahānena santāne uppajjanārahaṃ mānaṃ pajahati, ayaṃ upanissayapaccayabhūto māno phalūpacārena kusalo. Yo pana…pe… akusaloti yo pana māno parahiṃsanādivasena pavattamāno hutvā attano ca parassa ca dukkhaṃ nibbattayati, ayaṃ māno akusaloti vicayitvā veditabbo.

Because it should be asked, 'Is craving alone twofold as wholesome and unwholesome, or is there something else that is also twofold as wholesome and unwholesome?' it is said, 'Conceit too,' and so on. Because it should be asked, 'Which conceit is wholesome, and which conceit is unwholesome?' it is said, 'The conceit by relying on which one abandons conceit—this conceit is wholesome. But the conceit that produces suffering—this conceit is unwholesome.' Herein, 'the conceit…is wholesome' means: the conceit by relying upon and depending upon which abandonment occurs; by that abandonment, one abandons conceit liable to arise in the mental continuum. This conceit, being a condition of decisive support, is wholesome by way of its fruit. 'But the conceit…is unwholesome' means: the conceit that, proceeding in ways such as harming others, produces suffering for oneself and others. This conceit is to be understood as unwholesome after investigation.

“Saṃsārāpacayagāminīsu tāsu taṇhāsu katamā apacayagāminī taṇhā kusalā”ti pucchitabbattā “kusalā”ti vuttāya taṇhāya sarūpaṃ dassetuṃ “tattha yaṃ nekkhammasita”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Tatthāti tāsu saṃsārāpacayagāminīsu taṇhābhūtāsu kusalākusalāsu. Ayaṃ taṇhā kusalāti sambandho. “Ariyā puggalā santaṃ āyatanaṃ yaṃ ariyaphaladhammaṃ sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti, taṃ āyatanaṃ ariyaphaladhammaṃ ahaṃ kudāssu sacchikatvā viharissa”nti patthayantassa tassa kulaputtassa tasmiṃ ariyaphale pihā uppajjati, pihāpaccayā yaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati, idaṃ domanassaṃ “nekkhammasita”nti vuccati. Ayaṃ ariyaphale pihāsaṅkhātā taṇhā kusalā anavajjā anavajjaariyaphaladhammaṃ uddissa pavattattāti vicayitabbaṃ.

Because it should be asked, 'Among those cravings that lead to saṃsāra and to decline, which craving that leads to decline is wholesome?' in order to show the nature of the craving called 'wholesome,' it is said, 'Therein, that which is based on renunciation…' and so on. 'Therein' refers to those wholesome and unwholesome cravings that lead to saṃsāra and decline. The connection is: 'This craving is wholesome.' 'Noble individuals realize for themselves the peaceful sphere, the noble fruit, and having attained it, they dwell therein. When will I, too, realize for myself and dwell in that sphere, the noble fruit?'—when a clansman aspires in this way, a yearning for that noble fruit arises in him. Conditioned by that yearning, the displeasure that arises is called 'based on renunciation.' This craving, in the sense of a yearning for the noble fruit, should be investigated as being wholesome and blameless because it is directed toward the blameless noble fruit.

“Kathaṃ pavattā”ti vattabbattā “rāgavirāgā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yā rāgavirāgā cetovimutti pattabbā. Tadārammaṇā taṃ cetovimuttiṃ āgamma pavattā taṇhā kusalā anavajjā, yā avijjāvirāgā paññāvimutti pattabbā, tadārammaṇā taṃ paññāvimuttiṃ āgamma pavattā taṇhā kusalā anavajjāti vicayitabbā. Tāya paññāvimuttiyā vasena bhagavatā –

Because it should be asked, 'How does it arise?' it is said, 'from the fading away of lust…' and so on. The craving that arises in dependence on the liberation of mind to be attained—the fading away of lust—and which has that as its object, is wholesome and blameless. The craving that arises in dependence on the liberation by wisdom to be attained—the fading away of ignorance—and which has that as its object, is wholesome and blameless. This should be investigated. By means of that liberation by wisdom, the Blessed One has said:

“Tasmā [V 0.0353] rakkhitacittassa, sammāsaṅkappagocaro;

Sammādiṭṭhipurekkhāro, ñatvāna udayabbayaṃ;

Thinamiddhābhibhū bhikkhu, sabbā duggatiyo jahe”ti. (udā. 32; netti. 31, 65, 78) –

“Therefore, for one with a guarded mind, whose pasture is right intention, with right view as a forerunner, having known rise and fall, a bhikkhu, overcoming sloth and torpor, would abandon all bad destinations.” (Ud 32; Netti 31, 65, 78)

Gāthāyaṃ [M 0.0230] “sabbā duggatiyo jahe”ti padaṃ vuttaṃ, “tassā paññāvimuttiyā yo pavicayo kātabbo, katamo so pavicayo”ti pucchitabbattā “tassā ko pavicayo”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tassā paññāvimuttiyā ko pavicayoti ce puccheyya “aṭṭha maggaṅgāni – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhī”ti pavicayo veditabbo. “So pavicayo kattha daṭṭhabbo”ti pucchitabbattā “so katthā”tiādi vuttaṃ. So paññāvimuttiyā pavicayo kattha kasmiṃ dhamme daṭṭhabboti pucchati. Catutthe jhāne pāramitāya ukkaṃsagatāya catutthajjhānabhāvanāya so pavicayo daṭṭhabbo.

In the verse, the phrase 'would abandon all bad destinations' is stated. Because it should be asked, 'Regarding the investigation to be made concerning that liberation by wisdom, what is that investigation?' it is said, 'What is its investigation?' and so on. If one were to ask, 'What is the investigation of that liberation by wisdom?' the investigation should be understood as the eight path factors—right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration. Because it should be asked, 'Where is that investigation to be seen?' it is said, 'Where is it?' and so on. He asks: 'Where, in what dhamma, is the investigation of liberation by wisdom to be seen?' That investigation is to be seen in the fourth jhāna that has reached the summit of perfection, in the development of the fourth jhāna.

“Catutthe jhāne pāramitāyā”ti vuttamatthaṃ vivarituṃ “catutthe hi jhāne”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yo so catutthajjhānalābhī puggalo catutthe jhāne parisuddhaṃ pariyodātaṃ anaṅgaṇaṃ vigatūpakkilesaṃ mudu kammaniyaṃ ṭhitaṃ āneñjappattaṃ, iti aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṃ cittaṃ bhāvayati, so catutthajjhānalābhī puggalo tattha catutthe jhāne aṭṭhavidhaṃ vijjācaraṇaṃ adhigacchati. Katamaṃ aṭṭhavidhaṃ? Cha abhiññā, dve ca visese vā adhigacchatīti yojanā. Iddhividhādayo pañca, lokiyābhiññā ceva arahattamaggapaññā cāti cha abhiññā. Manomayiddhi ceva vipassanāñāṇañcāti dve ca visesā honti.

To explain the statement, 'In the perfection of the fourth jhāna,' the following was said: 'For in the fourth jhāna,' and so on. A person who has attained the fourth jhāna cultivates a mind that is endowed with eight factors in the fourth jhāna: purified, bright, stainless, free from blemishes, malleable, wieldy, steady, and having attained imperturbability. That person who has attained the fourth jhāna achieves eight kinds of knowledge and conduct in that fourth jhāna. What are the eight kinds? It is to be construed that one achieves six direct knowledges and two special qualities. The five beginning with the kinds of psychic power are mundane direct knowledges, and the wisdom of the path to arahantship is the sixth direct knowledge. The mind-made body and insight-knowledge are the two special qualities.

“Taṃ catutthajjhānacittaṃ kuto parisuddhaṃ…pe… kuto āneñjappatta”nti pucchitabbattā “taṃ cittaṃ yato parisuddha”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Taṃ cittaṃ yato upekkhāsatipārisuddhibhāvato parisuddhaṃ, tato upekkhāsatipārisuddhibhāvato pariyodātaṃ hoti. Sukhādīnaṃ paccayaghātena yato vītarāgādianaṅgaṇabhāvato anaṅgaṇaṃ, tato vītarāgādianaṅgaṇabhāvato vigatūpakkilesaṃ. Yato subhāvitabhāvato mudu, tato subhāvitabhāvato kammaniyaṃ. Yato parisuddhādīsu ṭhitabhāvato ṭhitaṃ, tato parisuddhādīsu ṭhitabhāvato āneñjappattaṃ hotītipi yojanā yuttā aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (netti. aṭṭha. 53) yugaḷato āgatattā. Saddhāvīriyasatisamādhipaññāobhāsehi pariggahitabhāvato āneñjappattaṃ. Saddhāya hi pariggahitaṃ cittaṃ paṭipakkhe assaddhiye na iñjati na calati, vīriyena pariggahitaṃ [M 0.0231] cittaṃ paṭipakkhe kosajje na iñjati, satiyā pariggahitaṃ [V 0.0354] cittaṃ paṭipakkhe pamāde na iñjati, samādhinā pariggahitaṃ cittaṃ paṭipakkhe uddhacce na iñjati, paññāya pariggahitaṃ cittaṃ paṭipakkhāya avijjāya na iñjati, obhāsagataṃ cittaṃ kilesandhakāre na iñjati. Iti imehi chahi dhammehi pariggahitaṃ catutthajjhānacittaṃ āneñjappattaṃ hoti. Evaṃ aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgatattā catutthajjhānacittaṃ channaṃ abhiññāñāṇānañca manomayiddhivipassanāñāṇānañca adhigamūpāyo hoti, tasmā so paññāvimuttiparicayo catutthajjhāne daṭṭhabboyevāti saṅkhepattho. Vitthārato pana aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (netti. aṭṭha. 53) “tattha upekkhāsatipārisuddhibhāvenā”tiādinā vā “aparo nayo”tiādinā vā vuttoyevāti amhehi na vutto.

Since it should be asked: 'That fourth jhāna consciousness, from what is it purified… from what has it attained imperturbability?' it is said: 'That consciousness, from what it is purified,' and so on. Because that consciousness is purified from the state of purity of equanimity and mindfulness, it is therefore bright. Because, by the destruction of the conditions for pleasure and so on, it is stainless from being free from lust and so on, it is therefore free from blemishes. Because it is malleable from being well-developed, it is therefore wieldy. Because it is steady from being established in purity and so on, it is therefore attained to imperturbability—this construction is also fitting, according to the commentary (Netti. Aṭṭha. 53), as it comes in pairs. It has attained imperturbability because it is encompassed by faith, energy, mindfulness, concentration, wisdom, and radiance. For the mind encompassed by faith does not waver or shake in the face of its opposite, faithlessness; the mind encompassed by energy does not waver in the face of its opposite, laziness; the mind encompassed by mindfulness does not waver in the face of its opposite, negligence; the mind encompassed by concentration does not waver in the face of its opposite, restlessness; the mind encompassed by wisdom does not waver in the face of its opposite, ignorance; the mind possessed of radiance does not waver in the darkness of the defilements. Thus, the fourth jhāna consciousness, encompassed by these six qualities, has attained imperturbability. In this way, because it is endowed with eight factors, the fourth jhāna consciousness becomes the means for attaining the six direct knowledges, the mind-made power, and insight-knowledge. Therefore, that cultivation of liberation by wisdom should be seen in the fourth jhāna—this is the concise meaning. In detail, however, it is indeed explained in the commentary (Netti. Aṭṭha. 53) with 'there, by the state of purity of equanimity and mindfulness…' and so on, or with 'another method…' and so on, but we have not elaborated on it.

“Yesaṃ rāgādiaṅgaṇānaṃ abhāvena anaṅgaṇaṃ, yesaṃ abhijjhādiupakkilesānaṃ abhāvena vigatūpakkilesaṃ, yāya cittassa ṭhitiyā abhāvena ṭhitaṃ, iñjanāya abhāvena āneñjappattaṃ, te rāgādiaṅgaṇādayo katamāya pakkhā”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha aṅgaṇā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tatthāti tesu rāgādiaṅgaṇādīsu aṅgaṇā ca rāgādiaṅgaṇā ca upakkilesā abhijjhādiupakkilesā ca santi, tadubhayaṃ rāgādiaṅgaṇaabhijjhādiupakkilesadvayaṃ taṇhāpakkho rāgādiaṅgaṇānaṃ taṇhāsabhāvattā, abhijjhādiupakkilesānañca taṇhāya anulomattā. Yā iñjanā phandanā yā ca cittassa aṭṭhiti anavaṭṭhānaṃ atthi, ayaṃ iñjanā aṭṭhiti diṭṭhipakkho iñjanāya ca aṭṭhitiyā ca micchābhinivesahetubhāvatoti pavicayo kātabbo.

Since it should be asked: 'That which is stainless due to the absence of the stains of lust and so on; that which is free from blemishes due to the absence of the blemishes of covetousness and so on; that which is steady due to the absence of instability of mind; that which has attained imperturbability due to the absence of agitation—to which side do these stains of lust and so on belong?' it is said: 'Therein, the stains,' and so on. Here, among these stains of lust and so on, there are stains—the stains of lust and so on—and blemishes—the blemishes of covetousness and so on. Both of these—the two kinds, stains of lust and so on and blemishes of covetousness and so on—belong to the side of craving, because the stains of lust and so on have the nature of craving, and the blemishes of covetousness and so on are conformable to craving. The agitation or trembling, and the instability or non-standing of the mind that exist—this agitation and instability belong to the side of views, because agitation and instability have wrong adherence as their cause. Thus the investigation should be made.

“Kiṃ pana catutthajjhānacittaṃ aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgatattāyeva channaṃ abhiññāñāṇānañca manomayiddhivipassanāñāṇānañca adhigamūpāyo hotī”ti pucchitabbattā “cattāri indriyānī”ti vuttaṃ. “Tassa catutthajjhānalābhino, dukkhindriyaṃ domanassindriyaṃ sukhindriyaṃ somanassindriyaṃ iti cattārindriyāni catutthajjhāne nirujjhanti, tassa catutthajjhānalābhino upekkhindriyaṃ avasiṭṭhaṃ bhavati, tasmāpi catutthajjhānacittaṃ vuttappakārānaṃ aṭṭhannaṃ ñāṇānaṃ adhigamūpāyo hoti, so ca adhigamūpāyabhāvo ciṇṇavasībhāvasseva bhaveyya, kathaṃ catutthajjhānamattalābhino ciṇṇavasībhāvo siyā”ti vattabbattā so catutthajjhānalābhī catutthajjhāneyeva aṭṭhatvā arūpasamāpattiyopi [M 0.0232] evaṃ katvā nibbatteti bhāveti, tasmā ciṇṇavasībhāvo hotīti dassetuṃ “so uparimaṃ samāpatti”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Tassattho aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (netti. aṭṭha. 53) vitthārato vutto, tasmā yojanamattaṃ karissāma.

Since it should be asked: 'Is it just because it is endowed with eight factors that the fourth jhāna consciousness is the means for attaining the six direct knowledges, the mind-made power, and insight-knowledge?' it is said: 'Four faculties.' For one who has attained the fourth jhāna, these four faculties cease in the fourth jhāna: the faculty of pain, the faculty of displeasure, the faculty of pleasure, and the faculty of joy. For one who has attained the fourth jhāna, the faculty of equanimity remains. Therefore, the fourth jhāna consciousness is also the means for attaining the eight kinds of knowledge mentioned. And that state of being a means of attainment would only come from practice and mastery. Since it should be said: 'How could one who has merely attained the fourth jhāna have practice and mastery?'—in order to show that one who has attained the fourth jhāna, having dwelt in the fourth jhāna itself, also produces and develops the formless attainments in this way, and thus has practice and mastery, it is said: 'He, the higher attainment…' and so on. Its meaning is stated in detail in the commentary (Netti. Aṭṭha. 53); therefore, we will give only the connection of the meaning.

So rūpāvacaracatutthajjhānalābhī yogāvacaro rūpāvacaracatutthajjhānasamāpattito uparimaṃ ākāsānañcāyatanasamāpattiṃ [V 0.0355] santato santatarato manasi karoti. Yathāvuttaṃ uparimaṃ samāpattiṃ santato manasi karoto tassa catutthajjhānalābhino yogāvacarassa catutthajjhāne saññā saññāpadhānā samāpatti oḷārikā viya hutvā saṇṭhahati, paṭighasaññā ca ukkaṇṭhā anabhirati hutvā saṇṭhahati, so yathāvuttena vidhinā manasi karonto yogāvacaro sabbaso niravasesato rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā “ākāsaṃ ananta”nti manasi katvā pavattamānaṃ ākāsānañcāyatanasamāpattiṃ sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati. Rūpasaññā rūpāvacarasaññā pañcavidhaabhiññābhinīhāro hoti. Nānattasaññā nānārammaṇesu vokāro akusalo pavattati. Evaṃ rūpāvacarajjhāne ādīnavadassī hutvā tā rūpasaññānānattasaññāyo ārammaṇe samatikkamati, assa yogāvacarassa paṭighasaññā ca abbhatthaṃ gacchati. Evaṃ iminā vuttanayena samatikkamena samāhitassa, santavuttinā arūpāvacarasamādhinā samāhitassa yogāvacarassa obhāso rūpāvacarajjhānobhāso antaradhāyati. Rūpānaṃ kasiṇarūpānaṃ jhānacakkhunā dassanañca antaradhāyatīti yojanā.

That meditator, an attainer of the fourth jhāna of the form-sphere, attends to the higher attainment, the base of the infinity of space, as peaceful and still more peaceful than the attainment of the fourth jhāna of the form-sphere. For that meditator, the attainer of the fourth jhāna who attends to the higher attainment as stated, the attainment in the fourth jhāna, which has perception as its chief component, seems gross, and the perception of resistance seems like vexation and discontent. That meditator, attending in the way described, by completely transcending perceptions of form, with the ending of perceptions of resistance, and by not attending to perceptions of diversity, enters and dwells in the base of the infinity of space, having realized it by attending: 'Space is infinite.' Perception of form is form-sphere perception; it is the basis for inclining the mind toward the five kinds of direct knowledge. Perception of diversity is the unwholesome deviation towards various objects that occurs. Thus, seeing the danger in the form-sphere jhānas, he transcends those perceptions of form and diversity as objects, and for that meditator the perception of resistance also comes to an end. Thus, for the meditator concentrated by this stated method of transcendence, concentrated with the peaceful-living formless-sphere concentration, the radiance of the form-sphere jhāna disappears, and the seeing of forms—kasiṇa-forms—with the jhāna-eye also disappears. This is how it is to be construed.

“Yena samādhinā samāhitassa, samāhitassa obhāso ca rūpānaṃ dassanañca antaradhāyati, so samādhi kittakehi aṅgehi samannāgato, kathaṃ paccavekkhitabbo”ti pucchitabbattā “so samādhī”tiādi vuttaṃ. So samādhīti yena rūpārūpāvacarasamādhinā samāhito, so duvidhopi samādhi anabhijjhābyāpādavīriyārambhehi tīhi upakārakaṅgehi ca passaddhisatīhi dvīhi parikkhāraṅgehi ca avikkhittena ekena sabhāvaṅgena ca chahi aṅgehi samannāgatoti paccavekkhitabbo punappunaṃ cintetabbo sallakkhetabbo[M 0.0233]. “Kathaṃ kattha paccavekkhitabbo”ti pucchitabbattā “anabhijjhāsahagataṃ me mānasaṃ sabbaloke”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Tesu chasu aṅgesu kittako samatho, kittakā vipassanā”ti pucchitabbattā ettako samatho, ettakā vipassanāti vibhajituṃ “tattha yañcā”tiādi vuttaṃ.

Since it should be asked: 'When one is concentrated with a certain concentration, radiance and the vision of forms disappear. With how many factors is that concentration endowed, and how should it be reviewed?' it is said: 'That concentration…' and so on. That concentration—the form-sphere and formless-sphere concentration with which one is concentrated—that twofold concentration should be reviewed as being endowed with six factors: with three supportive factors, namely, non-covetousness, non-ill will, and arousal of energy; with two requisite factors, namely, tranquility and mindfulness; and with one intrinsic factor, namely, non-distraction. It should be repeatedly reflected upon, considered, and noted. Since it should be asked: 'How and where should it be reviewed?' it is said: 'My mind is accompanied by non-covetousness toward the whole world…' and so on. Since it should be asked: 'Among these six factors, how much is serenity and how much is insight?'—in order to divide it into 'this much is serenity, this much is insight,' it is said: 'Therein, whatever…' and so on.

54. “Paññāvimuttī”ti vuttassa arahattaphalassa samādhissa samathavipassanāsaṅkhātā pubbabhāgapaṭipadā samādhimukhena ācariyena vibhattā, “tāya paṭipadāya labhitabbo arahattaphalasamādhi kittakena veditabbo”ti pucchitabbattā “so samādhi pañcavidhena veditabbo”ti vuttaṃ. Yo arahattaphalasamādhi samathavipassanāpaṭipadāya labhitabbo, so arahattaphalasamādhi pañcavidhena ñāṇadassanena veditabbo.

54. The preliminary practice, described as serenity and insight, for the concentration of the fruit of arahantship—which is called 'liberation by wisdom'—was analyzed by the Teacher through the gateway of concentration. Since it should be asked: 'In how many ways should the concentration of the fruit of arahantship, which is to be obtained by that practice, be known?' it was said: 'That concentration is to be known in five ways.' That concentration of the fruit of arahantship, which is to be obtained by the practice of serenity and insight, is to be known by the fivefold knowledge and vision.

“Kathaṃ pañcavidhañāṇadassanaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ bhavatī”ti vattabbattā “ayaṃ samādhī”tiādi [V 0.0356] vuttaṃ. Ayaṃ arahattaphalasamādhi appitappitakkhaṇe phalasamāpattisukhattā paccuppannasukho hoti, iti paccavekkhantassa assa arahato paccattameva ñāṇadassanaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ bhavati. Ayaṃ arahattaphalasamādhi āyatiṃ samāpajjitabbassa arahattaphalasamādhissa upanissayapaccayattā āyatiṃ sukhavipāko hoti, iti paccavekkhantassa…pe… bhavati. Ayaṃ arahattaphalasamādhi kilesaarīhi ārakattā ariyo, kāmāmisavaṭṭāmisalokāmisānaṃ abhāvato nirāmiso ca hoti, iti paccavekkhantassa…pe… bhavati. Ayaṃ arahattaphalasamādhi akāpurisehi sammāsambuddhapaccekabuddhasāvakabuddhehi sevitabbattā akāpurisasevito hoti, iti paccavekkhantassa…pe… bhavati. Ayaṃ arahattaphalasamādhi aṅgasantakilesadarathasantattā santo ceva divasampi samāpajjantassa atittikaraṇato paṇīto ca paṭippassaddhakilesena arahatā puggalena laddhattā paṭippassaddhiladdho ca arahattamaggasamādhisaṅkhātena ekodibhāvena adhigatattā ekodibhāvādhigato ca sasaṅkhārena sapayogena adhigatattā, nīvaraṇādipaccanīkadhamme niggayha anadhigatattā, aññe kilese vāretvā anadhigatattā, arahattamaggaphalabhāveneva pavattattā nasasaṅkhāraniggayhavāritagato hoti, iti paccavekkhantassa assa arahato paccattameva ñāṇadassanaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ bhavatīti pañcavidhena ñāṇadassanena so arahattaphalasamādhi vicayitvā veditabboti.

Because it was to be asked, 'How is the fivefold knowledge and vision present?' the passage beginning 'This concentration' was stated. This concentration that is the fruit of arahantship is presently pleasant at the moment of absorption because of the bliss of the fruition attainment; thus, for that arahant reflecting on it, knowledge and vision are present to himself. This concentration that is the fruit of arahantship has a pleasant result in the future because it is a decisive support condition for the future attainment of the concentration that is the fruit of arahantship; thus, for one reflecting... it is present. This concentration that is the fruit of arahantship is noble because it is far from the enemies that are the defilements, and it is unworldly because of the absence of the taints of sensual pleasures, the taints of the round, and the taints of the world; thus, for one reflecting... it is present. This concentration that is the fruit of arahantship is frequented by superior persons—that is, by Perfectly Self-Enlightened Ones, Paccekabuddhas, and enlightened disciples; thus, for one reflecting... it is present. This concentration that is the fruit of arahantship is peaceful, since it has stilled the fever of the defilements, its constituents, and it is sublime, since it is not tiresome even when entered upon for a whole day. It is attained through tranquility, having been obtained by the arahant, a person who has calmed the defilements. It is attained by unification, having been acquired through the state of unification designated as the concentration of the path to arahantship. It is not a state reached by deliberation, suppression, and warding off, for though it is attained with deliberation and exertion, it is not attained by suppressing opposing things like the hindrances, nor by warding off other defilements, but it proceeds simply by way of being the path and fruit of arahantship. Thus, for that arahant reflecting on it, knowledge and vision are present to himself. Therefore, that concentration that is the fruit of arahantship should be investigated and understood by means of the fivefold knowledge and vision.

“Paccuppannasukhādīsu [M 0.0234] samādhīsu kittako samatho, kittakā vipassanā”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha yo ca samādhi paccuppannasukho”tiādi vuttaṃ. Samatho, vipassanāti ca arahattaphalasamathavipassanāva adhippetā, na pubbabhāgasamathavipassanāti. Arahattaphalasamādhi pañcavidhena veditabboti ācariyena vutto, “tassa arahattaphalasamādhissa pubbabhāgapaṭipadāyaṃ vutto samādhi kittakena veditabbo”ti pucchitabbattā “so samādhi pañcavidhena veditabbo”ti vuttaṃ. Yo rūpāvacaracatutthajjhānasamādhi pubbabhāgapaṭipadāyaṃ vutto, so rūpāvacaracatutthajjhānasamādhi pañcavidhena pakārena veditabbo. “Katamenā”ti pucchitabbattā “pītipharaṇatā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Paṭhamadutiyajjhānesu paññā pītipharaṇatā hoti. Paṭhamadutiyatatiyajjhānesu paññā sukhapharaṇatā hoti. Catutthajjhāne cetopariyapaññā cetopharaṇatā hoti. Dibbacakkhupaññā ālokapharaṇatā hoti. Jhānaṃ paccavekkhitvā pavattamānapaññā paccavekkhaṇānimittaṃ hoti. Iti pañcavidhena paññāpakārena vicayitvā veditabboti. “Tesu pañcavidhesu pakāresu kittako samatho, kittakā vipassanā”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha yo ca pītipharaṇo”tiādi vuttaṃ.

Because it was to be asked, 'In the concentrations that are presently pleasant, etc., how much is serenity and how much is insight?' the passage beginning 'Therein, the concentration that is presently pleasant' was stated. By 'serenity' and 'insight' are meant the serenity and insight of the fruit of arahantship, not the serenity and insight of the preliminary phase. The concentration that is the fruit of arahantship is to be understood in five ways, as stated by the Teacher. Because it was to be asked, 'By how many ways is the concentration mentioned in the preliminary-phase practice for that concentration of the fruit of arahantship to be understood?' the passage 'That concentration is to be understood in five ways' was stated. The concentration of the fourth jhāna of the form realm, mentioned in the preliminary-phase practice, is to be understood in five modes. Because it was to be asked, 'By which ones?' the passage beginning 'pervasion by rapture' was stated. In the first and second jhānas, wisdom is pervasion by rapture. In the first, second, and third jhānas, wisdom is pervasion by pleasure. In the fourth jhāna, the wisdom of comprehending others' minds is pervasion by mind. The wisdom of the divine eye is pervasion by light. The wisdom that proceeds by reviewing the jhāna is the sign of reviewing. Thus, it should be understood by investigating it in these five modes of wisdom. Because it was to be asked, 'In these five modes, how much is serenity and how much is insight?' the passage beginning 'Therein, that which is pervasion by rapture' was stated.

55. Sampayogavasena samādhi ācariyena vibhatto, amhehi ca ñāto, “kathaṃ ārammaṇavasena [V 0.0357] vibhatto”ti pucchitabbattā “dasa kasiṇāyatanānī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Imehi dasahi ārammaṇehi kasiṇehipi samādhi vicinitvā veditabboti. “Tesu dasasu kittako samatho, kittakā vipassanā”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha yañcā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Kasiṇanti ca kasiṇamaṇḍalampi parikammampi paṭibhāganimittampi tasmiṃ paṭibhāganimitte uppannajjhānampi vuccati, idha pana sasampayuttajjhānameva adhippetaṃ.

55. Concentration has been analyzed by the Teacher by way of association, and it is known by us. Because it was to be asked, 'How is it analyzed by way of object?' the passage beginning 'The ten kasiṇa bases' was stated. Concentration should be understood by investigating it also by means of these ten objects, the kasiṇas. Because it was to be asked, 'Among these ten, how much is serenity and how much is insight?' the passage beginning 'Therein, whatever' was stated. The term 'kasiṇa' refers to the kasiṇa device, the preliminary development, the counterpart sign, and also the jhāna that has arisen in relation to that counterpart sign. Here, however, only the jhāna together with its associated states is intended.

“Kiṃ pana vuttappakāro samādhiyeva samathavipassanāya yojetabbo, udāhu aññopi yojetabbo”ti vattabbattā satipaṭṭhānādipubbabhāgapaṭipadābhedena anekabhedabhinno niravaseso ariyamaggopi vicayitvā yojetabboti dassetuṃ “evaṃ sabbo”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha evanti mayā vuttanayena vuttanayānusārena sabbo niravaseso satipaṭṭhānādipubbabhāgapaṭipadābhedena anekabhedabhinno ariyo maggo yojetabbo. Kathaṃ? Yena yena anabhijjhādiākārena paccuppannasukhatādiākārena [M 0.0235] samādhi mayā vutto, tena tena anabhijjhādiākārena paccuppannasukhatādiākārena yo yo ariyamaggo samathena yojetuṃ sambhavati, so so ariyamaggo samathena vicayitvā yojayitabbo. Yo yo ariyamaggo vipassanāya yojetuṃ sambhavati, so so ariyamaggo vipassanāya yojayitvā yojayitabboti attho gahetabbo.

Because it was to be said, 'But is it only the kind of concentration described that should be yoked to serenity and insight, or should something else also be yoked?' to show that the entire noble path without exception—divided into numerous divisions such as the preliminary-phase practice of the establishments of mindfulness, etc.—should also be investigated and yoked, the passage beginning 'Thus all' was stated. Herein, 'thus' means: in the way stated by me, according to the stated method, the entire noble path without exception—divided into numerous divisions such as the preliminary-phase practice of the establishments of mindfulness, etc.—should be yoked. How? In whatever mode concentration has been described by me—whether through the mode of non-covetousness, etc., or through the mode of being presently pleasant, etc.—in that same mode, whatever noble path it is possible to yoke to serenity, that noble path should be investigated and yoked to serenity. Whatever noble path it is possible to yoke to insight, that noble path should be investigated and yoked to insight. This is the meaning that should be taken.

“Yehi samathādhiṭṭhānehi vipassanādhammehi yojayitabbo, te samathādhiṭṭhānā vipassanādhammā katamehi dhammehi saṅgahitā”ti pucchitabbattā “te tīhi dhammehi saṅgahitā aniccatāya dukkhatāya anattatāyā”ti vuttaṃ, te samathādhiṭṭhānā vipassanādhammā “aniccatāya paññāya dukkhatāya paññāya anattatāya paññāyā”ti tīhi anupassanādhammehi saṅgahitā gaṇhitāti attho. Aniccatādinā sahacaraṇato anupassanāpaññāpi “aniccatā dukkhatā anattatā”ti vuccati.

Because it was to be asked, 'Regarding the foundations of serenity and phenomena of insight by which it is to be yoked, by which phenomena are they comprised?' the passage, 'They are comprised by three phenomena: by impermanence, by suffering, by non-self,' was stated. The meaning is that those foundations of serenity and phenomena of insight are comprised, are grasped, by the three phenomena of contemplation: 'by the wisdom of impermanence, by the wisdom of suffering, and by the wisdom of non-self.' Because it accompanies impermanence and so on, the wisdom of contemplation is also called 'impermanence, suffering, and non-self.'

“Yo yogī puggalo samathādhiṭṭhānaṃ vipassanaṃ bhāvayamāno hoti, so yogī puggalo kiṃ bhāvayatī”ti pucchitabbattā “so samathavipassanaṃ bhāvayamāno”tiādi vuttaṃ.

Because it was to be asked, 'When a meditator is developing insight that has serenity as its foundation, what is that meditator developing?' the passage beginning 'Developing serenity and insight' was stated.

Samathavipassanādīni bhāvayamāno puggalo rāgacarito dosacarito mohacaritoti tividho, “tattha katamo puggalo katamena katamena vimokkhamukhena niyyāti, katamāyaṃ katamāyaṃ sikkhanto, katamaṃ katamaṃ pajahanto, katamaṃ katamaṃ anupagacchanto, katamaṃ katamaṃ parijānanto, katamaṃ katamaṃ pavāhento, katamaṃ katamaṃ niddhunanto, katamaṃ katamaṃ vamento, katamaṃ katamaṃ nibbāpento, katamaṃ katamaṃ uppāṭento, katamaṃ katamaṃ vijaṭento niyyātī”ti pucchitabbattā [V 0.0358] “rāgacarito puggalo”tiādi vuttaṃ. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana “idāni yesaṃ puggalānaṃ yattha sikkhantānaṃ visesato niyyānamukhāni, yesañca kilesānaṃ paṭipakkhabhūtāni tīṇi vimokkhamukhāni, tehi saddhiṃ tāni dassetuṃ ‘rāgacarito’tiādi vutta”nti vuttaṃ. Tassatthopi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (netti. aṭṭha. 55) vuttoyeva.

A person developing serenity, insight, and so forth, is threefold: one of lustful temperament, one of hating temperament, and one of deluded temperament. Because it was to be asked: 'Therein, which person goes forth through which gate of deliverance, training in what, abandoning what, not approaching what, fully understanding what, dispelling what, shaking off what, vomiting what, extinguishing what, uprooting what, and disentangling what?' the passage beginning 'A person of lustful temperament' was stated. In the commentary, however, it is said: 'Now, to show the gates of deliverance which are especially the outlets for those persons training in a certain way, and the three gates of deliverance which are the counterparts to their defilements, together with them, the passage beginning "A person of lustful temperament" was stated.' Its meaning is also stated in the commentary (Netti-aṭṭha. 55).

“Kasmā [M 0.0236] tīṇi vimokkhamukhāni bhāvayanto tayo khandhe bhāvayatī”ti vattabbattā “tattha suññatavimokkhamukha”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Tatthāti tesu tīsu vimokkhamukhesu. Suññatavimokkhamukhaṃ paññākkhandho anattānupassanāya paññāpadhānattā. Animittavimokkhamukhaṃ samādhikkhandho aniccānupassanāya samādhipadhānattā. Appaṇihitavimokkhamukhaṃ sīlakkhandho dukkhānupassanāya sīlapadhānattā. Iti tīhi vimokkhamukhehi tiṇṇaṃ khandhānaṃ saṅgahitattā tīṇi vimokkhamukhāni bhāvayanto so yogī puggalo tayo khandhe bhāvayatiyevāti paññāpadhānādibhāvo aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (netti. aṭṭha. 55) vutto. Tayo khandhe bhāvayanto ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvayati. “Kasmā bhāvayatī”ti vattabbattā kāraṇaṃ dassetuṃ “tattha yā”tiādi vuttaṃ.

Because it was to be said, 'Why does one who develops the three gates of deliverance develop the three aggregates?' the passage beginning 'Therein, the gate of deliverance that is emptiness' was stated. 'Therein' means among those three gates of deliverance. The gate of deliverance that is emptiness is the aggregate of wisdom, because wisdom is predominant in the contemplation of non-self. The gate of deliverance that is the signless is the aggregate of concentration, because concentration is predominant in the contemplation of impermanence. The gate of deliverance that is the desireless is the aggregate of virtue, because virtue is predominant in the contemplation of suffering. Thus, because the three aggregates are comprised by the three gates of deliverance, that yogī who develops the three gates of deliverance indeed develops the three aggregates. The fact of wisdom and so forth being predominant is stated in the commentary (Netti-aṭṭha. 55). One who develops the three aggregates develops the Noble Eightfold Path. Because it was to be said, 'Why does one develop it?' to show the reason, the passage beginning 'Therein, that which' was stated.

Tiṇṇaṃ khandhānaṃ ariyaaṭṭhaṅgikamaggabhāvo vibhatto, amhehi ca jānito, “kathaṃ samathavipassanābhāvo jānitabbo”ti vattabbattā tiṇṇaṃ khandhānaṃ samathavipassanābhāvaṃ dassetuṃ “tattha sīlakkhandho cā”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Yo yogī puggalo samathavipassanaṃ bhāveti, tassa yogino puggalassa bhavaṅgāni katamaṃ bhāvanaṃ gacchantī”ti pucchitabbattā “yo samathavipassanaṃ bhāveti, tassā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Kāyo ca cittañca dve bhavaṅgāni upapattibhavassa aṅgāni bhāvanaṃ vaḍḍhanaṃ gacchanti. Sīlañca samādhi ca dve padāni dve pādā bhavanirodhagāminī paṭipadā bhāvanaṃ vaḍḍhanaṃ gacchanti.

The nature of the Noble Eightfold Path in the three aggregates has been analyzed and is known by us. Since it is to be asked, 'How is the nature of serenity and insight to be known?', to show the nature of serenity and insight in the three aggregates, the passage beginning 'Herein, the aggregate of virtue...' was stated. Since it is to be asked, 'For the yogī who develops serenity and insight, which constituents of existence (bhavaṅga) undergo development (bhāvana)?', the passage beginning 'For one who develops serenity and insight...' was stated. Body and mind, two constituents of existence, components of rebirth-existence, undergo development. Virtue and concentration, two steps, two feet of the practice leading to the cessation of becoming, undergo development.

“Kathaṃ gacchantī”ti vattabbattā “so hoti bhikkhū”tiādi vuttaṃ. Bhāvitakāyoti bhāvito kāyo kāyaābhisamācāriko, kāyasaṃvaro vā yena bhikkhunāti bhāvitakāyo. Sesesupi esa nayo. Kāye kāyaābhisamācārike, kāyasaṃvare vā bhāviyamāne sati sammākammanto, sammāvāyāmo ca dve dhammā bhāvanaṃ gacchanti kāyasamācārasīlattā. Sīle vācāsaṃvaraājīvasaṃvaravasena pavatte sīle bhāviyamāne sati sammāvācā ca sammāājīvo ca dve dhammā bhāvanaṃ gacchanti vācādisaṃvarasīlattā. Citte cittasaṃvaravasena pavatte citte bhāviyamāne sati sammāsati ca sammāsamādhi ca dve dhammā bhāvanaṃ gacchanti cittasaṃvarasīlattā. Paññāya bhāviyamānāya sati [V 0.0359] sammādiṭṭhi ca sammāsaṅkappo [M 0.0237] ca dve dhammā bhāvanaṃ gacchanti samānattā, upakārakattā ca. Sammāsaṅkappena hi punappunaṃ saṅkappantassa paññā vaḍḍhatīti.

Since it is to be asked, 'How do they go?', the passage beginning 'He is a bhikkhu...' is stated. 'Developed in body' (bhāvitakāyo) means a bhikkhu whose body, consisting of good bodily conduct, is developed, or by whom bodily restraint is developed. The same method applies to the rest. When the body is being developed in terms of good bodily conduct or bodily restraint, right action and right effort—these two qualities—undergo development because they are the virtue of bodily conduct. When virtue is being developed, specifically virtue proceeding by way of restraint of speech and restraint of livelihood, right speech and right livelihood—these two qualities—undergo development because they are the virtue of restraint of speech and so forth. When the mind is being developed, specifically the mind proceeding by way of mental restraint, right mindfulness and right concentration—these two qualities—undergo development because they are the virtue of mental restraint. When wisdom is being developed, right view and right intention—these two qualities—undergo development due to their similarity and their supportive role. For wisdom grows in one who repeatedly intends with right intention.

“Sammākammanto ca sammāvāyāmo ca dve dhammā kāyavaseneva vibhattā vicetabbā kiṃ, udāhu cittavasena vibhattā vicetabbā ki”nti pucchitabbattā “tattha yo ca sammākammanto”tiādi vuttaṃ. Kāyasucaritacetanābhūto yo ca sammākammanto, taṃsahito yo ca sammāvāyāmo siyā kāyiko, viratibhūto yo ca sammākammanto, taṃsahito yo ca sammāvāyāmo siyā cetasiko, tattha tesu kāyikacetasikabhūtesu sammākammantasammāvāyāmesu yo sammākammantasammāvāyāmo kāyasaṅgaho, so sammākammantasammāvāyāmo kāye kāyaābhisamācārike, kāyasaṃvare vā bhāvite sati bhāvanaṃ gacchati. Yo sammākammantasammāvāyāmo cittasaṅgaho, so sammākammantasammāvāyāmo citte cittasaṃvare bhāvite sati bhāvanaṃ gacchatīti yojanā.

Since it is to be asked, 'Should right action and right effort—these two qualities—be examined as classified by way of the body, or should they be examined as classified by way of the mind?', the passage beginning 'Herein, that right action which...' was stated. Right action which is the volition for good bodily conduct, and the right effort associated with it, would be bodily. Right action which is abstinence, and the right effort associated with it, would be mental. Among these right action and right effort, which are bodily and mental, the right action and right effort that are included in the body undergo development when the body is developed in terms of good bodily conduct or bodily restraint. The right action and right effort that are included in the mind undergo development when the mind is developed in terms of mental restraint. This is the connection.

“Samathavipassanaṃ bhāvayanto so yogī puggalo kittakaṃ adhigamaṃ gacchatī”ti vicayitabbattā “so samathavipassanaṃ bhāvayanto”tiādi vuttaṃ. Pañcavidhaṃ ariyamaggādhigamaṃ dassetuṃ “khippādhigamo cā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tassattho aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (netti. aṭṭha. 55) vibhatto. “Kena katamo adhigamo hotī”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha samathenā”tiādi vuttaṃ.

Since it is to be investigated, 'How much attainment does that yogī, developing serenity and insight, reach?', the passage beginning 'That one developing serenity and insight...' was stated. To show the five kinds of attainment of the noble path, the passage beginning 'And quick attainment...' was stated. Its meaning is explained in the commentary (Netti-aṭṭha. 55). Since it is to be asked, 'By what does which attainment occur?', the passage beginning 'Herein, by serenity...' was stated.

56. “Arakkhitena cittenā”tiādisuttattho veneyyānaṃ arahattaphalavimuttimukhena ācariyena vicayito vibhatto, amhehi ca ñāto, “desakassa dasabalasamannāgatassa dasa balāni kathaṃ vicayitabbānī”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha yo desayati, so dasabalasamannāgato”tiādi vuttaṃ. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana –

56. The meaning of the sutta beginning with 'With an unguarded mind' was examined and explained by the teacher for those to be guided, by way of the liberation of the fruit of Arahantship, and it is known by us. Since it is to be asked, 'How should the ten powers of the teacher, who is endowed with the ten powers, be investigated?', the passage beginning 'Herein, the one who teaches is endowed with the ten powers...' was stated. However, in the commentary—

“Iti mahāthero ‘tasmā rakkhitacittassā’ti gāthāya vasena arahattaphalavimuttimukhena vicayahārasampātaṃ niddisanto, desanākusalatāya anekehi suttappadesehi tassā pubbabhāgapaṭipadāya bhāvanāvisesānaṃ bhāvanānisaṃsānañca vibhajanavasena nānappakārato vicayahāraṃ dassetvā, idāni dasannaṃ [M 0.0238] tathāgatabalānampi vasena taṃ dassetuṃ ‘tattha yo desayatī’tiādimāhā”ti –

Thus, the great elder, indicating the application of the mode of investigation by way of the liberation of the fruit of Arahantship through the verse 'Therefore, of one with a guarded mind,' and having shown the mode of investigation in diverse ways—due to his skill in teaching—by analyzing through many sutta passages the distinctions in development and the benefits of development of that preliminary practice, now said, 'Herein, the one who teaches,' etc., in order to show it also by way of the ten powers of the Tathāgata.

Vuttaṃ. Tattha tatthāti tesu samathavipassanaṃ bhāvayantesu sāsitabbasāsakesu. Dasabalasamannāgato yo [V 0.0360] desako satthā “arakkhitena cittenā”tiādidhammaṃ deseti, ovādena sāvake na visaṃvādayati, tassa desakassa satthuno dasa balāni vicayitabbānīti yojanā.

It is said. Therein, 'in that context' refers to those who develop serenity and insight, that is, those to be instructed and the instructors. The Teacher, who is endowed with the ten powers and teaches the Dhamma beginning with 'With an unguarded mind,' does not mislead the disciples with his advice. The ten powers of that Teacher who teaches should be examined—this is the connection.

“Kinti desetī”ti pucchitabbattā “so tividha”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Tesu dasasu tathāgatabalesu ṭhānāṭṭhānañāṇaṃ paṭhamaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ nāma, “taṃ balaṃ kathaṃ vicayitabba”nti pucchitabbattā “so tathā ovadito”tiādi vuttaṃ. Attho aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (netti. aṭṭha. 56) vutto, pāḷivasenapi pākaṭo. “Etaṃ ṭhānaṃ na vijjatī”ti jānanaṃ aṭṭhānañāṇaṃ nāma, “etaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī”ti jānanaṃ ṭhānañāṇaṃ nāmāti ṭhānāṭṭhānānaṃ jānanañāṇaṃ paṭhamaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ vicayitabbanti adhippāyo veditabbo. (1)

Since it is to be asked, 'How does he teach?', it is said, 'He is threefold,' etc. Among these ten Tathāgata powers, the knowledge of what is possible and impossible is called the first Tathāgata power. Since it is to be asked, 'How should that power be investigated?', it is said, 'He is thus advised,' etc. Its meaning is stated in the commentary (Nettipakaraṇa Aṭṭhakathā 56) and is also clear from the Pāli text itself. Knowing that 'this is not possible' is called the knowledge of the impossible, and knowing that 'this is possible' is called the knowledge of the possible. Thus, the knowledge of knowing the possible and the impossible is the first Tathāgata power to be investigated—this intention should be understood. (1)

57. Ṭhānāṭṭhānañāṇaṃ paṭhamaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ācariyena vicayitaṃ vibhattaṃ amhehi ca ñātaṃ, “kathaṃ sabbatthagāminipaṭipadāñāṇaṃ dutiyatathāgatabalaṃ vicayitabba”nti pucchitabbattā “iti ṭhānāṭṭhānatā”ti vuttaṃ. “Ayaṃ paṭipadā imasmiṃ bhave gāminī, ayaṃ paṭipadā imasmiṃ bhave gāminī”ti sabbattha gāminiyā paṭipadāya jānanañāṇaṃ sabbatthagāminipaṭipadāñāṇaṃ nāmāti sabbatthagāminipaṭipadāñāṇaṃ dutiyaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ vicayitabbanti adhippāyo. (2)

57. The knowledge of what is possible and impossible, the first Tathāgata power, has been investigated and distinguished by the teacher, and is known to us. Since it is to be asked, 'How should the knowledge of the path leading to all destinations, the second Tathāgata power, be investigated?', it is said, 'Thus is the nature of what is possible and impossible.' The knowledge that 'this path leads to this state of existence, this path leads to this state of existence'—the knowledge of knowing the path leading everywhere—is called the knowledge of the path leading to all destinations. Thus, the knowledge of the path leading to all destinations, the second Tathāgata power, is to be investigated—this is the intended meaning. (2)

59. Sabbatthagāminipaṭipadāñāṇaṃ dutiyaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ācariyena vicayitaṃ, amhehi ca ñātaṃ, “kathaṃ anekadhātunānādhātuñāṇaṃ tatiyaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ vicayitabba”nti pucchitabbattā “iti sabbatthagāminī paṭipadā”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Ayaṃ dhātu ca ayaṃ dhātu ca anekadhātu nāma, ayaṃ dhātu ca ayaṃ dhātu ca nānādhātu nāmā”ti anekadhātunānādhātūnaṃ jānanañāṇaṃ anekadhātunānādhātuñāṇaṃ nāmāti anekadhātunānādhātuñāṇaṃ tatiyaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ vicayitabbanti. (3)

59. The knowledge of the path leading to all destinations, the second Tathāgata power, has been investigated by the teacher, and is known to us. Since it is to be asked, 'How should the knowledge of the many and various elements, the third Tathāgata power, be investigated?', it is said, 'Thus, the path leading everywhere,' etc. The knowledge that 'this element and this element are called the many elements; this element and this element are called the various elements'—the knowledge of knowing the many and various elements—is called the knowledge of the many and various elements. Thus, the knowledge of the many and various elements is the third Tathāgata power to be investigated. (3)

60. Anekadhātunānādhātuñāṇaṃ [M 0.0239] tatiyaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ācariyena vicayitaṃ vibhattaṃ, amhehi ca ñātaṃ, “kathaṃ sattānaṃ nānādhimuttikatāñāṇaṃ catutthaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ vicayitabba”nti pucchitabbattā “iti anekadhātunānādhātukassa lokassā”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Ime sattā evaṃ adhimuttā, ime sattā evaṃ adhimuttā”ti sattānaṃ adhimuccanānaṃ jānanañāṇaṃ sattānaṃ nānādhimuttikatāñāṇaṃ nāmāti sattānaṃ nānādhimuttikatāñāṇaṃ catutthaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ vicayitabbanti. (4)

60. The knowledge of the many and various elements, the third Tathāgata power, has been investigated and distinguished by the teacher, and is known to us. Since it is to be asked, 'How should the knowledge of the diverse inclinations of beings, the fourth Tathāgata power, be investigated?', it is said, 'Thus, of the world with its many and various elements,' etc. The knowledge that 'these beings are inclined in this way, these beings are inclined in this way'—the knowledge of knowing the inclinations of beings—is called the knowledge of the diverse inclinations of beings. Thus, the knowledge of the diverse inclinations of beings is the fourth Tathāgata power to be investigated. (4)

Sattānaṃ [V 0.0361] nānādhimuttikatāñāṇaṃ catutthaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ācariyena vibhattaṃ, amhehi ca ñātaṃ, “kathaṃ vipākavemattatāñāṇaṃ pañcamaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ vicayitabba”nti pucchitabbattā “iti te yathādhimuttā cā”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Evaṃ adhimuttānaṃ sattānaṃ idaṃ kammaṃ kaṇhaṃ, imassa kaṇhakammassa ayaṃ vipāko. Idaṃ kammaṃ sukkaṃ, imassa sukkakammassa ayaṃ vipāko”ti evamādīhi vipākānaṃ nānattajānanañāṇaṃ vipākavemattatāñāṇaṃ nāmāti vipākavemattatāñāṇaṃ pañcamaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ vicayitabbanti.

The knowledge of the diverse inclinations of beings, the fourth Tathāgata power, has been distinguished by the teacher, and is known to us. Since it is to be asked, 'How should the knowledge of the varying maturation of results, the fifth Tathāgata power, be investigated?', it is said, 'Thus, as they are inclined,' etc. The knowledge that 'for beings with such inclinations, this action is dark, and this is the result of this dark action; this action is bright, and this is the result of this bright action'—the knowledge of knowing the diversity of results in this way and so forth—is called the knowledge of the varying maturation of results. Thus, the knowledge of the varying maturation of results is the fifth Tathāgata power to be investigated.

62. Vipākavemattatāñāṇaṃ pañcamaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ācariyena vicayitaṃ, amhehi ca ñātaṃ, “kathaṃ jhānānaṃ saṃkilesavodānavuṭṭhānañāṇaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ vicayitabba”nti pucchitabbattā “iti tathā samādinnāna”ntiādi vuttaṃ. “Evaṃ samādinnānaṃ kammānaṃ jhānānaṃ vimokkhānaṃ samādhīnaṃ samāpattīnaṃ ayaṃ saṃkileso, idaṃ vodānaṃ, idaṃ vuṭṭhānaṃ, evaṃ saṃkilissati, evaṃ vodāyati, evaṃ vuṭṭhahatī”ti jhānānaṃ saṃkilesavodānavuṭṭhānānaṃ anāvaraṇañāṇaṃ jhānānaṃ saṃkilesavodānavuṭṭhānañāṇaṃ nāmāti jhānānaṃ saṃkilesavodānavuṭṭhānañāṇaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ vicayitabbanti. (5)

62. The knowledge of the varying maturation of results, the fifth Tathāgata power, has been investigated by the teacher, and is known to us. Since it is to be asked, 'How should the knowledge of the defilement, cleansing, and emergence of the jhānas, the sixth Tathāgata power, be investigated?', it is said, 'Thus for those who have undertaken,' etc. 'For those thus having undertaken these actions, jhānas, liberations, concentrations, and attainments: this is the defilement, this is the cleansing, this is the emergence; thus it becomes defiled, thus it becomes cleansed, thus it emerges.' The unobstructed knowledge of the defilement, cleansing, and emergence of the jhānas is called the knowledge of the defilement, cleansing, and emergence of the jhānas. Thus, the knowledge of the defilement, cleansing, and emergence of the jhānas, the sixth Tathāgata power, is to be investigated. (5)

63. Jhānānaṃ saṃkilesañāṇaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ācariyena vicayitaṃ, “kathaṃ indriyaparopariyattavemattatāñāṇaṃ sattamaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ vicayitabba”nti pucchitabbattā “iti tasseva samādhissā”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Evaṃ ādhipateyyaṭṭhena indriyāni, evaṃ akampiyaṭṭhena balānī”ti jānanena saha “ayaṃ mudindriyo, ayaṃ majjhindriyo, ayaṃ tikkhindriyo”ti parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ indriyabalānaṃ amudumajjhādhimattatājānanañāṇaṃamudumajjhādhimattatājānanañāṇaṃ indriyaparopariyattavemattatāñāṇaṃ nāmāti indriyaparopariyattavemattatāñāṇaṃ sattamaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ vicayitabbanti. (6)

63. The knowledge of the defilement, cleansing, and emergence of the jhānas, the sixth Tathāgata power, has been investigated by the teacher. Since it is to be asked, 'How should the knowledge of the diverse dispositions of the faculties of other beings, the seventh Tathāgata power, be investigated?', it is said, 'It is of that same concentration,' etc. The knowledge of knowing 'Thus the faculties in the sense of dominance, thus the powers in the sense of unshakability,' along with knowing of other beings and other individuals, 'This one has dull faculties, this one has middling faculties, this one has keen faculties,' which is the knowledge of discerning the dull, middling, and superior states of their faculties and powers, is called the knowledge of the diverse dispositions of the faculties of other beings. Thus, the knowledge of the diverse dispositions of the faculties of other beings, the seventh Tathāgata power, is to be investigated. (6)

64. Indriyaparopariyattañāṇaṃ [M 0.0240] sattamaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ācariyena vicayitaṃ, “kathaṃ pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ vicayitabbaṃ, kathaṃ dibbacakkhuñāṇaṃ navamaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ vicayitabba”nti pucchitabbattā “iti tattha yaṃ anekavihita”ntiādi vuttaṃ. “Ekaṃ jāti”ntiādinā jātivasena vā “evaṃnāmo”tiādinā nāmagottavaṇṇāhārasukhadukkhapaṭisaṃvedanāya pariyantavasena vā sākārassa sauddesassa anekavihitapubbenivāsassa taṃtaṃbhavassa asesato jānanañāṇaṃ pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇaṃ nāmāti pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ vicayitabbanti. (7)

64. The knowledge of the diverse dispositions of the faculties of other beings, the seventh Tathāgata power, has been investigated by the teacher. Since it is to be asked, 'How should the knowledge of the recollection of past lives, the eighth Tathāgata power, be investigated? How should the knowledge of the divine eye, the ninth Tathāgata power, be investigated?', it is said, 'Thus, in that case, whatever is of various kinds,' etc. The knowledge that knows completely and without remainder the various kinds of past lives of this or that existence, with their aspects and details—either by way of births, beginning 'one birth,' or by way of the range of name, clan, appearance, food, and experience of pleasure and pain, beginning 'of such a name'—is called the knowledge of the recollection of past lives. Thus, the knowledge of the recollection of past lives, the eighth Tathāgata power, is to be investigated. (7)

Cavamānaupapajjamānahīnapaṇītasuvaṇṇadubbaṇṇasugataduggatayathākammūpagānaṃ [V 0.0362] sattānaṃ asesato cutūpapātānaṃ jānanañāṇaṃ dibbacakkhuñāṇaṃ nāmāti dibbacakkhuñāṇaṃ navamaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ vicayitabbanti. (8-9)

The knowledge that knows without remainder the passing away and reappearance of beings—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate, faring according to their kamma—is called the knowledge of the divine eye. Thus, the knowledge of the divine eye, the ninth Tathāgata power, is to be investigated. (8-9)
