Pubbenivāsādiaṭṭhamanavamaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ācariyena vicayitaṃ vibhattaṃ, “kathaṃ sabbāsavakkhayañāṇaṃ dasamaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ vicayitabba”nti pucchitabbattā “iti tattha ya”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Bodhimūle saṃkilesamāranihanaṃ ñāṇaṃ uppannaṃ, idaṃ kilesamāranihanaṃ ñāṇaṃ sabbāsavakkhayañāṇaṃ nāmāti sabbāsavakkhayañāṇaṃ dasamaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ vicayitabbanti ayaṃ saṅkhepattho. Vitthārato pana pāḷito ca aṭṭhakathāto ca yatipotānampi pākaṭo bhaveyyāti maññitvā na dassito.(10)

The eighth and ninth Tathāgata powers, beginning with the recollection of past lives, have been investigated and analyzed by the teacher. Since it is to be asked, 'How should the tenth Tathāgata power, the knowledge of the destruction of the taints, be investigated?', it is said, 'Thus, in that case,' etc. The knowledge that arose at the foot of the Bodhi tree, which destroys the defilements and Māra—this knowledge that destroys the defilements and Māra is called the knowledge of the destruction of the taints. Thus, the tenth Tathāgata power, the knowledge of the destruction of the taints, is to be investigated. This is the meaning in brief. As for the detailed meaning, thinking it would be evident even to junior monks from the Pāli text and the commentary, it has not been shown. (10)

“Ettakova vicayahārasampāto paripuṇṇo”ti vattabbattā “niyutto vicayo hārasampāto”ti vuttaṃ. Ye ye suttappadesatthā vuttā, te te suttappadesatthā yena yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūtena vicayahārasampātena vicayitabbā, so so saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūto vicayahārasampāto niyutto yathārahaṃ nīharitvā yujjitabboti attho gahetabboti.

Because it can be said, 'The application of the Investigation method is complete just to this extent,' it is stated, 'The application of the Investigation method is established.' The meaning to be grasped is this: by whatever specific mode of explanation, which is an application of the Investigation method, the meanings of the various sutta passages that have been mentioned are to be investigated, that specific mode of explanation, which is an application of the Investigation method, is established. It should be extracted and applied as is appropriate.

Iti vicayahārasampāte sattibalānurūpā racitā

Thus is composed the section on the application of the Investigation method, in accordance with my ability and strength.

Vibhāvanā niṭṭhitā.

The Elucidation is finished.

Paṇḍitehi pana…pe… gahetabboti.

But it should be understood by the wise... (and so on)...

3. Yuttihārasampātavibhāvanā

3. Elucidation of the Application of the Reasoning Method

65. Yena [M 0.0241] yena vicayahārasampātena suttappadesatthā ācariyena vicayitabbā, amhehi ca ñātā, so vicayahārasampāto paripuṇṇo, “katamo yuttihārasampāto”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha katamo yuttihārasampāto”tiādi vuttaṃ. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana – “evaṃ nānānayehi vicayahārasampātaṃ vitthāretvā idāni yuttihārasampātādīni dassetuṃ ‘tattha katamo yuttihārasampāto’tiādi āraddha”nti (netti. aṭṭha. 65) vuttaṃ. Tatthāti tesu desanāhārasampātādīsu [V 0.0363] soḷasasu hārasampātesu katamo saṃvaṇṇanāviseso yuttihārasampāto nāmāti pucchati, pucchitvā yasmiṃ suttappadese vuttānaṃ atthānaṃ yuttibhāvo vicāretabbo, taṃ suttappadesaṃ nīharituṃ –

65. The application of the Investigation method, by which the meanings of sutta passages are to be investigated by the Teacher and are known by us, is complete. Because it should be asked, 'What is the application of the Reasoning method?' it is said, 'Herein, what is the application of the Reasoning method?' and so on. But in the commentary it is said: 'Having thus elaborated the application of the Investigation method in various ways, now, to show the application of the Reasoning method and so on, it begins, "Herein, what is the application of the Reasoning method?"' (Netti-aṭṭha 65). 'Herein' means: among those sixteen applications of the methods, beginning with the application of the Teaching method, he asks, 'What specific mode of explanation is called the application of the Reasoning method?' Having asked, in order to extract the sutta passage in which the logical coherence of the stated meanings is to be examined—

“Tasmā rakkhitacittassa, sammāsaṅkappagocaro;

Sammādiṭṭhipurekkhāro, ñatvāna udayabbayaṃ;

Thinamiddhābhibhū bhikkhu, sabbā duggatiyo jahe”ti. (udā. 32; netti. 31, 78) –

"Therefore, for one with a guarded mind,

whose pasture is right intention,

with right view as his forerunner,

having known rise and fall,

a bhikkhu, overcoming sloth and torpor,

would abandon all bad destinations." (Ud 32; Netti 31, 78)

Vuttaṃ. Tassaṃ gāthāyaṃ tasmā arakkhitacittassa māravasānugatattā satisaṃvaraindriyasaṃvarādivasena bhikkhu rakkhitacitto assa bhaveyya, tasmā kāmavitakkādimicchāsaṅkappagocarassa māravasānugatattā nekkhammasaṅkappādivasena bhikkhu sammāsaṅkappagocaro assa bhaveyya, tasmā micchādiṭṭhihatacittassa māravasānugatattā yonisomanasikārena bhikkhu udayabbayaṃ ñatvāna sammādiṭṭhipurekkhāro assa bhaveyya, tasmā thinamiddhena hatacittassa māravasānugatattā vīriyavasena bhikkhu thinamiddhābhibhū assa bhaveyya, tādiso bhikkhu sabbā duggatiyo jahe jahissatīti attho veditabbo.

It is said. In that verse, the meaning should be understood thus: Because an unguarded mind has fallen under the sway of Māra, a bhikkhu should have a guarded mind by means of restraint of mindfulness, restraint of the sense faculties, and so on. Because one whose pasture is wrong intention, such as sensual thoughts, has fallen under the sway of Māra, a bhikkhu should have right intention as his pasture by means of intentions of renunciation and so on. Because a mind struck by wrong view has fallen under the sway of Māra, a bhikkhu, having known rise and fall through wise attention, should have right view as his forerunner. Because a mind struck by sloth and torpor has fallen under the sway of Māra, a bhikkhu should overcome sloth and torpor by means of energy. Such a bhikkhu would abandon, will abandon, all bad destinations.

“Tassaṃ gāthāyaṃ kathaṃ yuttibhāvo vicāretabbo”ti vattabbattā “tasmā rakkhitacittassā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Rakkhitacittassa sammāsaṅkappagocaro bhavissatīti attho yujjati eva, no na yujjati. Micchāsaṅkappānampi jahitattā sammādiṭṭhipurekkhāro hutvā viharanto udayabbayaṃ paṭivijjhissatīti attho yujjati sammādiṭṭhipurekkhārassa udayabbayānupassanāsambhavato. Udayabbayaṃ paṭivijjhanto sabbā duggatiyo jahissatīti attho [M 0.0242] yujjati udayabbayānupassanānukkamena ariyamaggasambhavato. Sabbā duggatiyo jahanto sabbāni duggativinipātabhayāni samatikkamissatīti attho yujjati sabbesaṃ duggativinipātabhayānaṃ anuppajjanato.

Because it must be said, 'How is the logical coherence in that verse to be examined?' the verse beginning 'Therefore, for one with a guarded mind' was stated. The meaning 'For one with a guarded mind, right intention will be his pasture' is logical; it is not illogical. The meaning 'Having abandoned wrong intentions, dwelling with right view as his forerunner, he will penetrate rise and fall' is logical, because for one with right view as his forerunner, the contemplation of rise and fall is possible. The meaning 'Penetrating rise and fall, he will abandon all bad destinations' is logical, because the noble path can arise in sequence from the contemplation of rise and fall. The meaning 'Abandoning all bad destinations, he will overcome all fears of downfall into a bad destination' is logical, because all fears of downfall into a bad destination will not arise.

“Ettakova yuttihārasampāto paripuṇṇo”ti vattabbattā “niyutto yuttihārasampāto”ti vuttaṃ. Yena yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūtena yuttihārasampātena suttappadesatthānaṃ yuttibhāvo vicāretabbo[V 0.0364], so so saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūto yuttihārasampāto niyutto yathārahaṃ niddhāretvā yujjitabboti attho gahetabboti.

Because it can be said, 'The application of the Reasoning method is complete just to this extent,' it is stated, 'The application of the Reasoning method is established.' The meaning to be grasped is this: by whatever specific mode of explanation, which is an application of the Reasoning method, the logical coherence of the meanings of the sutta passages is to be examined, that specific mode of explanation, which is an application of the Reasoning method, is established. It should be determined and applied as is appropriate.

Iti yuttihārasampāte sattibalānurūpā racitā

Thus is composed the section on the application of the Reasoning method, in accordance with my ability and strength.

Vibhāvanā niṭṭhitā.

The Elucidation is finished.

Paṇḍitehi pana…pe… gahetabboti.

But it should be understood by the wise... (and so on)...

4. Padaṭṭhānahārasampātavibhāvanā

4. Elucidation of the Application of the Method of the Proximate Cause

66. Yena yena yuttihārasampātena suttappadesatthānaṃ yuttibhāvo ācariyena vibhāvito, amhehi ca ñāto, so yuttihārasampāto paripuṇṇo, “katamo padaṭṭhānahārasampāto”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha katamo padaṭṭhāno hārasampāto”ti pucchati.

66. By whatever application of the method of reasoning the logical coherence of the meanings of the sutta passages was explained by the teacher and known by us, that application of the method of reasoning is complete. Since it should be asked, 'What is the application of the method of the proximate cause?' he asks, 'Here, what is the application of the method of the proximate cause?'

Pucchitvā yasmiṃ suttappadese vuttāni padaṭṭhānāni nīharitāni, taṃ suttappadesaṃ nīharituṃ “tasmā rakkhitacittassa, sammāsaṅkappagocaroti gāthā”ti vuttā. Gāthāttho vuttova. “Katame gāthātthā katamesaṃ dhammānaṃ padaṭṭhānānī”ti pucchitabbattā “tasmā rakkhitacittassā”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Tasmā rakkhitacittassā”ti suttappadesassa atthabhūtā indriyesu guttadvāratā tiṇṇaṃ sucaritānaṃ padaṭṭhānaṃ nāma sucaritapāripūriyā āsannakāraṇattā. “Sammāsaṅkappagocaro”ti suttappadesassa atthabhūtā nekkhammasaṅkappādayo sammāsaṅkappā samathassa padaṭṭhānaṃ nāma kāmacchandaādinīvaraṇavikkhambhanassa āsannakāraṇattā. “Sammādiṭṭhipurekkhāro”ti suttappadesassa atthabhūtā kammassakatāsammādiṭṭhi ca sappaccayanāmarūpadassanasammādiṭṭhi [M 0.0243] ca vipassanāya padaṭṭhānaṃ nāma aniccānupassanādīnaṃ visesakāraṇattā. “Ñatvāna udayabbaya”nti suttappadesassa atthabhūtā udayabbayānupassanāpaññā dassanabhūmiyā padaṭṭhānaṃ nāma paṭhamamaggādhigamassa āsannakāraṇattā. “Thinamiddhābhibhū bhikkhū”ti suttappadesassa atthabhūtaṃ thinamiddhābhibhavanaṃ vīriyassa padaṭṭhānaṃ nāma āsannakāraṇattā. “Sabbā duggatiyo jahe”ti suttappadesassa atthabhūtā pahātabbajahanabhāvanāya ariyamaggabhāvanāya padaṭṭhānaṃ nāma pahātabbappahānena ariyamaggabhāvanāpāripūrisambhavato.

Having asked, in order to present the sutta passage from which the proximate causes were drawn, the verse, 'Therefore, for one with a guarded mind, right intention is the domain,' is cited. The meaning of the verse has already been stated. Since it should be asked, 'What are the meanings of the verse? Of which phenomena are they the proximate causes?' the passage beginning 'Therefore, for one with a guarded mind' is cited. The meaning of the passage 'Therefore, for one with a guarded mind' is that guarding the sense doors is the proximate cause for the three kinds of good conduct, because it is the immediate cause for the fulfillment of good conduct. The meaning of the passage 'right intention is the domain' is that right intentions, such as the intention of renunciation, are the proximate cause for serenity, because they are the immediate cause for the suppression of the hindrances such as sensual desire. The meaning of the passage 'With right view as a forerunner' is that the right view of the ownership of kamma and the right view that sees name-and-form with its conditions are the proximate cause for insight, because they are the specific cause for the contemplation of impermanence and so on. The meaning of the passage 'Having known the arising and passing away' is that the wisdom that contemplates arising and passing away is the proximate cause for the stage of vision, because it is the immediate cause for the attainment of the first path. The meaning of the passage 'A bhikkhu overcoming sloth and torpor' is that the overcoming of sloth and torpor is the proximate cause for energy, because it is the immediate cause. The meaning of the passage 'He would abandon all bad destinations' is that this is the proximate cause for the development of abandoning what is to be abandoned and for the development of the noble path, because the fulfillment of the development of the noble path comes about through the abandoning of what is to be abandoned.

“Ettakova [V 0.0365] padaṭṭhānahārasampāto paripuṇṇo”ti vattabbattā “niyutto padaṭṭhāno hārasampāto”ti vuttaṃ. Yena yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūtena padaṭṭhānahārasampātabhūtena suttappadesatthāni padaṭṭhānāni nīharitāni, so so saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūto padaṭṭhānahārasampāto niyutto yathārahaṃ niddhāretvā yujjitabboti attho gahetabboti.

Because it can be said, 'The application of the method of the proximate cause is complete just to this extent,' it is stated, 'The application of the method of the proximate cause is established.' The meaning to be grasped is this: by whatever specific mode of explanation, which is an application of the method of the proximate cause, the proximate causes, which are the meanings of the sutta passages, are drawn out, that specific mode of explanation, which is an application of the method of the proximate cause, is established and should be determined and applied as is appropriate.

Iti padaṭṭhānahārasampāte sattibalānurūpā racitā

Thus is composed the section on the application of the method of the proximate cause, in accordance with my ability and strength.

Vibhāvanā niṭṭhitā.

The Elucidation is finished.

Paṇḍitehi pana…pe… gahetabboti.

But it should be understood by the wise... (and so on)...

5. Lakkhaṇahārasampātavibhāvanā

5. Elucidation of the Application of the Method of the Characteristic

67. Yena yena padaṭṭhānahārasampātena suttappadesatthāni padaṭṭhānāni ācariyena niddhāritāni, amhehi ca ñātāni, so padaṭṭhānahārasampāto paripuṇṇo, “katamo lakkhaṇahārasampāto”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha katamo lakkhaṇo hārasampāto”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha tesu desanāhārasampātādīsu soḷasasu hārasampātesu katamo saṃvaṇṇanāviseso lakkhaṇahārasampāto nāmāti pucchati.

67. By whatever confluence of the method of the proximate cause the proximate causes, which are the meanings of the sutta passages, were determined by the teacher and known by us, that confluence of the method of the proximate cause is complete. Since it should be asked, 'What is the confluence of the method of the characteristic?' the passage beginning, 'Here, what is the confluence of the method of the characteristic?' is stated. He asks: 'Here, among those sixteen confluences of the methods, beginning with the confluence of the method of teaching, what specific mode of exposition is called the confluence of the method of the characteristic?'

“Katamehi suttatthehi samānalakkhaṇā katame dhammā gahitā”ti pucchitabbattā “tasmā”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Tasmā rakkhitacittassa, sammāsaṅkappagocaro”ti suttappadesena vuttaṃ idaṃ rakkhaṇaṃ satindriyaṃ gahitaṃ, satindriye [M 0.0244] gahite saddhādipañcindriyāni gahitāni bhavanti indriyaṭṭhena samānalakkhaṇattā. “Sammādiṭṭhipurekkhāro”ti suttappadesena vuttā sammādiṭṭhi gahitā, sammādiṭṭhiyā gahitāya ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo gahito bhavati. Taṃ kissa hetūti kāraṇaṃ pucchati. Pucchitvā kāraṇamāha “sammādiṭṭhito hī”tiādinā. Sammādiṭṭhihetuto sammāsaṅkappo hi yasmā pabhavati, tasmā, sammāsaṅkappato sammāvācā hi yasmā pabhavati, tasmā, sammāvācāto sammākammanto hi yasmā pabhavati, tasmā, sammākammantato sammāājīvo hi yasmā pabhavati, tasmā, sammāājīvato sammāvāyāmo hi yasmā pabhavati, tasmā, sammāvāyāmato sammāsatihi yasmā pabhavati, tasmā, sammāsatito [V 0.0366] sammāsamādhi hi yasmā pabhavati, tasmā, sammāsamādhito sammāvimutti hi yasmā pabhavati, tasmā, sammāvimuttito sammāvimuttiñāṇadassanaṃ hi yasmā pabhavati, tasmā, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo gahito bhavatīti.

Since it should be asked, 'By which meanings of the sutta are which phenomena with a common characteristic grasped?' the passage beginning 'Therefore' is stated. By the sutta passage, 'Therefore, for one with a guarded mind, right intention is the domain,' this guarding, the faculty of mindfulness, is grasped. When the faculty of mindfulness is grasped, the five faculties beginning with faith are also grasped because they have a common characteristic in the sense of being faculties. By the sutta passage, 'With right view as a forerunner,' right view is grasped. When right view is grasped, the Noble Eightfold Path is grasped. 'For what reason?'—the cause is asked. Having asked, he states the cause with the passage beginning, 'For from right view....' For right intention arises from right view; from right intention, right speech arises; from right speech, right action arises; from right action, right livelihood arises; from right livelihood, right effort arises; from right effort, right mindfulness arises; from right mindfulness, right concentration arises; from right concentration, right liberation arises; and from right liberation, right knowledge and vision of liberation arises. Therefore, the Noble Eightfold Path is grasped.

“Ettakova lakkhaṇahārasampāto paripuṇṇo”ti vattabbattā “niyutto lakkhaṇo hārasampāto”ti vuttaṃ. Yena yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūtena lakkhaṇahārasampātena suttappadesatthā samānalakkhaṇena gahitā bhavanti, so so saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūto lakkhaṇahārasampāto niyutto yathārahaṃ niddhāretvā yujjitabboti attho gahitoti.

Since it can be said, 'To this extent the confluence of the method of the characteristic is complete,' it is stated, 'The confluence of the method of the characteristic is established.' The meaning to be grasped is this: By whatever specific mode of exposition, which is the confluence of the method of the characteristic, the meanings of the sutta passages are grasped by way of a common characteristic, that specific mode of exposition, the confluence of the method of the characteristic, is established and should be determined and applied as is fitting.

Iti lakkhaṇahārasampāte sattibalānurūpā racitā

Thus is composed, in accordance with my ability and strength, the explanation on the confluence of the method of the characteristic.

Vibhāvanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation is concluded.

Paṇḍitehi pana…pe… gahetabboti.

But by the wise... (and so on)... should be grasped.

6. Catubyūhahārasampātavibhāvanā

6. Elucidation of the Confluence of the Fourfold Method

68. Yena yena lakkhaṇahārasampātena suttappadesatthā samānalakkhaṇena gahitā, so lakkhaṇahārasampāto paripuṇṇo, “katamo catubyūhahārasampāto”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha katamo catubyūho hārasampāto”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha tesu desanāhārasampātādīsu soḷasasu hārasampātesu katamo saṃvaṇṇanāviseso catubyūhahārasampāto nāmāti pucchati.

68. By whatever confluence of the method of the characteristic the meanings of the sutta passages are grasped by means of a similar characteristic, that confluence of the method of the characteristic is complete. Because it should be asked, 'Which is the confluence of the fourfold method?' the text beginning 'Therein, which is the confluence of the fourfold method?' was stated. Therein, among those sixteen confluences of the methods, beginning with the confluence of the method of teaching, it is asked what particular explanation is called the confluence of the fourfold method.

“Katamasmiṃ [M 0.0245] sutte katame nirutyādhippāyanidānapubbāparānusandhayo niddhāritā”ti pucchitabbattā “tasmā”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Tasmā rakkhitacittassā”ti suttappadese “rakkhīyate rakkhita”nti niruttiṃ “paripālīyatī”ti iminā pariyāyena dasseti, itisaddassa ādyatthattā “cintetīti cittaṃ, attano santānaṃ cinotīti cittaṃ, paccayehi citanti cittaṃ, cittavicittaṭṭhena cittaṃ, cittakaraṇaṭṭhena cittaṃ, rakkhitaṃ cittaṃ yassāti rakkhitacitto. Sammā saṅkappetīti sammāsaṅkappo, gāvo caranti etthāti gocaro, gocaro viyāti gocaro, sammāsaṅkappo gocaro assāti sammāsaṅkappagocaro. Sammā passatīti sammādiṭṭhi, sammādiṭṭhi purekkhāro [V 0.0367] assāti sammādiṭṭhipurekkhāro. Jānātīti ñatvāna. Udayo ca vayo ca udayabbayaṃ. Thinañca middhañca thinamiddhaṃ, abhibhavatīti abhibhū, thinamiddhaṃ abhibhūti thinamiddhābhibhū. Bhikkhatīti bhikkhū”ti niruttipi nīharitā. Tenāha – “iti-saddo ādyattho”ti (netti. aṭṭha. 68). Esā vuttappakārā paññatti nirutti nāmāti nīharitā.

Because it should be asked, 'In which sutta are which etymology, intention, origin, and sequential connection determined?' the text beginning 'Therefore...' was stated. In the sutta passage 'Therefore, for one with a guarded mind...' the etymology of 'guarded' (rakkhita) as 'it is guarded' (rakkhīyate) is shown by the synonym 'it is protected' (paripālīyati). Because the word `iti` has the sense of 'and so on,' the etymologies are also extracted thus: 'It thinks (cinteti), therefore it is mind (citta); it accumulates (cinoti) its own continuity, therefore it is mind; it is variegated (cita) by conditions, therefore it is mind; it is mind in the sense of being variegated (citta); it is mind in the sense of producing variegation (cittakaraṇa); one whose mind is guarded is a `rakkhitacitto`. One who intends rightly is `sammāsaṅkappo`. Cows (gāvo) roam (caranti) there (ettha), thus it is a pasture (gocaro); like a pasture, thus `gocaro`; one for whom right intention is the pasture is a `sammāsaṅkappagocaro`. One who sees rightly is `sammādiṭṭhi`; one for whom right view is the forerunner is a `sammādiṭṭhipurekkhāro`. Having known is `ñatvāna`. Arising and passing away is `udayabbayaṃ`. Sloth and torpor is `thinamiddhaṃ`; one who overcomes is `abhibhū`; one who overcomes sloth and torpor is a `thinamiddhābhibhū`. One who begs is a `bhikkhu`.' Thus the etymology is extracted. Therefore he said: 'The word `iti` has the sense of "and so on"' (Netti-aṭṭha. 68). This designation of the kind stated is extracted as 'etymology'.

Idha suttappadese bhagavato ko adhippāyoti ce puccheyya, ye sappurisā sabbāhi duggatīhi parimuccitukāmā bhavissanti, te sappurisā dhammacārino rakkhitacittā bhavissantīti ayaṃ adhippāyo. Ettha “tasmā rakkhitacittassā”tiādisuttappadese bhagavato adhippāyoti nīharitabbo.

If one should ask what the Blessed One's intention is here in this sutta passage, it is this: 'Those good persons who wish to be completely freed from all bad destinations will be righteous in conduct and have guarded minds'—this is the intention. Here, in the sutta passage beginning 'Therefore, for one with a guarded mind,' the intention of the Blessed One should be extracted.

“Katamaṃ nidāna”nti ce puccheyya, kokāliko sāriputtamoggallānesu theresu cittaṃ arakkhitvā padosayitvā mahāpadumaniraye yasmā upapanno, yasmā bhagavā ca satiārakkhena samannāgato sabbā duggatiyo jahati, tasmā ca sabbā duggatiyo jahitukāmo bhikkhu sappuriso rakkhitacitto assa bhaveyyāti nidānaṃ nīharitabbaṃ.

If one should ask, 'What is the origin?' it should be extracted thus: Because Kokālika, by not guarding his mind and by arousing malice toward the elders Sāriputta and Moggallāna, was reborn in the Great Paduma hell; and because the Blessed One, endowed with the protection of mindfulness, abandons all bad destinations; therefore a good person, a bhikkhu, who wishes to abandon all bad destinations should be one with a guarded mind. This is the origin to be extracted.

“Katamo pubbāparasandhī”ti ce puccheyya, suttamhi “satiyā cittaṃ rakkhitabba”nti yaṃ vacanaṃ vuttaṃ, tena pubbavacanena ayaṃ “tasmā rakkhitacittassa…pe… sabbā duggatiyo jahe”ti suttappadeso anusandhi saṃsandati sametīti pubbaparānusandhi niddhāritabboti.

If one should ask, 'What is the sequential connection?': In the sutta the statement was made, 'The mind should be guarded with mindfulness.' By that preceding statement, this sutta passage, 'Therefore, for one with a guarded mind … let him abandon all bad destinations,' connects, corresponds, and fits. Thus the sequential connection should be determined.

“Ettakova [M 0.0246] catubyūhahārasampāto paripuṇṇo”ti vattabbattā “niyutto catubyūho hārasampāto”ti vuttaṃ. Yena yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūtena catubyūhahārasampātena nirutyādhippāyanidānapubbāparānusandhi niddhāritabbo, so so saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūto catubyūhahārasampāto niyutto yathārahaṃ niddhāretvā yujjitabboti attho gahetabboti.

Because it should be said, 'To this extent the confluence of the fourfold method is complete,' the words 'the applied confluence of the fourfold method' were stated. The meaning to be grasped is this: By whatever specific mode of exposition, which is the confluence of the fourfold method, etymology, intention, origin, and sequential connection are to be determined, that very specific mode of exposition, the confluence of the fourfold method, is established, and should be determined and employed as is fitting.

Iti catubyūhahārasampāte sattibalānurūpā racitā

Thus, in the matter of the confluence of the fourfold method, this was composed in accordance with my strength and ability.

Vibhāvanā niṭṭhitā.

The Elucidation is finished.

Paṇḍitehi pana…pe… gahetabboti.

But by the wise ... (and so on) ... should be understood.

7. Āvaṭṭahārasampātavibhāvanā

7. Elucidation of the Confluence of the Revolving Method

69. Yena [V 0.0368] yena catubyūhahārasampātena nirutyādhippāyanidānapubbāparānusandhayo vibhattā, so catubyūhahārasampāto paripuṇṇo, “katamo āvaṭṭahārasampāto”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha katamo āvaṭṭo hārasampāto”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha katamo saṃvaṇṇanāviseso āvaṭṭahārasampāto nāmāti pucchati.

69. By whatever confluence of the fourfold method etymology, intention, origin, and sequential connection are analyzed, that confluence of the fourfold method is complete. Because it should be asked, 'Which is the confluence of the revolving method?' the text beginning 'Therein, which is the confluence of the revolving method?' was stated. Therein, it is asked what particular explanation is called the confluence of the revolving method.

“Katame suttatthā kathaṃ āvaṭṭetabbā”ti pucchitabbattā “tasmā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Nekkhammasaṅkappasaṅkhātasammāsaṅkappabahulo kasiṇādivasena, avihiṃsāsaṅkappasaṅkhātasammāsaṅkappabahulo mettādivasena adhigatāya cittekaggatāya cittaṃ ṭhapento saṃkilesato rakkhitacitto nāma hoti, “tasmā rakkhitacittassa, sammāsaṅkappagocaro”ti iminā rakkhitacitte vutte sati yā ekaggatā āvaṭṭetabbā, sā ayaṃ ekaggatā samatho. “Sammādiṭṭhipurekkhāro”ti iminā sammādiṭṭhipurekkhāre vutte sati yā paññā āvaṭṭetabbā, sā ayaṃ paññā vipassanā. “Ñatvāna udayabbaya”nti iminā udayabbayañāṇasamannāgate vutte sati yā dukkhaparijānanā āvaṭṭetabbā, sā ayaṃ dukkhaparijānanā dukkhapariññā. “Thinamiddhābhibhū bhikkhū”ti iminā puggalādhiṭṭhānena yaṃ thinamiddhābhibhavanaṃ vuttaṃ, idaṃ thinamiddhābhibhavanaṃ samudayappahānaṃ. “Sammā duggatiyo jahe”ti iminā yo sabbaduggatijahanasaṅkhāto anuppādo vutto, so ayaṃ anuppādo [M 0.0247] nirodho. Iti dukkhapariññāya pariññetabbaṃ dukkhasaccaṃ āvaṭṭetabbaṃ, samudayappahānena pahātabbaṃ samudayasaccaṃ āvaṭṭetabbaṃ, nirodhena nirodhasaccaṃ āvaṭṭetabbaṃ, samathavipassanāhi maggasaccaṃ āvaṭṭetabbanti imāni cattāri saccāni āvaṭṭetabbānīti.

Because it should be asked, 'Which meanings of the sutta should be revolved, and how?' the text beginning 'Therefore...' was stated. One who is abundant in right intention, identified as the intention of renunciation, by means of the kasiṇas, etc., or abundant in right intention, identified as the intention of non-harming, by means of loving-kindness, etc., by establishing the mind in the concentration attained, is called 'one with a guarded mind.' When 'one with a guarded mind' is stated in the phrase 'Therefore, for one with a guarded mind, whose pasture is right intention,' the concentration that should be revolved is this concentration, which is serenity (samatha). When 'one for whom right view is the forerunner' is stated, the wisdom that should be revolved is this wisdom, which is insight (vipassanā). When one endowed with the knowledge of arising and passing away is stated in the phrase 'having known the arising and passing away,' the full understanding of suffering that should be revolved is this full understanding of suffering, which is the full comprehension of suffering (dukkhapariññā). When the overcoming of sloth and torpor is stated by means of the individual-basis in 'a bhikkhu who has overcome sloth and torpor,' this overcoming of sloth and torpor is the abandoning of the origin (samudayappahāna). When the non-arising, referred to as the abandoning of all bad destinations, is stated in 'he would rightly abandon all bad destinations,' this non-arising is cessation (nirodha). Thus, the truth of suffering, which is to be fully comprehended by the full comprehension of suffering, should be revolved; the truth of the origin, which is to be abandoned by the abandoning of the origin, should be revolved; the truth of cessation should be revolved by means of cessation; the truth of the path should be revolved by means of serenity and insight. These are the four truths that should be revolved.

“Ettakova āvaṭṭo hārasampāto paripuṇṇo”ti vattabbattā “niyutto āvaṭṭo hārasampāto”ti vuttaṃ. Yena yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūtena āvaṭṭahārasampātena samathādayo āvaṭṭetabbā[V 0.0369], so so saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūto āvaṭṭahārasampāto niyutto yathārahaṃ niddhāretvā yujjitabboti attho gahetabboti.

Because it should be said, 'To this extent the confluence of the revolving method is complete,' the words 'the applied confluence of the revolving method' were stated. The meaning to be understood is this: by whatever confluence of the revolving method, which is a special explanation, serenity and so on are to be revolved, that very confluence of the revolving method, which is a special explanation, is 'applied'; that is, it should be employed after having been determined to be appropriate.

Iti āvaṭṭahārasampāte sattibalānurūpā racitā

Thus, in the matter of the confluence of the revolving method, this was composed in accordance with my strength and ability.

Vibhāvanā niṭṭhitā.

The Elucidation is finished.

Paṇḍitehi pana…pe… gahetabboti.

But by the wise ... (and so on) ... should be understood.

8. Vibhattihārasampātavibhāvanā

8. Elucidation of the Concurrence of the Guideline of Division

70. Yena yena āvaṭṭahārasampātena suttatthā āvaṭṭetabbā, so āvaṭṭahārasampāto paripuṇṇo, “katamo vibhattihārasampāto”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha katamo vibhattihārasampāto”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha katamo saṃvaṇṇanāviseso vibhattihārasampāto nāmāti pucchati.

70. The concurrence of the guideline of revolving, by which the meanings of the suttas are to be revolved, is complete. Because the question, 'What is the concurrence of the guideline of division?' should be asked, the passage beginning, 'Therein, what is the concurrence of the guideline of division?' was stated. Therein, one asks: 'What particular kind of exposition is this thing called the concurrence of the guideline of division?'

“Katame suttatthā kattha vibhattā”ti pucchitabbattā “tasmā rakkhitacittassā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yā “tasmā…pe… gocaro”ti gāthā vuttā, tissaṃ gāthāyaṃ vutto kusalapakkho dhammo kusalapakkhena dhammena satisaṃvaro dhammo niddisitabbo vibhajitabbo, akusalapakkhena dhammena niddisitabbo vibhajitabbo.

Because the question, 'Which meanings of the suttas are analyzed where?' should be asked, the passage beginning, 'Therefore, for one with a guarded mind...' was stated. The verse that was stated begins, 'Therefore ... pasture.' In this verse, the dhamma mentioned that is on the wholesome side—the dhamma of restraint by mindfulness—should be indicated and analyzed by means of a dhamma on the wholesome side; and [the corresponding dhamma on the unwholesome side] should be indicated and analyzed by means of a dhamma on the unwholesome side.

Kathaṃ? “Rakkhitacittassā”ti padena vutto kusalapakkho satisaṃvaro dhammo “cakkhudvārasaṃvaro…pe… manodvārasaṃvaro”ti chabbidhena kusalapakkhena dhammena niddisitabbo vibhajitabbo. “Sammāsaṅkappo”ti padena vutto kusalapakkho sammāsaṅkappo dhammo “nekkhammasaṅkappo abyāpāda-saṅkappo avihiṃsāsaṅkappo”ti tividhena kusalapakkhena dhammena [M 0.0248] vibhajitabbo. “Sammādiṭṭhipurekkhāro”ti padena vuttā kusalapakkhā dhammajāti “dukkhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminipaṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ, pubbante ñāṇaṃ, aparante ñāṇaṃ, pubbantāparante ñāṇaṃ, idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu ñāṇa”nti (dha. sa. 1063) aṭṭhavidhena kusalapakkhena dhammena vibhajitabbā. “Ñatvāna udayabbaya”nti padena vuttaṃ kusalapakkhaudayabbayañāṇaṃ dhammajātaṃ paññāsavidhena udayabbayañāṇena kusalapakkhena vibhajitabbaṃ. “Thinamiddhābhibhū”ti padena vuttaṃ thinamiddhābhibhavanaṃ kusalapakkhaṃ dhammajātaṃ “sotāpattimaggābhibhavanaṃ [V 0.0370] sakadāgāmimaggābhibhavanaṃ anāgāmimaggābhibhavanaṃ arahattamaggābhibhavana”nti catubbidhena kusalapakkhena vibhajitabbaṃ.

How so? The dhamma on the wholesome side, restraint by mindfulness, mentioned by the term 'for one with a guarded mind,' should be indicated and analyzed in six ways by means of a dhamma on the wholesome side: 'restraint of the eye-door ... restraint of the mind-door.' The dhamma on the wholesome side, right intention, mentioned by the term 'right intention,' should be analyzed in three ways by means of a dhamma on the wholesome side: 'intention of renunciation, intention of non-ill will, and intention of non-cruelty.' The kinds of dhammas on the wholesome side mentioned by the term 'preceded by right view' should be analyzed in eight ways by means of a dhamma on the wholesome side: 'knowledge of suffering, knowledge of the origin of suffering, knowledge of the cessation of suffering, knowledge of the path leading to the cessation of suffering, knowledge of the past, knowledge of the future, knowledge of the past and future, and knowledge of dhammas that are dependently arisen based on specific conditionality' (Dhs §1063). The kind of dhamma that is the wholesome knowledge of rise and fall, mentioned by the term 'having known rise and fall,' should be analyzed by the fifty kinds of wholesome knowledge of rise and fall. The kind of wholesome dhamma that is the overcoming of sloth and torpor, mentioned by the term 'having overcome sloth and torpor,' should be analyzed in four ways by means of a wholesome dhamma: 'overcoming by the path of stream-entry, overcoming by the path of once-returning, overcoming by the path of non-returning, and overcoming by the path of arahantship.'

Satisaṃvaro kusalapakkho “lokiyo satisaṃvaro, lokuttaro satisaṃvaro”ti dubbidhena vibhajitabboti. Lokiyo satisaṃvaro kāmāvacarovāti ekavidhena vibhajitabbo. Lokuttarā satisaṃvaro “dassanabhūmi, bhāvanābhūmī”ti dubbidhena vibhajitabbo. Kāmāvacaro satisaṃvaro “kāyānupassanāsatisaṃvaro vedanānupassanāsatisaṃvaro cittānupassanāsatisaṃvaro dhammānupassanāsatisaṃvaro”ti catubbidhena vibhajitabbo. Lokuttaro satisaṃvaropi tathā catubbidhena vibhajitabbo. Sammāsaṅkappasammādiṭṭhiyopi lokiyalokuttaravasena dubbidhādibhedena vibhajitabbā. Padaṭṭhānenapi padaṭṭhānahārasampāte vuttanayena vibhajitabbā.

Restraint by mindfulness, on the wholesome side, should be analyzed in two ways: as mundane restraint by mindfulness and supramundane restraint by mindfulness. Mundane restraint by mindfulness, being of the sense-sphere, should be analyzed in one way. Supramundane restraint by mindfulness should be analyzed in two ways: as the plane of vision and the plane of development. Sense-sphere restraint by mindfulness should be analyzed in four ways: as restraint by mindfulness through contemplation of the body, restraint by mindfulness through contemplation of feelings, restraint by mindfulness through contemplation of mind, and restraint by mindfulness through contemplation of dhammas. Supramundane restraint by mindfulness should also be analyzed similarly in four ways. Right intention and right view should also be analyzed with twofold and other divisions based on whether they are mundane or supramundane. They should also be analyzed by way of the proximate cause according to the method stated in the Concurrence of the Guideline of the Proximate Cause.

Akusalapakkhena “arakkhitena cittenā”ti padena vutto asaṃvaro “cakkhuasaṃvaro …pe… kāyaasaṃvaro, copanakāyaasaṃvaro, vācāasaṃvaro, manoasaṃvaro”ti aṭṭhavidhena vibhajitabbo. “Micchādiṭṭhihatenā”ti padena gahito micchāsaṅkappo “kāmavitakko byāpādavitakko vihiṃsāvitakko”ti tividhena vibhajitabbo. “Micchādiṭṭhī”ti padena vuttā micchādiṭṭhi “dukkhe aññāṇaṃ…pe…idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu aññāṇa”nti aṭṭhavidhena vibhajitabbā, dvāsaṭṭhidiṭṭhividhenapi vibhajitabbā. Thinamiddhaṃ pañcavidhena sasaṅkhārikavidhena vibhajitabbaṃ.

On the unwholesome side: non-restraint, mentioned by the term 'with an unguarded mind,' should be analyzed in eight ways: 'non-restraint of the eye ... non-restraint of the body, non-restraint of bodily agitation, non-restraint of speech, non-restraint of mind.' Wrong intention, which is taken by the term 'slain by wrong view,' should be analyzed in three ways: 'sensual thought, thought of ill will, and thought of cruelty.' Wrong view, mentioned by the term 'wrong view,' should be analyzed in eight ways: 'ignorance regarding suffering ... ignorance regarding dhammas that are dependently arisen based on specific conditionality'; it should also be analyzed in sixty-two ways according to the kinds of views. Sloth and torpor should be analyzed in five ways, by the classification of that which is prompted.

“Ettakova vibhattihārasampāto paripuṇṇo”ti vattabbattā “niyutto vibhattihārasampāto”ti vuttaṃ. Yena yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūtena vibhattihārasampātena suttappadesatthā vibhattā, so so [M 0.0249] saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūto vibhattihārasampāto niyuttoti yathāraha niddhāretvā yujjitabboti attho gahetabboti.

Because it can be said, 'The concurrence of the guideline of division is complete just to this extent,' it is called 'the applied concurrence of the guideline of division.' The meaning should be understood thus: by whatever concurrence of the guideline of division, which is a particular kind of exposition, the meanings of sutta passages are analyzed, that very concurrence of the guideline of division, which is a particular kind of exposition, is 'applied'; that is, it should be employed after having ascertained it to be suitable.

Iti vibhattihārasampāte sattibalānurūpā racitā

Thus, in the Elucidation of the Concurrence of the Guideline of Division, this was composed in accordance with my strength and ability.

Vibhāvanā niṭṭhitā.

The Elucidation is finished.

Paṇḍitehi pana…pe… gahetabboti.

But by the wise ... (as before) ... should be understood.

9. Parivattanahārasampātavibhāvanā

9. Elucidation of the Concurrence of the Guideline of Transformation

71. Yena [V 0.0371] yena vibhattihārasampātena suttappadesatthā vibhattā, so vibhattihārasampāto paripuṇṇo, “katamo parivattanahārasampāto”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha katamo parivattano hārasampāto”tiādi vuttaṃ.

71. The concurrence of the guideline of division, by which the meanings of the sutta passages are analyzed, is complete. Because the question, 'What is the concurrence of the guideline of transformation?' should be asked, the text states: 'Therein, what is the concurrence of the guideline of transformation?' and so on.

“Katame suttappadesatthā kathaṃ parivattetabbā”ti pucchitabbattā “tasmā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yā “tasmā…pe… gocaro”ti gāthā vuttā, tāya gāthāya yā samathavipassanā niddhāritā, tāya samathavipassanāya bhāvitāya akusalānaṃ nirodho phalaṃ payojanaṃ hoti, pariññātaṃ dukkhaṃ hoti, samudayo pahīno hoti, maggo bhāvito hotīti parivattetabbo. Paṭipakkhena pana samathavipassanāya abhāvitāya akusalānaṃ anirodho, apariññātaṃ dukkhaṃ, samudayo appahīno, maggo abhāvito hotīti parivattetabbo.

Since the question, 'How are the meanings of the sutta passages to be transformed?' is to be asked, the text states: 'Therefore,' and so on. Regarding the verse that was stated, 'Therefore ... pasture,' by that verse serenity and insight are determined. When that serenity and insight are developed, the cessation of unwholesome states is the fruit and benefit, suffering comes to be fully understood, the origin comes to be abandoned, and the path comes to be developed—thus it should be transformed. Conversely, when serenity and insight are undeveloped, there is no cessation of unwholesome states, suffering is not fully understood, the origin is not abandoned, and the path is not developed—thus it should be transformed.

“Ettakova parivattanahārasampāto paripuṇṇo”ti vattabbattā “niyutto parivattano hārasampāto”ti vuttaṃ. Yena yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūtena parivattanahārasampātena suttappadesatthā parivattetabbā, so so saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūto parivattanahārasampāto niyutto yathārahaṃ nīharitvā yujjitabboti attho gahetabboti.

Since it should be said, 'To this extent the application of the method of transformation is complete,' the text states: 'The application of the method of transformation is concluded.' The meaning should be grasped thus: by whatever specific exposition constituting the application of the method of transformation the meanings of the sutta passages are to be transformed, that specific exposition, the application of the method of transformation, is concluded, to be extracted and applied as is fitting.

Iti parivattanahārasampāte sattibalānurūpā racitā

Thus was composed, in accordance with my ability and strength, the section on the application of the method of transformation.

Vibhāvanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation is finished.

Paṇḍitehi pana…pe… gahetabboti.

But by the wise ... (as before) ... it should be understood.

10. Vevacanahārasampātavibhāvanā

10. The Explanation of the Application of the Method of Synonyms

72. Yena [M 0.0250] yena parivattanahārasampātena suttappadesatthā parivattetabbā, so parivattano hārasampātoti paripuṇṇo, “katamo vevacano hārasampāto”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha katamo vevacano hārasampāto”tiādi vuttaṃ.

72. The application of the method of transformation, by which the meanings of the sutta passages are to be transformed, is now complete. Since the question, 'What is the application of the method of synonyms?' is to be asked, the text states: 'Therein, what is the application of the method of synonyms?' and so on.

“Katamesaṃ [V 0.0372] suttappadesatthānaṃ, suttapadānaṃ vā katamāni vevacanānī”ti pucchitabbattā “tasmā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yā “tasmā…pe… gocaro”ti gāthā vuttā, tāya gāthāya “rakkhitacittassā”ti padena vuttassa cittassa, “rakkhitacittassā”ti ettha cittassa padassa vā “cittaṃ…pe… vijānitatta”nti yaṃ vacanaṃ vuttaṃ, idaṃ vacanaṃ vevacanaṃ, “mānasaṃ hadaya”ntiādivacanampi (dha. sa. 17, 63) cittassa vevacanaṃ. “Sammāsaṅkappagocaro”ti ettha sammāsaṅkappassa “nekkhammasaṅkappo abyāpādasaṅkappo avihiṃsāsaṅkappo”ti yaṃ vacanaṃ vuttaṃ, idaṃ vacanaṃ vevacanaṃ, “takko vitakko”tiādi (dha. sa. 7) vacanampi sammāsaṅkappassa vevacanaṃ. “Sammādiṭṭhipurekkhāro”ti ettha sammādiṭṭhipadassa “sammādiṭṭhi nāma paññāsatthaṃ paññākhaggo paññāratanaṃ paññāpatodo paññāpāsādo”ti yaṃ vacanaṃ vuttaṃ, idaṃ vacanaṃ vevacanaṃ, “paññā pajānanā vicayo”tiādi (dha. sa. 16) vacanampi sammādiṭṭhipadassa vevacanaṃ. “Thinaṃ thiyanā thiyitattaṃ cittassa, cittassa akallatā akammaññatā onāho pariyonāho antosaṅkoco”ti (dha. sa. 1162-1163) yaṃ vacanaṃ vuttaṃ, idaṃ vacanaṃ thinassa vevacanaṃ. “Kāyassa akallatā akammaññatā kāyālasiyaṃ soppaṃ supanā suppitatta”nti (dha. sa. 1163) yaṃ vacanaṃ vuttaṃ, idaṃ vacanaṃ middhassa vevacanaṃ. “Bhikkhako bhikkhū”tiādikaṃ (pārā. 45; vibha. 510) yaṃ vacanaṃ vuttaṃ, idaṃ vacanaṃ bhikkhupadassa vevacanaṃ. “Duggati apāyo vinipāto vaṭṭadukkhaṃ saṃsāro”tiādikaṃ yaṃ vacanaṃ vuttaṃ, idaṃ vacanaṃ duggatipadassa vevacanaṃ. Iti vevacanāni nīharitāni.

Since the question, 'What are the synonyms for which meanings of sutta passages, or for which sutta terms?' is to be asked, the text states: 'Therefore,' and so on. Regarding the verse that was stated, 'Therefore ... pasture,' for the mind (citta) mentioned in the term 'of one with a guarded mind' (rakkhitacittassā), or for the term 'mind' (citta) itself, the statement 'mind ... the state of having known' is a synonym. The statement 'mentality, heart,' etc. (Dhs. 17, 63) is also a synonym for mind. Here, in 'whose pasture is right intention' (sammāsaṅkappagocaro), the statement 'intention of renunciation, intention of non-ill will, intention of non-harming' is a synonym for right intention. The statement 'thought, applied thought,' etc. (Dhs. 7) is also a synonym for right intention. Here, in 'with right view as a forerunner' (sammādiṭṭhipurekkhāro), for the term 'right view,' the statement 'right view is named the weapon of wisdom, the sword of wisdom, the jewel of wisdom, the goad of wisdom, the palace of wisdom' is a synonym. The statement 'wisdom, understanding, investigation,' etc. (Dhs. 16) is also a synonym for the term right view. The statement 'sloth: sluggishness, the state of being sluggish of the mind, unsuitability of mind, unwieldiness of mind, covering, enveloping, internal stupor' (Dhs. 1162–1163) is a synonym for sloth (thina). The statement 'unsuitability of the body, unwieldiness of the body, bodily laziness, drowsiness, sleep, the state of being asleep' (Dhs. 1163) is a synonym for torpor (middha). The statement 'a mendicant, a bhikkhu,' etc. (Pārā. 45; Vibh. 510) is a synonym for the term bhikkhu. The statement 'bad destination, plane of misery, downfall, the suffering of the round, saṃsāra,' etc. is a synonym for the term bad destination (duggati). Thus the synonyms have been extracted.

“Ettakova vevacanahārasampāto paripuṇṇo”ti vattabbattā “niyutto vevacano hārasampāto”ti vuttaṃ. Yena yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūtena vevacanahārasampātena vevacanāni nīharitāni, so so [M 0.0251] saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūto vevacanahārasampāto niyutto yathāsambhavaṃ nīharitvā yujjitabboti attho gahitoti.

Since it should be said, 'To this extent the application of the method of synonyms is complete,' the text states: 'The application of the method of synonyms is concluded.' The meaning should be grasped thus: by whatever specific exposition constituting the application of the method of synonyms the synonyms have been extracted, that specific exposition, the application of the method of synonyms, is concluded, to be extracted and applied as is possible.

Iti vevacanahārasampāte sattibalānurūpā racitā

Thus was composed, in accordance with my ability and strength, the section on the application of the method of synonyms.

Vibhāvanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation is finished.

Paṇḍitehi pana…pe… gahetabboti.

But by the wise ... (as before) ... it should be understood.

11. Paññattihārasampātavibhāvanā

11. The Explanation of the Application of the Method of Designation

73. Yena [V 0.0373] yena vevacanahārasampātena vevacanāni niddhāritāni, so vevacanahārasampāto paripuṇṇo, “katamo paññattihārasampāto”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha katamo paññattihārasampāto”tiādi vuttaṃ.

73. By whatever application of the method of synonyms the synonyms are determined, that application of the method of synonyms is complete. Because it should be asked, 'What is the application of the method of designation?,' it is said, 'Therein, what is the application of the method of designation?' and so on.

“Katamā suttappadesabhūtā paññatti katamesaṃ dhammānaṃ paññattī”ti pucchitabbattā “tasmā”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Tasmā rakkhitacittassā”ti paññatti satiyā padaṭṭhānassa rakkhitabbassa cittassa paññāpanato satiyā padaṭṭhānapaññatti nāma. Satiyā hi rakkhitabbaṃ cittaṃ satiyā padaṭṭhānaṃ adhiṭṭhānaṃ nāma. Tenāha aṭṭhakathāyaṃ – “adhiṭṭhahitvā rakkhantiyā satiyā rakkhiyamānaṃ cittaṃ tassā adhiṭṭhānaṃ viya hotī”ti. “Sammāsaṅkappagocaro”ti paññatti samathassa bhāvanāya paññāpanato samathassa bhāvanāpaññatti nāma. “Sammādiṭṭhipurekkhāro, ñatvāna udayabbaya”nti paññatti dassanabhūmiyā nikkhepassa paññāpanato nikkhepapaññatti nāma. “Thinamiddhābhibhū bhikkhū”ti samudayassa anavasesappahānassa paññāpanato anavasesappahānapaññatti nāma. “Sabbā duggatiyo jahe”ti paññatti maggassa ariyamaggassa bhāvanāya paññāpanato bhāvanāpaññatti nāma.

Because it should be asked, 'What designation is a sutta passage, and of what phenomena is it a designation?,' it is said, 'Therefore...' and so on. The designation 'Therefore, for one with a guarded mind' is called the designation of the proximate cause of mindfulness, because it designates the mind that is to be guarded as the proximate cause of mindfulness. For the mind to be guarded by mindfulness is the proximate cause of mindfulness, called a foundation (adhiṭṭhāna). Therefore, it is said in the commentary: 'The mind, being guarded by mindfulness that guards it after having made a resolution, is like its foundation.' The designation 'Having right intention as one's resort' is called the designation of the development of serenity, because it designates the development of serenity. The designation 'Having right view as a forerunner, having known arising and passing away' is called the designation of laying down, because it designates the laying down of the stage of vision. The designation 'A bhikkhu who has overcome sloth and torpor' is called the designation of abandoning without remainder, because it designates the abandoning without remainder of the origin. The designation 'One should abandon all bad destinations' is called the designation of development, because it designates the development of the path, the noble path.

“Ettakova paññattihārasampāto paripuṇṇo”ti vattabbattā “niyutto paññattihārasampāto”ti vuttaṃ. Yena yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūtena paññattihārasampātena paññattippabhedā niddhāritā, so so [M 0.0252] saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūto paññattihārasampāto niyutto yathārahaṃ niddhāretvā yujjitabboti attho gahetabboti.

Since it should be said, 'To this extent the application of the method of designation is complete,' the text states: 'The application of the method of designation is concluded.' The meaning should be grasped thus: by whatever specific exposition constituting the application of the method of designation the types of designation are determined, that specific exposition, the application of the method of designation, is concluded, to be determined and applied as is fitting.

Iti paññattihārasampāte sattibalānurūpā racitā

Thus was composed, in accordance with my ability and strength, the section on the application of the method of designation.

Vibhāvanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation is finished.

Paṇḍitehi pana…pe… gahetabboti.

But by the wise... (the rest as before) ... should be understood.

12. Otaraṇahārasampātavibhāvanā

12. The Explanation of the Application of the Method of Descending

74. Yena [V 0.0374] yena paññattihārasampātena paññattippabhedā niddhāritā, so paññattihārasampāto paripuṇṇo, “katamo otaraṇo hārasampāto”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha katamo otaraṇo hārasampāto”tiādimāha.

74. By whatever application of the method of designation the types of designation are determined, that application of the method of designation is complete. Because it should be asked, 'What is the application of the method of descending?,' he says, 'Therein, what is the application of the method of descending?' and so on.

“Tattha tissaṃ gāthāyaṃ katamāni indriyāni niddhāretvā katamehi niddhāritehi dhammehi otaratī”ti pucchitabbattā “tasmā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yā “tasmā rakkhitacittassā”tiādigāthā vuttā, tissaṃ gāthāyaṃ “tasmā…pe… purekkhāro”ti suttappadesena sammādiṭṭhi gahitā, sammādiṭṭhiyā gahitāya pañcindriyāni saddhādipañcindriyāni gahitāni bhavanti.

Because it should be asked: 'Therein, in that verse, having determined which faculties, by which determined phenomena does one descend?,' it is said, 'Therefore...' and so on. The verse beginning 'Therefore, for one with a guarded mind...' was stated. In that verse, by the sutta passage 'Therefore... (and so on)... forerunner,' right view is taken. When right view is taken, the five faculties—the five faculties beginning with faith—are taken.

Tāniyeva saddhādipañcindriyāni vijjāya upakārattā vā padaṭṭhānattā vā vijjā bhavanti, vijjuppādā tādisāya vijjāya uppādā uppādahetuto avijjānirodho sambhavati, avijjānirodhā saṅkhāranirodho sambhavati…pe… jātinirodhā jarāmaraṇanirodho sambhavatīti. Ayaṃ otaraṇā paṭiccasamuppādena pañcindriyānaṃ otaraṇā nāma.

Those very five faculties beginning with faith become knowledge either because they are helpful to knowledge or because they are its proximate cause. From the arising of knowledge, from the cause of the arising of such knowledge, the cessation of ignorance occurs; from the cessation of ignorance, the cessation of volitional formations occurs... (and so forth) ... from the cessation of birth, the cessation of aging-and-death occurs. This is called the descending of the five faculties by way of dependent origination.

Tāniyeva pañcindriyāni sīlakkhandhena samādhikkhandhena paññākkhandhena tīhi khandhehi saṅgahitāni bhavanti saddhāvīriyehi sīlasambhavato, satiyā ca paññānuvattakattā. Ayaṃ otaraṇā khandhehi pañcindriyānaṃ otaraṇā nāma.

Those same five faculties are included in the three aggregates—the aggregate of virtue, the aggregate of concentration, and the aggregate of wisdom. This is so on account of the arising of virtue through faith and energy, and because mindfulness follows after wisdom. This is called the descending of the five faculties by way of the aggregates.

Tāniyeva pañcindriyāni saṅkhārapariyāpannāni bhavanti. Ye saṅkhārā anāsavā bhavanti, bhavaṅgā bhavahetū no bhavanti, te anāsavā saṅkhārā dhammadhātusaṅgahitā bhavanti dhammadhātuyā antogadhattā. Ayaṃ otaraṇā dhātūhi pañcindriyānaṃ otaraṇā nāma.

Those same five faculties are included in volitional formations. Those volitional formations that are untainted—which, while being factors of existence, are not causes of existence—are included in the phenomena-element because they are comprised within the phenomena-element. This is called the descending of the five faculties by way of the elements.

Sā [M 0.0253] anāsavā dhammadhātu dhammāyatanapariyāpannā bhavati, yaṃ āyatanaṃ anāsavaṃ bhavati, bhavaṅgaṃ bhavahetu no bhavati. Ayaṃ otaraṇā āyatanehi dhammadhātuyā otaraṇā nāma.

That untainted phenomena-element is included in the phenomena-base, which base is untainted; it is a factor of existence but not a cause of existence. This is called the descending of the phenomena-element by way of the bases.

“Ettakova otaraṇo hārasampāto paripuṇṇo”ti vattabbattā “niyutto otaraṇo hārasampāto”ti [V 0.0375] vuttaṃ. Yena yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūtena otaraṇahārasampātena suttappadesatthā otaritabbā, so so saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūto otaraṇo hārasampāto niyutto yathārahaṃ niddhāretvā yujjitabboti attho gahetabboti.

Because it should be said, 'Just this much is the complete application of the descending method,' it is said, 'the established application of the descending method.' By whatever specific application of the descending method, which is a particular kind of exposition, the meanings of sutta passages are to be penetrated, that specific application of the descending method is established; having determined it as is suitable, it should be applied. This is the meaning to be understood.

Iti otaraṇahārasampāte sattibalānurūpā racitā

Thus is composed the explanation on the application of the descending method, in accordance with ability and strength.

Vibhāvanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation is finished.

Paṇḍitehi pana…pe… gahetabboti.

But by the wise... (the rest as before) ... should be understood.

Ito paṭṭhāya “tattha katamo”tiādianusandhyattho ca pariyosāne “niyutto”tiādianusandhyattho ca vuttanayānusāreneva viññātabbo. Katthaci katthaci pāṭhe apākaṭaṃyeva yathābalaṃ kathayissāma.

From this point onwards, the meaning of connecting phrases such as 'Therein, what...?' and of concluding connecting phrases such as 'established...' should be understood in accordance with the method already explained. In some places, where the text is unclear, we will explain it according to our ability.

13. Sodhanahārasampātavibhāvanā

13. Elucidation of the Coalescence of the Mode of Cleansing

75. Yatthāti yasmiṃ pañhe. Ārambho attho suddho paripuṇṇo, so pañho niravasesato vissajjito bhavati. Yattha pañhe pana ārambho attho na suddho aparipuṇṇo koci vissajjetabbo avasiṭṭho, so pañho tāva vissajjito na bhavati.

75. Where means: in whatever question. When the initial statement and its meaning are clear and complete, that question is answered without remainder. But in a question where the initial statement and its meaning are not clear and are incomplete, and something remains to be answered, that question is not yet answered.

15. Parikkhārahārasampātavibhāvanā

15. Elucidation of the Coalescence of the Mode of Requisites

77. “Tasmā rakkhitacittassā”ti padena yo satisaṃvaro vutto, ayaṃ satisaṃvaro samathassa parikkhāro. “Sammāsaṅkappagocaro”ti padena yo sammāsaṅkappo vutto, so sammāsaṅkappo vipassanāya parikkhāroti vibhajitvā yojetabbo.

77. By the phrase 'Therefore, of one with a guarded mind,' the restraint by mindfulness is stated; this restraint by mindfulness is the requisite for serenity. By the phrase 'having right intention as its domain,' right intention is stated; that right intention is the requisite for insight. Thus it should be applied by way of analysis.

16. Samāropanahārasampātavibhāvanā

16. Elucidation of the Coalescence of the Mode of Imputation

78. “Tasmā [V 0.0376][M 0.0254] rakkhitacittassā”ti padena yaṃ rakkhitacittaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ rakkhitacittaṃ tiṇṇaṃ sucaritānaṃ kammānaṃ padaṭṭhānaṃ. Sammādiṭṭhiyā bhāvitāya ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvito bhavati ekato bhāvitabbattā, padaṭṭhānakāraṇattā ca. Tena vuttaṃ – “sammādiṭṭhito hī”tiādi. Yassa arahato samādhivimutti bhavati, ayaṃ arahā anupādiseso puggalo, ayaṃ samādhivimutti anupādisesā nibbānadhātu.

78. By the phrase 'Therefore, of one with a guarded mind,' the guarded mind that is mentioned is the proximate cause for the three kinds of good conduct. When right view is developed, the Noble Eightfold Path is developed, because it must be developed as a unity and because it is the foundational cause. Hence it is said: 'From right view…' and so on. For the arahant whose liberation is by concentration, this arahant is an individual with no remaining substratum; this liberation by concentration is the Nibbāna element with no remaining substratum.

“Desanāhārasampātādiko hārasampāto yena soḷasappabhedabhāvena suttappadesatthe niddhāretvā yujjito, soḷasappabhedabhāvo kena amhehi saddahitabbo”ti vattabbattā “tenāhā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tena soḷasappabhedabhāvena āyasmā mahākaccāno “soḷasa…pe… sutta”nti yaṃ vacanaṃ āha, tena vacanena soḷasappabhedabhāvo tumhehi saddahitabbo.

Since it should be asked, 'By what means should we accept this sixteenfold division, by which the coalescence of the modes, beginning with the Mode of Teaching, is applied after determining the meaning of a sutta passage?'—for this reason, the passage beginning 'Therefore he said...' was stated. By that statement which the Venerable Mahākaccāna spoke in connection with that sixteenfold division—'Sixteen... (and so forth) ...sutta'—by that statement you should accept the sixteenfold division.

“Ettakova hārasampāto paripuṇṇo”ti vattabbattā “niyutto hārasampāto”ti vuttaṃ. Yena yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūtena desanāhārasampātena suttappadesatthā niddhāritā, so so saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūto desanāhārasampātādihārasampāto niyutto yathārahaṃ niddhāretvā yujjitabboti attho gahetabbo, aṭṭhakathāyañca (netti. aṭṭha. 73, 76) tathā niddhāretvā yujjitoti.

Since it can be said, 'The coalescence of the modes is complete just to this extent,' it is called 'the appointed coalescence of the modes.' The meaning to be grasped is this: by whatever specific explanation, that is, the coalescence of the Mode of Teaching, the meanings of sutta passages have been determined, that very coalescence of the modes, beginning with the Mode of Teaching, which has become a specific explanation, is what is appointed and should be applied after being appropriately determined. And in the commentary (Netti-aṭṭha. 73, 76) too, it is determined and applied in this way.

Iti desanāhārasampātādihārasampāte sattibalānurūpā

Thus is the explanation on the coalescence of the modes, beginning with the Mode of Teaching, composed in accordance with ability and strength.

Racitā vibhāvanā niṭṭhitā.

This composed explanation is now concluded.

Paṇḍitehi pana aṭṭhakathāṭīkānusārena gambhīrattho vitthārato vibhajitvā gahetabboti.

However, the profound meaning should be comprehensively analyzed and grasped by the learned, according to the commentaries and sub-commentaries.

Nayasamuṭṭhānavibhāvanā

Elucidation of the Origin of the Methods

79. Yena yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūtena desanāhārasampātādinā hārasampātena ekasuttappadesatthā niddhāretvā vibhattā, so [M 0.0255] saṃvaṇṇanāvisesabhūto desanāhārasampātādihārasampāto paripuṇṇo, “katamaṃ nayasamuṭṭhāna”nti pucchitabbattā “tattha katamaṃ nayasamuṭṭhāna”ntiādi āraddhaṃ. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana –“evaṃ nānāsuttavasena, ekasuttavasena ca [V 0.0377] hāravicāraṃ dassetvā idāni nayavicāraṃ dassetuṃ ‘tattha katamaṃ nayasamuṭṭhāna’ntiādi āraddha”nti (netti. aṭṭha. 79) vuttaṃ. “Tattha katamo nandiyāvaṭṭanayo”tiādiṃ anārabhitvā “tattha katamaṃ nayasamuṭṭhāna”ntiādiārambhane kāraṇaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttameva. Tattha tatthāti tesu hārādīsu yo atthanayo saṃvaṇṇanānayena niddiṭṭho, tasseva atthanayassa samuṭṭhānaṃ bhūmiṃ pucchati “katamaṃ nayasamuṭṭhāna”nti.

79. Since that coalescence of the modes, beginning with the Mode of Teaching, which has become a specific explanation by which the meanings of a single sutta passage are determined and analyzed, is now complete, and since it should now be asked, 'What is the origin of the methods?,' the section beginning 'Therein, what is the origin of the methods?' is started. In the commentary, however, it is said: 'Having thus shown the investigation of the modes by way of various suttas and by way of a single sutta, now, to show the investigation of the methods, the section beginning "Therein, what is the origin of the methods?" is started' (Netti-aṭṭha. 79). The reason for beginning with 'Therein, what is the origin of the methods?' rather than 'Therein, what is the Nandiyāvaṭṭa method?' is explained in the commentary. 'Therein' means: among those things, the modes, etc. When it asks, 'What is the origin of the methods?,' it is asking about the origin and basis of that very method of meaning which was indicated by the method of explanation.

Kiñcāpi saṃvaṇṇanānayā niddiṭṭhā, tathāpi atthanayasaṃvaṇṇanānayānaṃ visesassa pākaṭaṃ kātuṃ puna kathayissāma. Taṇhāavijjāhi saṃkilesapakkhassa suttatthassa catusaccayojanamukhena nayanalakkhaṇo saṃvaṇṇanāviseso ceva samathavipassanāhi vodānapakkhassa suttatthassa catusaccayojanamukhena nayanalakkhaṇo saṃvaṇṇanāviseso ca nandiyāvaṭṭo nayo nāma. Tīhi akusalamūlehi lobhādīhi saṃkilesapakkhassa suttatthassa catusaccayojanamukhena nayanalakkhaṇo saṃvaṇṇanāviseso ceva tīhi kusalamūlehi alobhādīhi vodānapakkhassa suttatthassa catusaccayojanamukhena nayanalakkhaṇo saṃvaṇṇanāviseso ca tipukkhalo nayo nāma. Catūhi subhasaññādīhi vipallāsehi sakalasaṃkilesapakkhassa suttatthassa catusaccayojanamukhena nayanalakkhaṇo saṃvaṇṇanāviseso ceva catūhi asubhasaññādīhi avipallāsehi satipaṭṭhānehi, saddhindriyehi vā vodānapakkhassa suttatthassa catusaccayojanamukhena nayanalakkhaṇo saṃvaṇṇanāviseso ca sīhavikkīḷito nayo nāmāti vuttā nayā saṃvaṇṇanānayā nāma. Tesaṃ saṃvaṇṇanānayānaṃ samuṭṭhānaṃ pucchati “katamaṃ nayasamuṭṭhāna”nti.

Although the methods of explanation have been indicated, still, to make clear the distinction between the method of meaning and the method of explanation, we will speak again. The specific explanation characterized by guiding by way of applying the Four Truths to the sutta's meaning on the side of defilement through craving and ignorance, and the specific explanation characterized by guiding by way of applying the Four Truths to the sutta's meaning on the side of purification through serenity and insight—this is the method called Nandiyāvaṭṭa. The specific explanation characterized by guiding by way of applying the Four Truths to the sutta's meaning on the side of defilement through the three unwholesome roots of greed, etc., and the specific explanation characterized by guiding by way of applying the Four Truths to the sutta's meaning on the side of purification through the three wholesome roots of non-greed, etc.—this is the method called Tipukkhala. The specific explanation characterized by guiding by way of applying the Four Truths to the sutta's meaning on the side of complete defilement through the four perversions such as the perception of beauty, and the specific explanation characterized by guiding by way of applying the Four Truths to the sutta's meaning on the side of purification through the four non-perversions, that is, the establishments of mindfulness or the spiritual faculties—this is the method called Sīhavikkīḷita. The methods thus stated are called the methods of explanation. It asks about the origin of these methods of explanation with the question: 'What is the origin of the methods?'

Nayā pana nānāsuttato niddhāritehi taṇhāavijjādīhi mūlapadehi catusaccayojanāya nayato anubujjhiyamāno dukkhādiattho. So hi maggañāṇaṃ nayati sampāpetīti “nayo”ti vutto, so atthanayo nāma. Tasseva atthanayassa samuṭṭhānaṃ pucchati “katamaṃ nayasamuṭṭhāna”nti? Tasmā [M 0.0256] catusaccayojanāya nayaggāhato nīyati anupucchīyatīti nayo, ko so? Suttatthabhūto dukkhādiko attho. Nayati maggañāṇaṃ pāpetīti vā nayo, dukkhādiko atthova. Tenāha – “anubujjhiyamāno dukkhādiattho. So hi maggañāṇaṃ nayati sampāpetīti nayo”ti (netti. aṭṭha. 79). Samuṭṭhahanti nayā etenāti samuṭṭhānaṃ, kiṃ taṃ? Avijjātaṇhādikāraṇaṃ, taṃdīpanā saṃvaṇṇanā ca. Avijjātaṇhādinā hi dukkhādiatthanayā sambhavanti. Atha vā avijjātaṇhādīhi catusaccayojanā samuṭṭhānaṃ nāma. Tena vuttaṃ – “kiṃ pana taṃ? Taṃtaṃmūlapadehi catusaccayojanā”ti (netti. aṭṭha. 79). Evaṃ atthe gayhamāne sati saṃvaṇṇanānayāpi gahitā honti, nayānaṃ samuṭṭhānaṃ nayasamuṭṭhānaṃ, tasmiṃ nayasamuṭṭhāne.

Moreover, when the meaning of suffering and so forth is comprehended through the method of connecting the four truths, using root terms such as craving and ignorance, as determined from various suttas, that is called the method of meaning. For it leads and brings about path knowledge; hence, it is called 'the method'; that is the method of meaning. The origin of that very method of meaning is asked about: 'What is the origin of the method?' Therefore, it is called a method because it is led and inquired into through grasping the connection of the four truths. What is it? It is the meaning of suffering and so forth, which is the essence of the sutta. Or, the method is that which leads to path knowledge—the meaning of suffering and so forth. Hence, it is said: 'The meaning of suffering and so forth is comprehended. For it leads and brings about path knowledge; hence, it is called the method' (Netti. Aṭṭha. 79). That from which methods arise is called the origin. What is that? It is the cause consisting of ignorance and craving, along with its explanation and description. For by means of ignorance, craving, and so forth, methods of the meaning of suffering and so forth come into being. Alternatively, the connection of the four truths by ignorance, craving, and so forth is called the origin. Therefore, it is said: 'What then is that? It is the connection of the four truths by those respective root terms' (Netti. Aṭṭha. 79). Thus, when the meaning is grasped, the methods of explanation are also grasped. The origin of the methods is the origin of the method. In that origin of the method...

“Katamaṃ [V 0.0378] nandiyāvaṭṭanayasamuṭṭhāna”nti pucchitabbattā paṭhamaṃ nandiyāvaṭṭanayasamuṭṭhānaṃ dassetuṃ “pubbā koṭi na paññāyatī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Nandiyāvaṭṭanayasamuṭṭhānabhūtāya avijjāya ca taṇhāya ca pubbā koṭi “asukassa buddhassa bhagavato uppajjanakāle uppannā, asukassa cakkavattino uppajjanakāle uppannā”ti na paññāyati koṭiyā abhāvatoti yojanā. “Avijjātaṇhāsu katamā nīvaraṇaṃ, katamā saṃyojana”nti pucchitabbattā “tattha avijjā nīvaraṇaṃ taṇhā saṃyojana”nti vuttaṃ. Tatthāti tāsu avijjātaṇhāsu. Ādīnavapaṭicchādikattā avijjā nīvaraṇaṃ. Bhavesu saṃyojanato taṇhā saṃyojanaṃ. “Avijjānīvaraṇā sattā kathaṃ vicaranti, kathaṃ vuccanti, taṇhāsaṃyojanā sattā kathaṃ vicaranti kathaṃ vuccantī”ti pucchitabbattā “avijjānīvaraṇā sattā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Avijjānīvaraṇametesamatthīti avijjānīvaraṇā. Avijjāya saṃyuttā viya pavattā avijjāya abhinivisavatthūsu saṃyuttā viya pavattā sattā avijjāpakkhena vipallāsena niccādiabhinivesavatthubhūte rūpādiārammaṇe vicaranti vividhā caranti pavattanti, te niccādiabhinivisantā vicarantā sattā “diṭṭhicaritā”ti vuccanti. Taṇhāsaṃyojanametesanti taṇhāsaṃyojanā. Taṇhāya saṃyuttā viya pavattā, taṇhāya vā ārammaṇabhūte vatthukāme saṃyuttā viya pavattā sattā taṇhāpakkhena aṭṭhasatataṇhāvicaritena ārammaṇabhūte vatthusmiṃ vicaranti pavattantīti attho.

Since it should be asked, 'What is the origin of the Nandiyāvaṭṭa method?,' first, to show the origin of the Nandiyāvaṭṭa method, the passage beginning 'A first point is not discerned...' is stated. The connection is this: concerning the ignorance and craving that are the basis for the Nandiyāvaṭṭa method, a first point—such as 'it arose at the time of the arising of this or that Blessed One, a Buddha,' or 'it arose at the time of the arising of this or that wheel-turning monarch'—is not discerned because there is no such point. Since it should be asked, 'Between ignorance and craving, which is a hindrance and which is a fetter?,' it is said, 'Therein, ignorance is a hindrance and craving is a fetter.' 'Therein' means: between that ignorance and craving. Because it conceals the danger, ignorance is a hindrance. Because it fetters to states of existence, craving is a fetter. Since it should be asked, 'How do beings hindered by ignorance wander and how are they described? How do beings fettered by craving wander and how are they described?,' the passage beginning 'Beings hindered by ignorance...' is stated. 'Hindered by ignorance' means that the hindrance of ignorance exists for them. Beings who proceed as if yoked to ignorance, as if yoked to the objects of adherence connected with ignorance, wander—that is, they move about and proceed in various ways—in objects such as form, which have become the basis for adhering to permanence, etc., through the perversion on the side of ignorance. Those beings who wander while adhering to permanence and so on are called 'those of speculative behavior.' 'Fettered by craving' means that the fetter of craving exists for them. The meaning is that beings who proceed as if yoked to craving, or as if yoked to the sensual pleasures that are the objects of craving, wander and proceed in relation to that object on the side of craving, with the one hundred and eight applications of craving.

“Diṭṭhicaritā [M 0.0257] sattā kaṃ paṭipattiṃ anuyuttā viharanti, taṇhācaritā sattā kaṃ paṭipattiṃ anuyuttā viharantī”ti pucchitabbattā “diṭṭhicaritā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Diṭṭhicaritā sattā ito sāsanato bahiddhā pabbajitā hontāpi “sukhena adhigantabbaṃ sukhaṃ natthi, dukkhena adhigantabbaṃ sukhaṃ pana atthī”ti manasi karontā attakilamathānuyogaṃ pañcātapādipaṭipattiṃ anuyuttā viharanti. Taṇhācaritā sattā ito sāsanato bahiddhā pabbajitā hontāpi “kāme paṭisevantā lokaṃ vaḍḍhāpentā bahuṃ puññaṃ vaḍḍhāpentī”ti manasi karontā kāmesu kāmasukhallikānuyogaṃ paṭipattiṃ anuyuttā viharanti.

“Beings of speculative temperament—what practice do they pursue and live by? Beings of craving temperament—what practice do they pursue and live by?” Since this is to be asked, the passage beginning “beings of speculative temperament” is stated. Beings of speculative temperament, even having gone forth outside this Dispensation, thinking, “There is no happiness to be attained by pleasure; however, there is happiness to be attained by pain,” pursue and live by a practice devoted to self-mortification, such as the practice of the five fires. Beings of craving temperament, even having gone forth outside this Dispensation, thinking, “By enjoying sensual pleasures, they make the world prosper and accumulate much merit,” pursue and live by a practice devoted to indulgence in sensual pleasures.

“Kasmā diṭṭhicaritā tathāvidhaṃ paṭipattiṃ anuyuttā viharanti, kasmā taṇhācaritā tathāvidhaṃ paṭipattiṃ anuyuttā viharantī”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha kiṃ kāraṇa”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Tatthāti tattha tesu diṭṭhicaritataṇhācaritesu. Yaṃ yasmā kāraṇā viharanti, taṃ kāraṇaṃ kinti pucchati. Ito sāsanato bahiddhā yesaṃ puggalānaṃ saccavavatthānaṃ natthi, catusaccappakāsanā kuto ca atthi, samathavipassanākosallaṃ vā upasamasukhappatti vā kuto atthi, te puggalā upasamasukhassa anabhiññā viparītacetā hutvā evaṃ āhaṃsu “sukhena adhigantabbaṃ sukhaṃ natthi[V 0.0379], dukkhena adhigantabbaṃ sukhaṃ nāma atthī”ti. Te evaṃsaññī evaṃdiṭṭhī dukkhena sukhaṃ patthayamānā hutvā attakilamathānuyogamanuyuttā viharanti. Ito sāsanato bahiddhā yesaṃ puggalānaṃ saccavavatthānaṃ natthi, catusaccappakāsanā kuto ca atthi, samathavipassanākosallaṃ vā upasamasukhappatti vā kuto atthi, te puggalā upasamasukhassa anabhiññā viparītacetā hutvā evamāhaṃsu “yo kāme paṭisevati, so lokaṃ vaḍḍhayati, yo lokaṃ vaḍḍhayati, so bahuṃ puññaṃ pasavatī”ti. Te evaṃsaññī evaṃdiṭṭhī kāmesu sukhasaññī hutvā kāmasukhallikānuyogaṃ anuyuttā ca viharantīti yojanā kātabbā.

“Why do those of speculative temperament adhere to such a practice, and why do those of craving temperament adhere to such a practice?” Because this was to be asked, the passage beginning “What is the reason for that?” was stated. 'Therein' refers to those of speculative and craving temperaments. He asks, “What is the reason?” inquiring about the reason why they live thus. For those persons outside this Dispensation who have no determination of the truths, whence could there be an exposition of the Four Noble Truths? And whence could there be skill in serenity and insight or attainment of the happiness of peace? Those persons, being ignorant of the happiness of peace and having perverted minds, declared thus: “There is no happiness to be attained through pleasure; there is, however, a happiness to be attained through pain.” Holding such perceptions and views, desiring happiness through pain, they persist in the practice of self-mortification. For those persons outside this Dispensation who have no determination of the truths, whence could there be an exposition of the Four Noble Truths? And whence could there be skill in serenity and insight or attainment of the happiness of peace? Those persons, being ignorant of the happiness of peace and having perverted minds, declared thus: “Whoever indulges in sensual pleasures makes the world prosper; whoever makes the world prosper generates much merit.” Holding such perceptions and views, perceiving happiness in sensual pleasures, they persist in the practice of indulgence in sensual pleasures. This is how the connection should be made.

“Tathā viharantā kiṃ vaḍḍhayantī”ti pucchitabbattā “te tadabhiññā santā rogameva vaḍḍhayantī”ti vuttaṃ. “Tathā vaḍḍhayantā rogādīnaṃ bhesajjaṃ samathavipassanaṃ vaḍḍhayanti ki”nti pucchitabbattā “te rogābhitunnā gaṇḍapaṭipīḷitā sallānuviddhā nirayatiracchānayonipetāsuresu ummujjanimujjāni karontā ugghātanigghātaṃ paccanubhontā rogagaṇḍasallabhesajjaṃ na [M 0.0258] vindantī”ti vuttaṃ. Attho pana aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (netti. aṭṭha. 79) vutto. “Katame saṃkilesavodānā, katame rogādayo, katamaṃ bhesajja”nti pucchitabbattā “tattha attakilamathānuyogo”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tatthāti tesu saṃkilesavodānarogabhesajjādīsu. Attakilamathānuyogo ca kāmasukhallikānuyogo ca saṃkileso hoti, samathavipassanā vodānaṃ hoti, attakilamathānuyogo ca rogo hoti, samathavipassanā roganigghātakabhesajjaṃ…pe... samathavipassanā salluddhāraṇabhesajjaṃ hoti.

“Living thus, what do they increase?” Because this was to be asked, it was said: “They, being ignorant of that, increase only disease.” “By increasing thus, do they increase serenity and insight, the medicine for diseases and the like?” Because this was to be asked, it was said: “They, afflicted by disease, oppressed by tumors, pierced by darts, bobbing up and down in hell, the animal realm, the sphere of ghosts, and the host of titans, experiencing jolts and jars, do not find the medicine for the disease, tumors, and darts.” The meaning, however, is stated in the Commentary (Netti-aṭṭha. 79). “What are the defilements and purification? What are diseases and the like? What is the medicine?” Because this was to be asked, the passage beginning “Herein, the practice of self-mortification…” was stated. Herein—among those things such as defilements, purification, diseases, and medicine—the practice of self-mortification and the practice of indulgence in sensual pleasures are defilement. Serenity and insight are purification. The practice of self-mortification is a disease. Serenity and insight are the medicine that suppresses disease… Serenity and insight are the medicine that extracts the dart.

“Katamo katamaṃ sacca”nti pucchitabbattā “tattha saṃkileso dukkha”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Tatthāti tesu saṃkilesādīsu saṃkileso ekadesavasena dukkhaṃ dukkhasaccaṃ hoti. Tadabhisaṅgoti tasmiṃ saṃkilese abhisaṅgo viya pavatto lokiyadhammo niravasesavasena dukkhasaccaṃ hoti. Atha vā tasmiṃ dukkhe abhisaṅgo viya pavattā taṇhā dukkhasamudayo samudayasaccaṃ hoti. Taṇhānirodho dukkhanirodho nirodhasaccaṃ hoti. Samathavipassanā dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā maggasaccaṃ hoti. Imāni cattāri saccāni niddhāretvā yojetabbāni. “Tesu catūsu saccesu katamaṃ pariññeyyaṃ, katamo pahātabbo, katamo bhāvetabbo, katamo sacchikātabbo”ti pucchitabbattā “dukkhaṃ pariññeyya”ntiādi vuttaṃ.

“Which is which truth?” Because this was to be asked, it is said, “Therein, defilement is suffering,” and so on. Therein, among those things such as defilement, defilement is in part suffering, the truth of suffering. The attachment to it—the worldly states that proceed as if they were an attachment to that defilement—are, without remainder, the truth of suffering. Alternatively, craving, which proceeds as if it were an attachment to that suffering, is the origin of suffering, the truth of the origin. The cessation of craving is the cessation of suffering, the truth of cessation. Serenity and insight, the path leading to the cessation of suffering, is the truth of the path. These four truths should be determined and applied. “Among these four truths, which is to be fully understood, which is to be abandoned, which is to be developed, and which is to be realized?” Because this was to be asked, it is said, “Suffering is to be fully understood,” and so on.

80. Diṭṭhicaritataṇhācaritānaṃ attakilamathānuyogādivasena cattāri saccāni niddhāritāni, “kathaṃ diṭṭhicaritataṇhācaritānaṃ sakkāyadassane pavattibhedavasena cattāri saccāni niddhāritānī”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha diṭṭhicaritā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Atha vā “diṭṭhicaritataṇhācaritānaṃ [V 0.0380] sakkāyadassane katamo pavattibhedo”ti pucchitabbattā imesaṃ sakkāyadassane ayaṃ pavattibhedoti vibhajitvā dassetuṃ “tattha diṭṭhicaritā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tena vuttaṃ – “idāni diṭṭhicaritataṇhācaritānaṃ sakkāyadiṭṭhidassane pavattibhedaṃ dassetuṃ ‘diṭṭhicaritā’tiādi vutta”nti. Tatthāti tesu diṭṭhicaritataṇhācaritesu. Diṭṭhicaritā puggalā rūpaṃ “attā”ti attato upagacchanti…pe… viññāṇaṃ “attā”ti attato upagacchanti diṭṭhicaritānaṃ attābhinivesassa balavabhāvato, taṇhācaritā pana rūpaṃ vā [M 0.0259] “attā”ti rūpavantaṃ attānaṃ upagacchanti attani vā rūpaṃ, rūpasmiṃ vā “attā”ti attānaṃ upagacchanti…pe… viññāṇasmiṃ vā “attā”ti attānaṃ upagacchanti taṇhācaritānaṃ attaniyābhinivesassa balavabhāvato. Pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu ekekaṃ nissāya catubbidhattā vīsativatthukā ayaṃ micchādiṭṭhi “sakkāyadiṭṭhī”ti vuccati. Evaṃ diṭṭhicaritataṇhācaritānaṃ sakkāyadassane pavattibhedo viññātabboti attho.

80. The four truths have been determined for those of speculative and craving temperaments by way of self-mortification and so on.
