Because it should be asked, “How are the four truths determined for those of speculative and craving temperaments by way of the difference in the occurrence of the view of personal identity?” the passage beginning “In this context, those of speculative temperament…” was stated. Alternatively, because it should be asked, “For those of speculative and craving temperaments, what is the difference in the occurrence of the view of personal identity?” this was stated to analyze and show this difference. Thus it was said: “Now, to show the difference in the occurrence of the view of personal identity for those of speculative and craving temperaments, the passage beginning ‘those of speculative temperament’ was stated.” In this context refers to those of speculative and craving temperaments. Persons of a speculative temperament regard form as “self”… they regard consciousness as “self,” because of the strength of their adherence to a self. Persons of a craving temperament, however, regard the self as possessing form, or form as in the self, or the self as in form… they regard the self as in consciousness, because of the strength of their adherence to what is “mine.” This wrong view with its twenty bases—four for each of the five aggregates of clinging—is called “the view of personal identity.” The meaning is that the difference in the occurrence of the view of personal identity for those of speculative and craving temperaments should be understood in this way.

“Sakkāyadiṭṭhiyā katamo paṭipakkho”ti pucchitabbattā “tassā paṭipakkho”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tassā sakkāyadiṭṭhiyā pajahanavasena lokuttarā sammādiṭṭhi paṭipakkho, tassā sammādiṭṭhiyā anvāyikā anuguṇabhāvena pavattanakā dhammā ca sakkāyadiṭṭhiyā pajahanavasena paṭipakkhā bhavanti. “Katame dhammā anvāyikā”ti pucchitabbattā “sammāsaṅkappo”tiādi vuttaṃ. Sammāsaṅkappo…pe… sammāsamādhi ime dhammā anvāyikā honti. Ayaṃ sammādiṭṭhiādiko ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo tassā sakkāyadiṭṭhiyā paṭipakkho hoti pahāyakattā. “Te sammādiṭṭhiyādayo dhammā khandhato kittakā hontī”ti pucchitabbattā “te tayo khandhā”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Katamo khandho samatho, katamo khandho vipassanā”ti pucchitabbattā “sīlakkhandho samādhikkhandho ca samatho, paññākkhandho vipassanā”ti vuttaṃ. “Sakkāyādīsu katamo katamaṃ saccaṃ, katamo katamaṃ sacca”nti pucchitabbattā “tattha sakkāyo”tiādi vuttaṃ.

“What is the opposite of the view of personal identity?” Because this was to be asked, the passage beginning “Its opposite…” was stated. The supramundane right view is the opposite of that view of personal identity by way of its abandonment. The states that are consequential to that right view, proceeding in a way that is conducive to it, are also opposites to the view of personal identity by way of its abandonment. “What are the consequential states?” Because this was to be asked, the passage beginning “Right intention…” was stated. Right intention… right concentration—these are the consequential states. This Noble Eightfold Path, beginning with right view, is the opposite of that view of personal identity because it is the abandoner. “In terms of aggregates, how many are those states beginning with right view?” Because this was to be asked, the passage beginning “They are three aggregates…” was stated. “Which aggregate is serenity, and which aggregate is insight?” Because this was to be asked, it was said: “The aggregate of virtue and the aggregate of concentration are serenity; the aggregate of wisdom is insight.” “Among personal identity and so on, which is which truth?” Because this was to be asked, the passage beginning “Herein, personal identity…” was stated.

“Diṭṭhicaritataṇhācaritānaṃ sakkāyadiṭṭhitappaṭipakkhavasena cattāri saccāni niddhāritāni, kathaṃ antadvayamajjhimapaṭipadā niddhāritā”ti vattabbattā “tattha ye rūpaṃ attato”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tatthāti tesu diṭṭhicaritataṇhācaritesu ye diṭṭhicaritā puggalā rūpaṃ “attā”ti attato upagacchanti…pe… viññāṇaṃ “attā”ti attato upagacchanti. Ime diṭṭhicaritā puggalā “rūpādayo ca attā, rūpādīnañca aniccattā, attassāpi aniccattā attā ucchijjati, attā vinassati, attā paraṃ maraṇā na hotī”ti abhinivisanato “ucchedavādino”ti [V 0.0381] vuccanti. Ye taṇhācaritā puggalā rūpaṃ vā “attā”ti rūpavantaṃ attānaṃ upagacchanti…pe… viññāṇaṃ vā “attā”ti viññāṇavantaṃ attānaṃ upagacchanti. Attani vā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ upagacchanti. Ime taṇhācaritā puggalā “rūpādīhi attā añño [M 0.0260] aññattā attā nicco sassato”ti abhinivisanato “sassatavādino”ti vuccanti.

Since the four truths have been determined for those of speculative and craving temperaments by way of the view of personal identity and its opposite, it should be asked: 'How is the middle path that avoids the two extremes determined?' Therefore it is said: 'Therein, those who regard form as self,' and so on. 'Therein' means among those of speculative temperament and craving temperament. Those persons of speculative temperament who regard form as self ...pe... who regard consciousness as self. Because these persons of speculative temperament adhere to the view that 'form, etc., are the self, and since form, etc., are impermanent, the self too is impermanent; the self is annihilated, the self perishes, the self does not exist after death,' they are called 'annihilationists.' Those persons of craving temperament regard the self as possessing form ...pe... or the self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in the self, or the self as in consciousness. Because these persons of craving temperament adhere to the view that 'the self is other than form, etc.; because it is different, the self is permanent and eternal,' they are called 'eternalists.'

Tattha tesu ucchedavādīsassatavādīpuggalesu pavattā ucchedavādasassatavādā ubho antā antadvayapaṭipadā honti. Ayaṃ antadvayapaṭipadā saṃsārapavattanassa hetubhāvato saṃsārapavatti hoti, tassa antadvayassa paṭipajjanassa pajahanavasena majjhimapaṭipadāsaṅkhātova ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo paṭipakkho hoti pahāyakattā. Ayaṃ maggo saṃsāranivattanassa hetubhāvato saṃsāranivatti hoti. Tattha saṃsārapavattisaṃsāranivattīsu pavatti saṃsārapavatti dukkhaṃ dukkhasaccaṃ, tadabhisaṅgo tasmiṃ dukkhe abhisaṅgo taṇhā samudayo samudayasaccaṃ, taṇhānirodho dukkhanirodho nirodhasaccaṃ, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā maggasaccaṃ, iti imāni cattāri saccāni niddhāritāni. “Dukkhaṃ pariññeyya”ntiādimhi vuttanayova attho.

Therein, among those annihilationist and eternalist persons, the annihilationist and eternalist views that have arisen are both extremes, the path of the two extremes. This path of the two extremes, being the cause for the continuation of saṃsāra, is the continuation of saṃsāra. By way of abandoning the practice of that pair of extremes, the Noble Eightfold Path, reckoned as the middle path, is the counterpart, since it is the abandoner. This path, being the cause for the cessation of saṃsāra, is the cessation of saṃsāra. Therein, with regard to the continuation of saṃsāra and the cessation of saṃsāra: the continuation of saṃsāra is suffering, the truth of suffering. Attachment to it—attachment to that suffering—is craving, the origin, the truth of the origin. The cessation of craving is the cessation of suffering, the truth of cessation. The Noble Eightfold Path is the path leading to the cessation of suffering, the truth of the path. Thus these four truths are determined. The meaning is in the same way as was stated in the passage beginning, 'Suffering is to be fully understood.'

“Ucchedasassatassa kittako pabhedo, maggassa kittako”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha ucchedasassata”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha ucchedasassataariyamaggesu ucchedasassatadassanaṃ samāsato saṅkhepato vīsativatthukā sakkāyadiṭṭhi. Ucchedo pañcupādānakkhandhe nissāya pavattattā pañcavidho, sassatadassanaṃ ekekasmiṃ tidhā uppajjanato pannarasavidhanti vīsatividhaṃ hoti. Vitthārato dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhigatāni. Katamāni? Cattāro sassatavādā, cattāro ekaccasassatavādā, cattāro antānantavādā, cattāro amarāvikkhepavādā, dve adhiccasamuppannavādā, soḷasa saññīvādā, aṭṭha asaññīvādā, aṭṭha nevasaññīnāsaññīvādā, satta ucchedavādā, pañca diṭṭhadhammanibbānavādāti dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhigatāni veditabbāni. Vitthārato pana brahmajālasutte (dī. ni. 1.30 ādayo) āgatāni. Tesaṃ ucchedasassatadassanānaṃ tecattālīsaṃ bodhipakkhiyadhammā paṭipakkho maggo. Katame tecattālīsaṃ? “Aniccasaññā dukkhasaññā anattasaññā”ti tisso saññā ca “pahānasaññā virāgasaññā nirodhasaññā”ti tisso saññā cāti cha saññā ca “cattāro satipaṭṭhānā, cattāro sammappadhānā, cattāro iddhipādā, pañcindriyāni, pañca balāni, satta bojjhaṅgā, aṭṭha maggaṅgānī”ti tecattālīsaṃ bodhipakkhiyadhammā vipassanāvasena paṭipakkho maggo nāma.

Because it should be asked, 'What is the classification of annihilationism and eternalism, and what is that of the path?' it is said: 'Therein, annihilationism and eternalism,' and so on. Therein, among annihilationism, eternalism, and the noble path, the view of annihilationism and eternalism is, in brief, the twenty-grounded identity view. The annihilationist view is fivefold, since it occurs depending on the five clinging-aggregates. The eternalist view is fifteenfold, since it arises in three ways in regard to each aggregate. Thus it is twentyfold. In detail, there are sixty-two speculative views. What are they? Four doctrines of eternalism, four of partial eternalism, four of the finitude and infinitude of the world, four of eel-wriggling, two of fortuitous origination, sixteen of conscious post-mortem survival, eight of unconscious post-mortem survival, eight of neither-conscious-nor-unconscious post-mortem survival, seven of annihilationism, and five of Nibbāna here and now—thus sixty-two speculative views are to be understood. These are given in detail in the Brahmajāla Sutta (DN 1.30ff.). The counterpart path to these annihilationist and eternalist views consists of the forty-three qualities aiding enlightenment. What are the forty-three? The six perceptions—namely, the three perceptions of impermanence, suffering, and non-self, and the three perceptions of abandonment, dispassion, and cessation; and the thirty-seven qualities: the four establishments of mindfulness, the four right strivings, the four bases for spiritual power, the five spiritual faculties, the five powers, the seven enlightenment factors, and the eight path factors. These forty-three qualities aiding enlightenment are called the counterpart path by way of insight.

“Samathavasena [V 0.0382][M 0.0261] katamo paṭipakkho”ti vattabbattā “aṭṭha vimokkhā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Aṭṭha vimokkhā pākaṭā. Dasa kasiṇāyatanāni samathavasena paṭipakkho maggo nāma. “Katamaṃ ñāṇaṃ katamassa dhammassa padālana”nti pucchitabbattā “dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhigatānī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Diṭṭhicarite pavattāni diṭṭhigatāni, moho. Taṇhācarite pavattāni diṭṭhigatāni, jālaṃ. Anādivasena pavatto moho. Anidhanavasena pavattaṃ jālaṃ. Aṭṭha samāpattiyo samāpajjitvā tejetvā tikkhaṃ vipassanāñāṇañca ariyamaggañāṇañcañāṇavajiraṃ nāma bodhipakkhiyadhammānaṃ ñāṇapadaṭṭhānattā. Moho ca jālañca mohajālaṃ. Padāletīti padālanaṃ, kattari yupaccayo, mohajālassa padālananti mohajālapadālanaṃ. Padālanañhi duvidhaṃ vikkhambhanapadālanaṃ samucchedapadālananti. Pubbabhāge samathavipassanāvasena vikkhambhanapadālanaṃ, maggakkhaṇe samucchedapadālanaṃ eva daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tatthāti tasmiṃ mohajāle avijjā moho, bhavataṇhā jālaṃ. Attano ādhāraṃ puggalaṃ dukkhādīsu aṭṭhasu ṭhānesu mohetīti moho. Paṭhamaṃ jālaṃ jaṭaṃ lāyitvā jaṭāvasena lāti pavattatīti jālaṃ, attani jātaṃ macchasakuṇādikaṃ lāti gaṇhāti, lāpeti gaṇhāpetīti vā jālaṃ, jālaṃ viyāti jālaṃ. Tena vuttaṃ – “atītādibhedabhinnesu rūpādīsu, sakaattabhāvādīsu ca saṃsibbanavasena pavattanato jālaṃ bhavataṇhā”ti (netti. aṭṭha. 80). “Avijjātaṇhāhi attakilamathānuyogādīnaṃ kilesapakkhānaṃ niddhāraṇaṃ kataṃ kathaṃ kena saddahitabba”nti vattabbattā “tena vuccati ‘pubbā koṭi na paññāyati avijjāya ca bhavataṇhāya cā’ti” vuttaṃ.

Because it should be asked, 'By way of serenity, what is the counterpart?' it is said: 'The eight liberations,' and so on. The eight liberations are evident. The ten kasiṇa bases are called the counterpart path by way of serenity. Because it should be asked, 'What knowledge is the destroyer of what state?' it is said: 'The sixty-two speculative views,' and so on. The speculative views that occur in one of speculative temperament are delusion. The speculative views that occur in one of craving temperament are the net. Delusion occurs without a beginning; the net occurs without an end. Having entered upon and honed the eight attainments, the sharp insight knowledge and noble path knowledge are called the diamond-thunderbolt of knowledge because they are the proximate cause for the knowledge of the qualities aiding enlightenment. Delusion and the net are the net of delusion. 'Destroyer' (padālanaṃ) means 'that which destroys' (padāleti); the suffix -ana is in the agent sense. The destroyer of the net of delusion is the 'net-of-delusion-destroyer.' Destruction is twofold: destruction by suppression and destruction by eradication. Destruction by suppression by means of serenity and insight in the preliminary phase, and destruction by eradication at the moment of the path should be seen. Therein, in that net of delusion, ignorance is delusion and craving for being is the net. It is 'delusion' (moho) because it deludes the person who is its basis in regard to eight things, such as suffering. It is a 'net' (jālaṃ) because, having first cut the tangle (jaṭa), it proceeds by way of the tangle; or because it reaps (lāti), i.e., seizes, the fish, birds, etc., born within it, or causes them to be reaped; it is like a net. Thus it is said: 'Craving for being is a net because it proceeds by way of stitching things together in regard to form, etc., which are divided into past, etc., and in regard to one's own being, etc.' Because it should be asked: 'The explanation of the side of defilements—such as the devotion to self-mortification—by means of ignorance and craving has been given; how and by whom is this to be believed?' it is said: 'Therefore it is said: "A first point of ignorance and craving for being is not discerned."'

81. “Ito sāsanato bahiddhā diṭṭhicaritataṇhācaritānaṃ paṭipadādayo niddhāritā, sāsane diṭṭhicaritataṇhācaritānaṃ paṭipadādayo kathaṃ niddhāritabbā”ti vattabbattā “saṃkilesapakkhā suttatthā ācariyena dassitā, vodānapakkhasuttatthā kathaṃ dassitabbā”ti vattabbattā vā “tattha diṭṭhicarito asmiṃ sāsane”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tatthāti tesu diṭṭhicaritataṇhācaritesu. Diṭṭhicarito puggalo asmiṃ sāsane pabbajito hutvā catūsu paccayesu sallekhānusantatavutti bhavati. Kasmā? Yasmā sallekhe tibbagāravo, tasmā sallekhe tibbagāravattā. Taṇhācarito puggalo asmiṃ sāsane pabbajito hutvā sikkhānusantatavutti bhavati[M 0.0262]. Kasmā? Yasmā sikkhāya tibbagāravo, tasmā sikkhāya tibbagāravattā. Diṭṭhicarito puggalo sammattaniyāmaṃ okkamanto hutvā dhammānusārī puggalo bhavati. Kasmā? Diṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivisaye paññāsadisapavattanato. Taṇhācarito puggalo sammattaniyāmaṃ okkamanto hutvā saddhānusārī bhavati. Kasmā? Taṇhāvasena micchādhimokkhattā. Diṭṭhicarito puggalo sukhāya paṭipadāya, dandhābhiññāya ca niyyāti, sukhāya [V 0.0383] paṭipadāya, khippābhiññāya ca niyyāti sukhena kilesehi vikkhambhituṃ samatthattā. Taṇhācarito puggalo dukkhāya paṭipadāya, dandhābhiññāya ca niyyāti, dukkhāya paṭipadāya, khippābhiññāya ca niyyāti dukkhena kilesehi vikkhambhituṃ samatthattā.

81. Because it should be asked: 'The path, etc., for those of speculative and craving temperaments outside this Dispensation have been determined; how should the path, etc., for those of speculative and craving temperaments within this Dispensation be determined?' or because it should be asked: 'The meaning of suttas on the side of defilement has been shown by the Teacher; how should the meaning of suttas on the side of purification be shown?' it is said: 'Therein, a person of speculative temperament in this Dispensation,' and so on. 'Therein' means among those of speculative and craving temperaments. A person of speculative temperament who has gone forth in this Dispensation has a practice of continuous austerity in regard to the four requisites. Why? Because he has a strong respect for austerity. A person of craving temperament who has gone forth in this Dispensation has a practice of continuous training. Why? Because he has a strong respect for training. A person of speculative temperament, on entering the fixed course of rightness, becomes a Dhamma-follower. Why? Because his view proceeds in the domain of views in a way similar to wisdom. A person of craving temperament, on entering the fixed course of rightness, becomes a faith-follower. Why? Because of wrong resolve based on craving. A person of speculative temperament goes forth by way of the pleasant practice with slow direct knowledge, or by way of the pleasant practice with quick direct knowledge, because he is able to suppress the defilements with ease. A person of craving temperament goes forth by way of the painful practice with slow direct knowledge, or by way of the painful practice with quick direct knowledge, because he is able to suppress the defilements with difficulty.

“Tathā kasmā niyyātī”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha kiṃ kāraṇaṃ ya”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Yaṃ yena kāraṇena niyyāti, taṃ kāraṇaṃ kinti pucchati. Tassa taṇhācaritassa kāmā sukhena apariccattā hi yasmā bhavanti, tasmā kāmānaṃ sukhena apariccattattā tathā niyyāti. So taṇhācarito kāmehi vatthukāmakilesakāmehi viveciyamāno dukkhena paṭinissarati, dandhañca dhammaṃ catusaccadhammaṃ ājānāti. Yo pana ayaṃ puggalo diṭṭhicarito hoti, so ayaṃ diṭṭhicarito puggalo ādito ādimhiyeva kāmehi kilesakāmavatthukāmehi anatthiko bhavati. So diṭṭhicarito tato tehi kāmehi viveciyamāno khippañca sukhena paṭinissarati, khippañca dhammaṃ ājānāti.

Because it should be asked, 'Why does he proceed thus?' it is said, 'What is the reason there?' and so on. He asks: 'What is the reason by which he proceeds?' For one of a craving-natured disposition, sensual pleasures are not relinquished with ease. Therefore, because sensual pleasures are not relinquished with ease, he proceeds thus. That person of a craving-natured disposition, being disengaged from sensual pleasures—sensual objects and sensual defilements—renounces with difficulty and understands the Dhamma, the fourfold truth, slowly. But this person who is of a speculative disposition, from the very beginning is without need for sensual pleasures—sensual defilements and sensual objects. That person of a speculative disposition, being disengaged from those sensual pleasures, renounces quickly and with ease, and quickly understands the Dhamma.

“Taṇhācarito dukkhāya paṭipadāya dandhābhiññāya niyyāti, diṭṭhicarito sukhāya paṭipadāya khippābhiññāya niyyātīti ekekāya paṭipadāya bhavitabba”nti vattabbattā “dukkhāpi paṭipadā duvidhā dandhābhiññā ca khippābhiññā ca, sukhāpi paṭipadā duvidhā dandhābhiññā ca khippābhiññā cā”ti vuttaṃ. “Evaṃ sati ekova dvīhi dvīhi paṭipadāhi niyyātīti āpajjatī”ti vattabbattā “sattāpī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Taṇhācaritā sattāpi duvidhā mudindriyāpi tikkhindriyāpi, diṭṭhicaritā sattāpi duvidhā mudindriyāpi tikkhindriyāpīti yojanā kātabbā. Ye taṇhācaritadiṭṭhicaritā mudindriyā bhavanti, te taṇhācaritadiṭṭhicaritā dandhañca paṭinissaranti, dandhañca dhammaṃ ājānanti. Ye taṇhācaritadiṭṭhicaritā tikkhindriyā bhavanti, te taṇhācaritadiṭṭhicaritā khippañca paṭinissaranti, khippañca dhammaṃ ājānanti, tasmā ekekasseva ekekā paṭipadā [M 0.0263] yuttāvāti. “Imāhi paṭipadāhi niyyantiyeva, na niyyiṃsu niyyissantīti āpajjeyya vattamānavibhattiyā niddiṭṭhattā”ti vattabbattā “imā catasso”tiādi vuttaṃ. Atītepi imāhi catūhi paṭipadāhi niyyiṃsu, paccuppannesupi niyyanti, anāgatepi niyyissantīti attho gahetabbo yathā “pabbato tiṭṭhatī”ti.

Because it should be said: 'A person of a craving-natured disposition proceeds by the painful practice with slow direct knowledge, while a person of a speculative disposition proceeds by the pleasant practice with quick direct knowledge; thus there must be a single path for each,' it is therefore said: 'The painful practice is also twofold: with slow direct knowledge and with quick direct knowledge; and the pleasant practice is also twofold: with slow direct knowledge and with quick direct knowledge.' Because it could be said: 'This being so, it would follow that a single person proceeds by two paths,' it is said, 'Beings, too...' and so on. The connection should be made thus: Beings of a craving-natured disposition are also of two kinds, those with dull faculties and those with sharp faculties; and beings of a speculative disposition are also of two kinds, those with dull faculties and those with sharp faculties. Those of a craving-natured or speculative disposition who have dull faculties renounce slowly and understand the Dhamma slowly. Those of a craving-natured or speculative disposition who have sharp faculties renounce quickly and understand the Dhamma quickly. Therefore, for each single individual, a single path is appropriate. Because it could be said: 'It would follow that they proceed by these paths only now, that they did not proceed and will not proceed, because it is stated in the present tense,' it is said, 'These four...' and so on. The meaning should be understood thus: In the past, too, they proceeded by these four paths; in the present they proceed; and in the future they will proceed, just as in 'the mountain stands.'

Evanti evaṃ vuttappakārena. Ariyapuggalā catukkamaggaṃ paṭipadaṃ paññāpenti. “Kimatthaṃ paññāpentī”ti vattabbattā “abudhajanasevitāyā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Ayaṃ vuccati nandiyāvaṭṭassa nayassa bhūmīti taṇhāavijjānaṃ vasena saṃkilesapakkhe dvidisā catusaccayojanāpi samathavipassanānaṃ [V 0.0384] vasena vodānapakkhe dvidisā catusaccayojanāpi dassitā. Ayaṃ catubbidhā catusaccayojanā nandiyāvaṭṭassa nayassa samuṭṭhānaṃ bhūmi samuṭṭhānabhāvatoti. “Tathāvidhāya catusaccayojanāya nandiyāvaṭṭassa nayassa samuṭṭhānabhūmibhāvo kena saddahitabbo”ti vattabbattā “tenāhā”tiādi vuttaṃ.

'Thus' means in the manner described. Noble persons make known the practice of the fourfold path. Because it should be asked, 'For what purpose do they make it known?' it is said, 'For that which is frequented by the ignorant folk,' and so on. This is called the ground of the Nandiyāvaṭṭa method: a twofold direction with a four-cause connection on the side of defilement by way of craving and ignorance, and a twofold direction with a four-cause connection on the side of purification by way of serenity and insight, have been shown. This fourfold four-cause connection is the ground for the origination of the Nandiyāvaṭṭa method, because it is the ground of origination. Because it should be asked, 'By what should one have faith that such a fourfold four-cause connection is the ground for the origination of the Nandiyāvaṭṭa method?' it is said, 'Therefore he said...' and so on.

82. “Nandiyāvaṭṭassa nayassa samuṭṭhānabhūtā bhūmi dassitā, tassa nandiyāvaṭṭassa nayassa kattha katamā disā kittakena upaparikkhitabbā”ti vattabbattā “veyyākaraṇesu hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Hi-saddo pakkhantarattho. Ye disābhūtā āhārādayo dhammā veyyākaraṇesu “kusalākusalā”ti vuttaṃ, te disābhūtā āhārādayo dhammā duvidhena “ime akusalā dhammā saṃkilesadhammā, ime kusalā vodānadhammā”ti duvidhena upaparikkhitabbā ālocitabbā. “Katamena duvidhenā”ti pucchitabbattā “lokavaṭṭānusārī ca lokavivaṭṭānusārī cā”ti vuttaṃ. “Katamaṃ vaṭṭaṃ, katamaṃ vivaṭṭa”nti pucchitabbattā “vaṭṭaṃ nāma saṃsāro, vivaṭṭaṃ nibbāna”nti vuttaṃ. “Saṃsārassa katamo hetū”ti pucchitabbattā “kammakilesā hetu saṃsārassā”ti vuttaṃ. “Katamaṃ kammaṃ nāma, cetanāyeva kammaṃ nāma kiṃ, udāhu cetasikañca phaladānasamatthāsamatthampi kammaṃ ki”nti pucchitabbattā “tattha kamma”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Tatthāti tesu kammakilesesu. “Taṃ kammaṃ kathaṃ kena pakārena daṭṭhabba”nti ce vadeyya, yathā yena upacayena kataṃ kammaṃ phaladānasamatthaṃ hoti, tasmiṃ upacaye taṃ kammaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. “Te kilesā katamehi dhammehi niddisitabbā”ti ce puccheyya, sabbepi kilesā catūhi vipallāsehi niddisitabbā. “Te kilesā kattha [M 0.0264] daṭṭhabbā”ti ce puccheyya, dasavatthuke kilesapuñje te kilesā daṭṭhabbā.

82. Because it should be said: 'The ground that is the origin of the Nandiyāvaṭṭa method has been shown. Regarding that Nandiyāvaṭṭa method, where, which direction, and by how much should it be investigated?' it is said, 'In the explanations, indeed...' and so on. The word 'hi' (indeed) has the sense of an alternative. Those phenomena such as nutriment that constitute a direction, which are called 'wholesome and unwholesome' in the explanations, should be investigated and reflected upon in two ways: 'These are unwholesome phenomena, defiling phenomena; these are wholesome phenomena, purifying phenomena.' Because it should be asked, 'In which two ways?' it is said, 'Following the round of the world and following the rolling back of the round.' Because it should be asked, 'What is the round, what is the rolling back?' it is said, 'The round is saṃsāra, the rolling back is Nibbāna.' Because it should be asked, 'What is the cause of saṃsāra?' it is said, 'Kamma and defilements are the cause of saṃsāra.' Because it should be asked: 'What is called kamma? Is volition alone called kamma, or are mental factors also kamma, both those capable and incapable of giving a result?' it is said, 'Therein, kamma...' and so on. 'Therein' means among kamma and defilements. If one should say, 'How, in what way, is that kamma to be seen?'—it is to be seen in that accumulation by which the kamma that has been done becomes capable of giving a result. If one should ask, 'By what phenomena are those defilements to be designated?'—all defilements are to be designated by the four perversions. If one should ask, 'Where are those defilements to be seen?'—those defilements are to be seen in the mass of defilements with a tenfold basis.

“Katamāni dasa vatthūnī”ti ce puccheyya, cattāro āhārā, cattāro vipallāsā, cattāri upādānāni, cattāro yogā, cattāro ganthā, cattāro āsavā, cattāro oghā, cattāro sallā, catasso viññāṇaṭṭhitiyo, cattāri agatigamanānīti dasa vatthūnīti veditabbāni catunnaṃ kiccavasena ekattā. Ettha ca kilesānaṃ paccayo vatthukāmopi kilesopi kilesavatthu hoti purimānaṃ purimānaṃ kilesānaṃ pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ kilesānaṃ paccayabhāvato.

If one should ask, 'What are the ten bases?'—the four nutriments, the four perversions, the four kinds of clinging, the four yokes, the four bonds, the four taints, the four floods, the four darts, the four stations of consciousness, and the four wrong courses: these should be known as the ten bases, being a unity by way of the function of the foursomes. Here, the condition for defilements, the sensual object, is also a defilement and a basis for defilement, because the preceding defilements are a condition for the succeeding defilements.

“Katamo katamo katamassa katamassa vatthū”ti pucchitabbattā “paṭhame āhāre”tiādi vuttaṃ. Ālambitabbe paṭhame kabaḷīkārāhāre paṭhamo “rūpaṃ subha”nti vipallāso ārammaṇakaraṇavasena pavattati. Ālambitabbe dutiye phassāhāre dutiyo “phassapaccayā vedanā sukhā”ti [V 0.0385] vipallāso pavattati. Ālambitabbe tatiye cittāhāre tatiyo “cittaṃ nicca”nti vipallāso pavattati, ālambitabbe catutthe manosañcetanāhāre “dhammo attā”ti vipallāso ārammaṇakaraṇavasena pavattati. Ālambitabbe paṭhame “rūpaṃ subha”nti vipallāso paṭhamaṃ kāmupādānaṃ ārammaṇakaraṇavasena pavattati. Sesesupi yathārahaṃ nayānusārena yojetvā attho veditabbo.

Because it should be asked, 'Which is the basis for which?' it is said, 'In the first nutriment...' and so on. When the first, edible food, is taken as an object, the first perversion, 'form is beautiful,' occurs by way of making it an object. When the second, nutriment of contact, is taken as an object, the second perversion, 'feeling conditioned by contact is pleasant,' occurs. When the third, nutriment of consciousness, is taken as an object, the third perversion, 'consciousness is permanent,' occurs. When the fourth, nutriment of mental volition, is taken as an object, the perversion 'phenomena are self' occurs by way of making it an object. When the first nutriment is taken as an object, the perversion 'form is beautiful' occurs as the first clinging to sensual pleasures, by way of making it an object. For the rest, too, the meaning should be understood by applying the method as is appropriate.

83. “Tesu āhārādīsu katamo katamassa puggalassa upakkileso”ti vattabbattā “tattha yo cā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tatthāti tesu āhārādīsu, taṇhācaritadiṭṭhicaritesu vā. Taṇhācaritassa rūpavedanāsu tibbacchandarāgassa uppajjanato yo ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro, yo ca phassāhāro pavattati, ime kabaḷīkārāhāraphassāhārā taṇhācaritassa puggalassa upakkilesā bhavanti. Diṭṭhicaritassa dhammacittesu balavaattaniccābhinivesassa uppajjanato yo ca manosañcetanāhāro, yo ca viññāṇāhāro pavattati, ime manosañcetanāhāraviññāṇāhārā diṭṭhicaritassa puggalassa upakkilesā bhavanti. “Tattha yo ca asubhe subha”ntiādīsupi vuttanayānusārena attho gahetabboti. Purimānaṃ [M 0.0265] dvinnaṃ dvinnaṃ taṇhāpadhānattā ceva taṇhāsabhāvattā ca, pacchimānaṃ dvinnaṃ dvinnaṃ diṭṭhipadhānattā ceva diṭṭhisabhāvattā cāti.

83. Because it should be said, 'Among these—nutriment and so on—which is the defilement for which person?' it is said, 'Therein, whichever...' and so on. 'Therein' means among these—nutriment and so on—or among those of a craving-natured disposition and those of a speculative disposition. For a person of a craving-natured disposition, because of the arising of intense desire and lust for forms and feelings, both the nutriment of edible food and the nutriment of contact that occur become defilements for that person. For a person of a speculative disposition, because of the arising of strong adherence to a notion of self and permanence in regard to phenomena and consciousness, both the nutriment of mental volition and the nutriment of consciousness that occur become defilements for that person. The meaning should also be understood according to the method stated in 'Therein, whatever is beautiful in the unbeautiful...' and so on. This is because the former two have craving as their chief and have the nature of craving, and the latter two have views as their chief and have the nature of views.

84. “Katamasmiṃ paṭhamādike āhāre katamo paṭhamādiko vipallāso pavattatī”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha kabaḷīkāre āhāre”tiādinā nāmavasena niyametvā pubbe vuttatthameva dasseti. “Katamasmiṃ vipallāse ṭhito katamaṃ upādiyatī”ti pucchitabbattā “paṭhame vipallāse ṭhito”tiādi vuttaṃ. Paṭhame vipallāse ṭhito puggalo kāme yena upādānena upādiyati, idaṃ upādānaṃ “kāmupādānaṃ nāmā”ti vuccati. Sesesu iminā nayena yojanā kātabbā.

84. Because it should be asked, 'In which nutriment, the first and so on, does which perversion, the first and so on, occur?' it shows the meaning already stated by defining it by name with 'Therein, in the nutriment of edible food...' and so on. Because it should be asked, 'Established in which perversion does one cling to what?' it is said, 'Established in the first perversion...' and so on. A person established in the first perversion clings to sensual pleasures by means of a certain kind of clinging; this clinging is called 'clinging to sensual pleasures.' For the rest, the connection should be made by this method.

“Yena kāmupādānena kāmehi puggalo saṃyujjati, ayaṃ kāmupādānadhammo ‘kāmayogo’ti vuccatī”tiādinā yojanā kātabbā. Sesānaṃ yojanatthādayo pāḷito, aṭṭhakathāto ca pākaṭā.

The connection should be made thus: 'By whatever clinging to sensual pleasures a person is yoked to sensual pleasures, that phenomenon of clinging to sensual pleasures is called "the yoke of sensual pleasures,"' and so on. The connections, meanings, and so on, of the remaining terms are clear from the Pāli text and from the commentary.

85. “Āhārādīsu katame katamā disā”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha imā catasso disā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha tesu āhāracatukkādīsu dasasu catukkesu paṭhamo paṭhamo kabaḷīkārāhārādiko [V 0.0386] paṭhamā disā, dutiyo dutiyo phassāhārādiko dutiyā disā, tatiyo tatiyo viññāṇāhārādiko tatiyā disā, catuttho catuttho manosañcetanāhārādiko catutthā disāti veditabbā.

85. Since it is to be asked, 'Among the nutriments and so forth, which are which directions?,' it is said, 'Herein, these are the four directions,' etc. Herein, among those ten sets of four, such as the four nutriments, the first of each, beginning with the nutriment of edible food, is the first direction; the second of each, beginning with the nutriment of contact, is the second direction; the third of each, beginning with the nutriment of consciousness, is the third direction; the fourth of each, beginning with the nutriment of mental volition, is the fourth direction. Thus it should be understood.

“Tāsu catūsu disāsu tesu kabaḷīkārāhārādīsu dhammesu katame dhammā katamassa upakkilesā”ti pucchitabbattā ime āhārādayo dhammā imassa puggalassa upakkilesāti vibhattāti dassetuṃ “tattha yo ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro…pe… ime diṭṭhicaritassa udattassa upakkilesā”ti vuttaṃ. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana – “kabaḷīkārāhāro āhārotiādi āhārādīsu ye yassa puggalassa upakkilesā, taṃ vibhajitvā dassetuṃ āraddha”nti (netti. aṭṭha. 85) vuttaṃ. Dasannaṃ suttānanti ekadesabhūtānaṃ dasannaṃ suttānaṃ. Atthoti sabhāvadhammo. Saddattho hi asamānoti. “Byañjanameva nāna”nti etena ca saddatthassa nānattaṃ dasseti.

Since it should be asked, "In these four directions, among these phenomena such as the nutriment of edible food, which phenomena are the defilements of which person?," in order to show by analysis that these phenomena, such as nutriment, are the defilements of this individual, it is said: "The nutriment of edible food… these are the defilements of one of a speculative disposition, of the haughty." In the Commentary, however, it is said: "The nutriment of edible food, etc.—it is begun in order to show by analysis which defilements among the nutriments, etc., belong to which individual." ‘Of ten discourses’—this refers to ten discourses that are a portion. ‘Meaning’—this is an intrinsic nature of phenomena. For the meaning of the words is indeed not uniform. ‘Only the wording differs’—this also shows the diversity in the meaning of the words.

“Kabaḷīkārāhārādīsu [M 0.0266] katame āhārādayo katamena vimokkhamukhena pariññaṃ pahānaṃ gacchantī”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha yo ca kabaḷīkāro”tiādi vuttaṃ.

Since it should be asked, "Among the nutriments beginning with the nutriment of edible food, which nutriments, by which gateway to liberation, attain full understanding and abandoning?," it is said, "Therein, the nutriment of edible food..." and so forth.

Itīti evaṃ vuttappakārā. Sabbeti sabbe āhārādayo dhammā lokavaṭṭānusārino bhavanti. Teti te sabbe āhārādayo dhammā. Lokāti lokato vaṭṭato. Tīhi vimokkhamukhehi aniccānupassanādīhi niyyanti.

‘Thus’—this refers to what has been stated in this manner. ‘All’—this means all phenomena such as nutriment, etc., accord with the world’s round of existence. ‘Those’—this refers to all those phenomena such as nutriment, etc. ‘From the world’—this means from the world, from the round of existence. Through the three gateways to liberation, such as the contemplation of impermanence, etc., they go forth.

86. Saṃkilesapakkhe disābhūtā āhāracatukkādayo dasa catukkā dhammā ācariyena niddhāretvā dassitā, amhehi ca ñātā, “vodānapakkhe katame disābhūtā dhammā”ti pucchitabbattā vodānapakkhe disābhūte dhamme dassetuṃ “catasso paṭipadā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Cattāro vihārāti dibbavihārā brahmavihārā ariyavihārā āneñjavihārāti cattāro vihārā. Tesu rūpāvacarasamāpattiyo dibbavihārā, catasso appamaññāyo brahmavihārā, catasso phalasamāpattiyo ariyavihārā, catasso arūpasamāpattiyo āneñjavihārā cattāro acchariyā abbhutā dhammāti mānapahānaṃ ālayasamugghāto avijjāpahānaṃ bhavūpasamoti cattāro acchariyaabbhutadhammā. Cattāri adhiṭṭhānānīti saccādhiṭṭhānaṃ cāgādhiṭṭhānaṃ paññādhiṭṭhānaṃ upasamādhiṭṭhānanti cattāri adhiṭṭhānāni. Catasso samādhibhāvanāti chandasamādhibhāvanā vīriyasamādhibhāvanā cittasamādhibhāvanā vīmaṃsāsamādhibhāvanāti catasso samādhibhāvanā. Cattāro [V 0.0387] sukhabhāgiyāti indriyasaṃvaro tapo bojjhaṅgo sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggoti cattāro sukhabhāgiyā. Avasesā pākaṭā.

86. The ten tetrads of phenomena, such as the four nutriments, which act as directions on the side of defilement, have been determined and shown by the teacher, and are known by us. Therefore, since it should be asked, "Which phenomena act as directions on the side of purification?", to show the phenomena acting as directions on the side of purification, it is said, beginning with "the four courses of practice." ‘The four abodes’—these are the divine abodes, the Brahmā abodes, the noble abodes, and the imperturbable abodes. Among these, the form-sphere attainments are the divine abodes, the four immeasurables are the Brahmā abodes, the four fruition attainments are the noble abodes, and the four formless attainments are the imperturbable abodes. ‘The four amazing and wonderful phenomena’—these are the abandoning of conceit, the uprooting of attachment, the abandoning of ignorance, and the stilling of existence. ‘The four resolutions’—these are the resolution of truth, the resolution of renunciation, the resolution of wisdom, and the resolution of peace. ‘The four developments of concentration’—these are the development of concentration through zeal, the development of concentration through energy, the development of concentration through mind, and the development of concentration through investigation. ‘The four things pertaining to happiness’—these are sense restraint, austerity, the enlightenment factors, and the relinquishing of all acquisitions. The rest are obvious.

“Catūsu catūsu paṭipadādīsu katamo paṭipadādiko paṭhamo satipaṭṭhānādiko bhavatī”ti pucchitabbattā “paṭhamā paṭipadā paṭhamaṃ satipaṭṭhāna”ntiādi vuttaṃ. “Paṭipadādayo paññāpadaṭṭhānādikā, satipaṭṭhānādayo pana satipadaṭṭhānādikā, tasmā ‘paṭhamā paṭipadā paṭhamaṃ satipaṭṭhāna’ntiādiyojanā kātabbā”ti vattabbattā “paṭhamā paṭipadā bhāvitā bahulīkatā paṭhamaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ pūretī”tiādi vuttaṃ, pūrakapūretabbabhāvato tathā yojanā kātabbāti adhippāyo. Atha [M 0.0267] vā “bhāvitā bahulīkatā katame paṭipadādayo katame satipaṭṭhānādike pūrentī”ti pucchitabbattā “paṭhamā paṭipadā bhāvitā bahulīkatā paṭhamaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ pūretī”tiādi vuttaṃ.

Because it should be asked, "Among the fourfold groups of paths, etc., which path, etc., is the first foundation of mindfulness, etc.?" it is said, "The first path is the first foundation of mindfulness," etc. Because the paths, etc., are based on the footing of wisdom, etc., while the foundations of mindfulness, etc., are based on the footing of mindfulness, etc., therefore, it should be said that the connection should be made as "the first path is the first foundation of mindfulness," etc. Because it should be said that "the first path, when developed and cultivated, fulfills the first foundation of mindfulness," etc., the meaning is that the connection should be made in terms of what fulfills and what is to be fulfilled. Alternatively, because it should be asked, "Which paths, etc., when developed and cultivated, fulfill which foundations of mindfulness, etc.?" it is said, "The first path, when developed and cultivated, fulfills the first foundation of mindfulness," etc.

87. “Tesu dasasu paṭipadācatukkādīsu katame dhammā katamā disā, katame dhammā katamā disā”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha imā catasso disā paṭhamā paṭipadā, paṭhamo satipaṭṭhāno”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tatthāti tesu dasasu paṭipadācatukkādīsu. Imā mayā vuccamānā paṭhamā paṭipadādayo disā catasso disā bhavanti.

87. Since it should be asked, "Among those ten tetrads beginning with the paths, which phenomena are which direction, and which phenomena are which direction?" it is said, "Therein, these four directions are the first path, the first foundation of mindfulness," etc. ‘Therein’—this refers to those ten tetrads beginning with the paths. These first paths, etc., which are being spoken of by me, constitute the four directions.

“Tesu catūsu disābhūtesu paṭipadācatukkādīsu katamo disābhūto attho katamassa puggalassa bhesajja”nti pucchitabbattā “tattha paṭhamā paṭipadā…pe… diṭṭhicaritassa udattassa bhesajja”nti vuttaṃ.

Since it should be asked, "Among those fourfold groups of paths, etc., that act as directions, which item acting as a direction is the remedy for which individual?," it was said: "Therein, the first path... is the remedy for one of a speculative disposition, for the haughty."

“Tesu dasasu paṭipadādicatukkesu dhammesu katamo katamo katamaṃ katamaṃ vimokkhamukha”nti pucchitabbattā “tattha dukkhā ca paṭipadā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Attho pana ṭīkāyaṃ vitthārena vutto pākaṭo. Saṃkilesapakkhe disābhūtā āhāracatukkādayo dasa catukkā samatikkamitabbapahātabbabhāvena niddhāritā, vodānapakkhe pana disābhūtā paṭipadācatukkādayo dasa catukkā samatikkamapahāyakabhāvena niddhāritā.

Since it should be asked, 'Among those ten tetrads of phenomena beginning with the paths of practice, which is the door to liberation for which?', it is said, 'Therein, the painful path of practice,' and so on. The meaning, however, is explained in detail in the subcommentary and is clear. On the side of defilement, the ten tetrads, such as the four nutriments, which are indicative, are determined by their nature as what should be transcended and abandoned. On the side of purification, however, the ten tetrads, such as the four paths of practice, which are indicative, are determined by their nature as what accomplishes transcendence and abandonment.

“Tesaṃ āhāracatukkādīnaṃ dasannaṃ catukkānaṃ samatikkamanapahānasaṅkhātaṃ yaṃ vikkīḷitañca tesaṃ paṭipadācatukkādīnaṃ dasannaṃ catukkānaṃ bhāvanāsaṅkhātaṃ yaṃ vikkīḷitañca sacchikiriyāsaṅkhātaṃ yaṃ vikkīḷitañca atthi, taṃ tividhaṃ vikkīḷitaṃ katamesaṃ puggalānaṃ vikkīḷitaṃ [V 0.0388] bhavatī”ti pucchitabbattā “tesaṃ vikkīḷita”nti vuttaṃ. Atha vā “yathāvuttappakārehi vimokkhamukhehi ye buddhapaccekabuddhasāvakā vimucciṃsu, tesu buddhasseva vikkīḷitaṃ bhavati kiṃ, paccekabuddhasseva vikkīḷitaṃ bhavati kiṃ, sāvakasseva vikkīḷitaṃ bhavati kiṃ, udāhu sabbesaṃ buddhapaccekabuddhasāvakānaṃ vikkīḷitaṃ bhavati ki”nti vicāraṇāya sambhavato “tesaṃ vikkīḷita”nti vuttaṃ. Yathāvuttappakārehi vimokkhamukhehi ye buddhapaccekabuddhasāvakā mucciṃsu, tesaṃ buddhapaccekabuddhasāvakānaṃ vikkīḷitaṃ. Yaṃ āhāracatukkādīnaṃ dasannaṃ catukkānaṃ [M 0.0268] saparasantāne samatikkamanapahānañca yā paṭipadācatukkādīnaṃ dasannaṃ catukkānaṃ saparasantāne bhāvanāsampādanā, sacchikiriyāsampādanā ca atthi, idaṃ sabbaṃ vikkīḷitaṃ nāma bhavatīti attho.

Since it should be asked, 'The play designated as transcending and abandoning with regard to the ten tetrads beginning with the nutriments; and the play designated as development and the play designated as realization with regard to the ten tetrads beginning with the paths of practice—to which individuals does this threefold play belong?', it is said, 'Their play.' Or, since the consideration arises, 'Of those Buddhas, Paccekabuddhas, and disciples who were liberated through the doors to liberation as described, does the play belong only to the Buddha, or only to the Paccekabuddha, or only to the disciple, or does it belong to all Buddhas, Paccekabuddhas, and disciples?', it is said, 'Their play.' The play of those Buddhas, Paccekabuddhas, and disciples who were liberated through the doors to liberation as described. The meaning is that whatever transcending and abandoning of the ten tetrads beginning with the nutriments there is in one's own and others' continua, and whatever accomplishment of development and accomplishment of realization of the ten tetrads beginning with the paths of practice there is in one's own and others' continua, all this is called 'play'.

“Sabbesaṃ āhāracatukkādīnaṃ dasannaṃ catukkānaṃ sabbe paṭipadācatukkādayo dasa catukkā paṭipakkhā honti kiṃ, udāhu yathākkamaṃ catukkānaṃ catukkā paṭipakkhā honti ki”nti vicāraṇāya sambhavato yathākkamaṃ catukkānaṃ catukkā paṭipakkhā honti pahātabbapahāyakabhāvenāti dassento “cattāro āhārā tesaṃ paṭipakkho catasso paṭipadā”tiādimāha. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana – “idāni āhārādīnaṃ paṭipadādīhi yena samatikkamanaṃ, taṃ nesaṃ paṭipakkhabhāvaṃ dassento ‘cattāro āhārā tesaṃ paṭipakkho catasso paṭipadā’tiādimāhā”ti (netti. aṭṭha. 87) vuttaṃ. Tattha saṃkilesapakkhe cattāro ye āhārā niddhāritā, tesaṃ catunnaṃ āhārānaṃ vodānapakkhe yā catasso paṭipadā niddhāritā, tā catasso paṭipadā paṭipakkho āhārānaṃ pahātabbattā, paṭipadānaṃ pana pahāyakattā. Satipi āhārānaṃ appahātabbabhāve vipassanārammaṇattā āhārapaṭibaddhachandarāgappahānavasena pahātabbabhāvo vuttoti evamādiyojanā kātabbā.

Since the consideration arises, 'Are all ten tetrads beginning with the paths of practice the opposites of all ten tetrads beginning with the nutriments, or are the tetrads opposites of their corresponding tetrads?', to show that the tetrads are opposites of their corresponding tetrads in terms of what is to be abandoned and what abandons, he said, 'The four nutriments—their opposite is the four paths of practice,' and so on. In the Commentary, however, it is said: 'Now, showing by what means the nutriments, etc., are transcended by the paths of practice, etc., thereby demonstrating their nature as opposites, he said, “The four nutriments—their opposite is the four paths of practice,” and so on.' Therein, for the four nutriments determined on the side of defilement, the four paths of practice determined on the side of purification are the opposite, because the nutriments are to be abandoned, while the paths of practice are what abandon. Although the nutriments are not to be abandoned in themselves, since they are an object for insight, their 'to-be-abandoned' nature is stated in the sense of abandoning the desire and lust connected with the nutriments; the application should be made in this way.

Sīhāti sīhasadisā buddhā ca sīhasadisā paccekabuddhā ca sīhasadisā sāvakā cāti sīhasadisā visuṃ visuṃ yojetabbā. Sāvakā pana ahatarāgadosamohāpi santi, tepi “sīhā”ti maññeyyunti taṃ nivattāpanatthaṃ “hatarāgadosamohā”ti vuttaṃ. Hanitabbāti hatā, rāgo ca doso ca moho ca rāgadosamohā, hatā rāgadosamohā etehi sāvakehīti hatarāgadosamohā, sāvakāti yojanā kātabbā sāvakānaṃyeva byabhicārasambhavatoti. Tesaṃ sīhānaṃ buddhānaṃ, tesaṃ sīhānaṃ paccekabuddhānaṃ, tesaṃ sīhānaṃ sāvakānaṃ bhāvanā vodānapakkhe bhāvitabbānaṃ bodhipakkhiyadhammānaṃ bhāvanā vaḍḍhanā ca, sacchikiriyā vodānapakkheyeva sacchikātabbānaṃ [V 0.0389] phalanibbānānaṃ sacchikiriyā ca, byantīkiriyā saṃkilesapakkhe pahātabbānaṃ pahānasaṅkhātā byantīkiriyā ca vikkīḷitaṃ nāma bhavati.

‘Lions’ (sīhā): Buddhas are like lions, Paccekabuddhas are like lions, and disciples are like lions—thus, ‘lion-like’ should be applied to each separately. However, since there are disciples who have not destroyed greed, hatred, and delusion, to prevent them from being considered ‘lions,’ it is stated, ‘those who have destroyed greed, hatred, and delusion.’ ‘To be destroyed’ (hanitabbā) means ‘destroyed’ (hatā). Greed, hatred, and delusion are ‘greed-hatred-delusion’ (rāgadosamohā). ‘Greed-hatred-delusion have been destroyed by these disciples’ is the meaning of ‘hatarāgadosamohā.’ The connection should be made with ‘disciples’ because deviation is possible only in the case of disciples. For those lions—the Buddhas, those lions—the Paccekabuddhas, and those lions—the disciples, the cultivation and development of the factors of awakening to be cultivated on the side of purification; the realization of the fruits and Nibbāna to be realized on the side of purification; and the eradication, designated as the abandonment of what is to be abandoned on the side of defilement—this is called their ‘sport’ (vikkīḷita).

Indriyādhiṭṭhānanti [M 0.0269] saddhindriyādīnaṃ indriyānaṃ adhiṭṭhānaṃ pavattanaṃ bhāvanā, sacchikiriyā ca. Vipariyāsānadhiṭṭhānanti vipallāsānaṃ adhiṭṭhānaṃ pahānavasena appavattanaṃ, anuppādanañca saṅkhepato vikkīḷitaṃ nāmāti gahitaṃ. Indriyāni saddhindriyādīni saddhammagocaro saddhammassa vodānapakkhassa gocaro pavattanahetūti adhippetāni. Vipariyāsā vipallāsā kilesagocaro saṃkilesapakkhassa gocaro pavattihetūti adhippetā.

‘The foundation of the faculties’ (indriyādhiṭṭhāna) means the establishment, setting in motion, development, and realization of the faculties beginning with the faculty of faith. ‘The non-foundation of perversions’ (vipariyāsānadhiṭṭhāna) means the non-occurrence and non-arising of perversions by means of abandonment. In brief, this is taken to be what is called ‘sport’ (vikkīḷita). The faculties, beginning with the faculty of faith, are intended as having the good Dhamma as their domain, being the sphere of the purification side of the good Dhamma, and the cause of its occurrence. The perversions (`vipariyāsā` or `vipallāsā`) are intended as having the defilements as their domain, being the sphere of the defilement side, and the cause of their occurrence.

“Cattāro āhārātiādinā saṃkilesapakkhe āhāracatukkādīnaṃ dasannaṃ catukkānaṃ taṇhācaritādīnaṃ catunnaṃ puggalānaṃ upakkilesavibhāvanāmukhena yā niddhāraṇā ācariyena katā, ‘catasso paṭipadā’tiādinā ca vodānapakkhe paṭipadācatukkādīnaṃ dasannaṃ catukkānaṃ taṇhācaritādīnaṃ catunnaṃ puggalānaṃ vodānavibhāvanāmukhena yā niddhāraṇā ācariyena katā, sā ayaṃ niddhāraṇā katamassa nayassa samuṭṭhānaṃ bhūmīti vuccatī”ti pucchitabbattā “ayaṃ vuccati sīhavikkīḷitassa nayassa bhūmī”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha ayanti yā ayaṃ vuttanayena dvippakārā niddhāraṇā katā, sā ayaṃ dvippakārā niddhāraṇā sīhavikkīḷitassa nayassa bhūmi pavattiṭṭhānaṃ samuṭṭhānanti nayasamuṭṭhānakosallehi puggalehi vuccatīti yojanā kātabbāti.

Since it should be asked: 'The determination made by the Teacher, beginning with “The four nutriments,” regarding the ten tetrads on the side of defilement, starting with the tetrad of nutriments, for the four types of individuals, starting with the one of craving-temperament, by way of manifesting corruptions; and the determination made by the Teacher, beginning with “The four paths of practice,” regarding the ten tetrads on the side of purification, starting with the tetrad of paths of practice, for the four types of individuals, starting with the one of craving-temperament, by way of manifesting purification—this determination is called the ground and origination of which method?', it is stated, 'This is called the ground of the Lion’s Sport method.' Therein, 'this' means: the construction should be made that 'This twofold determination made in the manner described is called the ground (bhūmi), the place of occurrence (pavattiṭṭhāna), and the origination (samuṭṭhāna) of the Lion’s Sport method by individuals skilled in methods and their origination.'

“Vuttappakārāya niddhāritāya nayassa bhūmibhāvo kasmā viññāyatī”ti vattabbattā “tenāhā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tena vuttappakārāya niddhāraṇāya nayabhūmibhāvena “yo neti…pe… kusalāti cā”ti yaṃ vacanaṃ ācariyo āha, tena vacanena viññāyatīti.

Since it should be stated, 'Why is it understood that what has been determined in the manner described is the ground of the method?', the text beginning 'Therefore, he said' is stated. Because it is the ground for the method through the determination made in the manner described, it is understood by that statement which the Teacher spoke: 'That which leads… to the wholesome,' etc.

Sīhavikkīḷitanayabhūmi ācariyena vibhāvitā, amhehi ca ñātā, “katamā tipukkhalanayabhūmī”ti pucchitabbattā tipukkhalanayabhūmiṃ vibhāvetukāmo “tattha ye dukkhāya paṭipadāyā”tiādimāha. Evaṃ sati “ayaṃ saṃkileso, tīṇi akusalamūlānī”tiādivacanameva ācariyena vattabbaṃ, kasmā pana “tattha ye dukkhāya paṭipadāyā”tiādivacanaṃ vattabbanti? Saccaṃ, tipukkhalanayabhūmibhāvanā pana ugghaṭitaññuādipuggalattayavasena pavattā, tasmā ugghaṭitaññuādipuggalattayaṃ vibhāvetuṃ “tattha ye dukkhāya paṭipadāyā”tiādivacanaṃ vuttaṃ. Evamapi “tattha yo sukhāya paṭipadāya khippābhiññāya [V 0.0390] niyyāti, ayaṃ ugghaṭitaññū”tiādivacanameva vattabbaṃ[M 0.0270], kasmā pana “tattha ye dukkhāya paṭipadāyā”tiādivacanaṃ vattabbanti? Saccaṃ, ugghaṭitaññuādipuggalattayaṃ pana sīhavikkīḷitanayato tipukkhalanayassa niggacchanato nikkhamanato sīhavikkīḷitanayabhūmivibhāvanāyaṃ paṭipadāvibhāgato vibhāvitapuggalacatukkato niddhāritaṃ, sīhavikkīḷitanayabhūmivibhāvanāyaṃ paṭipadāvibhāgato vibhāvitaṃ puggalacatukkaṃ paṭhamaṃ vibhāvetuṃ “tattha ye dukkhāya paṭipadāyā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tatthāti yo paṭipadācatukko sīhavikkīḷitanayabhūmivibhāvanāyaṃ niddhārito, tasmiṃ paṭipadācatukke. Yeti ye dandhaudattā diṭṭhicaritapuggalā yathākkamaṃ sukhāya paṭipadāya dandhābhiññāya ca sukhāya paṭipadāya khippābhiññāya ca niyyanti, iti niyyakā dve puggalā ca niddhāritā. “Tesaṃ catunnaṃ puggalānaṃ katamo saṃkileso”ti pucchitabbattā “tesaṃ catunnaṃ puggalānaṃ ayaṃ saṃkileso”ti vissajjetuṃ “tesaṃ catunnaṃ puggalānaṃ ayaṃ saṃkileso”tiādi vuttaṃ. Cattāro āhārā niddhāritā…pe… cattāri agatigamanāni niddhāritāni, iti ayaṃ dasavidho āhāracatukkādicatukko tesaṃ catunnaṃ puggalānaṃ saṃkileso hoti. Tesaṃ catunnaṃ puggalānaṃ saṃkileso ācariyena niddhārito, “katamaṃ vodāna”nti pucchitabbattā “tesaṃ catunnaṃ puggalānaṃ idaṃ vodāna”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Catasso paṭipadā niddhāritā, catasso appamāṇā niddhāritā, iti idaṃ dasavidhaṃ paṭipadācatukkādicatukkabhūtaṃ dhammajātaṃ tesaṃ catunnaṃ puggalānaṃ vodānaṃ hoti.

The ground of the Lion’s Sport method has been explained by the Teacher, and it is known to us. Because it should be asked, ‘What is the ground of the three-basket method?’, wishing to explain the ground of the three-basket method, he said, ‘Therein, those who by the painful practice…,’ and so on. This being so, the statement that should have been made by the Teacher is, ‘This is defilement, the three unwholesome roots,’ etc. Why then was the statement, ‘Therein, those who by the painful practice…,’ etc., made? True, the explanation of the ground of the three-basket method proceeds by way of the three types of individuals: the one of quick understanding, and so on. Therefore, to explain these three types of individuals, the statement, ‘Therein, those who by the painful practice…,’ etc., was made. Even so, the statement that should have been made is, ‘Therein, one who goes forth by the pleasant practice with quick direct knowledge, this is the one of quick understanding,’ etc. Why then was the statement, ‘Therein, those who by the painful practice…,’ etc., made? True, the three types of individuals—the one of quick understanding, and so on—are determined from the four types of individuals explained by the division of practices in the explanation of the ground of the Lion’s Sport method, by emerging from the Lion’s Sport method into the three-basket method. To first explain the four types of individuals explained by the division of practices in the explanation of the ground of the Lion’s Sport method, ‘Therein, those who by the painful practice…,’ etc., was stated. ‘Therein’ (tattha) means: in that tetrad of practices which was determined in the explanation of the ground of the Lion’s Sport method. ‘Those’ (ye) means: those slow and ardent individuals of speculative temperament who, respectively, go forth by the pleasant practice with slow direct knowledge and by the pleasant practice with quick direct knowledge; thus, two individuals who go forth are determined. Because it should be asked, ‘What is the defilement of these four individuals?’, to answer, ‘This is the defilement of these four individuals,’ it is stated, ‘This is the defilement of these four individuals,’ and so on. The four nutriments are determined… the four wrong courses are determined. Thus, this tenfold tetrad, such as the tetrad of nutriments, is the defilement of these four individuals. The defilement of these four individuals has been determined by the Teacher. Because it should be asked, ‘What is the purification?’, it is stated, ‘This is the purification of these four individuals,’ and so on. The four practices are determined, the four immeasurables are determined. Thus, this tenfold collection of phenomena, which is the tetrad of practices, etc., is the purification of these four individuals.

88. “Tesu catūsu puggalesu katamo puggalo ugghaṭitaññū, katamo puggalo vipañcitaññū, katamo puggalo neyyo”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha ye”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Pubbepi ‘tattha ye’tiādinā cattāro puggalā niddhāritā, kasmā pana puna “tattha ye’tiādinā cattāro puggalā niddhāritā”ti ce vadeyya? Pubbe saṃkilesavodānaṃ sāmibhāvena niddhāritā, pacchā pana ugghaṭitaññuādīnaṃ avayavānaṃ samūhabhāvena niddhāritāti visesattho gahetabbo. Tattha ye…pe… ime dve puggalāti ettha yojanattho heṭṭhā vuttasadisova. Tatthāti tesu catūsu puggalesu. Yoti udatto diṭṭhicarito. Ayanti ayaṃ niyato udatto diṭṭhicarito. Puna yoti udattova taṇhācarito ca mando diṭṭhicarito ca. Sādhāraṇāyāti dukkhāya paṭipadāya khippābhiññāya ca sukhāya paṭipadāya dandhābhiññāya ca.

88. Because it should be asked, ‘Among these four individuals, which individual is the one of quick understanding, which individual is the one who understands through elaboration, and which individual is the trainable one?’, ‘Therein, those…,’ and so on, is stated. If one should ask, ‘Earlier, the four individuals were determined with ‘Therein, those…,’ etc. Why then are the four individuals determined again with ‘Therein, those…,’ etc.?’, the answer is: Earlier, they were determined by way of their ownership of defilement and purification; but later, they are determined by way of the collective nature of the components of the one of quick understanding, etc. This is the special meaning to be understood. Regarding ‘Therein, those… these two individuals,’ here the meaning of the construction is similar to what was stated previously. ‘Therein’ (tattha) means: among those four individuals. ‘Who’ (yo) means: the ardent individual of speculative temperament. ‘This’ (ayaṃ) means: this determined ardent individual of speculative temperament. Again, ‘who’ (yo) means: the ardent individual of craving-temperament and the slow individual of speculative temperament. ‘Common to both’ (sādhāraṇāya) means: by the painful practice with quick direct knowledge and by the pleasant practice with slow direct knowledge.

“Ugghaṭitaññuādayo [M 0.0271] tayo puggalā ācariyena niddhāritā, tesu tīsu puggalesu katamassa katamassa katamaṃ katamaṃ bhagavā upadisatī”ti pucchitabbattā “tattha bhagavā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Atha vā “paṭipadābhedena puggalabhedo ācariyena vibhāvito, kathaṃ desanābhedena [V 0.0391] puggalabhedo vibhāvito”ti vattabbattā desanābhedenapi puggalabhedaṃ vibhāvetuṃ “tattha bhagavā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tatthāti tesu tīsu ugghaṭitaññuādīsu puggalesu. “Samathadesanāvipassanādesanābhedeneva puggalabhedo vibhāvito”ti vattabbattā mududhammadesanātikkhadhammadesanābhedenapi puggalabhedaṃ vibhāvetuṃ “tattha bhagavā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Sesesupi evameva anusandhyattho vattabbo.

Because it should be asked, ‘Among these three individuals—the one of quick understanding, etc.—determined by the Teacher, to which of them does the Blessed One prescribe which teaching?’, ‘Therein, the Blessed One…,’ and so on, is stated. Alternatively, because it should be stated, ‘The Teacher has explained the differentiation of individuals by the difference in practices; how has the differentiation of individuals been explained by the difference in teachings?’, to explain the differentiation of individuals even by the difference in teachings, ‘Therein, the Blessed One…,’ and so on, is stated. ‘Therein’ (tattha) means: among those three individuals—the one of quick understanding, etc. Because it should be stated, ‘The differentiation of individuals is explained only by the difference in teachings on serenity and insight,’ to explain the differentiation of individuals even by the difference in teachings on mild Dhamma and sharp Dhamma, ‘Therein, the Blessed One…,’ and so on, is stated. In the remaining cases too, the meaning of the connection should be stated in the same way.

Visuṃ visuṃ paṭipadābhedena cattāro hutvā visuṃ ca sampiṇḍitā ca paṭipadābhedena ceva desanābhedena ca tayo hontīti vibhāvetuṃ “tattha ye”tiādiṃ puna vatvā “iti kho cattāri hutvā tīṇi bhavantī”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha cattāri tīṇīti liṅgavipallāsaniddeso, “cattāro tayo”ti pana pakatiliṅganiddeso kātabbova.

To explain that they become four separately by way of the difference in practices, and also become three separately and combined by way of the difference in practices and the difference in teachings, it is stated again, ‘Therein, those…,’ etc., and it is stated, ‘Thus, indeed, having become four, they become three.’ Here, ‘four, three’ (cattāri tīṇi) is a designation with gender inversion; but the designation with natural gender, ‘four, three’ (cattāro tayo), should indeed be made.

“Tesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ katamo saṃkileso”ti pucchitabbattā “tesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ ayaṃ saṃkileso”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha ayaṃ saṃkilesoti “tīṇi akusalamūlāni…pe… sīlavipatti diṭṭhivipatti ācāravipattī”ti niddhāritānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ iti ayaṃ samūho saṃkileso hoti. “Tesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ saṃkileso ācariyena niddhārito, kathaṃ vodānaṃ niddhāritabba”nti vattabbattā “tesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ idaṃ vodāna”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha idaṃ vodānanti “tīṇi kusalamūlāni…pe… tīṇi vimokkhamukhāni suññataṃ animittaṃ appaṇihita”nti niddhāritānaṃ kusaladhammānaṃ samūhabhūtaṃ iti idaṃ dhammajātaṃ vodānaṃ hoti.

Because it should be asked, ‘What is the defilement of those three individuals?’, it is said, ‘This is the defilement of those three individuals,’ and so on. Herein, ‘this is the defilement’ means: this aggregate of unwholesome states that have been determined—namely, ‘the three unwholesome roots… failure in virtuous behavior, failure in view, and failure in conduct’—is defilement. Because it should be stated, ‘The defilement of those three individuals has been determined by the Teacher; how should their purification be determined?’, it is said, ‘This is the purification of those three individuals,’ and so on. Herein, ‘this is the purification’ means: this collection of wholesome states that have been determined—namely, ‘the three wholesome roots… the three doors to liberation: emptiness, signlessness, and the desireless’—is purification.

“Vuttappakārena cattāro hutvā tayo puggalā bhavantīti ācariyena vibhāvitā, tayo hutvā kittakā puggalā bhavantī”ti vattabbabhāvato “iti kho cattāri hutvā tīṇi bhavanti, tīṇi hutvā dve bhavanti taṇhācarito ca diṭṭhicarito cā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Itīti heṭṭhā vuttappakārena cattāri cattāro hutvā tīṇi tayo bhavanti. Tīṇi tayo hutvā taṇhācarito ca diṭṭhicarito cāti dve puggalā bhavanti.

Because it should be stated, ‘In the manner stated, having been four, they become three persons, as has been explained by the Teacher. Having been three, how many persons do they become?’, it is therefore said, ‘Thus, having been four, they become three; having been three, they become two, namely, one of craving temperament and one of speculative temperament,’ and so on. ‘Thus’ means: in the manner stated above, having been four, they become three. Having been three, they become two persons, namely, one of craving temperament and one of speculative temperament.

“Tesaṃ [M 0.0272] dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ katamo saṃkileso”ti vattabbabhāvato “tesaṃ dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ ayaṃ saṃkileso”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha ayaṃ saṃkilesoti “taṇhā ca avijjā ca…pe… sassatadiṭṭhi ca ucchedadiṭṭhi cā”ti niddhāritānaṃ akusaladhammānaṃ iti ayaṃ samūho saṃkileso hoti.

Because it should be stated, ‘What is the defilement of those two individuals?’, it is said, ‘This is the defilement of those two individuals,’ and so on. Herein, ‘this is the defilement’ means: this aggregate of unwholesome states that have been determined—namely, ‘craving and ignorance… the eternalist view and the annihilationist view’—is defilement.

“Tesaṃ [V 0.0392] dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ saṃkileso ācariyena niddhārito, kathaṃ vodāna”nti vattabbabhāvato “tesaṃ dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ idaṃ vodāna”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Idaṃ vodānanti “samatho ca vipassanā ca…pe… saupādisesā ca nibbānadhātu, anupādisesā ca nibbānadhātū”ti niddhāritānaṃ kusaladhammānaṃ samūhabhūtaṃ iti idaṃ dhammajātaṃ vodānaṃ hoti.

Since it should be said: 'The defilement of those two individuals has been determined by the teacher; how is their purification?' it is said, 'This is the purification of those two individuals,' and so on. 'This is the purification' means this collection of wholesome states that have been determined, namely, 'serenity and insight... down to... the Nibbāna element with residue remaining and the Nibbāna element without residue remaining.' Thus, this mass of dhammas is purification.

“Tīṇi akusalamūlānī”tiādinā saṃkilesapakkhe akusalamūlatikādīnaṃ dvinnaṃ dvādasannaṃ tikānaṃ, tiṇṇaṃ ugghaṭitaññuādipuggalānaṃ saṃkilesavibhāvanāmukhena yā niddhāraṇā katā, “tīṇi kusalamūlānī”tiādinā vodānapakkhe kusalamūlatikādīnaṃ dvinnaṃ dvādasannaṃ tikānaṃ, tiṇṇaṃ ugghaṭitaññuādipuggalānaṃ vodānavibhāvanāmukhena yā niddhāraṇā katā, ayaṃ vuttappakāraniddhāraṇā tipukkhalassa ca nayassa, aṅkusassa ca nayassa bhūmi samuṭṭhānaṃ pavattihetu nāmāti yojetvā “taṇhā ca avijjā cā”tiādinā saṃkilesapakkhe taṇhāavijjādukādīnaṃ pannarasannaṃ dukānaṃ, dvinnaṃ taṇhācaritadiṭṭhicaritānaṃ puggalānaṃ vodānavibhāvanāmukhena yā niddhāraṇā katā, “samatho ca vipassanā cā”tiādinā vodānapakkhe samathavipassanādukādīnaṃ ekūnavīsatidukānaṃ, dvinnaṃ taṇhācaritadiṭṭhicaritānaṃ puggalānaṃ vodānavibhāvanāmukhena yā niddhāraṇā katā, ayaṃ vuttappakārā nandiyāvaṭṭassa nayassa bhūmītipi nīharitvā yojetabbā. Puggalādhiṭṭhānavasena hi nandiyāvaṭṭanayato sīhavikkīḷitanayassa sambhavo, sīhavikkīḷitanayato ca tipukkhalanayassa sambhavo hoti. Dhammādhiṭṭhānavasena pana sīhavikkīḷitanayato tipukkhalanayassa sambhavo, tipukkhalanayato ca nandiyāvaṭṭanayassa sambhavo hoti. Tenāha aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “ante ‘taṇhā ca avijjā cā’tiādinā samathassa nayassa bhūmi dassitā. Teneva hi ‘cattāri hutvā tīṇi bhavanti, tīṇi hutvā dve bhavantī’ti vutta”nti (netti. aṭṭha. 88).

The determination made in the defilement section, beginning with 'the three unwholesome roots,' concerning the twelve triads starting with the triad of unwholesome roots, by way of explaining the defilement of the three individuals beginning with the one of quick understanding; and the determination made in the purification section, beginning with 'the three wholesome roots,' concerning the twelve triads starting with the triad of wholesome roots, by way of explaining the purification of the three individuals beginning with the one of quick understanding—this determination made in the manner stated should be connected as being the ground, the origin, and the cause for the occurrence of the method of the three individuals and the method of the goad. And the determination made in the defilement section, beginning with 'craving and ignorance,' concerning the fifteen dyads starting with the dyad of craving and ignorance, by way of explaining the defilement of the two individuals of craving temperament and speculative-view temperament; and the determination made in the purification section, beginning with 'serenity and insight,' concerning the nineteen dyads starting with the dyad of serenity and insight, by way of explaining the purification of the two individuals of craving temperament and speculative-view temperament—this determination made in the manner stated should also be extracted and connected as the ground for the method of the rightward-coiling whorl. For, when the individual is the basis, the method of the lion's sport arises from the method of the rightward-coiling whorl, and the method of the three individuals arises from the method of the lion's sport. But when the Dhamma is the basis, the method of the three individuals arises from the method of the lion's sport, and the method of the rightward-coiling whorl arises from the method of the three individuals. Therefore it is said in the commentary: 'At the end, with “craving and ignorance,” etc., the ground for the method of serenity is shown. For this very reason it is said: “Having been four, they become three; having been three, they become two.”'

“Kasmā [M 0.0273] pana ayaṃ vuttappakārāya niddhāraṇāya tipukkhalassa ca nayassa, aṅkusassa ca nayassa bhūmibhāvo viññāyatī”ti vattabbabhāvato “tenāhā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tena yathāvuttassa niddhāraṇāya bhūmibhāvena ācariyo “yo akusale…pe… disālocanenāti cā”ti yaṃ vacanaṃ āha, tena vacanena vuttappakārāya niddhāraṇāya tipukkhala…pe… yassa bhūmibhāvo viññāyatīti attho.

Since it should be said, 'But why is this determination in the stated manner understood to be the ground for the method of the three individuals and the method of the goad?' 'Therefore he said,' etc., was stated. The meaning is: because of that state of being the ground for the determination as stated, the teacher spoke the words, 'One who is unskillful... and... by examining the directions'; by that statement, it is understood that this determination in the stated manner is the ground for the method of the three individuals... and the goad.

“Ettāvatā nayasamuṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ hoti, aññaṃ natthī”ti vattabbattā “niyuttaṃ nayasamuṭṭhāna”nti vuttaṃ. Yena yena nayasamuṭṭhānena saṃkilesapakkhe vā akusalā dhammā niddhāritā[V 0.0393], vodānapakkhe vā kusalā dhammā niddhāritā, taṃ taṃ nayasamuṭṭhānaṃ niyuttaṃ yathārahaṃ niddhāretvā yujjitabbanti attho gahetabbo.

Since it should be said, 'To this extent the origination of methods is complete; there is nothing more,' it is called 'the applied origination of methods.' The meaning to be understood is this: by whatever origination of methods unwholesome states are determined in the defilement section, or wholesome states are determined in the purification section, that origination of methods is 'applied.' Having determined them appropriately, one should apply them.

Nayakkamena pana saṅkhepato dassayissāmi – dve puggalā, tayo puggalā, cattāro puggalāti puggalā tikoṭṭhāsā bhavanti, catudisā, chadisā, aṭṭhadisāti disāpi tikoṭṭhāsā bhavanti. Tattha dve puggalāti taṇhācarito puggalo, diṭṭhicarito puggaloti dve puggalā bhavanti. Tayo puggalāti ugghaṭitaññupuggalo, vipañcitaññupuggalo, neyyapuggaloti tayo puggalā bhavanti. Cattāro puggalāti dukkhāpaṭipadādandhābhiññādibhedena bhinnā mudindriyo taṇhācarito puggalo, mudindriyo diṭṭhicarito puggalo, tikkhindriyo taṇhācarito puggalo, tikkhindriyo diṭṭhicarito puggaloti cattāro puggalā bhavanti. Catudisāti saṃkilesapakkhe dve dve disā, vodānapakkhe dve dve disāti catudisā bhavanti. Chadisāti saṃkilesapakkhe tisso tisso disā, vodānapakkhe tisso tisso disāti chadisā bhavanti. Aṭṭhadisāti saṃkilesapakkhe catasso catasso disā, vodānapakkhe catasso catasso disāti aṭṭhadisā bhavanti. Tesu dve dve taṇhācaritadiṭṭhicarite puggale, catudisā ca nissāya nandiyāvaṭṭanayasamuṭṭhānaṃ bhavati. Tayo ugghaṭitaññuvipañcitaññuneyyapuggale ca chadisā ca nissāya tipukkhalanayasamuṭṭhānaṃ bhavati. Dukkhāpaṭipadādandhābhiññādibhedena bhinne cattāro mudindriyataṇhācaritatikkhindriyataṇhācaritamudindriyadiṭṭhicaritatikkhindriyadiṭṭhicarite puggale ca aṭṭhadisā ca nissāya sīhavikkīḷitanayasamuṭṭhānaṃ bhavati[M 0.0274]. Ekekasmiṃ nayasamuṭṭhāne vibhajite disālocanaaṅkusanayasamuṭṭhānānipi vibhajitāni bhavanti.

Now I will explain briefly in systematic order. Persons are of three categories: two persons, three persons, and four persons. Directions are also of three categories: the four directions, the six directions, and the eight directions. Herein, the two persons are the person of craving temperament and the person of speculative-view temperament. The three persons are the person who understands upon a brief indication, the person who understands upon detailed explanation, and the person who needs to be led. The four persons are those differentiated by way of painful progress with slow direct knowledge, etc., namely: the person of craving temperament with dull faculties, the person of speculative-view temperament with dull faculties, the person of craving temperament with sharp faculties, and the person of speculative-view temperament with sharp faculties. The four directions are two directions in the defilement section and two directions in the purification section. The six directions are three directions in the defilement section and three directions in the purification section. The eight directions are four directions in the defilement section and four directions in the purification section. Among these, based on the two persons—the one of craving temperament and the one of speculative-view temperament—and the four directions, the origination of the method of the rightward-coiling whorl occurs. Based on the three persons—the one who understands upon a brief indication, the one who understands upon detailed explanation, and the one who needs to be led—and the six directions, the origination of the method of the three individuals occurs. Based on the four persons differentiated by painful progress with slow direct knowledge, etc.—the person of craving temperament with dull faculties, the person of craving temperament with sharp faculties, the person of speculative-view temperament with dull faculties, and the person of speculative-view temperament with sharp faculties—and the eight directions, the origination of the method of the lion's sport occurs. When each origination of a method is analyzed, the originations of the methods of examining the directions and the goad are also analyzed.

“Kathaṃ nandiyāvaṭṭanayasamuṭṭhānaṃ bhavatī”ti ce vadeyya? “Taṇhā ca avijjā ca ahirikañca anottappañca assati ca asampajaññañca ayonisomanasikāro ca kosajjañca dovacassañca ahaṃkāro ca mamaṃkāro ca assaddhā ca pamādo ca asaddhammassavanañca asaṃvaro ca abhijjhā ca byāpādo ca nīvaraṇañca saṃyojanañca kodho ca upanāho ca makkho ca paḷāso ca issā ca maccherañca māyā ca sāṭheyyañca sassatadiṭṭhi ca ucchedadiṭṭhi cā”ti (netti. 88) dukadukavasena desito ayaṃ disābhūto akusaladhammasamūho dvinnaṃ taṇhācaritadiṭṭhicaritānaṃ puggalānaṃ saṃkileso hotīti saṃkilesapakkhe saṃkilesasāmaññabhāvena yojetvā “imesu pannarasasu dukadukavasena desitesu disābhūtesu akusaladhammesu katamo akusaladhammo katamassa puggalassa disā”ti manasāva disādhammabhāvena oloketvā “ayaṃ ayaṃ paṭhamo paṭhamo akusaladhammo taṇhācaritassa puggalassa saṃkilesapakkhe [V 0.0394] paṭhamā disā nāma, ayaṃ ayaṃ dutiyo dutiyo akusaladhammo diṭṭhicaritassa puggalassa saṃkilesapakkhe dutiyā disā nāmā”ti visuṃ visuṃ yojetvā samudayasaccadukkhasaccāni yathārahaṃ nīharitvā vibhajitabbadhammasabhāvo ca yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesena dassito, so saṃvaṇṇanāviseso ca nandiyāvaṭṭanayasamuṭṭhānaṃ bhavati, tassa olokanā ca yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesena dassitā, so saṃvaṇṇanāviseso ca disālocananayasamuṭṭhānaṃ bhavati, tathā oloketvā disāvisesabhūtassa dhammavisesassa puggalānaṃ nayanañca yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesena nayati, so saṃvaṇṇanāviseso ca aṅkusanayasamuṭṭhānaṃ bhavati.

“If one were to ask, ‘How does the origination of the Nandiyāvaṭṭa method occur?’ it should be said: ‘Craving and ignorance, lack of conscience and lack of moral dread, lack of mindfulness and lack of clear comprehension, unwise attention and laziness, being difficult to admonish and I-making and my-making, lack of faith and heedlessness, not listening to the true Dhamma and lack of restraint, covetousness and ill will, hindrances and fetters, anger and resentment, contempt and domineering, envy and stinginess, deceit and craftiness, the view of eternalism and the view of annihilationism.’ (Netti. 88) This mass of unwholesome states, taught in pairs, which has become a direction, is the defilement of two types of individuals—those with a craving temperament and those with a speculative temperament. It should be applied to the side of defilement as a common feature of defilement. ‘Among these fifteen pairs of unwholesome states taught, which have become directions, which unwholesome state is the direction for which individual?’ Having mentally considered them as directional states, one should discern: ‘This first unwholesome state is the first direction for an individual with a craving temperament on the side of defilement; this second unwholesome state is the second direction for an individual with a speculative temperament on the side of defilement.’ Having distinguished them separately, one should extract the truths of origin and suffering as appropriate. And the nature of the phenomena to be analyzed, which is shown by a particular mode of exposition, that particular mode of exposition is the origination of the Nandiyāvaṭṭa method. The examination of this, which is shown by that particular mode of exposition, that particular mode of exposition is the origination of the method of examining the directions. And having examined thus, the guiding of individuals to the particular state that has become a specific direction, by which that particular mode of exposition guides, that particular mode of exposition is the origination of the method of the goad.

“Samatho ca vipassanā ca, hirī ca ottappañca, sati ca sampajaññañca, yonisomanasikāro ca vīriyārambho ca, sovacassañca dhamme ñāṇañca anvaye ñāṇañca, khaye ñāṇañca anuppāde ñāṇañca, saddhā ca appamādo ca, saddhammassavanañca saṃvaro ca, anabhijjhā ca abyāpādo ca, rāgavirāgā ca cetovimutti, avijjāvirāgā ca paññāvimutti, abhisamayo ca appicchatā ca, santuṭṭhi ca akkodho ca, anupanāho ca amakkho ca, apaḷāso [M 0.0275] ca issāpahānañca macchariyappahānañca vijjā ca, vimutti ca saṅkhatārammaṇo ca vimokkho, asaṅkhatārammaṇo ca vimokkho, saupādisesā ca nibbānadhātu, anupādisesā ca nibbānadhātū”ti (netti. 88) tikadukavasena desitaṃ idaṃ disābhūtaṃ kusalasamūhadhammajātaṃ dvinnaṃ taṇhācaritadiṭṭhicaritānaṃ puggalānaṃ vodānaṃ hotīti vodānapakkhe vodānasāmaññabhāvena yojetvā “imesu ekūnavīsatiyā dukadukavasena vā desitesu disābhūtesu dhammesu katamo katamo kusaladhammo katamassa katamassa puggalassa disā”ti manasāva disādhammabhāvena oloketvā “ayaṃ paṭhamo paṭhamo kusaladhammo taṇhācaritassa puggalassa vodānapakkhe paṭhamā disā nāma, ayaṃ dutiyo dutiyo kusaladhammo diṭṭhicaritassa puggalassa vodānapakkhe dutiyā disā nāmā”ti visuṃ visuṃ yojetvā maggasaccanirodhasaccāni yathārahaṃ nīharitvā vibhajitabbadhammabhāvo ca yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesena dassito, so saṃvaṇṇanāviseso ca nandiyāvaṭṭanayasamuṭṭhānaṃ bhavati, tassa olokanā ca yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesena dassitā, so saṃvaṇṇanāviseso ca disālocananayasamuṭṭhānaṃ bhavati, tathā oloketvā disāvisesabhūtassa dhammavisesassa puggalānaṃ nayanañca yena saṃvaṇṇanāvisesena nayati, so saṃvaṇṇanāviseso ca aṅkusanayasamuṭṭhānaṃ bhavati.

“‘Serenity and insight; conscience and moral dread; mindfulness and clear comprehension; wise attention and arousal of energy; being easy to admonish, knowledge in the Dhamma, and knowledge of consequence; knowledge of destruction and knowledge of non-arising; faith and heedfulness; listening to the true Dhamma and restraint; non-covetousness and non-ill will; dispassion for lust and liberation of mind; dispassion for ignorance and liberation by wisdom; breakthrough and fewness of wishes; contentment and non-anger; non-resentment and non-contempt; non-domineering, abandoning of envy, and abandoning of stinginess; true knowledge and liberation; liberation with a conditioned object and liberation with an unconditioned object; the Nibbāna element with residue remaining and the Nibbāna element without residue remaining.’ (Netti. 88) This collection of wholesome states, taught by way of triads and dyads, which has become a direction, is the purification for two types of individuals—those with a craving temperament and those with a speculative temperament.
