Imesaṃ ekabījiādīnaṃ puggalānaṃ sattādhiṭṭhānekadesatthattā ceva dassanabhāgiyatthattā ca sattādhiṭṭhānekadesaṃ dassanabhāgiyaṃ suttaṃ ettakehi puggalehi niddisitabbanti niyametvā ācariyena vibhattaṃ, amhehi ca ñātaṃ, “sattādhiṭṭhānekadesaṃ dassanabhāgiyaṃ suttaṃ kittakehi puggalehi niddisitabba”nti pucchitabbattā –

Because these individuals, such as the one-seeder, are a portion of the sevenfold foundation and are partakers of vision, the sutta partaking of vision, which is a portion of the sevenfold foundation, should be explained by this number of individuals—having determined this, it was divided by the teacher, and it is known by us. Since it should be asked, 'By how many individuals should the sutta partaking of vision, which is a portion of the sevenfold foundation, be explained?'—

“Bhāvanābhāgiyaṃ suttaṃ dvādasahi puggalehi niddisitabbaṃ sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipannena, sakadāgāminā, anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipannena, anāgāminā, antarāparinibbāyinā, upahaccaparinibbāyinā, asaṅkhāraparinibbāyinā, sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyinā[M 0.0349], uddhaṃsotena akaniṭṭhagāminā, saddhāvimuttena, diṭṭhippattena, kāyasakkhinā cāti bhāvanābhāgiyaṃ suttaṃ imehi dvādasahi puggalehi niddisitabba”nti –

The sutta partaking of development should be explained by twelve individuals: one practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning, a once-returner, one practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning, a non-returner, one who attains final Nibbāna in the intermediate period, one who attains final Nibbāna upon landing, one who attains final Nibbāna without exertion, one who attains final Nibbāna with exertion, one bound upstream heading to the Akaniṭṭha realm, one liberated by faith, one attained to view, and a bodily witness. Thus, the sutta partaking of development should be explained by these twelve individuals.

Vuttaṃ. Tatthāpi sattādhiṭṭhānekadesaṃ bhāvanābhāgiyaṃ suttanti gahetabbaṃ. Sakadā…pe… pannena sakadāgāmimaggaṭṭhena puggalena, sakadāgāminā sakadāgāmiphalaṭṭhena, anāgāmi…pe… pannena anāgāmimaggaṭṭhena, anāgāminā anāgāmiphalaṭṭhena, avihādīsu pañcasu suddhāvāsesu āyuvemajjhaṃ anatikkamitvā arahattaṃ patvā parinibbāyanasabhāvena antarāparinibbāyīnāmakena anāgāminā, āyuvemajjhaṃ atikkamitvā arahattaṃ patvā parinibbāyanasabhāvena upahaccaparinibbāyīnāmakena anāgāminā, asaṅkhārena appayogena arahattaṃ patvā parinibbāyanasabhāvena [V 0.0465] asaṅkhāraparinibbāyīnāmakena anāgāminā, sasaṅkhārena sappayogena arahattaṃ patvā parinibbāyanasabhāvena sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyīnāmakena anāgāminā, avihādīhi uddhaṃ atappādīsu upapattisotena arahattaṃ patvā parinibbāyanasabhāvena uddhaṃsotanāmakena anāgāminā, akaniṭṭhaṃ gantvā arahattaṃ patvā parinibbāyanasabhāvena akaniṭṭhagāmīnāmakena anāgāminā, saddhāya vimuttattā saddhāvimuttanāmakena anāgāminā, diṭṭhiyā paññāya nirodhaṃ pattattā diṭṭhippattanāmakena anāgāminā cāti imehi ekādasahi ajhānalābhīpuggalehi ca, kāyena nāmakāye phuṭṭhānaṃ arūpajhānānaṃ anantaraṃ nibbānaṃ sacchikaroti, iti sacchikaraṇato kāyasakkhīnāmakena jhānalābhinā cāti dvādasahi puggalehi niddisitabbaṃ.

It was stated. Herein, it should be understood that the sutta partaking of development, which is a portion of the sevenfold foundation, is to be designated by twelve individuals. These are: the person established on the path of once-returning; the once-returner, established in the fruit of once-returning; the person established on the path of non-returning; the non-returner, established in the fruit of non-returning; the non-returner named 'one who attains final Nibbāna in the interval,' who by nature attains arahantship and final Nibbāna in the five Pure Abodes, such as Avihā, without exceeding the middle of the lifespan; the non-returner named 'one who attains final Nibbāna upon landing,' who by nature attains arahantship and final Nibbāna after exceeding the middle of the lifespan; the non-returner named 'one who attains final Nibbāna without prompting,' who by nature attains arahantship and final Nibbāna without exertion; the non-returner named 'one who attains final Nibbāna with prompting,' who by nature attains arahantship and final Nibbāna with exertion; the non-returner named 'upstream-bound,' who by nature attains arahantship and final Nibbāna by the stream of rebirth upwards from Avihā and other realms to Atappā and other realms; the non-returner named 'Akaniṭṭha-bound,' who by nature attains arahantship and final Nibbāna after going to Akaniṭṭha; the non-returner named 'faith-liberated,' due to being liberated by faith; and the non-returner named 'attained-to-view,' due to having attained cessation by view, by wisdom—these eleven being individuals who have not attained jhāna; and the jhāna-attainer named 'bodily witness,' because he realizes Nibbāna with the mental body immediately after the formless jhānas that are to be touched by the body.

Imesaṃ vuttappakārānaṃ puggalānaṃ sattādhiṭṭhānekadesatthattā ceva bhāvanābhāgiyatthattā ca sattādhiṭṭhānekadesaṃ bhāvanābhāgiyaṃ suttaṃ ettakehi puggalehi niddisitabbanti niyametvā ācariyena vibhattaṃ, amhehi ca ñātaṃ, “kittakehi puggalehi sattādhiṭṭhānekadesaṃ asekkhabhāgiyaṃ suttaṃ niddisitabba”nti vattabbattā –

Because these individuals of the stated types are a portion of the sevenfold foundation and are partakers of development, the sutta partaking of development, which is a portion of the sevenfold foundation, should be explained by this number of individuals—having determined this, it was divided by the teacher, and it is known by us. Since it should be stated, 'by how many individuals should the sutta partaking of the non-learner, which is a portion of the sevenfold foundation, be explained?'—

“Asekkhabhāgiyaṃ suttaṃ navahi puggalehi niddisitabbaṃ saddhāvimuttena, paññāvimuttena, suññatavimuttena, animittavimuttena, appaṇihitavimuttena, ubhatobhāgavimuttena, samasīsinā, paccekabuddhehi, sammāsambuddhehi cāti asekkhabhāgiyaṃ suttaṃ imehi navahi puggalehi niddisitabba”nti –

“The discourse pertaining to the non-learner’s share should be designated by nine individuals: one liberated by faith, one liberated by wisdom, one liberated by emptiness, one liberated by the signless, one liberated by the desireless, one liberated in both ways, the equal-headed one, the Paccekabuddhas, and the Perfectly Self-Enlightened Ones. Thus, the discourse pertaining to the non-learner’s share should be designated by these nine individuals.”

Vuttaṃ[M 0.0350]. Tattha sattādhiṭṭhānekadesaṃ asekkhabhāgiyaṃ suttaṃ niddisitabbanti yojetabbaṃ. Saddhāya kilesehi vimuttattā arahattaphalakkhaṇe saddhāvimutto arahā, tena saddhāvimuttena. Paññāya vimuttattā arahattaphalakkhaṇe paññāvimutto arahā, tena paññāvimuttena. Suññatavipassanāsaṅkhātena anattānupassanena vimuttattā suññatavimutto arahā, tena suññatavimuttena. Animittānupassanāsaṅkhātena aniccānupassanena vimuttattā animittavimutto arahā, tena animittavimuttena. Appaṇihitānupassanāsaṅkhātena dukkhānupassanena vimuttattā appaṇihitavimutto arahā, tena appaṇihitavimuttena. Ubhato rūpakāyanāmakāyato ubhatobhāgato vimuttattā ubhatobhāgavimutto arahā, tena ubhatobhāgavimuttena. Purimā pañca puggalā ajhānalābhino gahitā, ubhatobhāgavimutto pana jhānalābhīgahito.

It was stated. Here, it should be understood that the discourse pertaining to the non-learner’s share, which is a portion of the sevenfold foundation, should be designated. The Arahant liberated by faith, at the characteristic moment of the fruit of arahantship, is liberated from defilements by faith; by that faith-liberated one. The Arahant liberated by wisdom, at the characteristic moment of the fruit of arahantship, is liberated by wisdom; by that wisdom-liberated one. The Arahant liberated by emptiness, being liberated by the contemplation of non-self, which is called emptiness-insight; by that emptiness-liberated one. The Arahant liberated by the signless, being liberated by the contemplation of impermanence, which is called signless-contemplation; by that signless-liberated one. The Arahant liberated by the desireless, being liberated by the contemplation of suffering, which is called desireless-contemplation; by that desireless-liberated one. The Arahant liberated in both ways, being liberated from both the form-body and the name-body; by that one liberated in both ways. The first five individuals are taken as those who have not attained absorption, while the one liberated in both ways is taken as one who has attained absorption.

Samasīsī nāma iriyāpathasamasīsī, rogasamasīsī, jīvitasamasīsīti tividhā honti. Imesu [V 0.0466] tīsu samasīsīsu yo arahā catūsu iriyāpathesu ekekasmiṃ iriyāpathe arahattaṃ patvā aññaṃ iriyāpathaṃ asaṅkamitvā tasmiṃ tasmiṃ iriyāpatheyeva parinibbāyati, ayaṃ arahā iriyāpathasamasīsī nāma. Yo arahā yasmiṃ roge uppanne arahattaṃ patvā tato rogato anuṭṭhahitvā tasmiṃ rogeyeva parinibbāyati, ayaṃ arahā rogasamasīsī nāma. Yo arahā paccavekkhaṇavīthiyānantaraṃ bhavaṅgaṃ otaritvā tato maraṇāsannajavanavīthiyānantarameva parinibbāyati, ayaṃ arahā vārasamatāya jīvitasamasīsī nāma. Vārasamatāti ca paccavekkhaṇavīthi maggavithyānuvattakattā paccavekkhaṇavīthianantaraṃ pavattamānāyapi maraṇāsannavīthi maggavīthianantaraṃ pavattāti vattabbārahā, tasmā vīthianantaratā vārasamatā nāma. Tāya vārasamatāya ca jīvitasamasīsī vutto.

The equal-headed are of three kinds: equal in posture, equal in illness, and equal in lifespan. Among these three equal-headed ones, the Arahant who attains arahantship in one of the four postures and, without moving to another posture, attains final Nibbāna in that very posture—this Arahant is called equal in posture. The Arahant who attains arahantship when a certain illness arises and, without recovering from that illness, attains final Nibbāna in that very illness—this Arahant is called equal in illness. The Arahant who, after the reviewing thought-process, descends into the life-continuum and immediately thereafter attains final Nibbāna in the death-proximate javana thought-process—this Arahant is called equal in lifespan due to the equality of turns. The equality of turns is so called because the reviewing thought-process follows the path thought-process; thus, even though the death-proximate thought-process arises after the reviewing thought-process, it can be said to arise after the path thought-process. Therefore, this immediacy of thought-processes is called 'equality of turns'. Due to this equality of turns, he is called equal in lifespan.

Saha paṭisambhidāhi arahattaṃ pāpuṇīti etthapi paccavekkhaṇavīthiyānantaraṃ bhavaṅgaṃ otaritvā bhavaṅgato vuṭṭhāya pavattavīthiyā paṭisambhidāñāṇāni pavattanti. Vuttanayena vīthianantaratāya vārasamatāya “saha paṭisambhidāhī”ti vuttaṃ. Bhagavato sabbaññutaññāṇampi paccavekkhaṇavīthiyānantaraṃ bhavaṅgaṃ otaritvā bhavaṅgato vuṭṭhāya pavattavīthiyā paṭhamaṃ pavattatīti veditabbaṃ. Iminā [M 0.0351] jīvitasamasīsinā, sabbehi paccekabuddhehi, sabbehi sammāsambuddhehi cāti imehi navahi puggalehi sattādhiṭṭhānekadesaṃ asekkhabhāgiyaṃ suttaṃ niddisitabbaṃ.

Regarding the statement, “He attained arahantship together with the analytical knowledges,” here, too, after the reviewing thought-process, the mind subsides into the life-continuum. Emerging from the life-continuum, the analytical knowledges arise in the active thought-process. In the manner stated, due to the immediacy of the thought-process, the equality of turns, it is said, “together with the analytical knowledges.” The Blessed One’s omniscient knowledge, too, should be understood as arising first in the active thought-process after emerging from the life-continuum, following the reviewing thought-process. Thus, by this one equal in lifespan, by all Paccekabuddhas, and by all Perfectly Self-Enlightened Ones—that is, by these nine individuals—the discourse pertaining to the non-learner’s share, which is a portion of the sevenfold foundation, should be designated.

Imesaṃ puggalānaṃ sattādhiṭṭhānekadesatthattā ceva asekkhabhāgiyatthattā ca evaṃ iminā “lokuttaraṃ suttaṃ sattādhiṭṭhāna”ntiādinā pakārena vuttehi imehi chabbīsatiyā puggalehi ariyehi dassanabhāgiyavāsanābhāgiyaasekkhabhāgiyasuttānaṃ vasena lokuttaraṃ suttaṃ sattādhiṭṭhānekadesaṃ suttaṃ niddisitabbaṃ.

Because these individuals are a portion of the sevenfold foundation and partake of the non-learner's share, the supramundane discourse—a discourse that is a portion of the sevenfold foundation—should be designated by these twenty-six noble individuals, who are spoken of in the manner beginning with 'the supramundane discourse has seven foundations,' by way of the discourses pertaining to the share of vision, the share of latent tendencies, and the share of the non-learner.

Imesaṃ chabbīsatiyā puggalānaṃ sakalalokuttarasuttatthattā ceva sattādhiṭṭhānekadesasuttatthattā ca lokuttaraṃ sattādhiṭṭhānekadesaṃ suttaṃ. Ettakehi puggalehi niddisitabbanti ācariyena niyametvā vibhattaṃ, amhehi ca ñātaṃ, “lokiyaṃ sattādhiṭṭhānekadesaṃ suttaṃ kittakehi puggalehi niddisitabba”nti vattabbattā “lokiyaṃ suttaṃ sattādhiṭṭhānaṃ ekūnavīsatiyā puggalehi niddisitabba”ntiādi vuttaṃ. “Te ekūnavīsati lokiyā puggalā katamehi dhammehi niddiṭṭhā samanvesitabbā”ti vattabbattā “te caritehī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Te ekūnavīsati lokiyā puggalā caritehi caritavisesehi niddiṭṭhā samanvesitabbāti. “Kathaṃ caritehi niddiṭṭhā”ti vattabbattā “keci rāgacaritā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Rāgacaritadosacaritādīhi caritehi ekūnavīsati lokiyapuggalā [V 0.0467] rāgacaritā, keci dosacaritā…pe… mohacarito cāti niddiṭṭhā. Iti niddiṭṭhehi imehi ekūnavīsatiyā puggalehi lokiyasattādhiṭṭhānekadesaṃ suttaṃ niddisitabbaṃ. “Lokiya”nti sāmaññavasena vuttampi “saṃkilesabhāgiyaṃ lokiya”nti visesato viññātabbaṃ.

For these twenty-six individuals, the supramundane discourse partially pertaining to the seven foundations is designated because of the meaning of the entire supramundane discourse and of the discourse partially pertaining to the seven foundations. It was determined and classified by the teacher that it should be designated by so many individuals, and it is known by us. Since it is to be stated, “By how many individuals should the mundane discourse partially pertaining to the seven foundations be designated?” it was said, “The mundane discourse pertaining to the seven foundations should be designated by nineteen individuals,” and so on. Since it is to be stated, “By what qualities should these nineteen mundane individuals be designated and investigated?” it was said, “By their temperaments,” and so on. These nineteen mundane individuals are to be designated and investigated by their temperaments, by their specific temperaments. Since it is to be stated, “How are they designated by their temperaments?” it was said, “Some are of greedy temperament,” and so on. The nineteen mundane individuals are designated by temperaments such as greedy temperament, hateful temperament, and so on, up to deluded temperament. Thus, by these nineteen designated individuals, the mundane discourse partially pertaining to the seven foundations should be designated. Although “mundane” is stated in a general sense, it should be specifically understood as “mundane, partaking of defilements.”

Lokiyaṃ sattādhiṭṭhānekadesaṃ suttaṃ ettakehi puggalehi niddisitabbanti ācariyena niyametvā vibhattaṃ, amhehi ca ñātaṃ, “vāsanābhāgiyaṃ sattādhiṭṭhānekadesaṃ suttaṃ katamehi puggalehi niddisitabba”nti vattabbattā “vāsanābhāgiya”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Vāsanābhāgiyaṃ sattādhiṭṭhānekadesaṃ suttaṃ sīlavantehi puggalehi, dhammehi ca niddisitabbanti yojetabbaṃ. “Kittakā sīlavantapuggalā”ti vattabbattā “te sīlavanto pañca puggalā”ti vuttaṃ. “Kittakā dhammā”ti vattabbattā “pakatisīla”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – pakatisīlavanto ca samādānasīlavanto ca cittappasādavanto [M 0.0352] ca samathavanto ca vipassanāvanto cāti pañca puggalā, pakatisīladhammo ca samādānasīladhammo ca cittappasādadhammo ca samathadhammo ca vipassanādhammo cāti pañca dhammāti imehi pañcahi puggalehi, imehi pañcahi dhammehi vāsanābhāgiyaṃ sattādhiṭṭhānekadesadhammādhiṭṭhānekadesaṃ suttaṃ yathākkamaṃ niddisitabbanti.

It was determined and classified by the teacher that the mundane discourse partially pertaining to the seven foundations should be designated by a certain number of individuals, and it is known by us. Since it is to be stated, “By which individuals should the discourse pertaining to the share of latent tendencies, partially pertaining to the seven foundations, be designated?” it was said, “Pertaining to the share of latent tendencies,” and so on. It should be understood that the discourse pertaining to the share of latent tendencies, partially pertaining to the seven foundations, is to be designated by virtuous individuals and by qualities. Since it is to be stated, “How many are the virtuous individuals?” it was said, “Those virtuous ones are five individuals.” Since it is to be stated, “How many are the qualities?” it was said, “Natural virtue,” and so on. This is what is meant: the naturally virtuous, those who undertake virtue, those with clarity of mind, those with serenity, and those with insight—these are the five individuals; and the quality of natural virtue, the quality of undertaken virtue, the quality of clarity of mind, the quality of serenity, and the quality of insight—these are the five qualities. By these five individuals and by these five qualities, the discourse pertaining to the share of latent tendencies, partially pertaining to the seven foundations and partially pertaining to the foundations of qualities, should be designated in due order.

Lokuttaraṃ sattādhiṭṭhānaṃ suttaṃ dassanabhāgiyavāsanābhāgiyaasekkhabhāgiyasuttehi niddisitabbanti ācariyena niyametvā vibhattaṃ, amhehi ca ñātaṃ, “lokuttaraṃ dhammādhiṭṭhānaṃ suttaṃ kittakehi suttehi niddisitabba”nti vattabbattā “lokuttaraṃ suttaṃ dhammādhiṭṭhānaṃ…pe… asekkhabhāgiyenā”ti vuttaṃ.

It was determined and classified by the teacher that the supramundane discourse of the seven foundations should be designated by the discourses pertaining to the share of vision, the share of latent tendencies, and the non-learner’s share, and it is known by us. Since it is to be stated, “By how many discourses should the supramundane discourse of the foundations of qualities be designated?” it was said, “The supramundane discourse of the foundations of qualities… by the one pertaining to the non-learner’s share.”

“Lokiyañca lokuttarañca sattādhiṭṭhānañca dhammādhiṭṭhānañca kittakehi niddisitabba”nti vattabbattā “lokiyañca…pe… ubhayena niddisitabba”nti vuttaṃ. Ubhayenāti lokiyalokuttarena, sattādhiṭṭhānadhammādhiṭṭhānena samānatthabhāvena niddisitabbanti.

Since it is to be stated, “By how many should the mundane and the supramundane, and the seven foundations and the foundations of qualities, be designated?” it was said, “The mundane… by both.” ‘By both’ means by the mundane and the supramundane, and by the seven foundations and the foundations of qualities; they should be designated because of having the same meaning.

“Ñāṇaṃ kittakehi niddisitabba”nti vattabbattā “ñāṇaṃ paññāyā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yasmiṃ yasmiṃ sutte ñāṇaṃ āgataṃ, tasmiṃ tasmiṃ sutte ñāṇaṃ ñāṇapariyāyena paññādinā niddisitabbanti.

Since it is to be stated, “By how many should knowledge be designated?” it was said, “Knowledge by wisdom,” and so on. In whichever discourse knowledge occurs, in that discourse knowledge should be designated by a synonym of knowledge, such as wisdom.

“Ñeyyaṃ kittakena niddisitabba”nti vattabbattā “ñeyyaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannehī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yasmiṃ yasmiṃ sutte ñeyyaṃ āgataṃ, tasmiṃ tasmiṃ sutte ñeyyaṃ ñeyyapariyāyena niddisitabbanti.

Since it is to be stated, “By how much should the knowable be designated?” it was said, “The knowable by the past, future, and present,” and so on. In whichever discourse the knowable occurs, in that discourse the knowable should be designated by a synonym of the knowable.

“Ñāṇañca [V 0.0468] ñeyyañca kittakena niddisitabba”nti vattabbattā “ñāṇañca ñeyyañca tadubhayenā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yasmiṃ yasmiṃ sutte ñāṇañeyyā āgatā, tasmiṃ tasmiṃ sutte ñāṇañeyyā ñāṇañeyyapariyāyena niddisitabbanti.

Since it is to be stated, “By how much should knowledge and the knowable be designated?” it was said, “Knowledge and the knowable by both of them,” and so on. In whichever discourse knowledge and the knowable occur, in that discourse knowledge and the knowable should be designated by a synonym of knowledge and the knowable.

Dassanasutte yathā niddiṭṭhaṃ, tathā upadhārayitvā labbhamānato niddisitabbaṃ. Bhāvanāsutte yathā niddiṭṭhaṃ, tathā upadhārayitvā labbhamānato niddisitabbaṃ. Tadubhayaṃ dassanañca bhāvanā ca sutte yathā niddiṭṭhaṃ, tathā upadhārayitvā labbhamānato niddisitabbaṃ.

As it is designated in the discourse on vision, so, having considered it, it should be designated as it is obtainable. As it is designated in the discourse on development, so, having considered it, it should be designated as it is obtainable. Both vision and development, as they are designated in the discourse, so, having considered them, they should be designated as they are obtainable.

“Sakavacanaṃ [M 0.0353] paravacana”ntiādīsupi evameva visuṃ visuṃ ca ekato ca sutte yathā niddiṭṭhaṃ, tathā upadhārayitvā labbhamānato niddisitabbanti yojanā kātabbā. “Ettakameva niddisitabba”nti vattabbattā “yaṃ vā panā”tiādi vuttaṃ.

Regarding ‘one’s own speech, another’s speech,’ and so on, in this very way the interpretation should be made: having considered how they are designated in the discourse, both separately and together, they should be designated as they are found. Since it is to be stated, “Only this much should be designated,” it was said, “Or whatever else,” and so on.

“Vipākassa hetu kammamevā”ti vattabbattā “duvidho hetū”tiādi vuttaṃ. Kilesā saṃkilesabhāgiyasuttena samānatthabhāvena niddisitabbā. Taṇhāsaṅkhāto samudayo vā kilesasaṅkhāto samudayo vā akusalasaṅkhāto samudayo vā saṃkilesabhāgiyena suttena samānatthabhāvena niddisitabbo. Lokiyakusalahetusaṅkhāto samudayo vā lokiyakusalasaṅkhāto samudayo vā vāsanābhāgiyena suttena samānatthabhāvena niddisitabbo.

Since it is to be stated, “The cause of result is kamma alone,” it was said, “Twofold cause,” and so on. Defilements should be designated by the discourse pertaining to the share of defilements, because of their similar meaning. The origin designated as craving, or the origin designated as defilements, or the origin designated as unwholesome, should be designated by the discourse pertaining to the share of defilements, because of their similar meaning. The origin designated as worldly wholesome causes, or the origin designated as worldly wholesome, should be designated by the discourse pertaining to the share of latent tendencies, because of their similar meaning.

Kammañca vipāko ca yathārahaṃ labbhamānasuttena niddisitabboti sāmaññavasena vibhatto, “kusalaṃ katamena niddisitabba”nti vattabbattā “tattha kusala”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Tatthāti tesu aṭṭhavīsatiyā sāsanapaṭṭhānasuttesu kusalaṃ catūhi suttehi samānatthabhāvena niddisitabbaṃ. “Katamehi catūhī”ti vattabbattā “vāsanābhāgiyenā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Lokiyakusalaṃ vāsanābhāgiyena niddisitabbaṃ samānatthattā, lokuttarakusalaṃ dassanabhāgiyena, vāsanābhāgiyena, asekkhabhāgiyena ca yathārahaṃ samānatthabhāvena niddisitabbaṃ. Kusalaṃ ettakehi niddisitabbanti niyametvā vibhattaṃ, “akusalaṃ katamena niddisitabba”nti vattabbattā “akusala”ntiādi vuttaṃ. “Kusalañca akusalañca katamena niddisitabba”nti vattabbattā “kusalañca akusalañca tadubhayena niddisitabba”nti vuttaṃ. Yasmiṃ yasmiṃ sutte tadubhayaṃ āgataṃ, tasmiṃ tasmiṃ sutte āgatena tadubhayena niddisitabbaṃ.

Kamma and result are analyzed in a general way, that they should be designated by the appropriate discourse as it is found. Since it is to be stated, “By what should the wholesome be designated?” it was said, “Herein, the wholesome,” and so on. ‘Herein’ means in these twenty-eight discourses of the foundation of the Dispensation, the wholesome should be designated by four discourses because of their similar meaning. Since it is to be stated, “By which four?” it was said, “By the one pertaining to the share of latent tendencies,” and so on. The worldly wholesome should be designated by the discourse pertaining to the share of latent tendencies because of its similar meaning; the supramundane wholesome should be designated by the discourses pertaining to the share of vision, the share of latent tendencies, and the non-learner’s share, appropriately, because of their similar meaning. It is determined and analyzed that the wholesome is to be designated by these many. Since it is to be stated, “By what should the unwholesome be designated?” it was said, “The unwholesome,” and so on. Since it is to be stated, “By what should both the wholesome and the unwholesome be designated?” it was said, “Both the wholesome and the unwholesome should be designated by both.” In whichever discourse both occur, in that discourse they should be designated by both as they have occurred therein.

“Anuññātaṃ katamena niddisitabba”nti vattabbattā “anuññāta”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Anuññātaṃ [V 0.0469] bhagavato anuññātāya samānatāya niddisitabbaṃ. “Katividhaṃ anuññāta”nti vattabbattā “taṃ pañcavidha”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Yaṃ anuññātaṃ yāsu yāsu bhūmīsu dissati, taṃ anuññātaṃ tāsu tāsu bhūmīsu āgatena samānena kappiyānulomena niddisitabbaṃ.

Since it is to be said, “By what should the permitted be indicated?”, therefore, “permitted,” etc., was stated. The permitted should be indicated as being similar to what was permitted by the Blessed One. Since it is to be said, “How many kinds of permitted are there?”, therefore, “it is fivefold,” etc., was stated. Whatever is permitted and is found in whatever grounds, that permitted should be indicated in those very grounds by what has come therein, being similar and in accordance with what is allowable.

Anuññātaṃ [M 0.0354] iminā niddisitabbanti ācariyena niyametvā vibhattaṃ, “paṭikkhittaṃ katamena niddisitabba”nti vattabbattā “paṭikkhittaṃ bhagavatā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Bhagavatā paṭikkhittaṃ bhagavatā paṭikkhittakāraṇena sutte āgatena vatthunā kāraṇaphalabhāvena niddisitabbaṃ. Yaṃ paṭikkhittaṃ yāsu yāsu bhūmīsu dissati, taṃ pana paṭikkhittaṃ tāsu tāsu bhūmīsu āgatena pākaṭena akappiyānulomena niddisitabbaṃ.

The teacher determined and analyzed that the permitted should be indicated by this. Since it is to be said, “By what should the prohibited be indicated?”, therefore, “prohibited by the Blessed One,” and so on, was stated. What is prohibited by the Blessed One should be indicated by the reason for the prohibition given by the Blessed One, by the subject matter that has come in the Sutta, as cause and effect. Moreover, whatever is prohibited and is seen in various grounds, that prohibited should be indicated in those very grounds by what has come therein, by what is evident, and in accordance with what is not allowable.

“Anuññātañca paṭikkhittañca katamena niddisitabba”nti vattabbattā “anuññātañca paṭikkhittañca tadubhayena niddisitabba”nti vuttaṃ. Yasmiṃ yasmiṃ sutte anuññātañca paṭikkhittañca āgataṃ, tasmiṃ tasmiṃ sutte āgatena tadubhayena niddisitabbaṃ.

Since it is to be said, “By what should the permitted and the prohibited be indicated?”, therefore, “the permitted and the prohibited should be indicated by both,” was stated. In whichever Sutta the permitted and the prohibited have come, in that very Sutta it should be indicated by both which have come therein.

“Thavo katamena niddisitabbo”ti vattabbattā “thavo pasaṃsāyā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yasmiṃ yasmiṃ sutte yā yā pasaṃsā āgatā, tasmiṃ tasmiṃ sutte āgatāya tāya tāya pasaṃsāya thavo niddisitabbo. “Yo thavo pasaṃsāya niddisitabbo, so thavo katividhena niddisitabbo”ti vattabbattā “so pañcavidhenā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Bhagavato thavo ca dhammassa thavo ca ariyasaṅghassa thavo ca ariyadhammānaṃ sikkhāya thavo ca lokiyaguṇasampattiyā thavo cāti pañcavidhena veditabbo. Iti evaṃ vuttappakārena pañcavidhena thavo niddisitabbo.

Since it is to be said, “By what should praise be indicated?”, therefore, “praise is by commendation,” etc., was stated. In whichever Sutta whatever commendation has come, in that very Sutta, praise should be indicated by that very commendation which has come therein. Since it is to be said, “Praise, which should be indicated by commendation, by how many ways should that praise be indicated?”, therefore, “it is by five ways,” etc., was stated. The praise of the Blessed One, the praise of the Dhamma, the praise of the Noble Sangha, the praise of the training in the Noble Dhamma, and the praise of worldly virtue and accomplishment—it should be understood as fivefold. Thus, praise should be indicated in five ways in the manner stated.

Amhākācariya amhākācariyena aṭṭhārasa mūlapadā sāsanapaṭṭhāne daṭṭhabbāti vuttā, “katamāni tāni aṭṭhārasa mūlapadānī”ti pucchitabbattā “indriyabhūmī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Sāsanapaṭṭhāne indriyabhūmi saddhindriyādiindriyabhūmi yehi navahi padehi niddisitabbā, sāsanapaṭṭhāne kilesabhūmi yehi navahi padehi niddisitabbā, evaṃ iminā pakārena etāni mūlapadāni nava padāni kusalapadāni, nava padāni akusalapadānīti aṭṭhārasa mūlapadāni honti. Sāsanapaṭṭhāne daṭṭhabbā, “kena kāraṇena aṭṭhārasa mūlapadā sāsanapaṭṭhāne daṭṭhabbāti viññāyatī”ti vattabbattā “tathā hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tathā hīti tato eva aṭṭhārasamūlapadānaṃ sāsanapaṭṭhāne daṭṭhabbattā “aṭṭhārasa mūlapadā kuhiṃ daṭṭhabbā? Sāsanapaṭṭhāne”ti yaṃ [M 0.0355] vacanaṃ vuttaṃ, tena vacanena viññāyatīti. “Kena mūlapadānaṃ navakusalapadanavaakusalapadabhāvena [V 0.0470] aṭṭhārasabhāvo viññāyatī”ti vattabbattā “tenāhā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tena mūlapadānaṃ navakusalapadanavaakusalapadabhāvato āyasmā mahākaccāno –

Our teacher said that the eighteen root principles should be seen in the foundation of the Dispensation. Since it is to be asked, “What are those eighteen root principles?”, therefore, “the sphere of faculties,” etc., was stated. In the foundation of the Dispensation, the sphere of faculties—such as the faculty of faith and so on—should be indicated by these nine terms; in the foundation of the Dispensation, the sphere of defilements should be indicated by these nine terms. Thus, in this way, these root principles consist of nine wholesome terms and nine unwholesome terms, making eighteen root principles. They should be seen in the foundation of the Dispensation. Since it is to be said, “For what reason is it understood that the eighteen root principles should be seen in the foundation of the Dispensation?”, therefore, “Because it is so,” etc., was stated. Because it is so, that is, because the eighteen root principles are to be seen in the foundation of the Dispensation, it is understood by the statement, “Where should the eighteen root principles be seen? In the foundation of the Dispensation.” Since it is to be said, “By what is the eighteenfold nature of the root principles, by way of nine wholesome terms and nine unwholesome terms, understood?”, therefore, “Therefore, he said,” etc., was stated. Therefore, because the root principles consist of nine wholesome terms and nine unwholesome terms, the Venerable Mahākaccāna said:

“Navahi ca padehi kusalā, navahi ca yujjanti akusalapakkhā;

Ete kho mūlapadā, bhavanti aṭṭhārasa padānī”ti. –

“By nine terms are the wholesome, and by nine are the unwholesome factions joined; these indeed are the root terms, becoming eighteen terms.”

Yaṃ vacanaṃ āha, tena “navahi…pe… padānī”ti vacanena mūlapadānaṃ navakusalapadanavaakusalapadabhāvena aṭṭhārasabhāvo viññāyatīti.

By that statement which he spoke, that is, by the statement, “By nine… up to… terms,” the eighteenfold nature of the root terms is understood by way of their being nine wholesome terms and nine unwholesome terms.

“Yaṃ yaṃ saṃkilesabhāgiyādisoḷasavidhaṃ sāsanapaṭṭhānañceva yaṃ yaṃ lokiyādiaṭṭhavīsatividhaṃ sāsanapaṭṭhānañca ācariyena niddhāritaṃ, ettakameva paripuṇṇaṃ, aññaṃ sāsanapaṭṭhānaṃ niddhāretvā yuttaṃ yujjitabbaṃ natthī”ti vattabbattā “niyuttaṃ sāsanapaṭṭhāna”nti vuttaṃ. Yathāniddhāritasāsanapaṭṭhānato yaṃ yaṃ aññaṃ sāsanapaṭṭhānaṃ niddhāritaṃ atthi, taṃ taṃ aññaṃ sāsanapaṭṭhānaṃ niyuttaṃ yathārahaṃ niddhāretvā yuttaṃ yujjitabbanti attho gahetabboti.

Since it is to be said, “Whatever sixteenfold foundation of the Dispensation pertaining to defilement and whatever twenty-eightfold foundation of the Dispensation pertaining to the worldly have been determined by the teacher, only that much is complete; there is no other foundation of the Dispensation that, having been determined, should be appropriately connected and applied,” therefore, “the determined foundation of the Dispensation” was stated. Whatever other foundation of the Dispensation exists that has been determined apart from the foundation of the Dispensation as determined, that other foundation of the Dispensation, having been appropriately determined, should be connected and applied as is fitting—this is the meaning to be understood.

“Yaṃ loko pūjayate…pe… niyuttaṃ sāsanapaṭṭhānanti yattako vacanakkamo bhāsito, ettakena vacanakkamena kiṃ netti samattā, udāhu asamattā”ti vattabbattā “ettāvatā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Āyasmatā mahākaccānena yā netti bhāsitā, bhagavatā sā netti anumoditā, mūlasaṅgītiyaṃ saṅgāyantehi therāsabhehi yā netti saṅgītā, sā netti “yaṃ loko pūjayate…pe… niyuttaṃ sāsanapaṭṭhāna”nti ettāvatā vacanakkamena samattā paripuṇṇāva hoti.

Since it is to be said, “Regarding the sequence of statements spoken so far, from ‘That which the world reveres…’ up to ‘…the determined foundation of the Dispensation,’ is the Netti complete or incomplete by this extent of the sequence of statements?”, therefore, “Thus far,” etc., was stated. The Netti spoken by the Venerable Mahākaccāna was approved by the Blessed One. The Netti that was recited by the chief elders during the First Council—that Netti, from “That which the world reveres…” up to “…the determined foundation of the Dispensation”—is complete and entirely sufficient by this extent of the sequence of statements.

Iti samattāya āyasmatā mahākaccānena bhāsitāya bhagavatā anumoditāya mūlasaṅgītiyaṃ saṅgāyantehi therāsabhehi saṅgītāya nettiyā atthavaṇṇanā saddhammapālanāmena mahādhammarājagurunā mahātherena racitā jinaputtānaṃ hitakarā nettivibhāvanā chabbīsādhikanavasate sakkarāje sāvaṇamāse sukkapakkhe navamadivase sūriyuggamanasamaye samattā.

Thus, the elucidation of the Netti, which is an exposition of the meaning of the Netti (that Netti having been spoken by the Venerable Mahākaccāna, approved by the Blessed One, and recited by the chief elders in the fundamental recitation), composed by the great elder named Saddhammapālana, the great royal teacher of the Dhamma, for the welfare of the sons of the Victorious One, was completed in the Sakka era, in the year nine hundred and twenty-six, in the month of Sāvaṇa, on the ninth day of the bright fortnight, at the time of sunrise.

Iti sāsanapaṭṭhāne sattibalānurūpā racitā vibhāvanā

Thus, this elucidation of the Foundation of the Dispensation was composed in accordance with my ability and strength.

Niṭṭhitā.

It is finished.

Nigamanakathā

Concluding Words

Sabbasattuttamo [V 0.0471][M 0.0356] nātho, loke uppajji nāyako;

Sambuddho gotamo jino, anekaguṇalaṅkato.

The supreme among all beings, the protector, the leader, arose in the world: the Fully Enlightened One, Gotama the Conqueror, adorned with countless virtues.

Sāsanaṃ tassa seṭṭhassa, aṭṭhavassasatādhikaṃ;

Dvisahassaṃ yadā pattaṃ, nimmalaṃ vaḍḍhanaṃ subhaṃ.

When the Dispensation of that Excellent One had reached two thousand and more than eight hundred years, it was pure, flourishing, and auspicious.

Tadā bhūmissaro mahādhammarājā mahiddhiko;

Āṇācakkena sāreti, rājā noanuvattake.

Then the lord of the earth, the great righteous king, possessed of great power, the king who cannot be turned back, sets in motion the Wheel of Command.

Laddhā setagaje vare, loke vimhayajānake;

Appamatto mahāvīro, puññaṃ katvābhimodati.

Having obtained an excellent white elephant, which causes wonder in the world, the diligent, great hero rejoices, having made merit.

Tasmiṃ vasseva sāvaṇe, māse navamadivase;

Sūriyuggamane kāle, nibbattāyaṃ vibhāvanā.

In that very year, in the month of Sāvaṇa, on the ninth day, at the time of sunrise, this elucidation was produced.

Yattakaṃ sāsanaṃ ṭhitaṃ, tattakaṃ racitaṃ mayā;

Ṭhātu nettivibhāvanā, jinaputtahitāvahā.

May this, composed by me, endure as long as the Dispensation endures; may the Nettivibhāvanā stand, bringing welfare to the sons of the Conqueror.

Iti taṃ racayantena, puññaṃ adhigataṃ mayā;

Hontu tassānubhāvena, sabbe vimuttibhāgino.

Thus, by composing this, I have acquired merit; by its power, may all beings become partakers of liberation.

Rājadevī [V 0.0472] puttanattā, panattā ca sajātikā;

Sabbe rajjasukhe ṭhatvā, carantu caritaṃ sukhī.

The queen, her sons, grandsons, and great-grandsons, and her kin, all established in royal bliss, may they live happily, practicing good conduct.

Devo kāle suvassatu, sabbo raṭṭhajano sukhī;

Aññamaññaṃ ahiṃsanto, piyo hotu hitāvahoti.

May the deva rain in due season; may all the people of the country be happy; not harming one another, may they be beloved and bring welfare.

Nettivibhāvinī niṭṭhitā.

The Nettivibhāvinī is completed.
